issue.title: Support images that refuse root SSH login
issue.body:
`ephemeral run-ssh` logs in as root:

https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/blob/5349e1398bb6cbea8f7378f29bcb9944225c10f1/crates/kit/src/ssh.rs#L146

and `to-disk` boots the target image itself as the installer:

https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/blob/5349e1398bb6cbea8f7378f29bcb9944225c10f1/crates/kit/src/to_disk.rs#L178-L183

So images that refuse root SSH (`PermitRootLogin no`, `AllowUsers`) can't be tested or installed without patching sshd in the VM.

Would it be possible to:
- log in as a configurable user (like `libvirt ssh --user`), and
- let `to-disk` use a separate installer image?

issue.title: bcvk requires sshd enabled in container image to be able to install into a disk image
issue.body:
As far as I could figure out so far, it looks like bcvk relies on sshd being enabled and started by default in the container image when trying to create disk images from it.

We should be able to dynamically enable the sshd service via a kernel parameter: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/kernel-command-line.html

Likely `systemd.wants=sshd.service`.

comment.body:
One more requirement for minimal images: `sshd` by itself is not sufficient.

I reproduced this with a very minimal bootc image (systemd, kernel, dnf, bootc, no sshd).

After adding openssh-server and openssh-clients, sshd came up and was listening:

```
sshd.service: Server listening on 0.0.0.0 port 22.
```

but bcvk still failed with `Timeout waiting for readiness after 240s`. The guest journal showed the interface came up as enp0s7 but there was no DHCP activity at all, because the image has no NetworkManager and no dhcp-client. qemu's hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 accepted the connection and then hung at banner exchange, since the guest had no address.

Once I added NetworkManager, readiness was achieved:

```
dhcp4 (enp0s7): state changed new lease, address=10.0.2.15
```

So the requirement is `sshd` plus a DHCP-capable network stack (NetworkManager, or systemd-networkd with DHCP enabled), plus the ssh client in the image, since bcvk execs ssh inside the ephemeral container.

Separately, to-disk also needs --filesystem on images without a bootc install config:

```
error: Installing to disk: Creating rootfs: No install configuration found, and no filesystem specified
```

With all of that, both to-disk and libvirt run succeed on the minimal image.

Assisted by AI tooling.

review.body: LGTM

issue.title: Image cache ignores --disk-size
issue.body:
In a nutshell:

1. `bcvk libvirt run --filesystem btrfs quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44`
2. Realize the above uses 20G disk by default and you filled it up, oops
3. `bcvk libvirt run --filesystem btrfs --disk-size 40G quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44`

Results in reusing the original qcow and the disk is still 20G despite explicit `--disk-size 40G`.

issue.title: Missing aarch64 release artifacts (only x86_64 currently published)
issue.body:
GitHub release assets are not published for aarch64, even though Packit builds aarch64 for [every COPR target](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/blob/main/.packit.yaml#L34-L46).
[v0.22.0](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/releases/tag/v0.22.0) and earlier ship only `bcvk-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`, and [`docs/src/installation.md`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/blob/main/docs/src/installation.md) likewise only mentions x86_64 for the OCI artifact.
Both publishing jobs run on x86_64 with no matrix ([`release.yml`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml#L18), [`main.yml`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/blob/main/.github/workflows/main.yml#L119)).

Is the absence of aarch64 artifacts intentional, please?

comment.body: Hmm we should definitely not be opening fds without O_CLOEXEC that sounds like a bug if so

Running full validation here rejects `add_virtiofs()` configurations whose socket parent directory does not exist yet, even without TPM enabled. `spawn_virtiofsd_async()` creates that directory, but this check now fails before setup can run. Limit this early check to TPM architecture support and leave full validation in the existing QEMU `spawn()` call after virtiofsd setup.

This spawn lets swtpm inherit the non-close-on-exec write ends created by `add_virtio_serial_pipe()`. With `--tpm` and `--execute` or journal streaming, shutdown can hang because `run_impl` waits for pipe EOF before dropping swtpm, which keeps those writers open after QEMU exits. Make the pipes close-on-exec while preserving explicit descriptor passing to QEMU, or close unrelated descriptors before executing swtpm.

issue.title: ephemeral: Add a TPM 2.0 emulated by swtpm
issue.body:
Allow adding a TPM 2.0 to ephemeral bcvk VMs, emulated by swtpm:

- `--tpm` attaches an ephemeral TPM. Its state is discarded with the container.

swtpm runs inside the container from the host's `/usr`, just like virtiofsd. QEMU attaches it as a `tpm-tis` device (`tpm-tis-device` on aarch64). This is the same tpm model `bcvk libvirt run` uses.

Added `test_run_ephemeral_tpm` which checks if the emulated TPM shows up under `/dev/tpmrm0`.

Assisted-by: AI

comment.body:
Just for some more context on how this can be used for some e2e verified boot testing: 

1. You create an "installer vm" with `bcvk ephemeral --tpm-state DIR` with a mounted empty disk.
2. Inside you set up the disk with LUKS and TPM and call `bootc install to-filesystem` on it. 
3. After creating a disk in the installer VM a 2nd vm can boot it reusing the previous TPM's state and unlock the disk unattended. This can be a `systemd-vmspawn` vm, etc.

The idea is that this emulates how you might set up a bare-metal device where the installer and the booted system post-install see the same TPM.

issue.title: ostree-ext: override root dir metadata on merge commit

labels.name: area/ostree
labels.description: Issues related to ostree

issue.body:
When building the merge commit in `write_merge_commit_impl()`, `write_dfd_to_mtree()` inherits the root dir metadata from the temp checkout dir, which causes its mode to be 0o755 rather than 0o555.

Manually override it to uid=0, gid=0, and importantly mode=0o555. This matches the expectations of the filesystem RPM and systemd's /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/root.conf.

Without this change, systemd-tmpfiles fails with `fchmod() of / failed: Read-only file system` on systems with a read-only root since systemd v261.

See https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/2238

Assisted-by: llm

---

I've manually confirmed that this resolves the root permissions issues (`0o755 -> 0o555`) locally by comparing output from systems with `bootc 1.17.1` to systems with this patch included, using both:

- RPM overrides in `cosa` builds of Fedora CoreOS
- Bootc builds using packages built using `just build` and run using `just test-tmt-nobuild --preserve-vm readonly`

Example output without patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
755
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00755 0 0      0 /
```

Vs with the patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
555
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00555 0 0      0 /
```

Of course, let me know if I'm missing anything or if any changes are required.

issue.body:
system-reinstall: Propagate boot mount in container

systemd gpt-auto-generator has automount for /boot which we need to
propagate inside the container for the service to mount the ESP at
/boot on access

Also, before remounting `/boot` as rw, check if it's readonly so we
don't fail the re-mount operation

---

composefs: Fix `install to-existing-root`

Fix a few issues with composefs path for `install to-existing-root`.

1. Composefs repository initialization
Since we mount `/sysroot:ro` at `/target`, composefs repository
initialization would fail with `Read only filesystem`. Fix it by
remounting `/target/sysroot` read-write

2. Handle bootloader
Get the current bootloader by reading `LoaderInfo` and try to install
the same one

---

cfs/to-existing-root: Bootloader support

To figure out which bootloader to install, get the host's bootloader
(read from LoaderInfo from efivars) and store it in state. Before
finalizing the bootloader, check if the detected bootloader is
compatible with the current image (as the bootloader on host and the one in
the new image might differ)

issue.title: Add `bootc discard-staged` to safely cancel a pending deployment
issue.body:
### Description
Bootc currently lacks a dedicated way to discard a staged deployment while keeping the **currently booted image** as the next-boot default. `bootc rollback` discards staging but queues the rollback image instead. This matters when a staged image fails a newly applied signature policy: skipping an agent-initiated reboot is insufficient because an unrelated reboot may still apply it. See [CVE-2026-16460](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2026-16460). This mechanism will also benefit the bootc-operator, since a signature policy could change between the time the deployment was staged and the reboot, this will enable the bootc-operator to discard the deployment.

### Expected behavior
- Works with OSTree and composefs backends, including ordinary and `--download-only` stages.
- Leaves booted image selected for next boot; preserves rollback deployment.
- Is safe and idempotent when no stage exists.
- Handles concurrent staging safely and documents how the tracked image reference changes.
- After success, `bootc status` shows no staged deployment; an unrelated reboot cannot apply the discarded image.
- Includes tests for both backends and next-boot behavior.

issue.title: tests: Add a sysext and confext test with a separate, empty /var
issue.body:
This adds a tmt test that stacks a directory sysext (over `/usr`) and a directory confext (over `/etc`) on a bootc host whose `/var` is a separate partition. The partition is empty when the host first boots from it, and it holds the extensions.

The test merges and unmerges each extension from a shell. It then replaces a merged extension with a new version and checks that `refresh` shows the new one. Finally it checks that `systemd-sysext.service` and `systemd-confext.service` merge them at boot from the separate `/var`, and that no unit has failed once that boot has settled. Each failure starts with the component that broke: `[layout]`, `[bootc]`, `[systemd-sysext]`, `[systemd-confext]` or `[test harness]`.

<!-- jmarrero: context/rationale -->

The change touches only the test file and the regenerated tmt lists. Booting a disk installed inside the VM isn't possible here, and root fills the rest of the VM's disk. So, like the XBOOTLDR test, the test shrinks the ESP, which holds about 8M of its 512M, to 128M. It puts the `/var` partition in the space that frees and mounts it from `/etc/fstab`. Only tmt's plan directory and scripts, taken from tmt's environment, are copied onto it.

The test runs on CentOS Stream 9 and 10 in image mode, on the ostree backend only. That is one VM, with three boots, in one matrix cell per distribution. `systemd-confext` only exists from systemd 254 on, so CentOS Stream 9 (systemd 252) tests the sysext and logs a SKIP for the confext. On newer systemd, a missing `systemd-confext` fails the test.

Finding: on CentOS Stream 9, merging relabels `/usr` (systemd/systemd#34387, fixed in 257 by systemd/systemd#35132):
- After a merge from a shell, `/usr` is `user_tmp_t`, and sshd refuses all new logins with `chroot("/usr/share/empty.sshd"): Permission denied`.
- After a merge by the service, `/usr` is `tmpfs_t`.

On systemd older than 257, the test reports exactly the label each way of merging gives as a `KNOWN ISSUE`, and fails on any other label change. It unmerges before tmt has to log in again. CentOS Stream 10's systemd 257 keeps the `/usr` and `/etc` labels, so the check is strict there. tmt has no result that warns without failing the plan, so the known issue only shows in the test's output. A RHEL backport would keep systemd at 252, so a TODO next to the version gate says to drop the exception then.

Finding: a merged confext keeps `/etc` read-only for the whole boot. On CentOS Stream 10, bootc's own `bootc-publish-rhsm-facts.service` then fails with `Writing etc/rhsm/facts/bootc.facts: Read-only file system`. The test reports that one unit as a `KNOWN ISSUE` until bootc skips it on a read-only `/etc`, and fails on any other unit that fails.

Not covered: `bootc upgrade` or `switch` with extensions merged.

Testing was on a 16-core devspace (bcvk 0.19.0, tmt 1.80.0). Images were built like CI's ostree cells, at this tree. Logs are in https://gist.github.com/jmarrero-bot/ebbba1edfa9d7a805f304a789afec21b.
- `just test-tmt-nobuild extensions-separate-var` passed on centos-9 (sysext, with the label KNOWN ISSUE lines) and on centos-10 (sysext and confext, with the rhsm KNOWN ISSUE).
- These deliberately broken variants each failed with a tagged message:
  - sysext extension-release, on both distros: `[systemd-sysext] ... is not visible under /usr`.
  - confext extension-release, on c10: `[systemd-confext] ... is not visible under /etc`.
  - replacing the extension without a refresh, on both: `[systemd-sysext] ... holds '... v1', expected '... v2'`.
  - `systemd-confext` treated as missing, on c10: `[systemd-confext] systemd 257 should have systemd-confext`.
  - a unit that fails 60s into the final boot, on c10: `[systemd-confext] late-fail-demo.service failed ...`.
- `just validate` passed.

Part of jmarrero-forge/tracker#88. The docs half is a separate PR.

The `Signed-off-by: Joseph Marrero Corchado <jmarrero@redhat.com>` on these commits was added on jmarrero's approval of the review draft: https://github.com/jmarrero-forge/bootc/pull/22#issuecomment-6918095271

issue.title: install: logically bound images are not installed with --composefs-backend
issue.body:
With `--composefs-backend`, `bootc install` doesn't copy logically bound images into the installed system. The install exits 0 and prints nothing about bound images. The same install without `--composefs-backend` puts the image in `/ostree/bootc/storage`.

Reproduced on `quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44` (bootc 1.16.13), binding a busybox image by a tag that is in the host storage before the install:

```
podman pull docker.io/library/busybox@sha256:f97baa533a26513c453a362be331a43eb60214302f449c16571b23cea141dce4
podman tag docker.io/library/busybox@sha256:f97baa533a26513c453a362be331a43eb60214302f449c16571b23cea141dce4 docker.io/library/busybox:latest
```

```
FROM quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44@sha256:5ab8ee5189bb0f3870279723f5343474df002d8d6f46564702b3ad3ba7382d98
COPY bound.container /usr/share/containers/systemd/bound.container
RUN mkdir -p /usr/lib/bootc/bound-images.d && ln -s /usr/share/containers/systemd/bound.container /usr/lib/bootc/bound-images.d/bound.container
```

```
# bound.container
[Container]
Image=docker.io/library/busybox:latest
```

```
podman build -t localhost/gaprepro:1 .
truncate -s 20G a.raw b.raw
podman run --rm --privileged --pid=host --security-opt label=type:unconfined_t \
  -v /dev:/dev -v /var/lib/containers:/var/lib/containers -v $PWD:/out localhost/gaprepro:1 \
  bootc install to-disk --via-loopback --filesystem ext4 --generic-image --wipe \
  --composefs-backend /out/a.raw
# the same again without --composefs-backend, writing b.raw
```

With each root partition mounted, `ostree/bootc/storage/overlay-images/images.json` on the ostree disk lists `busybox:latest`. The composefs disk has no container storage, and the only file on it that mentions busybox is the stock `000-shortnames.conf`.

The composefs install doesn't read `bound-images.d` at all. With a regular file there instead of a symlink, the ostree install fails with `Querying bound images: Not a symlink: bound.container`, and the composefs install completes.

`BoundImages::from_state` is called only from `ostree_install` ([install.rs L2092](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/66d4e4d65685895742934060fdaffa6f69793259/crates/lib/src/install.rs#L2092)), and the copy happens in `install_with_sysroot` ([L2029-L2043](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/66d4e4d65685895742934060fdaffa6f69793259/crates/lib/src/install.rs#L2029-L2043)). The composefs branch ([L2156-L2226](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/66d4e4d65685895742934060fdaffa6f69793259/crates/lib/src/install.rs#L2156-L2226)) has neither, and `plan-22-logically-bound-install` is skipped on composefs ([integration.fmf L69-L75](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/66d4e4d65685895742934060fdaffa6f69793259/tmt/plans/integration.fmf#L69-L75)).

I'd expect bound images to be present at first boot on both backends, as [bootc-logically-bound-images(7)](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/66d4e4d65685895742934060fdaffa6f69793259/docs/src/bootc-logically-bound-images.7.md#installation) describes.

Related: #2290, which pulls bound images on the composefs deploy path.

issue.title: Feature request: move `/usr/lib/bootc/initramfs-setup` to a separate subpackage
issue.body: I've been testing using [`mkosi-initrd`](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/mkosi-initrd) instead of Dracut, and it's been working really well so far. The only problem is that `mkosi-initrd` installs entire packages into the initramfs, and the `bootc` package depends on Podman, which means I have the entirety of Podman installed in my initramfs. Currently, I'm just running `rm /usr/bin/podman` in the build process, but it would be nice if something similar to e589fe15d7b482ff252c0c891ac1580aadb37da8 were implemented so that only `/usr/lib/bootc/initramfs-setup` and `/usr/lib/systemd/system/bootc-root-setup.service` would be installed.

issue.title: composefs backend: support state overlays (writable, image-reconciled subdirectories)
issue.body:
### Summary

State overlays work on the ostree backend and not on the composefs backend. It would be good to support them there, at least in the unsealed configuration, and to add them to the known issues list in `bootc-composefs.7.md` until then.

When the composefs-native backend was planned, bootc-dev/bootc#1190 listed the state overlay docs among ostree-era features the composefs path would need to keep honoring (https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/1190#issuecomment-2714380763). The backend is now stable, but state overlays are not on its parity list, have no tracking issue, and are silently skipped (ostreedev/ostree#3691).

### The use case

Many third-party host agents, especially security agents, install into `/opt/<vendor>` and write there at runtime: binaries, version symlinks, enrollment identity, and vendor-delivered content in one tree the vendor will not restructure. Two patterns:

1. **State and binaries mixed under `/opt`.** A writable directory whose binaries still come from the image. ostreedev/ostree#3120 named this case: software in `/opt` "often mixes code *and* state". ostreedev/ostree#3553 was filed by someone doing this for a vulnerability scanner agent.
2. **In-place self-updaters.** The agent's management plane pushes new files into its install directory (bootc-dev/bootc#2468 asked for a variant of this). State overlays do not make those updates permanent (the image wins at the next deployment change), but the agent runs and keeps its state.

### Why state overlays and not the alternatives

- **The image stays the authority.** At every deployment change, upper entries that shadow image content are pruned; only files the image does not ship, such as machine identity, are kept. Rollback gives a coherent pair: binaries roll back, identity stays.
- **Relocating the tree to `/var` is what people do instead, and it is worse.** Image content under `/var` is applied at install only, so the binaries freeze while the OS moves, and rollback cannot resynchronize them. `bootc container lint` already flags it. At least one vendor's published bootc recipe does it (https://github.com/CrowdStrike/falcon-bootc).
- **It is also simpler for the user.** That recipe has to move the tree into `/var/opt`, symlink it back, and on RHEL 9 add `semanage fcontext` rules so the moved binaries and libraries get the labels they would have had under `/opt`. A state overlay is one `systemctl enable` line: no relocation, no symlinks, no relabeling of the vendor's files, and the vendor's paths stay where it expects them.
- **Splitting state into `/var`** should stay the first recommendation, but only works when the writable paths can be separated from the binaries.
- **A container** is best where the vendor ships one, but most security agents are host installs, and logically bound images are not on this backend either (bootc-dev/bootc#2540).

Without state overlays, the composefs backend leaves these users the `/var` relocation, the least image-governed option. That matters more over time: upstream plans in-place moves from ostree to this backend, and bootc-dev/bootc#1190 framed it as a step toward phasing out ostree.

### Suggested scope

- **Unsealed composefs backend:** there is no integrity reason to exclude a writable overlay, so the ask is parity with the ostree backend, with the same semantics users rely on today: state written in the directory persists across reboots, content shipped in the image wins when the deployment changes, and rollback behaves the same way. How to build it is up to maintainers, however best fits the composefs root setup.
- **Sealed (fs-verity) configuration:** a writable overlay over measured content may be out of scope by design, as bootc-dev/bootc#2507 proposes for `usr-overlay`. If so, please say so in `bootc-composefs.7.md` rather than leaving a silent no-op.

### Naming

A composefs-native implementation is a natural point to adopt a backend-neutral unit name: `state-overlay@.service`, or `bootc-state-overlay@.service` if an unprefixed name is a concern. Keep `ostree-state-overlay@` as an alias so existing images keep working, and use scoped examples (`@opt-myvendor`, not `@opt`) in the docs.

### Known rough edges, not blockers

No way to see what the overlay holds or what a prune removed (a `notice` journal line would help; asked in the ostreedev/ostree#3120 review). The merged directory takes mode `0700` and label `var_t` from the upper, so non-root services cannot read it, and new files in it are labeled `var_t`. Docs show only the unscoped `@opt.service`. No state overlay tests in bootc (ostree has one); see also bootc-dev/bootc#1925.

### Related

- ostreedev/ostree#3691: fail visibly instead of skipping on this backend.
- bootc-dev/bootc#1190, bootc-dev/bootc#2540, bootc-dev/bootc#2507, bootc-dev/bootc#2468, bootc-dev/bootc#1925, ostreedev/ostree#3120.

@@ -393,6 +396,27 @@ pub(crate) struct InstallConfigOpts {
     #[clap(long)]
     #[serde(default)]
     pub(crate) bootloader: Option<Bootloader>,
+
+    /// The architecture of the image being installed. Defaults to the
+    /// architecture bootc runs on. Installing for another architecture is
+    /// supported for `install to-disk` with the composefs backend and
+    /// systemd-boot, and needs a systemd whose `bootctl install` supports
+    /// `--install-source`.
+    #[clap(long)]
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub(crate) target_arch: Option<TargetArch>,
+}
+
+impl InstallConfigOpts {
+    /// The architecture this install targets.
+    pub(crate) fn target_arch(&self) -> TargetArch {
+        self.target_arch.unwrap_or_else(TargetArch::host)
comment.body: On an x86_64-to-aarch64 BLS install, `setup_composefs_bls_boot` still calls `compute_new_kargs`, which filters the image's `kargs.d` files using the host architecture. This drops aarch64-specific entries and selects x86_64-specific entries, potentially losing the target's serial console or other required kernel arguments. Pass the target architecture through install-time kernel-argument computation while retaining host-based behavior for upgrades.

Before this pull, `install_to_filesystem_impl` calls `get_container_manifest_and_config`, which still selects the host platform. A foreign-only index can therefore fail before reaching this target-aware pull, while an index containing both architectures makes the disk-space check use the host image's layer sizes. Thread the selected target platform through that preliminary metadata lookup as well.

This incompatibility check runs after the `opts.wipe` block has already called `wipefs` on the disk and its partitions. An invocation combining `--wipe`, a foreign `--target-arch`, and active repart partitioning therefore destroys the existing partition signatures before reporting that the options are unsupported. Determine and reject this combination during preflight, before any wiping or other storage mutation.

comment.body: For dm-verity backed by two dm-crypt mappings over partitions of the same disk, `whole_disk()` compares the mappings' device numbers and incorrectly reports `SeveralDisks`. This leaves `volatile-root` pointing at the root dm device, so ESP/XBOOTLDR discovery still fails despite there being one backing disk. Resolve each slave's underlying device before comparing disks, and add this nested same-disk topology to the table-driven test.

When `ostree-prepare-root` has already created `volatile-root` from `/dev/gpt-auto-root`, the following `symlink()` ignores `EEXIST` and leaves the link pointing at the unlocked dm device. ESP/XBOOTLDR discovery and boot blessing therefore remain broken on this encrypted-root path despite resolving the backing partition. Update a pre-existing link that points at the original root device while preserving unrelated targets, and add coverage for this case.

issue.title: composefs: Stale ESPs on multi-disk roots make GC delete newer deployments
issue.body:
On the composefs backend, bootc writes boot artifacts to a single ESP. When the root sits on a multi-disk md RAID1 array, every other disk's ESP goes stale after the first upgrade. This causes two problems:

1. If the machine boots from a stale ESP, GC treats every deployment missing from that ESP as orphaned. It deletes their state directories and prunes their images from the shared root.
2. If the first disk dies, the machine silently boots the install image, several upgrades behind.

I'd like to agree on an approach here before sending a PR.

## Setup

- arm64 VM (KVM, edk2, Secure Boot off) with two disks and no NVRAM boot entries. The firmware boots `EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI` from the first disk that has one.
- Each disk has its own GPT table and ESP (`sda2`, `sdb2`). The ESPs sit outside any RAID.
- The root filesystem is on an md RAID1 array across one partition on each disk. `/var` is on a second RAID1 array.
- Installed with `bootc install to-existing-root --composefs-backend`. systemd-boot sits at the removable path on both ESPs, with UKIs. No XBOOTLDR partition.
- After the install, our installer copies the ESP that bootc wrote onto the other disk's ESP, once.
- Tested with bootc 1.17.3. The code at 0c5dd06 takes the same paths (see below).

## Reproducer

Three images: A (installed), B and C. Steps 1 to 5 and step 6 come from two runs of the same test.

1. Install A. Both ESPs match after the installer's copy.
2. `bootc switch` to B. bootc writes B's UKI and `loader/entries.staged/` to the booted ESP (`sda2`) only.
3. Reboot. Disk 0 boots B. `sda2` has entries for B and A. `sdb2` still has only A.
4. `bootc switch` to C and reboot. Disk 0 boots C. `sda2` holds C and B, and GC removed A's UKI and entry from it. `sdb2` still holds only A.
5. Blank disk 0 and boot. The firmware falls back to `sdb2`, and the machine boots A, two switches behind. `bootc status` shows no rollback. Nothing reports an error.
6. While booted into A from `sdb2`, run `bootc internals composefs-gc --prune-repo`. `/sysroot/state/deploy` holds A, B and C before. With `RUST_LOG=debug`, GC logs `bootloader_entries` containing only A, then cleans up B's and C's state directories as orphaned. It reports `Objects: 107 removed (649594714 bytes)` and `Pruned symlinks: 8 images, 39 streams`. Afterwards, `/sysroot/state/deploy` holds only A.

After step 6, B and C are gone along with their images. Replacing disk 0 and resyncing the array can't bring them back.

## Why

Line references are at 0c5dd06.

**bootc uses one ESP.**

- **Install** takes the first ESP among the root's backing disks: `find_first_colocated_esp()` in [`boot.rs:866`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/boot.rs#L866) and [`boot.rs:1909`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/boot.rs#L1909). `MountedImageRoot::new` also stops at the first ESP and carries a TODO for this ([`boot.rs:2212`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/boot.rs#L2212)).
- **A booted system** resolves one ESP from `LoaderDevicePartUUID` in `find_booted_from_esp()` ([`store/mod.rs:506`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/store/mod.rs#L506)). `Storage` holds a single `BootPartition` built from it ([`store/mod.rs:619`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/store/mod.rs#L619)). Upgrade, switch, rollback, finalize and GC all go through it.
- **Discovery** already finds every ESP. `find_colocated_esps()` walks the root's backing disks only ([`blockdev.rs:196`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/blockdev/src/blockdev.rs#L196)). The writers just use one of them.

**GC trusts that one ESP.** GC takes the set of live deployments from the entries on the booted ESP ([`gc.rs:302`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/gc.rs#L302), [`gc.rs:549`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/gc.rs#L549)). It deletes every state directory without an entry there ([`gc.rs:648`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/gc.rs#L648)). The guard at [`gc.rs:640`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/gc.rs#L640) only protects the booted deployment.

The rest of this section comes from reading the code. I haven't run it.

- **Normal operation reaches the same GC.** Step 6 used the internals command. Any `bootc upgrade` or `bootc switch` that stages a deployment runs the same GC with repo pruning ([`update.rs:511`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/update.rs#L511)). The GC at finalize skips pruning, and state-directory cleanup only runs with pruning ([`gc.rs:589`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/gc.rs#L589)). That explains why A's state directory survived step 4 on `sda2`.
- **A healthy array is exposed too.** It only takes one boot from the second disk, for example after a firmware update reorders boot entries or after disk 0 times out once.
- **Failure mode 2 has a time limit.** On a healthy disk 0, the next upgrade after step 4 would delete A's state directory. From then on, `sdb2` points at a deployment that no longer exists, and losing disk 0 leaves nothing bootable.

## Proposal

1. **Write every ESP on the root's backing disks.** This covers install, upgrade, switch, rollback and finalize. `Storage` would hold the set from `find_colocated_esps()` instead of a single `BootPartition`. [#2645](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/pull/2645) moved Type 1 entry writes to one place, which makes the loop cheaper.
2. **Compute GC liveness from the union of entries across those ESPs**, then clean each ESP. This keeps GC safe while the ESPs disagree, for example on an array that was degraded during an upgrade.
3. **Warn when an ESP is missing, and fail when a present ESP can't be written.** A degraded array must still upgrade from its remaining disk. A present ESP that silently stays stale is the bug this fixes.
4. **Enable it by default.** Discovery only covers the root's own disks, so a Windows ESP on another disk stays untouched ([#2554](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/2554)). Single-disk systems see no change.

Point 2 matters even without point 1. On its own, it prevents the data loss in step 6.

### Alternative: write one ESP, then sync the others

bootc would write the booted ESP as today. It would then sync the paths it owns (`EFI/Linux/bootc`, `loader/entries`, the systemd-boot binary) to the other ESPs, deletions included. This is a smaller change. It still has to pick a source of truth, though. After booting from the stale ESP, the sync would copy stale state over the good ESP. Writing every ESP and computing GC liveness from the union avoids that.

## Questions

1. Write every ESP, or write one and sync?
2. Should the GC liveness fix land first, as its own PR?
3. Should a present ESP that fails to write fail the operation, or warn?
4. Default on, or opt-in through an install config key?
5. With an XBOOTLDR partition ([#2573](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/pull/2573)), should the same rule apply per disk, writing each ESP and its sibling XBOOTLDR? I'd leave this out of the first PR.
6. Should `bootc status` report ESPs that disagree? Also a follow-up, in my view.

## Out of scope

The ostree backend has the same single-ESP TODO in `mount_esp_part` ([`bootloader.rs:47`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/0c5dd0649787f1af62933cf2a2f448a35acf9f8f/crates/lib/src/bootloader.rs#L47)). bootupd manages ESP content there, so it's a separate problem.

## Testing

- A unit test pinning `find_colocated_esps()` to the root's backing disks.
- A unit test for GC liveness across two boot directories that disagree.
- An integration test needs a VM with two disks and a RAID1 root. Can bcvk or the tmt plans attach a second disk? If not, I'd welcome pointers on where such a test should live.

The subsequent write_dfd_to_mtree() re-enumerates that tree and fails with EACCES, so an otherwise valid image can no longer be imported. issue.title: selinux: Ship policy module for install_t domain transitions
issue.body:
## Problem

When systemd directly runs a binary labeled `install_exec_t`, the SELinux policy transitions the process to `install_t` (which grants `mac_admin`). But when users wrap bootc in their own systemd services, the wrapper runs as `initrc_t` or `unconfined_service_t`, and there are no transition rules from those domains — so bootc never gets `install_t`. This silently breaks cross-major-version updates that need to write arbitrary SELinux labels.

This has been a pain point since the ostree days. Unlike rpm-ostree (a daemon where systemd handled the transition), bootc encourages users to wrap it in custom services where the entrypoint binary won't be `install_exec_t`.

Repro (from the issue):
```bash
# Direct exec — works:
systemd-run -u testservice -qPG -- /usr/bin/testservice  # → install_t

# Wrapper — broken:
systemd-run -u testservice -qPG -- /bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/testservice && echo done'  # → initrc_t
```

## Solution

Ship a small SELinux policy module that adds the missing `type_transition` rules from `initrc_t` and `unconfined_service_t` to `install_t` via `install_exec_t`. The module is built during the RPM build and loaded via `semodule` in `%post`.

Ref: RHEL-117256

issue.title: bootc permission failures with an selinux-confined root session
issue.body:
I'm working on a bootc-managed system build off of RHEL 10. The Containerfile applies STIG-mandated configuration changes, in particular, telling sudo to elevate the selinux context to `sysadm_t` and `sysadm_r` when becoming root (https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/red_hat_enterprise_linux_10/2026-03-11/finding/V-281250). The non-root user is configured to login with `staff_u`.

The end result is that rather than having an unconfined root user:

```
$ id -Z
unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
$ sudo -i
[sudo] password for foobar:
# id -Z
unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
```

I instead have this:

```
$ id -Z
staff_u:staff_r:staff_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
$ sudo -i
[sudo] password for foobar:
# id -Z
staff_u:sysadm_r:sysadm_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
```

Unfortunately, this prevents bootc from working entirely:

```
# bootc status
error: Status: Initializing storage: Acquiring sysroot: Remounting /sysroot read-write: Permission denied
```

The cause is this AVC denial:

```

node=localhost type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1777928077.035:495): arch=c000003e syscall=165 success=no exit=-13 a0=7f2e068fac7d a1=7f2e068fac7d a2=0 a3=200020 items=1 ppid=1849 pid=1857 auid=1000 uid=0 gid=0 euid=0 suid=0 fsuid=0 egid=0 sgid=0 fsgid=0 tty=pts1 ses=1 comm="tokio-runtime-w" exe=2F746D702F2E746D7033614575724D202864656C6574656429 subj=staff_u:sysadm_r:sysadm_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 key="export"
```

issue.title: composefs: Keep BLS entries when a signed GRUB started the system
issue.body:
A system set up for systemd-boot, with its UKIs and Type 1 entries, can also be started without systemd-boot: for example from a fallback firmware entry that goes through a distribution’s signed shim and GRUB, with GRUB booting the kernel and initramfs from its own configuration on the ESP, while shim doesn’t trust the system’s own key yet. GRUB is then the only loader that ran and names itself in LoaderInfo, and get_bootloader() takes any LoaderInfo other than systemd-boot’s or GRUB CC’s for a GRUB system, so bootc looks for a GRUB configuration under /boot that doesn’t exist, and bootc status fails on those starts, along with upgrade, switch and rollback.

For a generic GRUB it now probes the filesystem the way the non-EFI case already does, and treats the entries as BLS-compatible when /boot/loader/entries exists and there's no GRUB directory next to it. A GRUB with its own directory is still GRUB. The classifier's table test has both cases.

Assisted-by: AI

comment.body:
>> A systemd-boot install can also be started through a distribution's signed shim and GRUB,

> Ugh. I agree we probably need to support it but holy cow is it confusing.

Fair, I worded that badly. It's a system installed for systemd-boot, with its UKIs and Type 1 entries, but in our case there's a fallback firmware entry we use until shim trusts our key, and that start goes through Fedora's shim, GRUB and kernel instead. The GRUB config for it isn't under /boot and GRUB doesn't read the BLS entries, so bootc finds no GRUB directory and fails. The deployments and entries bootc manages are still the systemd-boot ones, which is why treating it as BLS-compatible is right there.

>  Wait I'm confused, shouldn't systemd-boot overwrite the LoaderInfo variable in this case?

systemd-boot doesn't run at all on that path. The firmware starts shim, shim starts GRUB, and GRUB boots the kernel and initramfs itself from its own config on the ESP. So LoaderInfo is GRUB's because GRUB is the only loader that ran.

I'll reword the description so it doesn't sound like GRUB chainloads systemd-boot.

issue.title: ostree-ext: override root dir metadata on merge commit

labels.name: area/ostree
labels.description: Issues related to ostree

issue.body:
When building the merge commit in `write_merge_commit_impl()`, `write_dfd_to_mtree()` inherits the root dir metadata from the temp checkout dir, which causes its mode to be 0o755 rather than 0o555.

Manually override it to uid=0, gid=0, and importantly mode=0o555. This matches the expectations of the filesystem RPM and systemd's /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/root.conf.

Without this change, systemd-tmpfiles fails with `fchmod() of / failed: Read-only file system` on systems with a read-only root since systemd v261.

See https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/2238

Assisted-by: llm

---

I've manually confirmed that this resolves the root permissions issues (`0o755 -> 0o555`) locally by comparing output from systems with `bootc 1.17.1` to systems with this patch included, using both:

- RPM overrides in `cosa` builds of Fedora CoreOS
- Bootc builds using packages built using `just build` and run using `just test-tmt-nobuild --preserve-vm readonly`

Example output without patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
755
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00755 0 0      0 /
```

Vs with the patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
555
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00555 0 0      0 /
```

Of course, let me know if I'm missing anything or if any changes are required.

issue.title: auto-updates fail with `opendir(boot): Operation not permitted` when /boot is a systemd automount that has idled out

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue appears to be valid

issue.body:
⚠️ DISCLAIMER. Report is generated by Claude Code while it was troubleshooting one of my bench systems.
I've read the report and indeed seems to be true.
If you don't want to read an LLM report, please stop here. Feel free to close the report.

---

## Summary

`bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service` does not declare `RequiresMountsFor=/boot`. On systems where `/boot` is a `systemd-gpt-auto-generator` automount with `TimeoutIdleSec=120`, `/boot` unmounts ~2 minutes after boot and the update timer then fires against an unmounted `/boot`, failing with:

```
error: Initializing storage: opendir(boot): Operation not permitted
```

The same failure hits `bootc status` and `bootc upgrade` run manually.

ostree hardened its own units against this exact hazard in ostreedev/ostree#2544; bootc's updater unit never got the equivalent.

## Environment

- bootc `1.16.7-1.fc44`
- ostree `2026.3-1.fc44`
- systemd `259.8-1.fc44`
- Base image `quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44`
- BIOS/GRUB boot: `sda1` BIOS boot, `sda2` vfat ESP (unused), `sda3` xfs root
- `/` is a composefs overlay; no `/etc/fstab`

## Symptom

```
Aug 21 18:40:55 systemd[1]: Starting bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service - Apply bootc updates...
Aug 21 18:40:56 bootc[2194]: error: Initializing storage: opendir(boot): Operation not permitted
Aug 21 18:40:56 systemd[1]: bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
```

Repeats on every timer firing. `opendir(...)` is libostree's `glnx_throw_errno_prefix` style, i.e. `EPERM` from `openat(sysroot_fd, "boot")`.

## Reproducer

Deterministic on an affected system:

```console
$ sudo umount /boot          # simulate the automount idling out
$ sudo bootc status
error: Status: opendir(boot): Operation not permitted
```

Note bootc's access does **not** trigger the automount — `/boot` remains unmounted afterwards. (I suspect this is because bootc re-execs under `unshare -m` and autofs won't service the request from that private mount namespace, but I haven't confirmed that.)

Touch `/boot` by any other means and bootc works again:

```console
$ ls /boot >/dev/null && sudo bootc status   # succeeds
```

## Root cause

Two generators both claim `/boot`:

- `ostree-system-generator` -> `/run/systemd/generator/boot.mount` (`What=/sysroot/boot`, `Options=bind`) — the real mount
- `systemd-gpt-auto-generator` -> `/run/systemd/generator.late/boot.automount` (`Where=/boot`, `TimeoutIdleSec=120`, described as "EFI System Partition Automount") — targeting the otherwise-unused ESP

When the autofs idle timer fires it tears down ostree's `/boot` bind mount. The ostree units survive this because they declare the dependency:

```console
$ systemctl show boot.mount -p RequiredBy
RequiredBy=ostree-finalize-staged.service ostree-boot-complete.service \
           ostree-finalize-staged-hold.service rpm-ostree-fix-shadow-mode.service local-fs.target

$ systemctl show bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service -p RequiresMountsFor
RequiresMountsFor=
```

## Why this is newly visible

This system ran fine for two weeks on ostree `2026.2` and broke on upgrade to `2026.3`, with bootc, systemd and the kernel at identical versions across both deployments. The behaviour change is ostreedev/ostree@62109dca ("prepare-root: create `/run/systemd/volatile-root` for composefs"), whose commit message states:

> With composefs enabled both are overlayfs mounts with an anonymous `st_dev` … As a result systemd-gpt-auto-generator silently skips all partition discovery: the ESP is never automounted on /boot

Before 2026.3, gpt-auto could not resolve the composefs root's block device and skipped partition discovery entirely, so `boot.automount` was never generated. Journal evidence — `Set up automount boot.automount` appears only in deployments running 2026.3:

```
boot -3: ostree 2026.2  automount=0
boot -2: ostree 2026.3  automount=1   <- /boot unmounted 2m41s after boot
boot -1: ostree 2026.2  automount=0
boot  0: ostree 2026.3  automount=1
```

So ostree 2026.3 makes gpt-auto work as intended, which in turn exposes the missing dependency in bootc. I'd expect this to affect any composefs-based bootc system with a discoverable ESP as 2026.3 rolls out.

## Proposed fix

Mirror what ostree does — add to `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
RequiresMountsFor=/boot
```

Verified as effective here via a drop-in: systemd then pulls in `boot.mount` and orders the service after it.

Two secondary suggestions:

1. `opendir(boot): Operation not permitted` is opaque for what is really "/boot is not mounted". A dedicated check with a clearer message would save a lot of digging.
2. Any other bootc command touching `/boot` (`bootc status`, `bootc upgrade`, `bootc switch`) has the same exposure when run from an idle shell, and can't be fixed by unit dependencies. Triggering the automount explicitly, or reporting a clear error, would help.

## References

- ostreedev/ostree#2544 — ostree's fix for the same hazard on its own units
- ostreedev/ostree@62109dca — the change that makes gpt-auto discover partitions on composefs roots
- systemd/systemd#13099 — gpt-auto generates `boot.automount` despite an existing `boot.mount`
- systemd/systemd#35017 — gpt-auto with overlay roots

body.title: ostree-ext: override root dir metadata on merge commit

labels.name: area/ostree
labels.description: Issues related to ostree

body.body:
When building the merge commit in `write_merge_commit_impl()`, `write_dfd_to_mtree()` inherits the root dir metadata from the temp checkout dir, which causes its mode to be 0o755 rather than 0o555.

Manually override it to uid=0, gid=0, and importantly mode=0o555. This matches the expectations of the filesystem RPM and systemd's /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/root.conf.

Without this change, systemd-tmpfiles fails with `fchmod() of / failed: Read-only file system` on systems with a read-only root since systemd v261.

See https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/2238

Assisted-by: llm

---

I've manually confirmed that this resolves the root permissions issues (`0o755 -> 0o555`) locally by comparing output from systems with `bootc 1.17.1` to systems with this patch included, using both:

- RPM overrides in `cosa` builds of Fedora CoreOS
- Bootc builds using packages built using `just build` and run using `just test-tmt-nobuild --preserve-vm readonly`

Example output without patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
755
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00755 0 0      0 /
```

Vs with the patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
555
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00555 0 0      0 /
```

Of course, let me know if I'm missing anything or if any changes are required.

body.diff_hunk:
@@ -624,6 +624,51 @@ fn cleanup_root(root: &Dir) -> Result<()> {
     Ok(())
 }
 
+/// Override the root directory metadata on an mtree to uid=0, gid=0,
+/// mode=0o555, preserving any existing xattrs (e.g. SELinux labels).
+///
+/// This ensures the committed root directory permissions match the
+/// `filesystem` RPM and systemd's `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/root.conf`.
body.body:
In bootc upstream we shouldn't have anything that is hardcoded about RPM or a specific distro/OS - while this is just a comment, I would make that clear.

That said! For this specific case again there's a HUGE detail in that in OCI images it's not required to include the root, and many don't!

More on that in https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/2238#issuecomment-6082074286 - please include direct links for that here.

So we should handle this - if the input OCI image has permissions for the root we should use them. If it doesn't, then let's match what composefs-rs is doing and take the permissions from the `/usr` directory.

(or of course...in theory we could look at the tmpfiles.d config now...but I am not sure I want to have parsing those be in the truly load bearing path)

I am not a fan of propagating hardcoding 0o555 in more places.

(Note contrast w/your rpm-ostree PR - there I think we *can* assume that the RPM content set includes metadata for the root)

I think here though...it is complicated and subtle in the true general case, but I'd just be happier if we hardcoded propagaing the perms of `/usr` (after unpacking all layers) instead to match composefs-rs.

body.body: I updated the approach to copy all the metadata like I believe https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/blob/main/crates/composefs/src/generic_tree.rs#L837 is doing. But I'm just now noticing you said perms of `/usr` specifically. Is that all we want propagated?

@@ -624,6 +624,51 @@ fn cleanup_root(root: &Dir) -> Result<()> {
     Ok(())
 }
 
+/// Override the root directory metadata on an mtree to uid=0, gid=0,
+/// mode=0o555, preserving any existing xattrs (e.g. SELinux labels).
+///
+/// This ensures the committed root directory permissions match the
+/// `filesystem` RPM and systemd's `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/root.conf`.
body.body: Let's do exactly the same as composefs-rs, all metadata: ownership, mtime, xattrs etc.

Metadata replay ignores directory deletion/recreation, so a directory created as 0777, whiteouted, and recreated as 0755 can inherit stale 0777 permissions. The base-checksum shortcut at lines 810–815 can likewise leave a recreated 0777 directory world-writable when a later layer restores the base's 0700 metadata. Invalidate accumulated metadata and base-checksum assumptions for deleted paths and descendants, and add deletion/recreation regression tests.

For an unprivileged BareUser import, applying a layer directory mode such as 0000 here removes the access permissions needed to read the scratch checkout. The subsequent write_dfd_to_mtree() re-enumerates that tree and fails with EACCES, so an otherwise valid image can no longer be imported. Keep scratch directories accessible in user checkouts and override the committed directory metadata separately rather than applying restrictive modes to the on-disk tree before committing it.

This heuristic changes a previously correct case: with a 0755 base directory, a derived layer setting 0700 followed by another explicitly restoring 0755 now produces 0700. The last layer is discarded as a synthesized parent, so the merged image can deny access that the final image layer intended to allow. Please preserve which directory entries were explicit during tar import and use that information here; permission bits alone cannot distinguish these cases.

LGTM that said I think a readonly tmt test that asserts `/` matches the rpm database would make sense in addition to a unit test.

Can be a followup
Marking requested changes per above

### 🟡 Changes recommended Directory metadata handling can retain stale world-writable permissions after deletion and recreation, discard explicit permission changes, and cause valid unprivileged imports to fail with EACCES.
3 open issues - [Invalidate directory metadata after deletion and recreation](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/pull/2571#discussion_r4569594636) · New - [Keep scratch directories accessible during unprivileged imports](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/pull/2571#discussion_r4569594663) · New - [Preserve explicit directory modes when merging layers](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/pull/2571#discussion_r4569594682) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses root-permission mismatches that cause systemd-tmpfiles failures on read-only systems. It updates OSTree merge commits to copy `/usr` mode and ownership to `/` and preserves lower-directory permissions in transient overlays. **Changes:** - Replay layer directory metadata before normalizing the merge commit’s root metadata. - Set `/usr` to mode 0555 in the test image before UKI sealing. - Add metadata regression tests and remove obsolete 0755 assertions. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `tmt/​tests/​booted/​readonly/​055-test-root-dirmeta.nu` | Check root metadata against `/usr`, with an upgrade exception for strict mode checks. | | `tmt/​tests/​booted/​readonly/​040-test-baseconfigs.nu` | Remove fixed 0755 expectations for transient overlays. | | `Dockerfile` | Set `/usr` permissions before sealing the UKI. | | `crates/​ostree-ext/​tests/​it/​main.rs` | Test root metadata and derived-layer permission preservation. | | `crates/​ostree-ext/​src/​container/​store.rs` | Replay directory metadata and normalize root mode and ownership. | | `crates/​initramfs/​src/​lib.rs` | Match transient overlay upper permissions to the lower directory. |

issue.title: rpm-ostree-5657: Build and test the RPM v6 importer draft (cgwalters-forge/rpm-ostree#15)
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Finish and test the midstream draft cgwalters-forge/rpm-ostree#15 ("importer: Decode RPM payloads with librpm", part of cgwalters-forge/rpm-ostree#14 for upstream rpm-ostree issue 5657). It switches payload decoding to librpm so that RPM v6 packages, which use the "stripped" cpio payload with magic `07070X`, can be imported. Its implement run timed out without any build or tests, because that sandbox lacked the development dependencies and couldn't run the CI buildroot container. This devspace has the capacity to do it properly.

## More detail

- Clone cgwalters-forge/rpm-ostree, check out PR #15's head, and build it in the project's CI buildroot container (or a Fedora container that has RPM 6).
- Build a paired v4 and v6 test package (the same content, one with each payload format) and add regression tests showing both import identically. Cover a large-file case if feasible.
- Run `make check` and the importer tests. Fix whatever the build or tests turn up, staying within #15's design (librpm reader adapted to the existing OSTree importer).
- Hand back by PR here, as boot-2402 did: `work/rpm-ostree-5657/` with the patch series to apply on top of #15's head (`git format-patch`) and `RESULTS.md`, saying plainly what was built and tested and what wasn't. A forge fix run will then apply the patches to #15.

issue.title: boot-2402: Find the cause of EUCLEAN in ostree CI auto-prune.sh (1 KiB ext4 loop mount on kernel 7.2.13)
issue.body:
Upstream ostree PR 3690's CoreOS CI (Jenkins `ostree/PR-3690`, builds 1–4 since 2026-11-06) fails the kola test `ext.ostree.destructive.auto-prune.sh` every time. It also fails `ext.config.networking.network-online-service` once. The auto-prune failure happens in the test's setup, before any ostree command:

```
+ truncate -s 699137405 /var/tmp/boot.img
+ mkfs.ext4 -b 1024 /var/tmp/boot.img        # e2fsprogs 1.47.4-2.fc45
+ mount -o loop /var/tmp/boot.img /var/mnt
mount: /var/mnt: fsconfig() failed: Structure needs cleaning.   # EUCLEAN
```

That was on Fedora CoreOS with kernel 7.2.13-300.fc45. The script is tests/kolainst/destructive/auto-prune.sh in ostreedev/ostree.

Find out whether this is environmental, unrelated to the PR:
1. In a Fedora 45 VM on kernel 7.2.13-300.fc45 with e2fsprogs 1.47.4-2.fc45, run exactly those three commands and capture `dmesg` after the failed mount. Then repeat on the previous Fedora kernel (7.1.x) and with `-b 4096`.
2. Find the cause: the kernel ext4 change or e2fsprogs default responsible. Check `dumpe2fs -h` on the image, and look at the ext4 changes between 7.1 and 7.2 and in e2fsprogs 1.47.4 for 1 KiB block sizes.
3. Confirm that ostree is not involved. The mount fails before ostree runs, but also run the same kola test against upstream ostree main, if feasible with cosa/kola. Otherwise state clearly that the failure happens before ostree code runs.
4. Propose the minimal test fix, for example a block size that still reproduces the small-/boot condition the test needs (the test only wants /boot smaller than the deployment data), or avoiding the loop mount. Draft it as a patch in the devspace with an explanation.

Write findings to work/boot-2402/EUCLEAN.md, with the patch and a five-line summary at the top.

issue.title: boot-2402-dirfd: Matrix results and recommendation for the detached /boot spike
issue.body:
Part of #44

Continues #46. The bootc matrix now ran for stock 2026.4, PR 3690 and the detached-mount prototype, and the README has the comparison and a recommendation: land PR 3690, which fixes the /boot-on-root bug, and keep the detached mount only as a possible follow-up. The prototype has a blocking bug on separate /boot. Its read-write private mount makes systemd's own `ro` mount of /boot fail until reboot. On separate /boot, stock already finalized correctly in every scenario.

The harness gained build and install scripts. Two fixes made it run every scenario: an `xargs -L` line-joining bug, and an automount step that did nothing with bootc's fstab. Silverblue and ostree main were not run this time: nested KVM was too slow, so the VMs ran directly on the runner. The notes are in README.md because DESIGN.md is a refused filename.

issue.title: implement: ostree fd-based /boot finalize for bootc#2402, VM-verified
issue.body:
The operator's P0: bootc-dev/bootc#2402. The fix belongs in ostree, and it has to be verified in real VMs on this RHEL runner.

## The bug
On BIOS-booted systems with a same-partition layout (no separate /boot partition) and an unused ESP, systemd-gpt-auto-generator creates `boot.automount` (TimeoutIdleSec=120) for the ESP. That automount sits in front of ostree's generator `boot.mount`, which bind-mounts `/sysroot/boot` onto `/boot`.

When the automount idles out, `ostree-finalize-staged.service` (its ExecStop at shutdown) fails with `error: Remounting /boot read-write: Invalid argument`, and the staged deployment is silently dropped. From a separate mount namespace (`unshare -m`), accessing /boot gives EPERM.

This reproduces on stock Fedora 44 bootc (ostree 2026.4, systemd 259) and on centos-bootc stream10.

## The fix the maintainer asked for
ostreedev/ostree PR 3689 checks whether /boot is a mountpoint and bind-mounts it if not. The maintainer's review of that PR sets the direction:

> I'm thinking what would work best is if we actually put the mount of `/boot` we need into say `/run/ostree/boot` or so (and really, we could probably just cut over to relying on the new mount API, so we always mount it as a fd?). This relates very strongly to the "boot fd holder" service we have - we could just extract the fd from that right?

So finalization should stop depending on the global `/boot` path and on remounting it. It should write through a private, writable boot mount held as an fd, which no automount, idle expiry or mount namespace can take away. Use the new mount API: `open_tree(OPEN_TREE_CLONE)` with `mount_setattr` to clear RDONLY on the detached clone, or `fsopen`/`fsmount`.

The "boot fd holder" is `src/boot/ostree-finalize-staged-hold.service`, which runs `ostree admin finalize-staged --hold` (see `src/ostree/ot-admin-builtin-finalize-staged.c`). `src/libostree/ostree-soft-reboot.c` already uses `open_tree`/`move_mount`, so follow its style and its fallbacks.

Choose how finalize gets the right fd, and justify the choice in the commit message. Two options:
- open it early in the hold process and hand it over (the systemd fd store, or making the holder the finalizer);
- open a detached clone of `/sysroot/boot` at finalize.

Keep these working: a separate /boot partition; older kernels without the new mount API, with a clean fallback to today's path; SELinux labels; soft-reboot.

## Work
Clone ostreedev/ostree at main and make the change there, following its `AGENTS.md`, its C style (glnx, autoptr) and its commit style. Each commit ends with `Assisted-by: https://github.com/cgwalters/cgwalters#llms`, with no Signed-off-by.

## Verification, in VMs on this runner
Use bcvk or the equivalent, with BIOS firmware, a `to-disk` same-partition layout that leaves an unused ESP, and **no fstab workaround**.
1. Stock ostree: confirm the bug reproduces. A staged upgrade is dropped after more than 120 s idle.
2. Your build, layered into a Fedora bootc image: after more than 185 s idle, a staged upgrade finalizes at reboot and the new deployment boots, with the old one as rollback. `unshare -m ostree admin status` also works.
3. A separate /boot partition install still stages and finalizes.
4. ostree's own relevant tests pass. Add a test where the tree has a harness for one.

Report each result truthfully, with key log lines. Never claim a result you didn't get.

## Hand-back
Open one PR in this repository that adds `work/ostree-2402/`, containing:
- `git format-patch` output of your ostree commits;
- `RESULTS.md` with the design choice, each verification result and its key log lines, and anything unverified or any risk.

Don't post anything to ostreedev or bootc-dev/bootc.

issue.title: P0 boot-2402: Spike finalize through a detached /boot dirfd instead of the /boot path
issue.body:
P0, part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#1396 (upstream bootc issue 2402). The operator's design idea, 2026-11-08: "I really wonder if we can just fix things so that in the case where there's no separate `/boot` partition we try hard to change everything to use a totally different mount point like again in fact just operating through a detached dirfd instead of absolute path."

- **When `/boot` is on the root filesystem:** reach it through the sysroot's own fd, never through the host's `/boot` mount point.
- **When `/boot` is a separate partition:** open it as a detached mount, via `fsopen`/`fsconfig`/`fsmount`, or `open_tree(OPEN_TREE_CLONE)` of the device's mount, and do every bootloader write through that dirfd with `*at()` calls. That way an automount on `/boot` can neither idle out underneath us nor be required.
- **Compare with upstream ostree PR 3690's approach.** Say what each gets right and wrong: SELinux labelling, fsync and durability of the bootloader entries, systemd's view of `/boot`, and older kernels without the new mount API. Also cover `ostree admin` commands users run interactively.

issue.title: P0 boot-2402: Harness and test matrix for how /boot is mounted, including the fstab question
issue.body:
P0, part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#1396 (upstream bootc issue 2402: finalize fails once the `/boot` automount idles out; the candidate fix is upstream ostree PR 3690). The operator, 2026-11-08: "This is an embarrassing bug that undermines our core principle that bootc updates Just Work so let's spend some tokens and resources on this."

**Goal:** a tested, reproducible answer to how `/boot` gets mounted on today's image-based Fedora and RHEL hosts, and when the automount idle-out can bite. Use VMs on this runner (bcvk or qemu). Post exact commands and outputs.

1. **A repeatable harness.** Write scripts under `work/boot-2402/` that boot a given image or ISO install in a VM, run an update (ostree/rpm-ostree upgrade, or bootc upgrade/switch), wait past the automount idle timeout, reboot, and check that the new deployment booted. Look at what Fedora's openQA does for Silverblue and IoT upgrade tests, and reuse its approach where it helps. Cover at least:
   - current Fedora Silverblue (installed from the current ISO or a disk image), since that is where users hit this;
   - a bootc image from quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc, installed with `bootc install to-disk`;
   - CentOS Stream 10 bootc.
2. **The fstab question.** Does a `/boot` entry in `/etc/fstab` stop systemd-gpt-auto-generator from creating its `/boot` automount? issue.title: devspace: Log in over SSH as an unprivileged runner-sandbox user
issue.body:
SSH sessions on a devspace ran as `runner`, the same uid (with passwordless sudo) as the workflow steps. The running keepalive step's `/proc/PID/environ` holds `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`/`_URL`, so any build script started over SSH could mint GitHub OIDC tokens that the Tailscale OAuth client trusts.

- **Separate uid (the boundary).** Sessions log in as a new user, `runner-sandbox`, with no sudo. Another uid can't read `Runner.Worker`'s or any step's environ or memory. `scripts/setup-runner-sandbox.mjs` (Node) creates it (kvm group and subuids; not libvirt, whose `qemu:///system` access is root-equivalent). It also fixes the real exposures of the umask-000 image:
  - `/home/runner` and `/opt/hca` become private, since the runner's `.credentials` and the compute agent's token were world-readable;
  - world write permission is removed, because `runner-sandbox` could otherwise add a polkit rule granting itself root;
  - `/etc/environment` loses runner's `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (actions/runner-images#14649), so logins get their own runtime directory;
  - the ssh crypto-policies include loses its group write bit, since ssh refuses a group-writable config.
- **No sudo or polkit for runner-sandbox.** It is in no sudoers rule or admin group anyway; a sudoers rule (`runner-sandbox ALL=(ALL:ALL) !ALL`) makes that explicit, and when polkit is installed a rule answers no to all its requests, `pkexec` included.
- **Use the token once.** The keepalive step, which lives as long as the devspace, re-executes itself without `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` and `ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN`. `tailscaled`, started by the action with `sudo -E`, still holds the token, readable only by root.
- **Hardening on top:** `ptrace_scope=1`, Cockpit's socket disabled, and no instance metadata service for `runner-sandbox` or its rootless containers.

The toolchain moves into the workflow (`packages.txt`), since sessions can't install packages. `scripts/runner-sandbox.mjs` is the single definition of the user and of how a step runs something as it (`run0`, so it gets its own login session like an SSH login's, with a fixed environment); `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` uses it for the dotfiles, and #3's agent.yml runs the same setup script. A first commit references the workflow's actions by major tag (checkout v7, tailscale v4) instead of SHAs, for Renovate.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

What's left: anything running as `runner` or root during setup (the runner, the actions it uses, package scriptlets), and root processes that are already running (tailscaled, sshd). `NoNewPrivileges` for the runner itself isn't possible from inside a job, because `Runner.Listener`/`Worker` run under the image's `hosted-compute-agent.service` and restarting that would end the job. Narrowing the Tailscale federated identity's claims and keeping `tag:bootc-dev-sandbox`'s ACL tight limit what a minted token is worth.

Testing, at this head (0edf5c1), on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace started from main (run 36275733071; main predates runner-sandbox, so this branch was pushed there):
- `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` (15 passed); `actionlint` and `node --check` locally.
- `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs` ran twice cleanly. Then runner-sandbox logged in over SSH, through a PAM sshd with this workflow's auth settings (on 127.0.0.1:2222, as its own unit, so the login got a systemd session). There `sudo -n true` and `sudo -l` fail, `pkexec` says "Not authorized", `systemctl restart sshd` gets "Access denied" (without the polkit rule, an earlier run showed it asking for interactive authentication instead), and `su` to root or runner fails authentication (both passwords are locked in the image, so nothing to lock). Rootless podman ran a container, `bcvk ephemeral run-ssh` booted centos-bootc:stream10, and runner keeps its sudo. Script and logs: https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/619656d679aad001f51cfa7b806942d1
- Outside the setup's `-xdev` sweep, `/run`, `/dev/shm` and `/mnt` have no world-writable non-sticky files other than sockets. `/mnt` is empty, and there is no swap on this runner size.
- `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` (runner-sandbox's dotfiles) and #3's isolation check (12 checks) passed at 558171a (run 36240484839). The token scrub and sshd admitting only runner-sandbox were covered by run 36206810916. None of these changed here.
- At 619398e (this head; the change since 0edf5c1 makes `/var/run/tailscale` root's only, since tailscaled's LocalAPI socket is 0666 and lets any user `tailscale nc` through the node and `tailscale status` the tailnet; the keepalive now runs `sudo tailscale status --self`): `cargo test` (15 passed) on a 16-core devspace (run 36415814928). There, with the directory at the image's 0755, `tailscale nc <tailnet host> 22` as runner-sandbox connected and `tailscale status` listed the tailnet; after the setup script both fail with permission denied, and `sudo tailscale status` still works for runner.
- At 391d342 (`runner-sandbox.mjs` uses `run0` instead of plain `systemd-run`, per review): on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (run 36487000792), `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` for a freshly created user, #3's isolation check (15 ok, applied on #3's head), rootless `podman run` through `asSandbox` (systemd cgroup manager, runroot in `/run/user/UID`), exit statuses passed through, and `cargo test` (15 passed). machinectl shell, run0 and systemd-run compared in a bcvk CentOS Stream 10 VM and on the runner: https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/f932edce0622dba38e1b9018c01c6c31
- At 7cb2947 (this head; the same plus `env -u` dropping the `SUDO_USER`/`SUDO_UID`/`SUDO_GID` run0 sets, and `CollectMode=inactive-or-failed`, since run0 otherwise leaves a failed unit for every nonzero exit): on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (run 36488428943), `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` for a fresh user, `asSandbox` env has no `SUDO_*`, rootless `podman run` (systemd cgroups, runroot in `/run/user/1002`, exit 5 passed through), no failed units left, `cargo fmt --check`/`clippy -D warnings`/`cargo test` (15 passed). #3's and #5's checks at their restacked heads are in those PRs.
- devspace.yml itself (including the Tailscale action at v4 and checkout at v7) can only run from the default branch, so it is untested as a whole until merged.

homegit's bot-devspace now logs in as `runner-sandbox` and falls back to `runner` (cgwalters-bot/homegit#7).

The `Signed-off-by: Colin Walters <walters@verbum.org>` on these commits was added on cgwalters's approval of the review draft: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox/pull/2#pullrequestreview-5402692966

Generated-by: https://github.com/cgwalters/#llms

issue.title: boot-2402: History of /boot on the physical root, the ostree bind, and gpt-auto automounts
issue.body:
Deep research for the bootc 2402 P0 (cgwalters-forge/tracker#1396). Write one durable document, work/boot-2402/HISTORY.md, that a maintainer can read top to bottom. This is history and analysis, not new VM tests: work/boot-2402/RESULTS.md (now on main) holds the test evidence, so cite its rows and don't repeat them.

Questions:
1. **When is /boot on the physical root?** For each installer and image path, and its history: `bootc install to-disk` and `to-filesystem` (Stream 9 and 10, Fedora), Anaconda (bootc and rpm-ostree kickstarts, autopart), osbuild and image-builder (bootc-image-builder disk images), Fedora CoreOS and RHCOS (coreos-installer, the separate boot partition), rpm-ostree and Silverblue, and bootupd's role. Which produce /boot on root, with or without fstab lines, and since which release or commit.
2. **How did ostree come to bind-mount /boot read-only, and to remount it?** The history of `ostree-prepare-root`, the read-only sysroot and /boot bind, `_ostree_sysroot_ensure_writable` and finalize-staged. Cite commits, PRs and issues in the ostree git log, with the reasoning given at the time.
3. **systemd gpt-auto-generator's /boot and ESP automounts.** When it gained the automount and the 120 s idle timeout, the `LoaderDevicePartUUID` gate, and the BIOS path that skips it, across v239 to v262. Note which RHEL and Stream versions ship which behavior.
4. **Prior reports and fixes.** Earlier issues and PRs in ostree, bootc, rpm-ostree, systemd, bootupd and Fedora or CentOS trackers about /boot automounts, finalize failures, or "Remounting /boot read-write". Also earlier fix attempts, such as masking boot.automount (upstream ostree PR 3664, rejected) and the /efi direction. Say why each was accepted or rejected.
5. **Synthesis.** Why upstream ostree PR 3690's approach is right. What residual risks remain (UEFI via GRUB BLI, systemd changes). What durable fixes belong in bootc and installers too, for example writing an fstab line or `x-systemd.automount=no`.

issue.title: test: Reproduce bootc 2402 via the update timer after /boot idles out
issue.body:
Write a bootc integration test (tmt, under bootc's `tmt/tests`) that reproduces bootc-dev/bootc issue 2402 and fails on current main.

Our CI misses the bug because every upgrade test reboots well within the `/boot` automount's idle timeout (systemd-gpt-auto-generator's `boot.automount`, 120s by default). The test should go the way real systems hit it:
1. Boot an image where `/boot` is a gpt-auto automount, and stage nothing yet.
2. Let `/boot` idle out. Shorten `TimeoutIdleSec` with a drop-in to keep the test fast, and assert that `/boot` is really unmounted.
3. Push an update and fire the built-in `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer`/service, not a direct `bootc upgrade`. It stages the update and reboots, which runs `ostree-finalize-staged`.
4. Assert that the new deployment booted. On main, finalize fails with `opendir(boot): Operation not permitted`, and the old deployment boots.

Run it in a VM with bcvk on current bootc main to show it fails. Then run it with ostree built from upstream ostree PR 3690 (branch `bot/boot-finalize-2402` of cgwalters-forge/ostree) to show it passes. Hand the test back as a PR on this devspace repo under `work/bootc-2402-test/`, with both runs' logs summarized in a short RESULTS.md.

issue.title: Add ImageProxy::open_varlink_socket
issue.body:
Newer skopeo versions (protocol 0.2.9) can hand out a varlink socket for an opened image through the OpenVarlinkSocket method.  Over that socket layers can be transferred by position, passing file descriptors for content already on disk instead of copying it through the proxy.

Expose the method, returning the connected socket as an OwnedFd so the caller can wrap it with the varlink client of its choice, and add supports_open_varlink_socket() to probe for it.

issue.title: gateway: Reload operator tokens without a restart
issue.body:
## Problem

The gateway reads `operator-tokens.yaml` only at startup (`Operators::load`). Praxis watches `praxis.yaml` and the files a filter declares, and `run_token` declares none. So adding, rotating or revoking an operator token needs a gateway restart, and a restart ends every registered run and resets the caps (#33).

Deployments already update the file in place. On Kubernetes, a ConfigMap mounted as a directory (not with `subPath`) is swapped atomically by the kubelet within about a minute of the change. Only the gateway re-reading it is missing.

## Proposal

Watch the operator tokens file and swap the operator set atomically when it changes:

- Parse and validate the new file completely before swapping. A file that fails keeps the old operators and logs a warning, as a failed `praxis.yaml` reload does.
- Operators whose hash is in both the old and new file keep their state: in-flight count, token caps and usage counters. Only added entries start fresh, and only removed entries are dropped.
- A removed token is refused from the next request. Requests already in flight finish.
- Log `operator tokens loaded` with the names, as at startup.
- Handle the kubelet's `..data` symlink swap, not only in-place writes. Watch the directory, or poll the content hash every few seconds.

With that, rotating a token needs no downtime: add the new entry, move clients to the new token, then remove the old entry.

## Acceptance

Integration tests show that a token added to the file is admitted and a removed one refused, without a restart and without resetting any run's caps or ending a run. An invalid file must keep the old set. The test should cover a symlink-swap update the way the kubelet does it. INTERNALS.md "Operator tokens" should describe the new behaviour.

Related: #33 (keeping runs across a rolling update).

issue.title: Credentialless runs: an authenticated network-identity and trusted lifecycle contract
issue.body:
Part of tracker#1311 and agentic-job#2903. Implement one opt-in broker admission contract after the operator answers the identity/deployment question. A run's agent must hold no bearer, key or client private key; even run-management credentials stay outside the agent machine's readable view. Preserve the existing default authenticated routes. Acceptance: authenticated unique job identity, ambiguous/shared identity refused, one active binding per identity, no forwarded-header spoofing, no agent self-registration/rebinding/new cap, expiry and trusted revocation remove access, bounded usage/status without token disclosure, existing accounting and streaming retained. Document peer-preservation and disposable-node assumptions and configuration rollout. No deployment changes or permissive unauthenticated fallback. The design research is evidence, not approval: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agentic-job/issues/2903#issuecomment-6648179732.

Q: Approve a credentialless identity mechanism and identify a deployment/listener that preserves authenticated per-job identity without shared NAT or concurrent unrelated jobs. Can registration, OIDC and lifecycle credentials stay on a trusted machine outside the agent's readable process/filesystem view? issue.title: gateway: Refresh usage windows at startup without inference
issue.body:
After a restart, the first reading of a provider's usage window comes from the next inference response. Until then the grant treats the window as partly used and holds the pool until it resets. On 3 Nov one pool stayed held for days after a 1% first reading.

Where the provider exposes a usage or limits endpoint, or a minimal request whose response headers carry the window, query it at startup and on a timer, so readings are fresh without spending tokens. Document what is possible for each provider. Related to #53.
