issue.title: Xenon: podman auto-update cannot pull from ghcr.io (stale stored login)
issue.body:
On Xenon, `podman pull ghcr.io/cgwalters-bot/praxis-credential-broker-gateway:main` as `sandbox-walters` fails with `Requesting bearer token: received unexpected HTTP status: 403 Forbidden`. The packages are public and an anonymous pull (`--authfile` naming an empty `{}` file) works, so the cause is a stored ghcr.io login that the registry now refuses, apparently in `~/.docker/config.json` (`~/.config/containers/auth.json` has no ghcr.io entry). I did not read or change it.

Effect: `podman auto-update`, which INTERNALS.md gives as the way to deploy after a merge, would fail the same way. The 2026-10-06 deploy pulled the three images anonymously instead.

Fix on the host: `podman logout ghcr.io` (or remove that entry), or log in again with a valid token.

issue.title: Size the per-run token cap from real run records
issue.body:
Since #15 the `run` rule (20M tokens per run per API over 6h, `praxis.yaml`) counts real tokens, cached input in full, where it used to count a flat 10k per request. Long agent runs make about 200 requests, so at 50-100k tokens of context each a run may now reach the cap.

Once a few metered agent runs have finished, read their run records (`tokens.total`, `cache_read`) and decide whether 20M is right, should be raised, or should weight cached input lower. The options and a recommendation are in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/379#issuecomment-6015910631.

issue.title: gateway: Report prompt-cache hit rates in /usage
issue.body:
#44 logs each Codex request's prompt-cache use in credential-proxy, but reading the cache share still means reading the logs. With `cache_stats: true` on `run_token`, `/usage` now has a `cache` section. It gives the hit rate (cached ÷ input) for each provider and model over the last hour and the last day. It also lists the ten busiest `prompt_cache_key` sessions, each with its request count, its first request's input, and its hit rate from the second request on. The gateway logs one warning per session whose hit rate is under 50% from its third request on.

The counting happens in the gateway rather than the proxy, because the gateway serves `/usage` and already sees every injected response's usage, Anthropic and Mistral included. It reads the session key from the Codex request body, which Praxis has already buffered. issue.title: Size the per-run token cap from real run records
issue.body:
Since #15 the `run` rule (20M tokens per run per API over 6h, `praxis.yaml`) counts real tokens, cached input in full, where it used to count a flat 10k per request. Long agent runs make about 200 requests, so at 50-100k tokens of context each a run may now reach the cap.

Once a few metered agent runs have finished, read their run records (`tokens.total`, `cache_read`) and decide whether 20M is right, should be raised, or should weight cached input lower. The options and a recommendation are in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/379#issuecomment-6015910631.

issue.title: Registration without proof: review follow-ups (reload bound, ignored fields, docs)
issue.body:
Non-blocking notes from the review of #19 (registration without proof), left for a follow-up so the reviewed head could merge unchanged:

1. The "unproven runs never fill the registry" bound is checked when the policy is loaded, not across a reload. A reload of `praxis.yaml` that changes `unproven` or `max_secs` keeps runs remembered under the old settings, so more than 1024 can be remembered and registration without proof then gets 503 until old ones are forgotten. Proven runs stay protected. Either say in INTERNALS.md to restart rather than reload when changing these, or count the unproven runs still remembered at load.
2. A policy with only `unproven` (no `workflows`, `repository_ids` or `owner_ids`) silently ignores `entry_workflows` and `events`. Refuse them there.
3. INTERNALS.md and the comment in `filter.rs` overstate `Sec-Fetch-Site`: browsers send it only to trustworthy origins, so a plain-HTTP page made same-origin by DNS rebinding sends `Origin` alone. The refusal still holds, since a page's `POST` always carries `Origin`; the text should say that `Origin` is what catches it.
4. A few long unwrapped lines in INTERNALS.md.

A part-way window stays part-way until its reset (`a_window_first_read_part_way_is_so_until_it_resets`), so a fresh reading doesn't clear it. Codex stays held until its weekly reset and anthropic for several days, even though both subscriptions are well under pace.

That makes the grant unusable as a consumer's budget source: with `budget.source: broker`, the pass leaves out held pools and would start nothing on either pool for days.

A part-way window only means attribution between consumers is unknown for the part read before the first reading. Hold it only when the conservative bound is over the consumer's share, i.e. when the consumer is charged all of the window's use so far. Otherwise report it as fresh but `part_way: true`, so a consumer can see that the attribution is approximate. Keep the top-level `hold` rule from #58 (per window, not stale). The no-inference refresh (#57) makes this rarer but doesn't fix it, because part-way is about attribution, not freshness.

Tests:
- a part-way window under its share by the conservative bound does not hold
- one over it does
- a restart with a saved state file doesn't hold a pool that was under budget before the restart

issue.title: gateway: Stop the grant holding a pool that has no fresh reading, and age restored windows
issue.body:
Found reviewing #48. Two follow-ups that must land before a consumer takes its budget from `/usage/grant`.

1. Top-level `hold` is true when any pool is stale, unread or left out (`budget.rs`), and a consumer that starts nothing on top-level `hold` never produces the reading that would clear it. A pool idle for over five hours, or a first boot with an empty state file, gets there. Leave staleness and unread pools out of top-level `hold`, or have the consumer probe them. `a_restored_window_past_its_reset_is_no_reading` asserts the current behaviour.
2. A restored window is never aged until a complete reading replaces it, so if a provider stops sending complete headers after a restart, the grant can read `hold: false` for up to seven days while runs spend unmeasured. Treat it as stale when `now - max(observed_at, loaded_at)` is over five hours, with `loaded_at` kept in memory. Fix this with or after item 1: alone it would deadlock an idle consumer.

Smaller: range-check values loaded from the state file (a negative `used` or `window_secs: 0` can read `hold: false` until the next complete reading), and add a test for `keep_state`.

[The docs explicitly confirm these restart losses](https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/praxis-credential-broker/blob/de1804d57991775d830bc448f301c06816bf9dca/INTERNALS.md#L1012-L1035).

Expected reproduction: register a run, incur metered Mistral spend, wait for the state write, restart with the same file, then reuse the token and read the spend/grant. The token lookup will be empty and the spend history lost. This is code-confirmed, **not runtime-reproduced here**: `cargo test -p praxis-gateway usage::tests:: --locked --offline` exits 101 because installed Rust 1.93.1 is below the required 1.96.

The important design boundary: per-run token caps are **not** in `Runs`; [they belong to separate weighted, reservation-based filters](https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/praxis-credential-broker/blob/de1804d57991775d830bc448f301c06816bf9dca/praxis.yaml#L210-L281). The [pinned dependency constructs fresh private in-memory ledgers](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/ai/blob/1f0b72d624fcdddec9c74a3a08b14836936131c0/filters/src/token_rate_limit/mod.rs#L303-L340), without a public file snapshot/restore interface. Saving run records alone will not preserve cap enforcement.

Please settle two points: (1) extend the dependency with ledger persistence hooks, or deliberately change accounting ownership/backend? (2) retain the existing five-second best-effort checkpoint semantics, or require durable registration/admission/settlement before acknowledging requests, including a policy for interrupted reservations? The latter matters because the current writer has no shutdown flush.

Once settled, implementation needs a new schema that reads v1, bounded run/hash/expiry and ledger restore, hourly spend buckets plus their original start time, write notifications for non-window mutations, and a real process-restart test proving the same token works, remaining caps do not reset, and spend/grant decisions survive. Also cover v1 migration, expiry and interrupted requests; never persist raw bearer tokens. No code changes or PR made.

issue.title: gateway: Refresh usage windows at startup without inference
issue.body:
After a restart, the first reading of a provider's usage window comes from the next inference response. Until then the grant treats the window as partly used and holds the pool until it resets. On 3 Nov one pool stayed held for days after a 1% first reading.

Where the provider exposes a usage or limits endpoint, or a minimal request whose response headers carry the window, query it at startup and on a timer, so readings are fresh without spending tokens. Document what is possible for each provider. Related to #53.

issue.title: gateway: Persist run registrations, per-run caps and the spend meter in the usage state
issue.body:
PR #48 persisted the usage windows and their attribution, but on restart the gateway still forgets registered runs, their per-run token caps, and the weekly spend meter for providers without a provider-side limit. After a restart an in-flight run can fail, and a spend-capped provider can go over its share.

Extend the `--usage-state` file to cover these. Keep it versioned and backward compatible with the #48 format. Add an integration test that restarts the gateway mid-run and checks that the run continues and the spend meter is kept.

issue.title: gateway: Stop the grant holding a pool that has no fresh reading, and age restored windows
issue.body:
Found reviewing #48. Two follow-ups that must land before a consumer takes its budget from `/usage/grant`.

1. Top-level `hold` is true when any pool is stale, unread or left out (`budget.rs`), and a consumer that starts nothing on top-level `hold` never produces the reading that would clear it. A pool idle for over five hours, or a first boot with an empty state file, gets there. Leave staleness and unread pools out of top-level `hold`, or have the consumer probe them. `a_restored_window_past_its_reset_is_no_reading` asserts the current behaviour.
2. A restored window is never aged until a complete reading replaces it, so if a provider stops sending complete headers after a restart, the grant can read `hold: false` for up to seven days while runs spend unmeasured. Treat it as stale when `now - max(observed_at, loaded_at)` is over five hours, with `loaded_at` kept in memory. Fix this with or after item 1: alone it would deadlock an idle consumer.

Smaller: range-check values loaded from the state file (a negative `used` or `window_secs: 0` can read `hold: false` until the next complete reading), and add a test for `keep_state`.

issue.body:
Part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#1224; the activation step that #195 left open when #281 merged.

#281 (merged 2026-11-16 as 56a4085) added the default-off `prose-*` chain to `cgwalters-review.yml` and closed #195 with `Closes`, although its own description says to keep the issue open until live acceptance. Caller pin rollout and copying the two prose files to each caller's trusted base follow the decision and are ordinary work.

issue.title: ci: Run the ci workflow in the merge queue
issue.body:
Ruleset 24147876 already requires the one check `ci`, which `.github/workflows/ci.yml` produces as a single job, and `workflows-check.yml` already has `merge_group`. But `ci.yml` runs on `pull_request` and `push` only, so a merge-queue entry would never get the required check and the queue cannot be turned on.

Change for this repository: add `merge_group: {types: [checks_requested]}` to `on:` in `ci.yml`. The single `ci` job is already what the ruleset requires, so no aggregate job is needed (the epic's note that actions needs the aggregate is stale on this point). The ruleset change, adding the queue and dropping `strict_required_status_checks_policy` as agent-board's ruleset does, is the controller's and is tracked separately on the epic.

Part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#1727.

issue.title: wrapper: Add artifact-only external execution mode with no apply authority
issue.body:
Part of tracker#1215; runtime follow-up to closed agentic-job#2891 and merged #3189. Design: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agentic-job/blob/main/docs/dispatch.md#external-vm-runner-to-midstream-draft ; implementation slices: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agentic-job/blob/main/docs/plan.md#external-runner-implementation-slices . The documentation is not deployment authorization or runtime proof.

Goal: an external mode in `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` with policy/agent/check only, fixed dispatch identity/base and artifact handback, and no apply, write or lifecycle credential in the agent or tests. Keep hosted unchanged, all external profiles disabled and the mode unreachable by default.

**Done:** #280 documents the integration requirements in the README. Released preflight and evidence support exists.

**Blocked upstream (agentic-job):**
1. Implement checkout has no pin to the dispatched base, so policy/run/check cannot be bound to an exact base.
2. The inference token on the agent host still carries lifecycle authority; it needs endpoint-only inference and usage, with the lifecycle kept off the agent host.

**Left once both are released:** wire the external mode using those interfaces. Acceptance: lint and a mocked workflow prove credential isolation, capability refusal before inference, and cleanup on failure and cancellation.

Merging #280 does not finish this issue.

issue.title: workflows: Add a wrapper canary that runs a real dispatch and review
issue.body:
#136 changed both agent wrappers, passed every check and review, and then broke every agent run for hours: nothing ran a real agent through a pull request's own wrappers, and the review ran the base branch's copy. This adds a wrapper canary. `wrapper-canary-gate.yml` sets a `wrapper-canary` status on every pull request to main. The status is success unless the pull request changes `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` or `cgwalters-review.yml`; otherwise it stays pending until `wrapper-canary.yml` passes. The gate uses `pull_request_target`, but runs base code and reads only the file list over the API.

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers, both fixed: the gate shared a file with the `@wrapper-canary` call, which GitHub resolves for every run, and the push procedure let a fork push run unread code. Still open:
- The ~10-minute bound is documented, not enforced. The dispatch wrapper has no timeout input, so its own 75-minute limit applies.
- A `pull_request` job named `wrapper-canary` in a fork could perhaps satisfy the required status, the same weakness `ci` has.
- Board-test's review runs are found by "newest since the reopen", not matched to the scratch pull request.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test, new file `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`:

  ```yaml
  name: wrapper-canary-review
  on:
    pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
      types: [reopened]
  permissions: {}
  jobs:
    review:
      if: github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)
      uses: cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary
      permissions: {contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: write, actions: read, id-token: write, statuses: write}
  ```

  board-test also needs the variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`, and its `AGENT` must be unset or a real agent.
- Tailnet federation and inference broker: admit `job_workflow_ref` `cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary` and `.../cgwalters-review.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary`.
- cgwalters-forge/actions:
  - The branch `wrapper-canary`, created at main, with a ruleset that lets only maintainers update it.
  - The variables `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`: a scratch issue, and a non-draft scratch pull request opened by a collaborator, both in board-test.
  - The environment `agent-apply`, and access to the organization secret `CGWALTERS_BOT_PAT`.
  - Last, the main ruleset's required status check `wrapper-canary`.

Closes #138

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers, both fixed: the gate shared a file with the `@wrapper-canary` call, which GitHub resolves for every run, and the push procedure let a fork push run unread code. Still open:
- The ~10-minute bound is documented, not enforced. The dispatch wrapper has no timeout input, so its own 75-minute limit applies.
- A `pull_request` job named `wrapper-canary` in a fork could perhaps satisfy the required status, the same weakness `ci` has.
- Board-test's review runs are found by "newest since the reopen", not matched to the scratch pull request.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test, new file `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`:

  ```yaml
  name: wrapper-canary-review
  on:
    pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
      types: [reopened]
  permissions: {}
  jobs:
    review:
      if: github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)
      uses: cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary
      permissions: {contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: write, actions: read, id-token: write, statuses: write}
  ```

  board-test also needs the variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`, and its `AGENT` must be unset or a real agent.
- Tailnet federation and inference broker: admit `job_workflow_ref` `cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary` and `.../cgwalters-review.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary`.
- cgwalters-forge/actions:
  - The branch `wrapper-canary`, created at main, with a ruleset that lets only maintainers update it.
  - The variables `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`: a scratch issue, and a non-draft scratch pull request opened by a collaborator, both in board-test.
  - The environment `agent-apply`, and access to the organization secret `CGWALTERS_BOT_PAT`.
  - Last, the main ruleset's required status check `wrapper-canary`.

Closes #138

issue.title: workflows: Add org-review.yml for an organization ruleset to require

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

issue.body:
Today every repository carries its own review.yml, and a new one gets no review until someone copies the file in. org-review.yml is that caller made a required workflow: it runs on pull_request_target and calls cgwalters-review.yml at the commit tracker pins (d8e22f7), so the job_workflow_ref the tailnet and broker admit does not change. .github/rulesets/org-review.json is the ruleset for the operator to apply: evaluate mode, all repositories' default branches, no bypass actors, requiring the workflow at refs/heads/main of this repository.

Part of #129

The default task is not wired. At d8e22f7 the wrapper hardcodes workflow/review.toml and workflow/review.md, and agentic-job v0.6.2's policy reads them only from the target's checkout. So a repository without them fails policy. A fallback needs a review-task input on the wrapper, at a new pin, with the admission moved too.

Operator steps, none taken here: set the organization variables AGENT, AGENT_MODEL, AGENT_RUNNER, AGENT_CONFIG, AGENT_CONFIG_REPO, AGENT_CONFIG_PATH, INFERENCE_URL, INFERENCE_AUDIENCE and AGENT_REAL_REVIEWS. The wrapper at d8e22f7 defaults INFERENCE_URL to an older host, so set it. Then create the ruleset from the JSON (`gh api -X POST orgs/cgwalters-forge/rulesets --input .github/rulesets/org-review.json`), narrowed to one repository first. Merging this needs an owner bypass: workflows-check refuses a new pull_request_target trigger and its zizmor ignore.

Follow-ups from review: in a repository that keeps its review.yml, both workflows share the wrapper's `review-pull-N` concurrency group and cancel each other's agent job, so drop that repository's review.yml (step 4) when adding it. The required run passes when the wrapper skips (drafts; ruleset workflows never get ready_for_review) and whatever the verdict. workflows-check.md pins its ruleset to a commit SHA rather than a branch, which the operator may prefer here too. There is no merge_group trigger.

Verified with `node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs` (42 pass), actionlint, and zizmor offline. The runner-labels lint needs cargo, which wasn't available, so it did not run; the workflow has no runs-on of its own. One review pass; its one blocker is the missing default task above.

issue.title: workflows: Add a wrapper canary that runs a real dispatch and review
issue.body:
#136 changed both agent wrappers, passed every check and review, and then broke every agent run for hours: nothing ran a real agent through a pull request's own wrappers, and the review ran the base branch's copy. This adds a wrapper canary. `wrapper-canary-gate.yml` sets a `wrapper-canary` status on every pull request to main. The status is success unless the pull request changes `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` or `cgwalters-review.yml`; otherwise it stays pending until `wrapper-canary.yml` passes. The gate uses `pull_request_target`, but runs base code and reads only the file list over the API.

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

issue.body:
Today every repository carries its own review.yml, and a new one gets no review until someone copies the file in. org-review.yml is that caller made a required workflow: it runs on pull_request_target and calls cgwalters-review.yml at the commit tracker pins (d8e22f7), so the job_workflow_ref the tailnet and broker admit does not change. .github/rulesets/org-review.json is the ruleset for the operator to apply: evaluate mode, all repositories' default branches, no bypass actors, requiring the workflow at refs/heads/main of this repository.

Part of #129

The default task is not wired. At d8e22f7 the wrapper hardcodes workflow/review.toml and workflow/review.md, and agentic-job v0.6.2's policy reads them only from the target's checkout. So a repository without them fails policy. A fallback needs a review-task input on the wrapper, at a new pin, with the admission moved too.

Operator steps, none taken here: set the organization variables AGENT, AGENT_MODEL, AGENT_RUNNER, AGENT_CONFIG, AGENT_CONFIG_REPO, AGENT_CONFIG_PATH, INFERENCE_URL, INFERENCE_AUDIENCE and AGENT_REAL_REVIEWS. The wrapper at d8e22f7 defaults INFERENCE_URL to an older host, so set it. Then create the ruleset from the JSON (`gh api -X POST orgs/cgwalters-forge/rulesets --input .github/rulesets/org-review.json`), narrowed to one repository first. Merging this needs an owner bypass: workflows-check refuses a new pull_request_target trigger and its zizmor ignore.

Follow-ups from review: in a repository that keeps its review.yml, both workflows share the wrapper's `review-pull-N` concurrency group and cancel each other's agent job, so drop that repository's review.yml (step 4) when adding it. The required run passes when the wrapper skips (drafts; ruleset workflows never get ready_for_review) and whatever the verdict. workflows-check.md pins its ruleset to a commit SHA rather than a branch, which the operator may prefer here too. There is no merge_group trigger.

Verified with `node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs` (42 pass), actionlint, and zizmor offline. The runner-labels lint needs cargo, which wasn't available, so it did not run; the workflow has no runs-on of its own. One review pass; its one blocker is the missing default task above.

issue.title: workflows: Add a wrapper canary that runs a real dispatch and review
issue.body:
#136 changed both agent wrappers, passed every check and review, and then broke every agent run for hours: nothing ran a real agent through a pull request's own wrappers, and the review ran the base branch's copy. This adds a wrapper canary. `wrapper-canary-gate.yml` sets a `wrapper-canary` status on every pull request to main. The status is success unless the pull request changes `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` or `cgwalters-review.yml`; otherwise it stays pending until `wrapper-canary.yml` passes. The gate uses `pull_request_target`, but runs base code and reads only the file list over the API.

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers, both fixed: the gate shared a file with the `@wrapper-canary` call, which GitHub resolves for every run, and the push procedure let a fork push run unread code. Still open:
- The ~10-minute bound is documented, not enforced. The dispatch wrapper has no timeout input, so its own 75-minute limit applies.
- A `pull_request` job named `wrapper-canary` in a fork could perhaps satisfy the required status, the same weakness `ci` has.
- Board-test's review runs are found by "newest since the reopen", not matched to the scratch pull request.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test, new file `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`:

  ```yaml
  name: wrapper-canary-review
  on:
    pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
      types: [reopened]
  permissions: {}
  jobs:
    review:
      if: github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)
      uses: cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary
      permissions: {contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: write, actions: read, id-token: write, statuses: write}
  ```

  board-test also needs the variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`, and its `AGENT` must be unset or a real agent.
- Tailnet federation and inference broker: admit `job_workflow_ref` `cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary` and `.../cgwalters-review.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary`.
- cgwalters-forge/actions:
  - The branch `wrapper-canary`, created at main, with a ruleset that lets only maintainers update it.
  - The variables `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`: a scratch issue, and a non-draft scratch pull request opened by a collaborator, both in board-test.
  - The environment `agent-apply`, and access to the organization secret `CGWALTERS_BOT_PAT`.
  - Last, the main ruleset's required status check `wrapper-canary`.

Closes #138

issue.title: wrapper: Document external execution integration blockers
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Document the exact upstream interfaces needed before exposing external execution. Released preflight and evidence support exists, but implement checkout lacks a dispatched-base pin and its inference token still carries lifecycle authority on the agent host. No runtime workflow, pin, caller or deployment changes.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/actions/issues/232

Verified: README Markdown lint, wrapper fixtures, Rust lint tests, runner-label checks and diff whitespace checks passed. Full workflow/security lint could not run: Docker has no daemon and Podman fails at OCI startup; live KVM/inference/lifecycle checks were not run.

Review: one adversarial pass; no blockers or nits left open.

Runtime implementation remains blocked on reviewed producer base-pin and endpoint-only inference/usage interfaces; the README links immutable source evidence and the existing inference work.

```checkpoint
{"reason":"incomplete","done":"Documented verified integration requirements; hosted workflows and pins unchanged.","left":"Implement and test the external wrapper after reviewed producer interfaces are available.","next":"Obtain exact-base policy/run/check binding and off-agent inference lifecycle support, then resume the wrapper slice without enabling callers."}
```

Closes #232

issue.title: ci: Gate wrapper canaries behind explicit dispatch
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Continue #139 with an off-by-default, environment-gated dispatch controller instead of a new privileged PR trigger. It runs an implement/noop and scratch event review through the admitted head wrappers, checks their resolved commits and handbacks, and cancels unfinished sessions at eight minutes; existing required ci checks the evidence when enabled.

Part of #138

Verified: 34 Node tests including the pinned policy compiler, Rust tests, actionlint, markdownlint and runner-label policy pass. Offline zizmor could not start its container (126); the base-exemptions shape check fails (1), so exemptions need a separate base-first merge. No live sessions or settings changes were performed.

Review: two passes; last found no blockers, with an important follow-up to avoid applying base-freshness checks to unrelated PRs. Full coverage of unmerged action dependencies behind immutable/main pins also remains unresolved.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge/actions: `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-dispatch.yml`, `jobs.dispatch.with.canary = true` is included here. Repository variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_REQUIRED = true` only after provisioning; `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL` must be the selected board-test scratch item numbers. Keep main's existing required `ci` check. Configure the protected admission branch, main-only approval environment and tokens as documented in README.
- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test: `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`, `on.pull_request_target.types = [reopened]`, `jobs.review.if = github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)`, `jobs.review.uses = cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary`; use the six permission grants of this repository's review caller. Repository variables: `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL = selected scratch PR number`, `AGENT = opencode`; leave `AGENT_REAL_REVIEWS` unset. Existing real inference settings and base-owned review bounds/task are prerequisites.
- Deployment broker/tailnet configuration: admit the two wrappers' `job_workflow_ref` values at `refs/heads/wrapper-canary` with existing owner-ID restrictions. The private deployment file paths and scratch item numbers were not supplied; no deployment values were guessed.

```checkpoint
{"reason":"incomplete","done":"Draft replacement for #139's canary, tests, runbook and two review passes. Changes are uncommitted for the handback patch.","left":"Fix unrelated-PR freshness follow-up, resolve unmerged pinned action coverage, land base exemptions separately, provision caller and broker/tailnet settings, then run live canaries.","next":"Continue #139 from this draft; first fix freshness scoping and agree how candidate action dependencies can be exercised without weakening privileged pins."}
```

issue.title: review: Document the advisory publication prerequisite
issue.body:
Part of #195

Document why the pinned helper cannot safely publish verdict-free, head-bound prose suggestions, and record the immutable checklist and rollout prerequisites. Add a direct-wiring regression for the main review publisher; no advisory pass or caller setting is enabled.

Verified: 20 wrapper tests and the full lint test suite pass; actionlint, offline zizmor, runner-labels and changed-file formatting pass. Docker lint and containerized online zizmor failed due to environment access; full formatting found pre-existing differences in pins.rs.

Review: one pass, no blockers for this partial handback; follow-ups are transitive/behavioral isolation coverage and documenting the legacy REJECT verdict alias.

Left undone: helper API extension, bounded advisory implementation, cheap-model deployment selection, functional scenario tests and authorized smoke test.

```checkpoint
{"reason":"incomplete","done":"Documented the pinned API blocker, immutable checklist and rollout prerequisites; added and tested direct main-publication wiring coverage.","left":"Release a head-bound verdict-free policy/check/apply contract, then implement the separate bounded opt-in prose pass and scenario tests.","next":"Extend agentic-job's checked comment publication contract and update immutable wrapper pins before adding advisory configuration."}
```

issue.title: workflows: Add a wrapper canary that runs a real dispatch and review
issue.body:
#136 changed both agent wrappers, passed every check and review, and then broke every agent run for hours: nothing ran a real agent through a pull request's own wrappers, and the review ran the base branch's copy. This adds a wrapper canary. `wrapper-canary-gate.yml` sets a `wrapper-canary` status on every pull request to main. The status is success unless the pull request changes `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` or `cgwalters-review.yml`; otherwise it stays pending until `wrapper-canary.yml` passes. The gate uses `pull_request_target`, but runs base code and reads only the file list over the API.

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers, both fixed: the gate shared a file with the `@wrapper-canary` call, which GitHub resolves for every run, and the push procedure let a fork push run unread code. Still open:
- The ~10-minute bound is documented, not enforced. The dispatch wrapper has no timeout input, so its own 75-minute limit applies.
- A `pull_request` job named `wrapper-canary` in a fork could perhaps satisfy the required status, the same weakness `ci` has.
- Board-test's review runs are found by "newest since the reopen", not matched to the scratch pull request.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test, new file `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`:

  ```yaml
  name: wrapper-canary-review
  on:
    pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
      types: [reopened]
  permissions: {}
  jobs:
    review:
      if: github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)
      uses: cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary
      permissions: {contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: write, actions: read, id-token: write, statuses: write}
  ```

  board-test also needs the variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`, and its `AGENT` must be unset or a real agent.
- Tailnet federation and inference broker: admit `job_workflow_ref` `cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary` and `.../cgwalters-review.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary`.
- cgwalters-forge/actions:
  - The branch `wrapper-canary`, created at main, with a ruleset that lets only maintainers update it.
  - The variables `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`: a scratch issue, and a non-draft scratch pull request opened by a collaborator, both in board-test.
  - The environment `agent-apply`, and access to the organization secret `CGWALTERS_BOT_PAT`.

## Executive summary

Continue #139 with an off-by-default, environment-gated dispatch controller instead of a new privileged PR trigger. It runs an implement/noop and scratch event review through the admitted head wrappers, checks their resolved commits and handbacks, and cancels unfinished sessions at eight minutes; existing required ci checks the evidence when enabled.

Part of #138

Verified: 34 Node tests including the pinned policy compiler, Rust tests, actionlint, markdownlint and runner-label policy pass. Offline zizmor could not start its container (126); the base-exemptions shape check fails (1), so exemptions need a separate base-first merge. No live sessions or settings changes were performed.

Review: two passes; last found no blockers, with an important follow-up to avoid applying base-freshness checks to unrelated PRs. Full coverage of unmerged action dependencies behind immutable/main pins also remains unresolved.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge/actions: `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-dispatch.yml`, `jobs.dispatch.with.canary = true` is included here. Repository variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_REQUIRED = true` only after provisioning; `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL` must be the selected board-test scratch item numbers. Keep main's existing required `ci` check. Configure the protected admission branch, main-only approval environment and tokens as documented in README.
- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test: `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`, `on.pull_request_target.types = [reopened]`, `jobs.review.if = github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)`, `jobs.review.uses = cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary`; use the six permission grants of this repository's review caller. issue.body:
Today every repository carries its own review.yml, and a new one gets no review until someone copies the file in. org-review.yml is that caller made a required workflow: it runs on pull_request_target and calls cgwalters-review.yml at the commit tracker pins (d8e22f7), so the job_workflow_ref the tailnet and broker admit does not change. .github/rulesets/org-review.json is the ruleset for the operator to apply: evaluate mode, all repositories' default branches, no bypass actors, requiring the workflow at refs/heads/main of this repository.

Part of #129

The default task is not wired. At d8e22f7 the wrapper hardcodes workflow/review.toml and workflow/review.md, and agentic-job v0.6.2's policy reads them only from the target's checkout. So a repository without them fails policy. A fallback needs a review-task input on the wrapper, at a new pin, with the admission moved too.

Operator steps, none taken here: set the organization variables AGENT, AGENT_MODEL, AGENT_RUNNER, AGENT_CONFIG, AGENT_CONFIG_REPO, AGENT_CONFIG_PATH, INFERENCE_URL, INFERENCE_AUDIENCE and AGENT_REAL_REVIEWS. The wrapper at d8e22f7 defaults INFERENCE_URL to an older host, so set it. Then create the ruleset from the JSON (`gh api -X POST orgs/cgwalters-forge/rulesets --input .github/rulesets/org-review.json`), narrowed to one repository first. Merging this needs an owner bypass: workflows-check refuses a new pull_request_target trigger and its zizmor ignore.

Follow-ups from review: in a repository that keeps its review.yml, both workflows share the wrapper's `review-pull-N` concurrency group and cancel each other's agent job, so drop that repository's review.yml (step 4) when adding it. There is no merge_group trigger.

Verified with `node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs` (42 pass), actionlint, and zizmor offline. The runner-labels lint needs cargo, which wasn't available, so it did not run; the workflow has no runs-on of its own. One review pass; its one blocker is the missing default task above.

issue.title: workflows: Add a wrapper canary that runs a real dispatch and review
issue.body:
#136 changed both agent wrappers, passed every check and review, and then broke every agent run for hours: nothing ran a real agent through a pull request's own wrappers, and the review ran the base branch's copy. This adds a wrapper canary. `wrapper-canary-gate.yml` sets a `wrapper-canary` status on every pull request to main. The status is success unless the pull request changes `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` or `cgwalters-review.yml`; otherwise it stays pending until `wrapper-canary.yml` passes. The gate uses `pull_request_target`, but runs base code and reads only the file list over the API.

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers, both fixed: the gate shared a file with the `@wrapper-canary` call, which GitHub resolves for every run, and the push procedure let a fork push run unread code. Still open:
- The ~10-minute bound is documented, not enforced. The dispatch wrapper has no timeout input, so its own 75-minute limit applies.
- A `pull_request` job named `wrapper-canary` in a fork could perhaps satisfy the required status, the same weakness `ci` has.
- Board-test's review runs are found by "newest since the reopen", not matched to the scratch pull request.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test, new file `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`:

  ```yaml
  name: wrapper-canary-review
  on:
    pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
      types: [reopened]
  permissions: {}
  jobs:
    review:
      if: github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)
      uses: cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary
      permissions: {contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: write, actions: read, id-token: write, statuses: write}
  ```

  board-test also needs the variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`, and its `AGENT` must be unset or a real agent.
- Tailnet federation and inference broker: admit `job_workflow_ref` `cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary` and `.../cgwalters-review.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary`.
- cgwalters-forge/actions:
  - The branch `wrapper-canary`, created at main, with a ruleset that lets only maintainers update it.
  - The variables `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`: a scratch issue, and a non-draft scratch pull request opened by a collaborator, both in board-test.
  - The environment `agent-apply`, and access to the organization secret `CGWALTERS_BOT_PAT`.
  - Last, the main ruleset's required status check `wrapper-canary`.

Closes #138

issue.title: wrapper: Document external execution integration blockers
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Document the exact upstream interfaces needed before exposing external execution. Released preflight and evidence support exists, but implement checkout lacks a dispatched-base pin and its inference token still carries lifecycle authority on the agent host. No runtime workflow, pin, caller or deployment changes.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/actions/issues/232

issue.title: intake: Stage operator mentions made in inline review comments
issue.body:
The operator mentioned `@cgwalters-bot` with a request ("verify+review all of this and diff ...") in an **inline review comment** on a public upstream PR, upstream rpm-ostree PR 5662, at 2026-11-17T21:46Z. That repository has a midstream fork, cgwalters-forge/rpm-ostree, with issues enabled. Two local applying passes on main (52adc0d) ran after the comment:

- **What they logged:** `coreos/rpm-ostree#5662 activity: cgwalters reviewed (commented) (direction)`.
- **What's missing:** neither printed a `notifications:` decision line for the thread or staged an issue in the fork. Both still printed decision lines for other upstream threads.

So operator-direction intake missed an operator mention that sits in a review comment rather than an issue comment. Either the `commenter:OPERATOR mentions:BOT` search doesn't return threads where the mention is only in an inline review comment, or the admission step drops review comments for threads the bot doesn't author.

Fix it so that an operator mention in an inline review comment, or in a review body, on an upstream PR is staged in the matching midstream fork like any other mention. If search can't find these, read the operator's review comments on the threads it does return. Add a regression test for an upstream PR whose only mention is an inline review comment.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: poll: Treat a repository without review.yml as no review job, not an error
issue.body:
A local applying pass on main (c47d20a) failed with "1 operation(s) of the pass failed" because it walked a bot PR in a repository that has no review workflow:

```
cgwalters-forge/.github#5 error: GET repos/cgwalters-forge/.github/actions/workflows/review.yml/runs?head_sha=...&event=pull_request_target&per_page=10: GitHub HTTP status 404: not found
```

A missing review workflow is an answer: the PR has no review-job verdict, and only the operator's review counts. A read-only request for [the followed PR's](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/.github/pull/5) current head returned HTTP 404 from the exact workflow-runs endpoint. At [c47d20a, review_rerun propagates that read failure](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agent-board/blob/c47d20a73495cc4d1b4bb5bfdc3810c8ce6c7520/crates/board-forge/src/poll.rs#L7033-L7045); [review_runs](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agent-board/blob/c47d20a73495cc4d1b4bb5bfdc3810c8ce6c7520/crates/board-forge/src/poll.rs#L7212-L7223) has the same exposure for dispatched reviews. issue.title: release-train: Find callers across all repositories instead of a list
issue.body:
Operator direction: no hand-kept repository lists; tools like this iterate over every repository by default.

The release train moves only the callers listed in tracker's `.github/release-train/config.json`, and there are two of them (tracker and agent-board). Every other caller drifts. The org site's review wrapper sat at agentic-job v0.5.2 until its policy job began failing every run (HTTP 403 fetching its own release commit), which blocked cgwalters-forge.github.io#18. The controller is fixing that one by hand in cgwalters-forge.github.io#19.

`release-train` should discover its callers itself: every non-archived, non-fork repository of the owner whose workflows pin one of the configured `wrappers` files by commit, using code search or one tree read per repository through the store's cache. Explicit `callers` entries become exceptions only, for extra files such as test fixtures. Report each caller it found, with the pin it has.

issue.title: poll: Route protected-path hand-backs to the controller, not the operator
issue.body:
Agent runs can't hand back `.github/**` or `.gitignore`, so any change that needs a workflow edit stalls. cgwalters-forge.github.io#18 (the Zensical port) put its `site.yml` diff in the PR body. Its fix round correctly pushed nothing, and the poll then stopped and parked the PR on the operator's requested review for a day. The controller applied the diff by hand.

That's mechanical work, not an operator decision:
- When a run's hand-back names a protected-path diff, the pass should route it to a privileged controller step that applies it to the PR branch, or to a narrow bounds file that allows exactly those paths for this repository. Only a change to the trust boundary itself (bounds, rulesets, credentials) should go to the operator.
- "Fix round pushed no new head" should hold for the controller with the run's stated reason, not stop on a requested operator review.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: release-train: Find callers across all repositories instead of a list
issue.body:
Operator direction: no hand-kept repository lists; tools like this iterate over every repository by default.

The release train moves only the callers listed in tracker's `.github/release-train/config.json`, and there are two of them (tracker and agent-board). Every other caller drifts. The org site's review wrapper sat at agentic-job v0.5.2 until its policy job began failing every run (HTTP 403 fetching its own release commit), which blocked cgwalters-forge.github.io#18. The controller is fixing that one by hand in cgwalters-forge.github.io#19.

`release-train` should discover its callers itself: every non-archived, non-fork repository of the owner whose workflows pin one of the configured `wrappers` files by commit, using code search or one tree read per repository through the store's cache. Explicit `callers` entries become exceptions only, for extra files such as test fixtures. Report each caller it found, with the pin it has.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: poll: Route protected-path hand-backs to the controller, not the operator
issue.body:
Agent runs can't hand back `.github/**` or `.gitignore`, so any change that needs a workflow edit stalls. cgwalters-forge.github.io#18 (the Zensical port) put its `site.yml` diff in the PR body. Its fix round correctly pushed nothing, and the poll then stopped and parked the PR on the operator's requested review for a day. The controller applied the diff by hand.

That's mechanical work, not an operator decision:
- When a run's hand-back names a protected-path diff, the pass should route it to a privileged controller step that applies it to the PR branch, or to a narrow bounds file that allows exactly those paths for this repository. Only a change to the trust boundary itself (bounds, rulesets, credentials) should go to the operator.
- "Fix round pushed no new head" should hold for the controller with the run's stated reason, not stop on a requested operator review.

Part of #1047.

comment.body:
**Valid historical failure; routing partly exists, but protected-patch application needs a design first.** The [fix-run handback](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/cgwalters-forge.github.io/pull/18#issuecomment-6926557867) names the protected files; the [poll stop](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/cgwalters-forge.github.io/pull/18#issuecomment-6931523133) then requests operator review. This confirms the sequence in recorded evidence, not a new live reproduction. The workflow correction is now [on that branch](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/cgwalters-forge.github.io/commit/a02a8b5bb34695dd1bef3d9070da25a2af517637).

Existing [EmptyFix routing](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agent-board/blob/c47d20a/crates/board-forge/src/poll.rs#L4110-L4119) supports a supervisor hold without requesting operator review; its targeted regression test passed locally (1 test). But the caller's [pass configuration](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/blob/8ed83a2/.github/pass.json) omits pr.supervisorHolds, and its [supervisor configuration](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/blob/8ed83a2/.github/supervisor/config.json) omits the supervisor_hold daily cap. The [documented feature](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agent-board/blob/c47d20a/docs/pass.md#infrastructure-stops) is off by default: enabling this route is caller follow-through, not a new routing algorithm.

Recommended design: reuse that queue, preserving the run's reason as diagnostic evidence, never authorization. Specify the missing protected-change proposal/check/apply contract in agentic-job: immutable run/attempt, repository and head binding; exact permitted paths; independent validation; stale-head refusal and idempotent application. Tracker owns caller wiring; board consumes the validated outcome and preserves genuine human holds. A PR-body diff alone must not authorize privileged writes ([existing boundary](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agent-board/blob/c47d20a/AGENTS.md#L43-L48)). No bounds relaxation or new privileged executor is authorized here. What remains unclear is that contract and deployment dependency, not an operator engineering choice; design and split those implementation slices first. The separate .gitignore checker defect already has [agentic-job#3407](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agentic-job/issues/3407).

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Discover release-train callers from the wrappers owner's complete repository inventory so unlisted repositories cannot be silently skipped. Keep configured files as additive fixture exceptions, resolve existing bot forks by parent identity, and optionally reuse revalidated bounded cache responses. Incomplete inventory visibility fails closed; existing write authorization and credential boundaries stay unchanged.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agent-board/issues/1087

Verified: `just fmt`, `cargo test -p board-forge release_train --locked -- --nocapture` (28 tests), `just check`, `git diff --check`, and `just decision-diff /tmp/opencode/agent-board-base` all exited 0. CLI docs regenerated with `just cli-docs`. General pass replay summaries (not discovery coverage):
```text
base: exit 0, summary: dispatched 1/1, writes 3/3, held 5, requests 57 (epics 17, schedule 37, status 3)
head: exit 0, summary: dispatched 1/1, writes 3/3, held 5, requests 57 (epics 17, schedule 37, status 3)
no change in 44 line(s)
```

The read-only caller-config preview (`cargo run --locked -q -p agent-board -- release-train --config /tmp/opencode/release-train-config.json`) exited 0 at the version-bump wait, before discovery. `/user` returned HTTP 403 with this run's token. Synthetic extensions exercise the missing-site discovery and edit, but neither the historical recording nor this live preview proves deployed org-site remediation. No live apply was run. Owner-level public/private counts must be available to the existing credential before deployment; missing visibility now halts rather than accepting a partial inventory.

Review: two adversarial passes; the final delta review left no blockers or important nonblocking findings.

## Caller settings

Caller repository: `cgwalters-forge/tracker`. Deployment dependency: in `.github/workflows/release-train.yml`, set `env.AGENT_BOARD_REV` to the reviewed commit containing this PR (resolve the exact SHA after merge; this run does not deploy it). In that repository's `.github/release-train/config.json`, remove `.github/workflows/review.yml` from both `callers[].files` lists; retain `.github/agentic-job/config-test/tests/config.rs` for tracker and `.github/agentic-job/test_review.py` for agent-board, plus their fork overrides. issue.title: dispatch: Start a job straight from an issue without a plan comment
issue.body:
Operator direction: agent-board should be able to look at an issue and dispatch it directly.

`agent-board dispatch` only starts a job from an accepted plan comment, so a fully specified issue the controller files still waits through triage and planning, one pass each, before any work starts. The controller ended up bypassing agent-board with a raw `gh workflow run dispatch.yml` (agentic-job#4312, tracker run 44089733918), which also skips the dispatch record and pass accounting.

`agent-board dispatch ISSUE --kind implement [--pool P] [--task-from-body]` should:
- Build the task from the issue body, or from a given brief, when there's no plan.
- Check the same bounds, pool and wip admission as the pass, and record the dispatch in the store and on the issue, so the pass sees the run and doesn't start it again.
- Accept several items for one run (#1082).

issue.title: poll: Route protected-path hand-backs to the controller, not the operator
issue.body:
Agent runs can't hand back `.github/**` or `.gitignore`, so any change that needs a workflow edit stalls. cgwalters-forge.github.io#18 (the Zensical port) put its `site.yml` diff in the PR body. Its fix round correctly pushed nothing, and the poll then stopped and parked the PR on the operator's requested review for a day. The controller applied the diff by hand.

That's mechanical work, not an operator decision:
- When a run's hand-back names a protected-path diff, the pass should route it to a privileged controller step that applies it to the PR branch, or to a narrow bounds file that allows exactly those paths for this repository. Only a change to the trust boundary itself (bounds, rulesets, credentials) should go to the operator.
- "Fix round pushed no new head" should hold for the controller with the run's stated reason, not stop on a requested operator review.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: plan: Let one implement run take a set of items and land them as a stack
issue.body:
Operator direction: one implement run should be able to take several related issues or PRs as context and produce a stack of PRs, or a few commits per PR, instead of one run per issue that each wait their turn and conflict.

This needs:
- **Plans:** a job plan that names several items (issues, or PRs it supersedes), with the overlap check waiving the PRs it names (see #1081).

- **Bounds:** tracker's implement bounds allow more than one `create_pull_request` per run, stacked on the run's own branches.
- **Closing:** closing what the run supersedes once its stack merges.

First manual use: agentic-job#4312, dispatched directly (tracker run 44089733918) as one PR with one commit per superseded PR.

A local applying pass on main (c47d20a) failed with "1 operation(s) of the pass failed" because it walked a bot PR in a repository that has no review workflow:

```
cgwalters-forge/.github#5 error: GET repos/cgwalters-forge/.github/actions/workflows/review.yml/runs?head_sha=...&event=pull_request_target&per_page=10: GitHub HTTP status 404: not found
```

A missing review workflow is an answer: the PR has no review-job verdict, and only the operator's review counts. The pass should treat that 404 as "no review workflow here" rather than a failed operation, and say so once per repository. Add a test for a followed PR in a repository without the workflow.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: poll: Route protected-path hand-backs to the controller, not the operator
issue.body:
Agent runs can't hand back `.github/**` or `.gitignore`, so any change that needs a workflow edit stalls. cgwalters-forge.github.io#18 (the Zensical port) put its `site.yml` diff in the PR body. Its fix round correctly pushed nothing, and the poll then stopped and parked the PR on the operator's requested review for a day. The controller applied the diff by hand.

That's mechanical work, not an operator decision:
- When a run's hand-back names a protected-path diff, the pass should route it to a privileged controller step that applies it to the PR branch, or to a narrow bounds file that allows exactly those paths for this repository. Only a change to the trust boundary itself (bounds, rulesets, credentials) should go to the operator.
- "Fix round pushed no new head" should hold for the controller with the run's stated reason, not stop on a requested operator review.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: pass: Rebuild a stuck cluster of overlapping approved PRs as one stack
issue.body:
When several approved PRs from the bot overlap and each waits behind another (`wait: open-pr-cap: land X first; overlapping paths`), none of them lands, and rebasing them one at a time makes each landing conflict the next. In agentic-job, six approved PRs on `docs/plan.md` sat like this for about three days, and the controller filed agentic-job#4312 by hand to rebuild them as one stack.

When the pass finds a cluster of overlapping approved PRs from the bot that have waited longer than a threshold, it should plan one implement run that rebuilds them as a single stack on main: one commit per PR, with "Supersedes #N" for each. The cluster should go ahead of the open-PR cap, and the superseded PRs should be closed once the stack merges.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: release-train: Find callers across all repositories instead of a list
issue.body:
Operator direction: no hand-kept repository lists; tools like this iterate over every repository by default.

The release train moves only the callers listed in tracker's `.github/release-train/config.json`, and there are two of them (tracker and agent-board). Every other caller drifts. The org site's review wrapper sat at agentic-job v0.5.2 until its policy job began failing every run (HTTP 403 fetching its own release commit), which blocked cgwalters-forge.github.io#18. The controller is fixing that one by hand in cgwalters-forge.github.io#19.

`release-train` should discover its callers itself: every non-archived, non-fork repository of the owner whose workflows pin one of the configured `wrappers` files by commit, using code search or one tree read per repository through the store's cache. Explicit `callers` entries become exceptions only, for extra files such as test fixtures. Report each caller it found, with the pin it has.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: docs: Split pass.md into one short page per feature
issue.body:
docs/pass.md is 6,415 lines and 68,000 words, and 194 commits touched it in November alone. Every new pass option adds a section to it, so nearly every agent-board PR overlaps every other on this one file (#1072, #1073 and #1074 queued behind each other on it), and the overlap check serializes otherwise independent work.

Split it into one short file per feature under docs/pass/ (holds, budget, changes stage, reserveOperator, openPrCap, and so on), with docs/pass.md kept as a one-screen index. While splitting, cut each part to current behavior: drop the issue-number history and the narrative of how each option came about, which git log and the issues keep. Update inbound anchors (`git grep 'pass.md#'`).

Land it when no open PR edits docs/pass.md, or fold those PRs' doc hunks in.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: dispatch: Start an issue without a plan comment
issue.body:
dispatch: Start an issue without a plan comment

A fully specified issue the controller files waited through triage and
planning before any work started, so the controller bypassed agent-board
with a raw `gh workflow run`, skipping the dispatch record and the pass's
WIP and pacing. `agent-board dispatch --kind implement` with `--task` or
`--task-from-body` now starts the issue directly.

It builds a hosted plan validated as a plan comment is, posts it as the
token's own and dispatches exactly that plan by the existing protocol, so
the record is the same one a later pass reads and it never starts the issue
again. The concrete threat is a start outside the pass skipping its WIP
limit and pacing (#382), so the mode requires the pass configuration with
`leases` on and takes a lease at the send, as the pass's own starts do.
The body counts only as a plan writer's own unedited text. Off unless

issue.title: poll: Route protected-path hand-backs to the controller, not the operator
issue.body:
Agent runs can't hand back `.github/**` or `.gitignore`, so any change that needs a workflow edit stalls. cgwalters-forge.github.io#18 (the Zensical port) put its `site.yml` diff in the PR body. Its fix round correctly pushed nothing, and the poll then stopped and parked the PR on the operator's requested review for a day. The controller applied the diff by hand.

That's mechanical work, not an operator decision:
- When a run's hand-back names a protected-path diff, the pass should route it to a privileged controller step that applies it to the PR branch, or to a narrow bounds file that allows exactly those paths for this repository. Only a change to the trust boundary itself (bounds, rulesets, credentials) should go to the operator.
- "Fix round pushed no new head" should hold for the controller with the run's stated reason, not stop on a requested operator review.

issue.title: dispatch: Start a job straight from an issue without a plan comment
issue.body:
Operator direction: agent-board should be able to look at an issue and dispatch it directly.

`agent-board dispatch` only starts a job from an accepted plan comment, so a fully specified issue the controller files still waits through triage and planning, one pass each, before any work starts. The controller ended up bypassing agent-board with a raw `gh workflow run dispatch.yml` (agentic-job#4312, tracker run 44089733918), which also skips the dispatch record and pass accounting.

`agent-board dispatch ISSUE --kind implement [--pool P] [--task-from-body]` should:
- Build the task from the issue body, or from a given brief, when there's no plan.
- Check the same bounds, pool and wip admission as the pass, and record the dispatch in the store and on the issue, so the pass sees the run and doesn't start it again.
- Accept several items for one run (#1082).

Part of #1047.

review.body:
VERDICT: APPROVE

Reviewed admitted head `8bdc006987a0e53771f02bc684f2009896c55602` against merge base `59116b2115b5c40c369042ba5630e2918191ba11`.

## Follow-ups

- **important** — `crates/board-forge/src/plan.rs:1670-1673`: Cleanup does not cover all definitely-unsent failures. After posting the plan, `dispatch_with` can fail before posting any dispatch record—for example, its initial comment read can fail, or its living-status-ledger check can refuse the issue. Neither error is `Refused`, so this branch leaves the newly posted plan behind. Retrying the same `--kind` command then fails with “holds a plan; dispatch it without --kind”; that suggested fallback also drops this mode's lease wrapper. Track whether a dispatch could actually have been sent, remove the plan on definitely-unsent errors, and retain it on ambiguous sends. Add coverage for a failure between posting the plan and posting the record, not just lease refusal.

- **important** — `crates/board-forge/src/plan.rs:1645-1655`: The initial no-plan/no-record check is not an issue-wide claim. Two invocations can both pass it; A can post and start its plan before B posts its different plan. B's later checks are keyed to B's plan, so A's dispatch record does not stop B. Once A's lease has been bound to its run, admission no longer sees a pending reservation for that issue and can admit B when WIP has room. This can start two implement jobs for the same issue, despite recording both. The documentation acknowledges the race, but caller serialization is not enforced here. An issue-wide claim or a mandatory shared concurrency mechanism would make the once-only guarantee reliable; cover that interleaving.

Bounds assessment: this adds an authorized path to start an implement job and write its plan/dispatch comments. The worst observed outcomes are a stranded plan and duplicate implement jobs as described above. issue.title: poll: Keep untested midstream drafts out of the promotion wait
issue.body:
## Executive summary

A bot midstream draft whose own description says it is incomplete or untested used to wait as if ready to promote whenever `continuation.untested` was off. The poll now spots those words whatever the setting. With the setting off, it waits with its own reason, `a midstream draft that says it is untested, waiting for the operator`. The board lists it as `review-untested`, apart from the promotion group and the quiet waits. With the setting on, the existing continuation path is unchanged.

Once a continuation has run on the branch, the head commit message is what counts as the evidence. That now survives operator resets and stops, which still give fresh round counts. A new marker field, `continued_before`, records it, and every reset path keeps it. The word matcher now matches whole words and skips clearly negated phrasing such as "no longer incomplete" or "nothing untested", and phrasing about the code such as "Fix incomplete decoding".

## More detail

Nothing here enables `continuation.untested`, names a runner profile or widens bounds. The caller setting that takes effect would be `pr.continuation.untested` in the tracker's `.github/pass.json`. It is absent there today; `.github/poll/agent-board.json` is legacy. It stays off until an admitted runner and an end-to-end continuation proof exist. A real partial-draft observation is still needed as acceptance evidence.

Known limits:
- After a continuation, a later fix round's commit becomes the head commit message that is read. This was already the case and is unchanged.
- A commit subject that uses one of the words about the code, other than right after fix/fixes/fixed, still matches. This costs a bounded wait or round.
- A quiet `promote` entry cached before deploy replays until its next whole read, at most 4h.

issue.title: pass: Rebuild a stuck cluster of overlapping approved PRs as one stack
issue.body:
When several approved PRs from the bot overlap and each waits behind another (`wait: open-pr-cap: land X first; overlapping paths`), none of them lands, and rebasing them one at a time makes each landing conflict the next. In agentic-job, six approved PRs on `docs/plan.md` sat like this for about three days, and the controller filed agentic-job#4312 by hand to rebuild them as one stack.

When the pass finds a cluster of overlapping approved PRs from the bot that have waited longer than a threshold, it should plan one implement run that rebuilds them as a single stack on main: one commit per PR, with "Supersedes #N" for each. The cluster should go ahead of the open-PR cap, and the superseded PRs should be closed once the stack merges.

issue.title: pass: Rebuild a stuck cluster of overlapping approved PRs as one stack
issue.body:
When several approved PRs from the bot overlap and each waits behind another (`wait: open-pr-cap: land X first; overlapping paths`), none of them lands, and rebasing them one at a time makes each landing conflict the next. In agentic-job, six approved PRs on `docs/plan.md` sat like this for about three days, and the controller filed agentic-job#4312 by hand to rebuild them as one stack.

When the pass finds a cluster of overlapping approved PRs from the bot that have waited longer than a threshold, it should plan one implement run that rebuilds them as a single stack on main: one commit per PR, with "Supersedes #N" for each. The cluster should go ahead of the open-PR cap, and the superseded PRs should be closed once the stack merges.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: pass: Rebuild a stuck cluster of overlapping approved PRs as one stack
issue.body:
When several approved PRs from the bot overlap and each waits behind another (`wait: open-pr-cap: land X first; overlapping paths`), none of them lands, and rebasing them one at a time makes each landing conflict the next. In agentic-job, six approved PRs on `docs/plan.md` sat like this for about three days, and the controller filed agentic-job#4312 by hand to rebuild them as one stack.

When the pass finds a cluster of overlapping approved PRs from the bot that have waited longer than a threshold, it should plan one implement run that rebuilds them as a single stack on main: one commit per PR, with "Supersedes #N" for each. The cluster should go ahead of the open-PR cap, and the superseded PRs should be closed once the stack merges.

Part of #1047.

issue.title: ci: Run in the merge queue behind one aggregate ci check
issue.body:
`.github/workflows/check.yml` runs one job, `check`, on `push` and `pull_request` only, and the repository has no ruleset of its own, so pull requests merge directly and siblings invalidate each other as they land.

Pattern to copy: agent-board's .github/workflows/ci.yml (forge-infra's is the smallest copy): `on:` has `pull_request`, `merge_group: {types: [checks_requested]}` and `push: {branches: [main]}`; one job named `ci` with `if: ${{ always() }}` and `needs:` on every other job runs `jq -e 'all(.[]; .result == "success")'` over `toJSON(needs)`, so the ruleset requires only `ci`, on both pull-request and merge-group commits.

Change for this repository: add the `merge_group` trigger, keep `push` to `main` only, and add the aggregate `ci` job that needs `check`. Once `ci` reports on a merge-group commit, the controller adds the ruleset with the queue (tracker's docs/rulesets/cgwalters-forge-agent-board.json; that step is tracked separately on the epic).

Part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#1727.
