issue.title: opencode: Add a generic self-hosted openai-compatible provider and a trimmed local agent
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Let agenthome's default opencode config reach self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints as well as the broker, so that some work can run on self-hosted models only. Keep it generic and public: a placeholder address only, no hosts. The real address is substituted privately in the derived config.

## More detail

Edit `opencode/opencode.json` (opencode 2.x):

- **Provider.** Add a second provider, `local`, in 2.x's `providers` form. The legacy `provider` + `npm` form listed the models in opencode 2.3.0, but runs returned "Model unavailable". Use package `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, with `settings.baseURL` set to a placeholder such as `http://local-inference.invalid/v1` and `settings.apiKey` set to `"none"`.
- **Models.** Use llama.cpp router models (the IDs are the GGUF base names), each with context 32768, output 4096 and cost 0: `Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M`, `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4` and `granite-4.0-h-tiny-Q4_K_M`.
- **Agent.** Add a primary agent `local` with a one-line system prompt, only the `bash` and `read` tools, and model `local/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M`. The trimmed prompt matters on small iGPUs: prompt processing runs at 200-400 tokens/s, and the default build prompt plus tool schemas is about 9,900 tokens (about 45 s before the first token), while the trimmed agent sends about 4,600.
- **Enabled providers.** Add `local` to `enabled_providers` next to `praxis`.

`just check`'s placeholder enforcement must cover the new baseURL. Validate the JSON against opencode 2.x's schema where available.

VERDICT: APPROVE — no concrete blocker found.

Reviewed admitted head `6a6d02c7f7ec1627ddb66b5f04220eb5a82954d5`, diffed against `origin/main` at merge-base `11b1561bdfa00fbf8855a48cbc6f44aa2c778715`.

### Follow-ups
- **important** — `README.md:95–106`: the launcher/version assertion and my sandbox model-list preview are not evidence of the operator's real derived configuration. Please supply the caller/configuration identity (without its private endpoint or credentials), exact preview command, reviewed revision, and redacted output listing all three local model IDs, with confirmation that no inference or caller changes occurred. The PR body still describes the superseded `providers.local.settings.baseURL` key; the admitted profile uses `provider.local.options.baseURL`. No inspectable real-caller preview artifact was supplied.

### Security scope
The worst configuration failure would send private session content to an unintended provider. The new file is opt-in rather than an edit to the hosted provider/runner configuration; it enables only `local`, overrides existing explicit agent models, disables sharing, and ships only an inert `.invalid` endpoint. The validator also rejects native `providers` entries in the hosted profiles, closing rather than opening that alternate configuration path. The profile is not a security sandbox: its allowed bash can execute arbitrary commands, and later project configuration can override routing, as documented. No workflow, merge-policy, owner assignment, dependency manifest or lockfile changes are present.

From `/home/runner-sandbox/work/review-head`:
- `opencode --version` → exit 0, `1.18.35`; `opencode --help`, `opencode models --help`, and `opencode debug --help` → exit 0. Model listing has no documented `--json` option.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG="$PWD/opencode/opencode-local.json" opencode --pure models local` → exit 0; listed exactly the three configured `local/` IDs. This uses the admitted file instead of installing or changing the caller's derived configuration.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG="$PWD/opencode/opencode-local.json" opencode --pure debug agent local` → exit 0; resolved the local model and only bash/read enabled. No inference was requested.
- `mkdir /tmp/opencode/review95` → exit 1, permission denied; no disposable home was created. Trials therefore used the existing sandbox configuration, not an isolated real-caller reproduction.

No test suites, formatters, linters, live inference, or CI-result queries were run.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Add a second opencode provider, `local`, for self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints (llama.cpp router models), and a trimmed primary agent `local` that uses it with only `bash` and `read` and a one-line prompt, so some work can run on self-hosted models only. The address is a `.invalid` placeholder; `just check-config` now enforces placeholders for 2.x `providers` entries too and refuses extra keys in their settings and model entries.

Verified with `just check` (exit 0); the JSON's shape was compared against opencode 2.x's published schema, as no opencode binary was available. One review pass, no blockers. Follow-ups it raised: the `local` agent and provider now reach every hosted run and eval bundle (`opencode-runner.json` could disable the agent, as it does for `fast` and `architect`), and legacy `provider.praxis.models` entries still aren't key-restricted.

## Caller settings

Repository and file: the operator's private derived opencode configuration (not named in the issue). Key: `providers.local.settings.baseURL`. Value: the real endpoint, e.g. `http://<host>:<port>/v1`, in place of `http://local-inference.invalid/v1`.

issue.title: opencode: Add a self-hosted openai-compatible provider and local agent
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Add a second opencode provider, `local`, for self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints (llama.cpp router models), and a trimmed primary agent `local` that uses it with only `bash` and `read` and a one-line prompt, so some work can run on self-hosted models only. The address is a `.invalid` placeholder; `just check-config` now enforces placeholders for 2.x `providers` entries too and refuses extra keys in their settings and model entries.

Verified with `just check` (exit 0); the JSON's shape was compared against opencode 2.x's published schema, as no opencode binary was available. One review pass, no blockers. Follow-ups it raised: the `local` agent and provider now reach every hosted run and eval bundle (`opencode-runner.json` could disable the agent, as it does for `fast` and `architect`), and legacy `provider.praxis.models` entries still aren't key-restricted.

## Caller settings

Repository and file: the operator's private derived opencode configuration (not named in the issue). Key: `providers.local.settings.baseURL`. Value: the real endpoint, e.g. `http://<host>:<port>/v1`, in place of `http://local-inference.invalid/v1`.

Generated-by: https://github.com/cgwalters/#llms

Closes #94

Add an offline allocation/enforcement evidence checker and complete opt-in evaluation bundles through the shared tier resolver, leaving normal routing unchanged. This makes the first readiness slice usable without inventing capacity or launching measurements.

Part of #52

The existing [report](eval/report.md#current-runner-contract-and-external-prerequisites) records the pinned runner contract and a concrete external reservation/enforcement follow-up. Verification: `just check` passes all 66 tests; the archived-summary test matches `summarize-eval` output. Initial diagnostic/number-spelling test failures and whitespace findings were fixed.

Review: one adversarial pass, no blockers; follow-ups are stricter artifact URL syntax and independent assertions of the full built-in agent set, plus a no-inference configuration-load test when available.

issue.title: opencode: Add a generic self-hosted openai-compatible provider and a trimmed local agent
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Let agenthome's default opencode config reach self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints as well as the broker, so that some work can run on self-hosted models only. Keep it generic and public: a placeholder address only, no hosts. The real address is substituted privately in the derived config.

## More detail

Edit `opencode/opencode.json` (opencode 2.x):

- **Provider.** Add a second provider, `local`, in 2.x's `providers` form. The legacy `provider` + `npm` form listed the models in opencode 2.3.0, but runs returned "Model unavailable". Use package `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, with `settings.baseURL` set to a placeholder such as `http://local-inference.invalid/v1` and `settings.apiKey` set to `"none"`.
- **Models.** Use llama.cpp router models (the IDs are the GGUF base names), each with context 32768, output 4096 and cost 0: `Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M`, `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4` and `granite-4.0-h-tiny-Q4_K_M`.
- **Agent.** Add a primary agent `local` with a one-line system prompt, only the `bash` and `read` tools, and model `local/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M`. The trimmed prompt matters on small iGPUs: prompt processing runs at 200-400 tokens/s, and the default build prompt plus tool schemas is about 9,900 tokens (about 45 s before the first token), while the trimmed agent sends about 4,600.
- **Enabled providers.** Add `local` to `enabled_providers` next to `praxis`.

`just check`'s placeholder enforcement must cover the new baseURL. Validate the JSON against opencode 2.x's schema where available.

issue.title: eval: Publish measured role-prompt comparison and adoption verdict
issue.body:
Publish the measured role-prompt comparison and adoption verdict for cgwalters-forge/tracker#782.

Done: tier map (agenthome#53), shared role files in both tool forms (agenthome#56, canonical since #86), offline protocol and summarizer, now in agent-board (agent-board#1017: docs/eval.md, eval/arms.json, eval/manifest.json). agenthome is configuration only (agenthome#76); no new Rust lands there. Pull requests agenthome#87 and agenthome#93 (offline readiness checks, Rust in agenthome) are superseded by that import and do not complete this issue; a merge of either must not close it.

Prerequisites, each a sibling sub-issue of tracker#782: the frozen task sample in agent-board's manifest; the assembled and archived arm bundles with the manifest's configuration; the opt-in eval dispatch in tracker with one probe per arm proving the runner loads the roles. Do not start cells before all three are merged.

Then: run the predeclared matrix (tasks x three arms x cold and warm x three repetitions, 36 or 54 cells) in the archived order under the existing per-run limits and board pace, each cell with a lease, no retries or added cells; record every run in agent-board's eval/runs.json in the protocol's record format with unavailable metrics marked unavailable; summarize with agent-board eval summarize; publish the report next to the protocol with linked runs, configuration digests, independently checked outcomes, limitations and an explicit win, no-win or inconclusive verdict under quality-cost-time-v1. No evidence means blocked, not a synthetic success. Spend beyond the existing bounds stays with the operator.

VERDICT: APPROVE — no blocker found in the offline-only change.

Reviewed admitted head `c14dbe7c61ce5e32f4449058aa436606b3ada5c6` against `origin/main`, merge-base `b68e3f632a870aa1bb681b811693bdf86c1ff077`.

### Follow-ups
- **important** — `src/readiness.rs:139–145`: evidence is bound only to phase counts/limits, not the bundle/configuration digest. A different role/model bundle with the same plan can reuse delivery/cache assertions and still receive `evidence-consistent`. Bind these assertions to immutable configuration/environment pins before connecting this checker to execution. Currently this is bounded by explicit manual evidence validation and the absence of a launcher.
- **important** — `eval/report.md:104–118`: the pinned source audit is not real-caller preview evidence. Please supply the caller/configuration, exact command and revision, installed-profile digest, and a no-apply run artifact showing effective role/model selection when the independently enforced capacity/probe gates permit it. The report correctly acknowledges that runtime evidence is absent; local rendering does not close this gap.
- **nit** — `tests/check_config.py:783–795`: plain `--help` selects unittest's parser and never advertises `--eval-arm` or `--output`; successful rendering also prints nothing, and filesystem failures expose tracebacks. Make the renderer discoverable and give a short completion/actionable error message without running tests. The generated JSON files already provide machine-readable artifacts.
- **nit** — `src/readiness.rs:31–33`: the source check accepts bare `https://` and URLs containing userinfo, despite the documented nonsecret HTTPS-artifact requirement. Validate URL structure and reject embedded credentials. No URL is fetched here, so this is not an SSRF path.

### Bounds
The worst plausible merged outcome is someone mistaking self-asserted evidence for permission to spend, or staging a bundle whose effective runtime models differ from its recorded map. This patch itself cannot launch either: the checker only reads JSON, never fetches evidence or executes commands, returns `inferenceAuthorized: false`, and has no workflow consumer. Rendering writes only into a newly created local directory; ordinary profiles, permissions, provider settings, workflows and dependency pins are unchanged. Documentation retains the independent capacity, reservation, child-inclusive enforcement and runtime-proof gates.

### Tried
- `python3 tests/check_config.py --help`: exit 0; unittest help only.
- `python3 tests/check_config.py --eval-arm single-strong --output /tmp/opencode/review93-strong`: exit 1 because the sandbox's `/tmp/opencode` is root-owned. Retried locally, without changing permissions.
- `python3 tests/check_config.py --eval-arm single-strong --output .review93-final-strong`, `python3 tests/check_config.py --eval-arm single-cheap --output .review93-final-cheap`, and `python3 tests/check_config.py --eval-arm tiered --output .review93-final-tiered`: each exit 0, no console output, four artifacts each. Inspection of the first equivalent local render confirmed single-model maps, the tiered default agent, and unchanged provider/general-agent permissions. Disposable artifact files were removed.
- `cargo run --locked -- check-eval-readiness --help` and `cargo run --locked -- check-eval-readiness eval/readiness.json`: each exit 127; Cargo is unavailable, so neither Rust CLI behavior nor the pending-input rejection was exercised.

No test suite, formatter, linter, CI lookup, live caller, inference or settings change was run. This read-only review cannot update the linked findings document.

## Executive summary

Operator direction: the coordinator agent must have the controller's knowledge and use judgment. It must not run the board command and bail when it hits a limit. Update `skills/supervisor/SKILL.md` with the lessons of 2026-11-15, written as judgment rather than rules to obey blindly.

## More detail

Lessons to add (keep them short):

- Rebase conflicting bot PRs; don't close them. Closing throws away finished work. Close only PRs that are genuinely superseded.

- Fixes the operator directed often ship opt-in. Check that the config actually turned them on (agent-board#1019).
- Use the `agent-board` CLI to diagnose and act. When it can't do what is needed, file the gap in agent-board instead of scripting around it.
- Midstream membership comes from repository metadata (a fork with the bot-midstream topic), never hardcoded repository lists.

## Executive summary

After the Zensical port (#4297, cgwalters-forge/agentic-job#4303) `site/` holds Python, not JavaScript, but two Astro-era exceptions remain. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s JavaScript check still lists `site/` in the paths where new `.mjs`/`.cjs` files may be added, so a JavaScript file could land there unchecked. `.gitignore` still ignores `/site/node_modules/`, `/site/dist/` and `/site/.astro/` instead of what the new build leaves behind. Drop `site/` from the CI allowlist and replace the Astro ignore lines with the Zensical build outputs.

discussion.title: Why haven't I adopted agentic-job and agenthome into my personal agents
discussion.body:
Hi Colin, I'm starting this discussion as feedback why I haven't adopted your 2 projects inside my personal agents.

TL;DR: you run agents in Github's runners, I run them locally in my homelab, closely tied to my forgejo deployment

Here is a summary from my software engineer agent (for some reason she wrote it in my voice, sorry about that):

Short answer: we borrowed the ideas, but neither project fits the shape of what we run today as-is.

**What we run.** My setup is a few long-lived agents in rootless podman containers on a home server, plus interactive agents on my laptops. The unattended ones watch a self-hosted Forgejo inbox, keep memory across runs, work through forks and PRs, and I review everything before merge. The laptop ones are plain interactive shells (Claude Code, pi, opencode), with different inference and config at home and at work.

**agentic-job.** We read it in late October (around v0.6.4) and liked the threat model a lot: assume prompt injection succeeds, keep credentials out of the agent's reach, and publish only through checked "safe outputs". Our agents today do hold their forge token, push key and model token, and publish comments directly, so this is exactly where we are weaker. We did not adopt it because:

- It is GitHub Actions-first. On Forgejo only the `apply --forge forgejo` side existed. The workflow, OIDC run registration and `secure-host` assume disposable GitHub-style VM runners with systemd 257+; our Forgejo runners run jobs as containers, so a trial needs a one-shot VM runner first.
- The credential broker registers runs with GitHub's OIDC token, which Forgejo Actions does not provide, and it documents API keys only; we run on a Claude subscription.
- It is a job model: disposable, no memory, no interactive shell. Our inbox watchers and laptop agents would have to be rebuilt around it.
- It was a week old and moving fast when we looked.

What happened instead: a Forgejo trial of agentic-job, compared side by side with our setup on the same task, is still on my list but never started (Tomas: I'm actually ask my agents now to proceed with the trial). The parts we most want to reuse are the safe-outputs pattern for forge writes and the broker/proxy as the secret store for our agents, so the model key never enters the container. That last one is an open issue on our new tool (below).

**agenthome.** We read it in mid-November and it matched the configuration half of my problem very closely: one rules file rendered per harness, base settings plus per-run overlays, a `check` that fails on stale rendered files, and a tiers manifest mapping prompt tiers to models per provider pool. We did not adopt it because:

- It is the config repo of your bot for agentic-job runs, and its renderer reads from the checkout it was built from, so it is not something another operator can point at their own config.
- It has no container, mounts or secret handling; that lives in agentic-job, in a shape that does not fit an interactive laptop agent.
- At the time it had no license, so we could not take code or text from it. (I see it is now MIT OR Apache-2.0, thank you, which changes this point.)

So we started our own small Rust tool, bree: a rootless podman runtime for local agents with `work` and `home` profiles, plus a renderer that builds each harness's config from shared blocks. Its README credits agenthome and agentic-job as the inspiration; the layout, overlays, `check` and tiers ideas all come from agenthome. It is early and will be published on GitHub.

**Where we would like to converge.** Now that agenthome is licensed, sharing the config format or the renderer is on the table instead of reimplementing it, and the agentic-job broker is the planned secret source for bree. Happy to compare notes on both.

issue.title: ostree/bootc: Make partition mount targets follow symlinks in the target system
issue.body:
Fedora bug 2520626 (Red Hat Bugzilla, public): on Fedora Silverblue 44 with a separate /home partition, the system boots to rescue mode after ostree 2026.3:

```
home.mount: Mount path /home is not canonical (contains a symlink).
Failed to mount home.mount - Home Partition.
```

The cause, from the bug's investigation: ostree 2026.3 creates `/run/systemd/volatile-root`, so `systemd-gpt-auto-generator` can now find the root disk. It sees the home partition tagged with the Discoverable Partitions home type GUID (933ac7e1-2eb4-4f13-b844-0e14e2aef915) and synthesizes `home.mount` for `/home`. On ostree systems `/home` is a symlink to `var/home`, so systemd refuses that mount. Anaconda wrote `UUID=... /home ext4 ...` into fstab, not `/var/home`, so the generator doesn't see an existing mount for the canonical path. Workarounds today are `systemd.gpt_auto=0` or retyping the partition by hand.

The operator's direction, also stated in the bug: anaconda should make partition mount targets follow symlinks in the target system.

## Investigate and prototype

1. **Follow symlinks for mount targets.** When anaconda installs an ostree or bootc payload and a requested mount point resolves to a symlink inside the deployment (`/home` → `/var/home`, also `/srv`, `/opt`, `/mnt`, `/root`, `/usr/local`, and any others the deployment defines), write the canonical path into fstab and mount at it. Find where the rpm-ostree and bootc payloads already special-case `/var` and its subdirectories (`pyanaconda/modules/payloads/payload/rpm_ostree/`, and the fstab writing in the storage module) and resolve each mount point against the deployment root, never the installer's own root. Handle symlink chains and refuse links that escape the root.
2. **Partition type.** Check whether anaconda, via blivet, assigns the DPS home GUID because the mount point is `/home`. When the actual mount point is `/var/home`, or anaconda writes an explicit fstab entry anyway, the generic Linux filesystem type is arguably the correct one. Report what blivet does and whether to change it, or whether item 1 alone suffices because the generator skips paths fstab already covers.
3. Say whether existing installs need a migration or documentation note. That's a write-up only; don't build it.

## Deliverable

A draft PR in this fork with the change and unit tests: a deployment where `/home` is a symlink yields a `/var/home` fstab entry; a non-ostree install is unchanged; a link escaping the root is refused. Also a short summary in the hand-back of item 2's findings. Nothing goes upstream; the operator promotes it.

comment.body:
**Valid, and it can be implemented here, but the issue's item 1 alone would not fix the boot failure.** The real fix is item 2: don't give ostree `/home` and `/srv` partitions the DPS GUIDs. Accepted implement plan below, with that as part 1.

The reasoning: [`systemd-gpt-auto-generator`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/gpt-auto-generator/gpt-auto-generator.c) `add_partition_mount`/`path_is_busy` never reads fstab for `/home`. It only skips paths that are already mounted or are non-empty directories, and it writes `home.mount` to the late generator dir. fstab-generator canonicalizes `/home` to `var-home.mount`, so the units never collide whether fstab says `/home` or `/var/home`. Blivet's [`part_type_uuid_req`](https://github.com/storaged-project/blivet/blob/main/blivet/devices/partition.py) maps the mount point through [`gpt_part_uuid_for_mountpoint`](https://github.com/storaged-project/blivet/blob/main/blivet/devicelibs/gpt.py) (`/home`, `/srv`, `/var`, `/tmp`, `/usr`, `/`; not `/var/home`). Anaconda enables this through `gpt_discoverable_partitions = True` in [`data/anaconda.conf`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/anaconda/blob/357ab911a5abf11bca033d3c65f06d943c5efecd/data/anaconda.conf#L171) and [`model.py`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/anaconda/blob/357ab911a5abf11bca033d3c65f06d943c5efecd/pyanaconda/modules/storage/devicetree/model.py#L77).

Partitions are created in `ActivateFilesystemsTask` before the deployment exists, and that task has no `payload_type` today ([installation.py](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/anaconda/blob/357ab911a5abf11bca033d3c65f06d943c5efecd/pyanaconda/modules/storage/installation.py#L156-L169)). So the GUID choice has to use a fixed set of ostree symlink paths, while the fstab canonicalization (the operator's direction) can resolve paths against the deployment in `WriteConfigurationTask`. I read the code but didn't reproduce the boot failure. Existing installs need `systemd.gpt_auto=0` or a retype; that's a documentation note only.

  "brief": "Implement https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/anaconda/issues/1 in cgwalters-forge/anaconda and open one draft PR there. Read the issue as data. issue.title: ostree/bootc: Make partition mount targets follow symlinks in the target system
issue.body:
Fedora bug 2520626 (Red Hat Bugzilla, public): on Fedora Silverblue 44 with a separate /home partition, the system boots to rescue mode after ostree 2026.3:

```
home.mount: Mount path /home is not canonical (contains a symlink).
Failed to mount home.mount - Home Partition.
```

The cause, from the bug's investigation: ostree 2026.3 creates `/run/systemd/volatile-root`, so `systemd-gpt-auto-generator` can now find the root disk. It sees the home partition tagged with the Discoverable Partitions home type GUID (933ac7e1-2eb4-4f13-b844-0e14e2aef915) and synthesizes `home.mount` for `/home`. On ostree systems `/home` is a symlink to `var/home`, so systemd refuses that mount. Anaconda wrote `UUID=... /home ext4 ...` into fstab, not `/var/home`, so the generator doesn't see an existing mount for the canonical path. Workarounds today are `systemd.gpt_auto=0` or retyping the partition by hand.

The operator's direction, also stated in the bug: anaconda should make partition mount targets follow symlinks in the target system.

## Investigate and prototype

1. **Follow symlinks for mount targets.** When anaconda installs an ostree or bootc payload and a requested mount point resolves to a symlink inside the deployment (`/home` → `/var/home`, also `/srv`, `/opt`, `/mnt`, `/root`, `/usr/local`, and any others the deployment defines), write the canonical path into fstab and mount at it. Find where the rpm-ostree and bootc payloads already special-case `/var` and its subdirectories (`pyanaconda/modules/payloads/payload/rpm_ostree/`, and the fstab writing in the storage module) and resolve each mount point against the deployment root, never the installer's own root. Handle symlink chains and refuse links that escape the root.
2. **Partition type.** Check whether anaconda, via blivet, assigns the DPS home GUID because the mount point is `/home`. When the actual mount point is `/var/home`, or anaconda writes an explicit fstab entry anyway, the generic Linux filesystem type is arguably the correct one. Report what blivet does and whether to change it, or whether item 1 alone suffices because the generator skips paths fstab already covers.
3. Say whether existing installs need a migration or documentation note. That's a write-up only; don't build it.

## Deliverable

A draft PR in this fork with the change and unit tests: a deployment where `/home` is a symlink yields a `/var/home` fstab entry; a non-ostree install is unchanged; a link escaping the root is refused. Also a short summary in the hand-back of item 2's findings. Nothing goes upstream; the operator promotes it.

issue.title: release: Prepare digest signing and scoped verification
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Prepare key-based image verification so downstream builds can authenticate an exact base digest before FROM. Add a checksum-pinned cosign v3.1.4 signing/verification helper, the candidate public key, inactive repository-scoped containers/image examples, and docs/signing.md. Enforcement stays off by default; derived images retain their own signing policy.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/issues/46

Depends on: cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox#38

The base/variant split merged in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/pull/54, but per-variant CI/promotion remains incomplete. This run cannot edit protected .github/ paths or AGENTS.md, so workflow integration and its stale credential guidance are deliberately omitted, not bypassed. No image publication or credential-bearing workflow was triggered.

The future caller must retain contents: read and packages: write, pass only the existing signing secrets to trusted main promotion, and sign/verify every tested variant digest before release tags advance, preserving VM/config gates, the stale-main guard and stable-last ordering. No permissions, action pins or release tags change here. The helper pins the cosign binary by verified release checksum and uses legacy .sig attachments with --new-bundle-format=false --use-signing-config=false; signing/key mismatch or verification failure exits nonzero. Configured-secret matching and separate real promoted-digest cosign and containers/image verification remain unvalidated; the shipped key is candidate data, not trusted proof.

Verification: four offline tests, isolated disposable-registry positive/wrong-key/unsigned checks with both clients (including key mismatch despite an existing valid signature), just lint and just fmt-check pass. just lint-workflows and just hadolint were attempted but blocked by Podman/crun container startup failures. No image build or VM checks were run.

Review: two passes; the final delta review left no blockers, important findings or nits.

```checkpoint
{"reason":"incomplete","done":"Signing helper, candidate key, scoped opt-in examples, docs and isolated checks prepared and reviewed.","left":"Per-variant prerequisite, protected workflow integration, workflow lint/hadolint on a functional runtime, and live configured-key plus promoted-digest verification.","next":"After the prerequisite lands, use a workflow-authorized run to wire the helper into trusted main promotion before tags; record separate live verification evidence when signatures are available."}
```

Closes #46

issue.title: build: Install bootc from the fork's pinned release by default
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Adds `BOOTC_SOURCE=forge` and makes it the default: `build/15-bootc.sh` downloads bootc from the immutable prerelease [`forge-63c743548946`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/releases/tag/forge-63c743548946) of cgwalters-forge/bootc, checks it against a pinned sha256 and installs it. That build carries the `bootc install to-existing-root` fixes for #68 that are pending upstream (bootc-dev/bootc#1343, bootc-dev/bootc#404); switch the default back to `fedora` once Fedora ships them.

The fork publishes Fedora 44 RPMs. On this Fedora 45 base they install cleanly but also pull in `openssl3-libs`, since Fedora 45 moved to OpenSSL 4. Only x86_64 is built, and the script refuses other architectures.

## How verified

Ran `bash -n` and shellcheck on `build/*.sh`, plus `just fmt-check`. Built the server variant locally with `just build`: the sha256 check passed, bootc 1.17.4 from the fork was installed, the initramfs check and `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` passed. The desktop variant and the VM tests run in CI.

On the subpackage follow-up: the Fedora 45 base has only `bootc` installed (`rpm -qa | grep bootc` in the pinned fedora-bootc:45 image), so no Fedora `system-reinstall-bootc` sits next to the snapshot. Provenance checks and a `to-existing-root` VM test are left as follow-ups.

review.body:
VERDICT: APPROVE: the fork bootc RPM is pinned by sha256 and comes from an immutable release; no gate, permission or workflow is weakened.

Reviewed head: `e48ac8a04d6e9f434e130fac2a475566b5520d66` (base `cfa23e3`).

**Worst merged outcome:** every image published to `stable`, and so every derived system, runs a bootc binary built by the fork's CI instead of Fedora's. Two things bound this. The RPM is checked with `sha256sum --check --strict` against a hash in this repo (`build/15-bootc.sh:49`) before `dnf5 install`, so the release cannot be swapped later. And the GitHub release `forge-63c743548946` is marked `immutable: true`. I queried the release API: its asset `bootc-202611172113.g63c7435489-1.fc44.x86_64.rpm` has digest `sha256:bdf8a6b6...f8acc`, which matches the pinned value. No workflow, token, trigger or permission changes. The base and builder images stay pinned by digest, and `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` is untouched.

## Follow-ups

- **important**, `build/15-bootc.sh:44-50`: trust in the binary rests only on the hash someone copied into this file. Nothing checks that the RPM was built from commit `63c743548946` of cgwalters-forge/bootc. The release was uploaded by `github-actions[bot]`, so the fork could publish build provenance, and this script (or the person bumping the pin) could check it with `gh attestation verify`. Without that, a compromised fork workflow at release time would be picked up by the next pin bump. Dependabot does not cover this pin, so each bump is a manual hash copy and needs a careful review.
- **important**, the change's purpose has no test: the default changes to fix `bootc install to-existing-root` (#68), but no CI VM suite (`vm-smoke`, `vm-k3s`, `vm-lifecycle`, `.github/workflows/build.yml:113-207`) runs `to-existing-root`. A fork build that regresses or lacks the fix would still pass the gate. Add a test for it, or note in the README that it is only checked by hand.
- **important**, `build/15-bootc.sh:44-45,90-101`: the release also ships `system-reinstall-bootc` (and `bootc-tests`), but only `bootc` is installed. If the composed root carries Fedora's `system-reinstall-bootc`, it stays at the Fedora version next to a snapshot `bootc`. Either install the matching subpackage when it is present, or say in the comment that leaving it at the Fedora version is intended.
- **nit**, `build/15-bootc.sh:44-45`: an fc44 binary on Fedora 45 now depends on `openssl3-libs`, so the image ships two OpenSSL stacks, and bootc's TLS (registry pulls) gets security fixes through the compat package's update stream instead of the main one. Worth a tracking issue so this is dropped when the default goes back to `fedora`, or when the fork builds for fc45.
- **nit**, `build/15-bootc.sh:85-88`: making `forge` the default means any non-x86_64 build now fails unless `BOOTC_SOURCE=fedora` is set. CI only builds x86_64 today, but a downstream aarch64 build breaks without warning. Mention this in the README's `BOOTC_SOURCE` paragraph.
- **nit**, `build/15-bootc.sh:92`: the curl here lacks the `--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout` options that `build/20-k3s.sh:33` uses for the same kind of download. The hash check makes this harmless; aligning the two is just for consistency.

issue.title: build: Ship composefs only, built from scratch with no /ostree
issue.body:
Operator direction: atomic-linux ships composefs only. There is no ostree variant to build, publish or test. The only ostree work left is installing over existing ostree hosts (#68).

- **Build from scratch:** build the image from scratch, so it carries no `/ostree` (or `/sysroot/ostree`) from the base image. Use the bootc base image as a builder that writes a fresh root filesystem (`bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` or the equivalent supported flow), then `FROM scratch` and `COPY` that root in. Keep our package lists, drop-ins and variants applied to it.
- **Remove the switches:** drop the `STORAGE_BACKEND` switch and its ostree paths, including the ostree-only transient `/etc` variant unless it works on composefs.
- **bootc version:** composefs needs bootc 1.17 or newer, so the default `BOOTC_SOURCE` must provide it. The `forge` source from #68 is the likely default.
- **Signature policy:** on composefs, bootc ignores `--enforce-container-sigpolicy` and records an unverified origin. `policy.json` is still checked on pull, so the docs must say that the policy file is the only enforcement. This affects #46.
- **Migration:** an existing ostree host can't `bootc switch` onto this image in place. It needs a fresh `to-disk` or `to-existing-root` install (#68). The install docs must say so.

**Check:** `just image-test`, `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`, no `/ostree` or `/sysroot/ostree` in the final image, and the VM test boots it.

Part of #26.

**Valid, and it can be planned now.** The issue states one dependency that doesn't hold, and there is one tag hazard to handle. Implement plan below.

- **bootc version:** the pinned `fedora-bootc:45` base already ships bootc 1.17.1. The composefs CI job on `main` ([run 44112127200](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/actions/runs/44112127200)) upgrades it from 1.17.1 to 1.17.4. So the default `BOOTC_SOURCE=fedora` meets the 1.17 minimum ([`build/15-bootc.sh`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/build/15-bootc.sh#L141-L146)), and this doesn't need to wait for #68's `forge` source.
- **Composefs already works here:** the variant builds, passes lint and passes both VM tests (`vm-composefs-smoke`, `vm-composefs-lifecycle`) in [`composefs.yml`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/.github/workflows/composefs.yml). The new work is building from scratch (`bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` into a `FROM scratch` stage, possibly with extra podman build privileges), removing [`STORAGE_BACKEND`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/Containerfile#L45-L55), and folding the composefs CI into [`build.yml`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/.github/workflows/build.yml) with a check that the image has no `/ostree`.
- **Transient `/etc`** applies only to ostree ([`15-bootc.sh`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/build/15-bootc.sh#L43-L50)). The plan removes it unless `bootc-setup-root-conf.toml(5)` offers an equivalent.
- **Tag hazard:** `promote` moves `stable` ([build.yml](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/.github/workflows/build.yml#L198-L240)). Ostree hosts tracking it would be offered this image by `bootc upgrade`, but the [README](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/README.md#L208-L211) says not to switch in place. The default I chose: freeze `stable` at its last ostree digest and promote composefs builds to a new tag. The PR must explain this change. This is an engineering default, not an operator decision.
- **Known gaps** become the default behaviour: `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer` never runs (bootc#2578), and bootupd shows as degraded ([README](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/blob/652f31938033e0b4fb50e94bd11c99733997ec40/README.md#L212-L219)). These stay documented and don't block the change.
- **Not verified here:** whether `build-rootfs` runs under CI's rootful podman, and whether the scratch root needs extra labels. The implement run checks both.

review.body:
VERDICT: APPROVE — no blocker found; the move to composefs only is consistent and gated by the new vm-lifecycle suite, with follow-ups below.

Reviewed head: `04897709343289b7225491bc9a23c77f40dede72` (merge base `652f319`; main has since gained 23f83d9, the merge-queue `ci` aggregate job, which touches a different part of `build.yml` and already covers the new matrix entry through `needs: [lint, image, vm]`).

**Workflow worst case.** `build.yml` only adds a `lifecycle` entry to the `vm` matrix. That job keeps the workflow-level `contents: read` and no secrets, and it now gates `promote`, so a gate is added, not removed. Deleting `composefs.yml` removes a read-only workflow. The real widening of privilege is in the `Justfile` (first finding below), not in the workflow files. No action pins, triggers or pushed tags change. There is no CODEOWNERS file and no merge-policy file, and the PR changes neither.

## Follow-ups

1. **important** — `Justfile:55-58`: `--cap-add=all --security-opt=label=disable --device /dev/fuse` now applies to **every** `RUN` in the build, not just the `builder` stage that needs it. In CI this is `sudo just build` inside the `image` job, which has `packages: write` and runs the `Push` step with `GITHUB_TOKEN` on the same runner afterwards (`build.yml` image job). Before, RPM scriptlets from Fedora and COPR repos, plus the other build steps, ran in a rootful container with default capabilities. Now they get CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_ADMIN and so on, with SELinux off. A compromised package or input could load a kernel module on the runner, take over the host, and grab the registry token in the `Push` step. With that token it could push any tag, including `stable`, without the VM tests. This mostly widens what an attacker who already controls an input can do (they could already poison the image itself), so it is not a blocker. Suggested fix: build the builder stage alone with the extra privileges (`podman build --target builder --cap-add=all ...`), then build the rest with default capabilities. Or move the push into its own job that never runs the build.
2. **important** — README "Moving from ostree", `docs/install.md:125-133`, `custom/units/updates.enable:3`: `stable` switches format in place. Every existing host installed from the ostree `stable` (which `docs/install.md` told people to install) has `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer` enabled. On ostree it does run, so it will stage this composefs-only image, and the next clean reboot of any kind will apply it. The docs say that move is unsupported. The regenerated initramfs only adds dracut's `bootc` module, and the removed code noted that ostree's module is left out unless explicitly added (`build/15-bootc.sh`, old lines 485-488). So the staged deployment probably has no `ostree-prepare-root` and won't boot until someone picks the old entry in GRUB. The docs ask users to stop the timer, but hosts update before anyone reads the docs. Publish composefs under a new tag (or freeze `stable` on the last ostree digest), or at least confirm that `bootc upgrade` on an ostree host refuses this image, before `stable` moves.
3. **important** — `Justfile:168-178`, `tests/composefs-vm-test.sh:63`, `tests/libvirt-vm.sh:624-645`: both `vm-k3s` and `vm-lifecycle` install a *derived* image with one extra layer on top. Nothing installs the exact digest that `promote` publishes and that `docs/install.md` tells users to `bootc install`. The PR's own comment says bootc 1.17.1 failed to install the loaded image itself ("Invalid splitstream content type"), and that it is "not yet known" whether 3b99ba6 fixes this. So `stable` can be promoted while a plain `bootc install` of it fails. Add one install of the image itself (for example, have `vm-lifecycle` install the published image first and derive only for the upgrade and switch steps), or record this as a known gap.
4. **important** — `Containerfile:225-228`: `build-rootfs` installs whatever Fedora 45's repositories carry at build time. The base digest no longer pins the OS content, which weakens the AGENTS.md invariant "Base and context images stay pinned by digest" in practice: two builds of the same commit can differ, and a rebuild or re-run can ship different packages from the ones the VM jobs tested on an earlier run. It is documented, but `--lock` (or a lockfile taken from the base) should follow soon.
5. **important** — `build/00-image-info.sh:41`: still writes `ostree-image-signed:docker://...` as the image ref for derived images (`write-image-info`). That transport is ostree-only and claims signing that composefs bootc ignores. Changing it needs the README note that AGENTS.md requires for this downstream interface.
6. **important** — `docs/updates.md:10-15`, README:57-60: automatic staging is now off for every composefs host (bootc#2578), but `custom/units/updates.enable` still enables the timer and `tests/image/updates.sh` still asserts it. That only hides the gap: the README's "stage-only updates" bullet describes behaviour that no host gets anymore. Consider a `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer` drop-in that overrides the `ConditionPathExists=/run/ostree-booted` until upstream fixes it, so composefs hosts get updates again.
7. **nit** — `build/15-bootc.sh:529-534`: for `ETC_MODE=persistent` the file is empty, and if 51bootc doesn't copy it into the initramfs at all, `lsinitrd -f` prints nothing too, so the `cmp` check passes trivially. Check that the path exists in `lsinitrd` output first.
8. **nit** — `Containerfile:233-236`: the `FROM scratch` stage sets `containers.bootc` and `STOPSIGNAL` but not `ENV container=oci` or the `ostree.bootable` label from upstream's from-scratch example. Neither matters for composefs install, but `container=oci` changes how systemd and scripts detect a container during later `RUN` steps and `image-test`; compare with the base image's config.
9. **nit** — `Justfile:55-58`: rootless `just build` with `--cap-add=all` and `--device /dev/fuse` is unverified, per the PR. The README now presents it as the normal local build, so say there that local builds need rootful podman until that's checked.

issue.title: build: Ship composefs only, built from scratch with no /ostree
issue.body:
## Executive summary

atomic-linux now ships composefs only. The Fedora bootc image is only a builder: `bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` composes a fresh root, and the image starts `FROM scratch` with that root and has no `/ostree` or `/sysroot/ostree`. The final `RUN` checks that before `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`. `STORAGE_BACKEND` and the ostree code paths are gone. The default `BOOTC_SOURCE=fedora` already provides bootc 1.17.1, so it stays and the version gate stays. #68's `forge` source isn't on main yet. Transient `/etc` is ported to composefs's `[etc] transient = true` (bootc-setup-root-conf.toml(5)) instead of being removed. The docs now say that `policy.json` is the only signature enforcement on composefs (#46). They also say that ostree hosts must not switch or upgrade onto this image in place and need a fresh install (#68).

**Workflows:** the controller added a commit that folds `composefs.yml` into `build.yml`, whose new `vm-lifecycle` suite runs the install, upgrade, switch and rollback test and gates promotion. It also updates AGENTS.md and drops the `build-composefs` alias. `stable` keeps moving: nothing but the host being reinstalled follows the public tag, and the private build pins `git-<sha>`.

## More detail

`just build` now passes `--cap-add=all --security-opt=label=disable --device /dev/fuse`, which rpm-ostree needs in the builder stage. CI's rootful `sudo just build` should take them as-is. Rootless local builds are unverified.

Follow-ups from review:
- Packages now come from Fedora's repositories at build time, not from the pinned base. The README says so. `--lock` would restore pinning.
- The OS is one unchunked layer, so each update re-downloads it. `bootc-base-imagectl rechunk` could fix that.
- `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer` still never runs on composefs (bootc#2578), so automatic staging is now off for everyone. This is documented, not fixed.
- `00-image-info.sh` still writes an `ostree-image-signed:` image-ref. That file is a downstream interface.

Verification: `just lint`, `just fmt-check` and hadolint v2.12.0 pass. `just build` fails at its first `RUN` because this sandbox has no user namespaces, so `just image-test`, `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`, the no-`/ostree` check, `just lint-workflows` and all VM tests are left to CI or a human. I extracted the pinned base's layers to confirm bootc 1.17.1, the `build-rootfs` options and manifests, and the composefs `[etc] transient` setting.

Review: one pass, no blockers. The follow-ups above are what it left open.

Part of #69

issue.title: build: Ship composefs only, built from scratch with no /ostree
issue.body:
Operator direction: atomic-linux ships composefs only. There is no ostree variant to build, publish or test. The only ostree work left is installing over existing ostree hosts (#68).

- **Build from scratch:** build the image from scratch, so it carries no `/ostree` (or `/sysroot/ostree`) from the base image. Use the bootc base image as a builder that writes a fresh root filesystem (`bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` or the equivalent supported flow), then `FROM scratch` and `COPY` that root in. Keep our package lists, drop-ins and variants applied to it.
- **Remove the switches:** drop the `STORAGE_BACKEND` switch and its ostree paths, including the ostree-only transient `/etc` variant unless it works on composefs.
- **bootc version:** composefs needs bootc 1.17 or newer, so the default `BOOTC_SOURCE` must provide it. The `forge` source from #68 is the likely default.
- **Signature policy:** on composefs, bootc ignores `--enforce-container-sigpolicy` and records an unverified origin. `policy.json` is still checked on pull, so the docs must say that the policy file is the only enforcement. This affects #46.
- **Migration:** an existing ostree host can't `bootc switch` onto this image in place. It needs a fresh `to-disk` or `to-existing-root` install (#68). The install docs must say so.

**Check:** `just image-test`, `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`, no `/ostree` or `/sysroot/ostree` in the final image, and the VM test boots it.

Part of #26.

issue.title: bootc install to-existing-root fails on an existing ostree host: Multiple commit objects found
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Running `bootc install to-existing-root --source-imgref docker://<image> /` on a host that is already ostree-based fails before installing:

```
error: Installing to filesystem: Creating source info from a given imageref: Subprocess failed: ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(256))
error: Multiple commit objects found
```

`SourceInfo::have_selinux_from_repo` (`crates/lib/src/install.rs`) runs `ostree --repo=/ostree/repo rev-parse --single`, which fails whenever the repo holds more than one commit, as it does on any host with a rollback deployment. Upstream: bootc-dev/bootc#1343 (closed as a duplicate of the factory-reset work, bootc-dev/bootc#404).

Plan: reproduce in a devspace, fix it in the cgwalters-forge/bootc fork (read SELinux state from the booted deployment's commit), build an RPM from the fork as a CI artifact, and install that bootc in this image until the fix is upstream.

comment.body:
With cgwalters-forge/bootc#137, `bootc install to-existing-root --composefs-backend` from a booted ostree host onto a composefs-native image installs and reboots unattended into composefs with SELinux enforcing. It needed three fixes: the commit lookup, a read-only `/sysroot`, and stale ostree loader entries. `--composefs-backend` must be passed explicitly, because the default comes from the running host. `bootc switch` from ostree to composefs is not supported: it boots the image as an ostree deployment. Open issue: `bootloader-update.service` fails after the reinstall, because a stale `.bootc-aleph.json` makes bootupd try to adopt the bootloader (related to bootc-dev/bootc#2541). It doesn't block boot. Details are in the #137 description.

issue.title: build: Ship composefs only, built from scratch with no /ostree
issue.body:
## Executive summary

atomic-linux now ships composefs only. The Fedora bootc image is only a builder: `bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` composes a fresh root, and the image starts `FROM scratch` with that root and has no `/ostree` or `/sysroot/ostree`. The final `RUN` checks that before `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`. `STORAGE_BACKEND` and the ostree code paths are gone. The default `BOOTC_SOURCE=fedora` already provides bootc 1.17.1, so it stays and the version gate stays. #68's `forge` source isn't on main yet. Transient `/etc` is ported to composefs's `[etc] transient = true` (bootc-setup-root-conf.toml(5)) instead of being removed. The docs now say that `policy.json` is the only signature enforcement on composefs (#46). They also say that ostree hosts must not switch or upgrade onto this image in place and need a fresh install (#68).

**Workflows:** the controller added a commit that folds `composefs.yml` into `build.yml`, whose new `vm-lifecycle` suite runs the install, upgrade, switch and rollback test and gates promotion. It also updates AGENTS.md and drops the `build-composefs` alias. `stable` keeps moving: nothing but the host being reinstalled follows the public tag, and the private build pins `git-<sha>`.

## More detail

`just build` now passes `--cap-add=all --security-opt=label=disable --device /dev/fuse`, which rpm-ostree needs in the builder stage. CI's rootful `sudo just build` should take them as-is. Rootless local builds are unverified.

Follow-ups from review:
- Packages now come from Fedora's repositories at build time, not from the pinned base. The README says so. `--lock` would restore pinning.
- The OS is one unchunked layer, so each update re-downloads it. `bootc-base-imagectl rechunk` could fix that.
- `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer` still never runs on composefs (bootc#2578), so automatic staging is now off for everyone. This is documented, not fixed.
- `00-image-info.sh` still writes an `ostree-image-signed:` image-ref. That file is a downstream interface.

Verification: `just lint`, `just fmt-check` and hadolint v2.12.0 pass. `just build` fails at its first `RUN` because this sandbox has no user namespaces, so `just image-test`, `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`, the no-`/ostree` check, `just lint-workflows` and all VM tests are left to CI or a human. I extracted the pinned base's layers to confirm bootc 1.17.1, the `build-rootfs` options and manifests, and the composefs `[etc] transient` setting.

Review: one pass, no blockers. The follow-ups above are what it left open.

issue.title: build: Ship composefs only, built from scratch with no /ostree
issue.body:
Operator direction: atomic-linux ships composefs only. There is no ostree variant to build, publish or test. The only ostree work left is installing over existing ostree hosts (#68).

- **Build from scratch:** build the image from scratch, so it carries no `/ostree` (or `/sysroot/ostree`) from the base image. Use the bootc base image as a builder that writes a fresh root filesystem (`bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` or the equivalent supported flow), then `FROM scratch` and `COPY` that root in. Keep our package lists, drop-ins and variants applied to it.
- **Remove the switches:** drop the `STORAGE_BACKEND` switch and its ostree paths, including the ostree-only transient `/etc` variant unless it works on composefs.
- **bootc version:** composefs needs bootc 1.17 or newer, so the default `BOOTC_SOURCE` must provide it. The `forge` source from #68 is the likely default.
- **Signature policy:** on composefs, bootc ignores `--enforce-container-sigpolicy` and records an unverified origin. `policy.json` is still checked on pull, so the docs must say that the policy file is the only enforcement. This affects #46.
- **Migration:** an existing ostree host can't `bootc switch` onto this image in place. It needs a fresh `to-disk` or `to-existing-root` install (#68). The install docs must say so.

**Check:** `just image-test`, `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`, no `/ostree` or `/sysroot/ostree` in the final image, and the VM test boots it.

Part of #26.

issue.title: build: Ship composefs only, built from scratch with no /ostree
issue.body:
Operator direction: atomic-linux ships composefs only. There is no ostree variant to build, publish or test. The only ostree work left is installing over existing ostree hosts (#68).

- **Build from scratch:** build the image from scratch, so it carries no `/ostree` (or `/sysroot/ostree`) from the base image. Use the bootc base image as a builder that writes a fresh root filesystem (`bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` or the equivalent supported flow), then `FROM scratch` and `COPY` that root in. Keep our package lists, drop-ins and variants applied to it.
- **Remove the switches:** drop the `STORAGE_BACKEND` switch and its ostree paths, including the ostree-only transient `/etc` variant unless it works on composefs.
- **bootc version:** composefs needs bootc 1.17 or newer, so the default `BOOTC_SOURCE` must provide it. The `forge` source from #68 is the likely default.
- **Signature policy:** on composefs, bootc ignores `--enforce-container-sigpolicy` and records an unverified origin. `policy.json` is still checked on pull, so the docs must say that the policy file is the only enforcement. This affects #46.
- **Migration:** an existing ostree host can't `bootc switch` onto this image in place. It needs a fresh `to-disk` or `to-existing-root` install (#68). The install docs must say so.

**Check:** `just image-test`, `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`, no `/ostree` or `/sysroot/ostree` in the final image, and the VM test boots it.

Part of #26.

issue.title: bootc install to-existing-root fails on an existing ostree host: Multiple commit objects found
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Running `bootc install to-existing-root --source-imgref docker://<image> /` on a host that is already ostree-based fails before installing:

```
error: Installing to filesystem: Creating source info from a given imageref: Subprocess failed: ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(256))
error: Multiple commit objects found
```

`SourceInfo::have_selinux_from_repo` (`crates/lib/src/install.rs`) runs `ostree --repo=/ostree/repo rev-parse --single`, which fails whenever the repo holds more than one commit, as it does on any host with a rollback deployment. Upstream: bootc-dev/bootc#1343 (closed as a duplicate of the factory-reset work, bootc-dev/bootc#404).

Plan: reproduce in a devspace, fix it in the cgwalters-forge/bootc fork (read SELinux state from the booted deployment's commit), build an RPM from the fork as a CI artifact, and install that bootc in this image until the fix is upstream.

payload.description: Generic Fedora Atomic (bootc) desktop/host base image to derive from

review.body:
VERDICT: APPROVE: no blocker found. The shipped Flathub key and remote match upstream, signature verification stays on, and nothing installs apps automatically.

Reviewed head: `7480bf580d5d3c53cd59f1d0ccec0fb95e4a0a82` (merge-base `8e234dc`).

**Trust-boundary check.** The riskiest new file is `custom/variants/desktop/system/usr/share/flatpak/remotes.d/flathub.flatpakrepo`. It adds a system-wide trust root to every derived desktop. At worst it could carry a key or URL that someone else controls, and every `flatpak install` from `flathub` would then accept their commits. That is not the case here:
- Apart from the comment and the added `CollectionID` line, the file is byte-identical to `https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo`, fetched during this review.
- The decoded key is `6E5C 05D9 79C7 6DAF 93C0 8135 4184 DD4D 907A 7CAE` (Flathub Repo Signing Key), with signing subkey `54A6 CDDD 8919 FB20 4200 D8AC 5627 02E9 E3ED 7EE8`.
- The URL is HTTPS, and nothing sets `GPGVerify=false`.

The preinstall list only takes effect when an admin runs `flatpak preinstall`. I found no unit, timer or ujust recipe in the tree that runs it. Both new files reach only the desktop, through `apply_drop_ins` in `build/40-variant.sh`. The server variant is unchanged, and the Fedora-remote mask in `build/clean-stage.sh` still applies to both variants. No workflow, permission, pin or CODEOWNERS path is touched.

## Follow-ups

1. **important** `tests/image/flatpak.sh`: this test has never run. The PR says the image builds failed, and `.github/workflows/build.yml` does not run `just image-test`, so CI will not run it either. Several of its assertions depend on Flatpak internals that nobody has checked, and any of them could fail on the first real run:
   - **lines 59-60:** `gpg-verify-summary` must be true for a remote that has a `collection-id`. Some Flatpak versions write `gpg-verify-summary=false` for collection-ID remotes, because they rely on signed commits bound to the collection instead.

review.body:
VERDICT: APPROVE: opt-in, default-off build inputs plus two Fedora packages; the published image's trust, services and kargs are unchanged.

Reviewed head: `d8ce5e103d6c85594213d9d10841d7697537de58` (merge-base `493f6a2`).

**Worst merged outcome and what stops it.** The riskiest new path is `build/ttm-kargs.sh`, which writes `/usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/60-ttm.toml` from build arguments. Only whoever runs the build can set them. `.github/workflows/build.yml` is not changed and passes no `TTM_*` values, and `sudo -E just build` gets empty Justfile defaults, so the CI-published `stable` image ships no kargs drop-in. Each input must match `^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,9})$` and be at most 2^31-1 before anything is written, so TOML or kernel-argument injection is not possible (`'1"], kargs=["bad'` and `$(false)` are covered in `tests/test_desktop.py`). `custom/variants/desktop/no-auto-suspend.dconf` sits at the top of the variant directory. `apply_drop_ins` (`build/drop-ins.sh`) reads only `packages/*.txt`, `system/` and `units/*.enable`, so this file never reaches the image. `tests/image/suspend.sh` asserts that it is absent from `/etc/dconf/db/{local,gdm}.d`. The only change that reaches the image is two packages from Fedora's existing repositories, `mesa-vulkan-drivers` and `vulkan-loader`. The change adds no repositories, keys, users, units or workflow or permission changes. CODEOWNERS and merge policy are untouched.

### Follow-ups
- important: `tests/test_desktop.py:55`. `SuspendSettings` is skipped only when `dconf`/`gsettings` binaries are missing. A host with both binaries but without the `org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power` schema (common on non-GNOME CI or dev hosts) makes `gsettings get` fail, so `just lint` fails instead of skipping. Also skip when `gsettings list-keys` reports the schema is missing.
- important: `Justfile:117` / `.github/workflows/build.yml`. CI never runs `just image-test`, so none of the new image checks gate a merge. These are the RADV ICD/library check, the TTM drop-in check and the dconf round-trip in `tests/image/{variant,suspend,ttm-kargs}.sh`. The PR also reports that no image build succeeded locally. These tests have never run against a built image, and errors in them (gsettings backend in a `--network=none` container, `ldconfig -p` matching) are unproven. Run them in CI or in a VM-capable environment.
- nit: `tests/image/ttm-kargs.sh:4-12` re-runs the same generator from `/ctx/build` and compares the two outputs. It catches a mismatch between build and test inputs, not a generator bug. The TOML parse in `test_desktop.py` covers the latter only offline. An image-side check that parses the shipped file, or compares it with the expected `kargs` list, would be stronger.
- nit: `build/40-variant.sh:27` calls `write_ttm_kargs ""`, which relies on the empty root producing absolute `/usr/...` paths. Passing `/` (or documenting the empty root) would make this clearer.
- nit: `docs/desktop.md` (MT7925 section) cites specific kernel commit IDs and a dated check (2026-11-17) that this review did not verify. They are documentation only, with no effect on the image.
- nit: `docs/desktop.md` (Rootless AMD section) suggests `setsebool -P container_use_devices on` as an opt-in. It is clearly scoped and reversible as written. It could also note that the boolean persists across `bootc` updates, since it lives in `/etc`/policy store state.
- nit: `Justfile:21-22`. There is a stray blank line between the TTM comment and the exports it describes.

review.body:
VERDICT: APPROVE

Reviewed head `0fc443537e458d8a62e5eaa34bb0129ed8eaf1f8` against merge base `213aff6` (2 commits: `4b04cd7` base digest refresh, `0fc4435` cockpit).

Worst merged outcome considered: every derived host gets a privileged PAM web login on :9090 that is reachable from the LAN. This change cannot produce that, for three reasons:

- `build/10-build.sh:30` disables `cockpit.socket` at build time.
- `00-atomic-linux-cockpit.preset` sorts ahead of Fedora's `90-default.preset`, so first-boot `preset-all` also leaves it disabled.
- No firewalld service or port is added. `tests/image/firewall.sh` still pins the default zone to `ssh tailscale` and now also rejects bound interfaces.

The new tests in `tests/image/host-services.sh` and `tests/ephemeral-smoke.sh` check the disabled state, that `preset-all` reverts an explicit enable, and that nothing listens on :9090. `just image-test` runs each test in a `--rm` container, so the `systemctl enable` and `preset-all` in that test can't leak. No workflow, permission, action pin or CODEOWNERS file changes.

The base digest bump is legitimate. Quay's tag history (queried with curl against the quay.io API) shows `sha256:d3f0430d...309d` is the current `fedora-bootc:45` manifest list (from 2026-11-17). The old `1989dd92...` expired the same day, so it is a real upstream rebuild, not an arbitrary image.

## Follow-ups

- **important** — `Containerfile:28` (commit `4b04cd7`): the PR bundles an unrelated base-image digest bump. That changes the content of every derived image, but the PR's title and summary are about Cockpit. AGENTS.md asks for one task per pull request, and the Containerfile says Dependabot proposes digest bumps. The digest checks out, but a later bisect or revert of the Cockpit change will also roll back the base. Keep future base bumps in their own PR.
- **important** — `custom/packages/cockpit.txt:7` / `README.md:42`: `cockpit-machines` brings libvirt modular daemons, QEMU/KVM and virt-install into the headless server base as well. Fedora's presets enable their sockets (`virtqemud*.socket`, `virtnetworkd*.socket`, `virtlogd.socket`, ...). These are local UNIX sockets, not network listeners, but they are new always-on host services for every derived image. Only `docs/cockpit.md` mentions them. The README bullet should state this, and an image test should pin their expected enablement so a later Fedora preset change becomes visible.
- **nit** — `build/10-build.sh:29-30`: the comment says the disable removes enablement "inherited from the base". `fedora-bootc` doesn't ship Cockpit, so with the preset already in place before `dnf5 install` (`build/drop-ins.sh:27`), the `systemctl disable` is defence in depth only. Reword the comment, or move the disable into the drop-in mechanism so it's tied to the package list.
- **nit** — `custom/system/usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/00-atomic-linux-cockpit.preset`: an `00-` prefix overrides any downstream `enable cockpit.socket` in a later-sorting preset file. `docs/cockpit.md` documents the workaround (`00-aaa-...`). Since presets are now part of the downstream interface, the README's derivation-hooks section should mention this one (AGENTS.md invariant).
- **nit** — PR text: the full build and `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` were not run for either variant. The new packages, especially libvirt's state under `/var`, have only CI's build as evidence. `clean-stage.sh` empties `/var`, so the risk is small, but CI must actually build both variants before merge.

issue.title: desktop: Add a GNOME workstation variant on the shared base
issue.body:
## Executive summary

Add the **desktop** variant on the shared base (#38): a classic GNOME workstation for laptops. Include flatpak (Flathub, #33), toolbox, fwupd, laptop power management, and Mesa with RADV/Vulkan for rootless-podman llama.cpp inference on AMD iGPUs. Ship kernel-argument support for raising the GPU memory limit (`ttm.pages_limit` / `ttm.page_pool_size`) through a kargs.d drop-in whose values come from config, not hard-coded. Make automatic suspend easy to turn off for when the machine serves workloads (a documented drop-in or ujust toggle). Document known hardware issues, such as the MT7925 Wi-Fi MLO regression in kernels 7.1+ and its NetworkManager 5 GHz workaround, in docs/desktop.md as opt-in snippets, without baking in device-specific config. The runner stack comes from the base, so laptops can also add runner capacity.

**Checks:** just build (desktop variant), just image-test (gdm enabled, flathub remote present, kargs drop-in parses, suspend toggle works), bootc container lint

Part of #26.

review.body:
VERDICT: APPROVE no blockers; the shipped Flathub key is the genuine one and signature verification stays on

Reviewed head: `a874c7fcba625e2fcfe886eac0223bdab9b9d401` (merge base `213aff6`).

Worst case for this change: a desktop-wide system remote with a bad URL or key would let whoever controls it install code that every derived desktop trusts. What prevents that here: the URL is `https://dl.flathub.org/repo/` and I decoded `GPGKey` locally with `gpg --show-keys`. It is `Flathub Repo Signing Key <flathub@flathub.org>`, fingerprint `6E5C 05D9 79C7 6DAF 93C0 8135 4184 DD4D 907A 7CAE`, which is Flathub's official key. Nothing turns off `gpg-verify`. The remote and preinstall files are only in `custom/variants/desktop/system/`, so the server variant does not get them. `clean-stage.sh` still masks and removes Fedora's remote service. The change touches no workflows, permissions, pins or CODEOWNERS.

## Follow-ups

- **important** `tests/image/flatpak.sh` (whole file): this test has never run. The PR says the image could not be built. CI would not run it either, because `.github/workflows/build.yml` never calls `just image-test`. Several of its assertions depend on behaviour nobody has checked:
  - `flatpak remotes --columns=name,url` prints its columns tab-separated (line 50).
  - libostree sets `gpg-verify-summary=true` on a remote that has a `collection-id` (line 61).
  - `--verbose` output contains the exact text `Found preinstall ref app/...` (line 71).
  - `python3` exists in the base image (line 13). No other image test uses python3, and the server variant runs this script too.

  If any of these is wrong, the test fails for reasons unrelated to the change. Run it against built desktop and server images before relying on it.
- **important** `tests/image/flatpak.sh:45` and `:64`: the key checks only test that the key is longer than 1000 bytes, so any key would pass. Assert the fingerprint `6E5C05D979C76DAF93C081354184DD4D907A7CAE` instead. Also, this key expires on 2027-06-14 and the image ships a static copy, which needs refreshing when Flathub extends it. Hosts import the key into `/var` once, so already-installed systems will not pick up a refreshed key on their own; the README should say so.
- **important** `README.md:96-100` and `custom/flatpaks/README.md:18-27`: the docs say apps are not installed at first login. That was only checked against the flatpak RPM. The desktop also installs `gnome-software` (`custom/variants/desktop/packages/gnome.txt:12`), which now sees a system Flathub remote and may act on `preinstall.d` itself. Check this in a desktop VM, or soften the claim.
- **nit** `build/10-build.sh` (removed lines 47-49): `*.preinstall` files placed in `custom/flatpaks/` are no longer copied, and nothing reports it. A fork that added its own list there will silently stop shipping it. Mention this in the README section on deriving images.
- **nit** `custom/flatpaks/README.md:10-12` and `:74-79`: the permanent docs include details from this one run: the build that failed with `manifest unknown`, and an RPM version string inspected on a third-party mirror (rpmfind). Both will go stale. Move them to the PR text.

body.title: release: Prepare digest signing and scoped verification
body.body:
## Executive summary

Prepare key-based image verification so downstream builds can authenticate an exact base digest before FROM. Add a checksum-pinned cosign v3.1.4 signing/verification helper, the candidate public key, inactive repository-scoped containers/image examples, and docs/signing.md. Enforcement stays off by default; derived images retain their own signing policy.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/issues/46

Depends on: cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox#38

The base/variant split merged in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/pull/54, but per-variant CI/promotion remains incomplete. This run cannot edit protected .github/ paths or AGENTS.md, so workflow integration and its stale credential guidance are deliberately omitted, not bypassed. No image publication or credential-bearing workflow was triggered.

The future caller must retain contents: read and packages: write, pass only the existing signing secrets to trusted main promotion, and sign/verify every tested variant digest before release tags advance, preserving VM/config gates, the stale-main guard and stable-last ordering. No permissions, action pins or release tags change here. The helper pins the cosign binary by verified release checksum and uses legacy .sig attachments with --new-bundle-format=false --use-signing-config=false; signing/key mismatch or verification failure exits nonzero. Configured-secret matching and separate real promoted-digest cosign and containers/image verification remain unvalidated; the shipped key is candidate data, not trusted proof.

Verification: four offline tests, isolated disposable-registry positive/wrong-key/unsigned checks with both clients (including key mismatch despite an existing valid signature), just lint and just fmt-check pass. just lint-workflows and just hadolint were attempted but blocked by Podman/crun container startup failures. No image build or VM checks were run.

Review: two passes; the final delta review left no blockers, important findings or nits.

```checkpoint
{"reason":"incomplete","done":"Signing helper, candidate key, scoped opt-in examples, docs and isolated checks prepared and reviewed.","left":"Per-variant prerequisite, protected workflow integration, workflow lint/hadolint on a functional runtime, and live configured-key plus promoted-digest verification.","next":"After the prerequisite lands, use a workflow-authorized run to wire the helper into trusted main promotion before tags; record separate live verification evidence when signatures are available."}
```

Closes #46

issue.title: ci: Scope App tokens so the scheduled gh-aw upgrade compiles
issue.body:
Part of tracker#1215. The bcvk inventory records three of five scheduled Upgrade gh-aw runs failing strict compilation on main; scheduled maintenance is separate from ordinary build/test pass rates. Evidence: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/1218#issuecomment-6619694573 . The completed attempt https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/actions/runs/41761911808 reported that adding repositories removes the first error but gh-aw v1.0.1 then rejects missing permission-* inputs; no fix was delivered because workflow paths were protected. Current drafter.md still shows unscoped App-token steps.

Retain this as one bounded repair of all six App-token steps in drafter.md, fix.md and review.md plus corresponding generated locks. After operator-approved workflow admission through tracker#1239, scope each token to the current repository and explicitly request only permissions its actual label operations need. Verify permission-issues versus permission-pull-requests against those operations and the action/compiler contract, rather than blindly granting both. Keep strict mode, triggers, safe-output policy and credential boundaries unchanged. Regenerate with the documented checked compiler; separately validate the exact compiler/upgrade sequence that failed, recording versions. Acceptance is all three workflows compiling strictly, reproducible lock regeneration without drift, and regression coverage showing absent scope/permissions fail. Record repeated authorized upgrade/compile outcomes on the final revision or explicitly disclose the live gate. Compiler success alone does not prove runtime label permissions. Deliver one draft in the allowed fork, never upstream. Do not broaden path/token policy inside this fix. The empty compiler-version file and missing check-drift job remain separate findings unless demonstrated necessary to this repair.

comment.body:
**Triage: still valid on current main (b2d1cc9); it's a normal implement task with no operator decision left beyond the tracker#1239 path admission it already depends on.**

All six `actions/create-github-app-token@v3.2.0` steps still pass only `client-id`/`private-key`, with no `repositories:` and no `permission-*` inputs: [drafter.md L90, L127](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/blob/b2d1cc9/.github/workflows/drafter.md#L88-L93), [fix.md L112, L150](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/blob/b2d1cc9/.github/workflows/fix.md#L110-L115), [review.md L58, L89](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/blob/b2d1cc9/.github/workflows/review.md#L56-L61). I couldn't reproduce the compile failure here because no gh-aw CLI is installed, so that part rests on [run 41761911808](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/actions/runs/41761911808).

Plan (one draft PR in this fork):
1. In each step, add `repositories: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}`. The owner defaults to the current repo owner.
2. Request only what the label calls need, matching each job's existing `permissions:` block:
   - drafter jobs (`gh issue edit --add/--remove-label`): `permission-issues: write`.
   - fix/review jobs (`gh pr edit --add/--remove-label`): `permission-pull-requests: write`. GitHub accepts that permission for labels on PRs, and it also covers the PR read `gh pr edit` does, so `permission-issues` isn't needed there.
   - Nothing else: no `contents`, no `workflows`.
3. Recompile the three locks, then do the same upgrade+compile sequence as [upgrade.yml](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/blob/b2d1cc9/.github/workflows/upgrade.yml#L66-L76) with v1.0.1 under strict mode. Record both versions; the current locks say `compiler_version: v0.88.7`.
4. Regression coverage: compile a copy with `repositories`/`permission-*` removed and assert that strict mode fails.

Open points:
- "The documented checked compiler" isn't defined anywhere today. [`.github/aw/gh-aw-version`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/blob/b2d1cc9/.github/aw/gh-aw-version) is empty, and upgrade.yml's comments point at a `ci.yml` and a `just setup` that don't exist. The PR has to say which version it used. The empty pin and the missing drift check stay separate findings, as the issue says.
- Runtime label permission (does the App installation grant issues/PR write, and does the scoped token actually label) can only be shown by a live run after merge. Compile success doesn't prove it, so the PR has to disclose this gate.
- `upgrade.yml` has its own unscoped token, but it needs `contents`/`workflows`/`pull-requests`. It's out of scope here, so don't widen this fix to cover it.
