issue.title: ephemeral: Give /var its own tmpfs, add --var-size

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
The ephemeral VM's `/var` was a directory on the initramfs `/run` tmpfs, which systemd caps at 20% of RAM. With the default 4G of memory that's ~780MiB, and there was no knob to raise it short of adding lots of memory, so e.g. a quadlet pulling a 2+GiB image at boot runs out of space. It also meant filling `/var` filled `/run`.

This mounts a dedicated tmpfs for `/var`, defaulting to 50% of guest RAM (the kernel's tmpfs default), and adds `--var-size` to `ephemeral run`/`run-ssh` (a size like `10G` or a percentage of guest RAM like `75%`). Together with `--add-swap` it allows a `/var` bigger than guest RAM. The size is passed to the initramfs unit as a drop-in in the CPIO that bcvk already appends, and the value is checked on the host so it can't inject other mount options or unit syntax. One behavior change to note: overfilling a `/var` that is larger than the memory available to back it now ends in the guest running out of memory rather than ENOSPC; the docs say so and suggest `--memory`/`--add-swap`.

A separate prep commit makes `parse_size` reject sizes that overflow `u64` (e.g. `17179869184G` used to wrap to 0), which also affects `--add-swap`.

The option is CLI-only for now; the varlink `Run` call keeps the default size.

## Is a tunable tmpfs the right first step?

In the issue, @cgwalters suggested making `/var` a bind mount of a directory inside the podman container, so its contents land in the host's container storage (the container's overlay upper). That removes the RAM limit completely, at the cost of a guest→host round trip for every write to `/var`.

I didn't do that here because of podman inside the guest. I checked on a devspace: with a host directory shared over bcvk's current virtiofsd setup (`--bind`, no `--xattr`), rootful podman in a centos-bootc:stream10 guest using that directory as its storage root fails with `'overlay' is not supported over <unknown> ... backing file system is unsupported for this graph driver`, and setting a `trusted.*` xattr there fails with `Operation not supported`. So with today's virtiofsd options, a virtiofs `/var` would break container storage in the guest. I didn't test whether enabling xattrs in virtiofsd would make overlay storage work, or whether podman would then be usable but slow.

A middle option would be a sparse file on the host attached as a virtio-blk scratch disk and formatted for `/var` in the initramfs, reusing the plumbing `--add-swap` already has. That gives a real block filesystem (overlay works, no RAM limit) at the cost of an mkfs at boot and needing mkfs tools in the initramfs.

Is a tunable tmpfs OK as the first step, with one of those as a follow-up if needed?

The second problem in the issue, `bcvk libvirt run --filesystem ext4` failing with `rm: cannot remove '/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay': Device or resource busy`, has the same cause as #351: the to-disk install VM booted the image's `default.target`, so the quadlet started and held files open under `/var/lib/containers`. e2be03d ("to-disk: Switch to a minimal boot target for to-disk installation") already fixed that on main.

Part of #200

## Testing

Run on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace with KVM, using `quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10` and `df -h /var /run` inside `bcvk ephemeral run --execute`:

| | `/var` size |
|---|---|
| main, default 4G memory | 782M (the same tmpfs as `/run`) |
| this PR, default | 2.0G (`/run` still 782M) |
| `--var-size 3G` | 3.0G |
| `--var-size 75%` | 2.9G |
| `--memory 8G --add-swap 10G --var-size 10G` | 10G |

With the last configuration, `podman pull quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:43` (1.96 GB) inside the guest succeeds, using 2.0G of `/var`. `--var-size 10G,exec` and `--var-size 99999999999T` are rejected when the arguments are parsed, and `--add-swap 17179869184G` now fails with "Size too large".

- `make validate` (fmt, clippy, rustdoc with `-D warnings`) and `cargo test -p bcvk` (85 tests, including the new `test_parse_size`, `test_parse_var_size` and `test_cpio_var_size_dropin`) pass.
- Integration tests with `cargo test --release -p integration-tests`: all 11 `to_disk` tests pass, including `test_to_disk_quadlet`. `test_run_ephemeral_mount_layout` now also checks that `/var` comes from the separate `bcvk-var` tmpfs, and it passes, as does the new `test_run_ephemeral_var_size`. Of the 33 `ephemeral` tests, 31 pass. The other two, `test_varlink_ephemeral_run_ps_and_ssh` and `test_run_ephemeral_journal_output`, time out waiting 120s for boot when the whole set runs in parallel. That reproduces identically on main, and both pass when run alone. `just test-integration` itself couldn't run because `go-md2man` isn't available on RHEL 10, so the same steps were run by hand.
- The man pages were regenerated with `cargo xtask sync-manpages`.

issue.title: to-disk: Save guest dmesg and virtiofsd logs when the install fails

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
When `bootc install` fails in the to-disk VM, the guest kernel log and the virtiofsd logs are removed along with the container, and those are exactly what would explain flakes like the ESTALE errors from the host storage share in #157.

Now, before removing the container, bcvk saves the guest `dmesg` (fetched over SSH with a 30s timeout, since the guest may be wedged) and both virtiofsd logs to a file in the temporary directory, and prints one line with its path:

```
Logs from the failed install VM were saved to /tmp/bcvk-to-disk-failure-xGBUm7.log
```

If none of the three can be read (e.g. the VM never came up), no file is written and the reasons are logged at debug level. The tails of the logs (200 lines each) go to stderr only with `--debug`, debug logging, or `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS` set, since most failures (a broken image, a bad install option) are plain user errors that a wall of kernel log wouldn't help with. If the file can't be written, the tails are printed instead. This is documented in `docs/src/testing.md`. Base-disk creation for `libvirt run` goes through the same code, so it's covered too. For the varlink `to-disk` call, the path line goes to the server's stderr.

The integration test harness sets `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS`. For the logs to actually reach the test output, the to-disk integration tests now run bcvk through a small helper that includes its stdout and stderr in the error when it fails, since xshell's `.output()?` drops captured stderr on a non-zero exit.

To support the dmesg timeout, `ssh::connect_captured` gained a `timeout` argument; it had no callers before.

The companion nextest change that serializes the `test_to_base_disk_*` tests is a separate PR.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace with KVM:

- `make validate` and `cargo test` pass (84 + 22 unit tests, including table-driven tests for the log formatting).
- A deliberately failing integration test (a scratch test, not included here, running `to-disk --disk-size 2G` through the new helper under `cargo nextest run -P integration`) failed with bcvk's stderr in the test output: the `bootc install` out-of-space error, the path line, the dmesg tail (last 200 of 647 lines) and both virtiofsd logs. The junit report has them too.
- Forced failures by hand (the same 2G disk):
  - `bcvk to-disk`: prints the install error and the one-line path, and the 668-line file holds the full logs.
  - With `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS=1`, and with `--debug`: the three tails are printed as well.
  - `bcvk libvirt run --root-size 2G`: the base-disk failure also prints the path line.
  - The plain, env var and `libvirt run` cases were checked on the previous revision; that code is unchanged, and `--debug` was checked on this one.
- `test_to_disk` passes under the integration profile.

Not tested: the case where all three logs are unavailable.

CI note (2026-09-24): the [`integration-tests (2)` failure](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/actions/runs/35955666987/job/107510910165) is unrelated to this change: `test_run_tmpfs` failed with exit 255 from `ephemeral run-ssh` (ssh itself failing), a path this PR doesn't touch, matching the `ConnectTimeout` banner-exchange flake targeted by cgwalters-forge/bcvk#8. All to-disk tests in that partition passed. Reran the failed jobs once.

Related: #157

issue.title: ci: Retry test image pulls and prefetch Fedora CoreOS

labels.name: review:quick
labels.description: High-confidence bot draft: skim and approve

issue.body:
CI keeps failing on transient quay.io errors that have nothing to do with the change under test. `just pull-test-images` is a single `podman pull` with only podman's built-in retries (3 quick retries a few seconds apart), which isn't enough to ride out an unexpected EOF from quay's CDN mid-blob ([example](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/35025230255)). The Ignition tests also pull `quay.io/fedora/fedora-coreos:stable` in the middle of the test run, so a 502/504 or dropped connection there fails a test directly ([1](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34819196417), [2](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34878492147), [3](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34780568246)).

This wraps each pull in `pull-test-images` in a retry loop with exponential backoff (5 attempts, 15s doubling, about 4 minutes of total delay) and adds the FCOS image to the prefetched set. The image name now lives only in the Justfile and reaches the tests as `BCVK_FCOS_IMAGE`, like the other test images, instead of three copies kept in sync by a comment. The tests that pull an image already in that set (the Ignition tests, the varlink images tests, and the to-disk imgref test) now only pull it when `podman image exists` says it is missing, so in CI they reuse the prefetched copy, while still working when run standalone. (`podman pull --policy missing` would say this directly, but podman 4 on the Ubuntu 24.04 runners doesn't have it.)

Note that FCOS is now pulled by the build job and each of the 4 integration partitions (5 pulls per CI run), rather than only by the partitions that happen to run an Ignition test.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace with KVM:

- `make validate` and `cargo test` pass (82 + 22 unit tests).
- `just pull-test-images` pulled all six images, FCOS included. With `ALL_BASE_IMAGES=localhost:1/nonexistent:x` it retried after 15/30/60/120s and failed after 5 attempts with a clear error (checked on the previous revision; the loop is unchanged).
- `cargo nextest run -P integration` for the touched tests: all 9 passed (the 4 registered Ignition tests, `test_to_disk_different_imgref_same_digest`, and the 3 `test_varlink_images_list*` tests). With `BCVK_FCOS_IMAGE=localhost/does-not-exist:x`, `test_run_ephemeral_ignition_invalid_path` fails pulling that image, so the variable is honored. `test_libvirt_ignition_works` is commented out upstream, so it only gets the same mechanical change.
- Rerun on the current revision (another 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace, podman 5.8, libvirt/qemu-kvm/virtiofsd installed): `make validate` and the unit tests pass; the same 9 integration tests pass with the images prefetched; after `podman rmi` of FCOS, `test_run_ephemeral_ignition_invalid_path` pulls it and passes.

CI note: the first revision [failed `integration-tests (2)`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/actions/runs/35952096935/job/107496126532) because `podman pull --policy` doesn't exist in podman 4 (`Error: unknown flag: --policy`); fixed by the `podman image exists` check above.

issue.title: ci: Scope App tokens so the scheduled gh-aw upgrade compiles
issue.body:
Part of tracker#1215. The bcvk inventory records three of five scheduled Upgrade gh-aw runs failing strict compilation on main; scheduled maintenance is separate from ordinary build/test pass rates. Evidence: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/1218#issuecomment-6619694573 . The completed attempt https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/actions/runs/41761911808 reported that adding repositories removes the first error but gh-aw v1.0.1 then rejects missing permission-* inputs; no fix was delivered because workflow paths were protected. Current drafter.md still shows unscoped App-token steps.

Retain this as one bounded repair of all six App-token steps in drafter.md, fix.md and review.md plus corresponding generated locks. After operator-approved workflow admission through tracker#1239, scope each token to the current repository and explicitly request only permissions its actual label operations need. Verify permission-issues versus permission-pull-requests against those operations and the action/compiler contract, rather than blindly granting both. Keep strict mode, triggers, safe-output policy and credential boundaries unchanged. Regenerate with the documented checked compiler; separately validate the exact compiler/upgrade sequence that failed, recording versions. Acceptance is all three workflows compiling strictly, reproducible lock regeneration without drift, and regression coverage showing absent scope/permissions fail. Record repeated authorized upgrade/compile outcomes on the final revision or explicitly disclose the live gate. Compiler success alone does not prove runtime label permissions. Deliver one draft in the allowed fork, never upstream. Do not broaden path/token policy inside this fix. The empty compiler-version file and missing check-drift job remain separate findings unless demonstrated necessary to this repair.

The planned implement run ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/actions/runs/42011590140)) found the same thing. Instead of a fake writer it opened #24, a docs-only draft that records the prerequisites. Nothing has changed since:

- The shared wrapper on [actions `main`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/actions/blob/d38a1379dd1d41f84460806b05ffa90a4a5eea7c/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml#L293) (`d38a137`) still rejects drafts at admission and at submit (`pull.draft !== false`, lines 293 and 809). It has no `agent-board-review-result-v1` job. The [actions README](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/actions/blob/main/README.md#draft-classifier-reviews-blocked-on-the-checked-helper) says the draft extension "is **not available**".
- The tracking request, cgwalters-forge/actions#200, is still open.
- The consumer side is ready: cgwalters-forge/agent-board#680 merged, adding `RESULT_JOB` in `board-forge/src/poll/drafts.rs` and the contract in `docs/poll.md`.
- bcvk has only the gh-aw `.github/workflows/review.md` and `review.lock.yml`. It has no `workflow_dispatch` review caller and no `workflow/review.md` or `workflow/review.toml`. The [tracker README](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/blob/main/README.md) lists bcvk#24 as one of the open prerequisites.

The acceptance criteria need provenance from that writer job, plus offline fixtures that exercise it. Neither can exist until the wrapper exposes the writer, and adding a local writer would defeat the boundary. Once actions#200 lands with an immutable SHA, a small implement plan can follow: add the base-owned dispatch caller with the trusted task and bounds pinned to that SHA, settle which workflow is the single source of automatic reviews, and add the fixtures.

Until then this waits on the shared design in actions#200. Separately, the docs-only #24 needs a decision: land it or close it.

issue.title: ci: Retry test image pulls and prefetch Fedora CoreOS

labels.name: review:quick
labels.description: High-confidence bot draft: skim and approve

issue.body:
CI keeps failing on transient quay.io errors that have nothing to do with the change under test. `just pull-test-images` is a single `podman pull` with only podman's built-in retries (3 quick retries a few seconds apart), which isn't enough to ride out an unexpected EOF from quay's CDN mid-blob ([example](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/35025230255)). The Ignition tests also pull `quay.io/fedora/fedora-coreos:stable` in the middle of the test run, so a 502/504 or dropped connection there fails a test directly ([1](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34819196417), [2](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34878492147), [3](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34780568246)).

This wraps each pull in `pull-test-images` in a retry loop with exponential backoff (5 attempts, 15s doubling, about 4 minutes of total delay) and adds the FCOS image to the prefetched set. The image name now lives only in the Justfile and reaches the tests as `BCVK_FCOS_IMAGE`, like the other test images, instead of three copies kept in sync by a comment. The tests that pull an image already in that set (the Ignition tests, the varlink images tests, and the to-disk imgref test) now only pull it when `podman image exists` says it is missing, so in CI they reuse the prefetched copy, while still working when run standalone. (`podman pull --policy missing` would say this directly, but podman 4 on the Ubuntu 24.04 runners doesn't have it.)

Note that FCOS is now pulled by the build job and each of the 4 integration partitions (5 pulls per CI run), rather than only by the partitions that happen to run an Ignition test.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace with KVM:

- `make validate` and `cargo test` pass (82 + 22 unit tests).
- `just pull-test-images` pulled all six images, FCOS included. With `ALL_BASE_IMAGES=localhost:1/nonexistent:x` it retried after 15/30/60/120s and failed after 5 attempts with a clear error (checked on the previous revision; the loop is unchanged).
- `cargo nextest run -P integration` for the touched tests: all 9 passed (the 4 registered Ignition tests, `test_to_disk_different_imgref_same_digest`, and the 3 `test_varlink_images_list*` tests). With `BCVK_FCOS_IMAGE=localhost/does-not-exist:x`, `test_run_ephemeral_ignition_invalid_path` fails pulling that image, so the variable is honored. `test_libvirt_ignition_works` is commented out upstream, so it only gets the same mechanical change.
- Rerun on the current revision (another 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace, podman 5.8, libvirt/qemu-kvm/virtiofsd installed): `make validate` and the unit tests pass; the same 9 integration tests pass with the images prefetched; after `podman rmi` of FCOS, `test_run_ephemeral_ignition_invalid_path` pulls it and passes.

CI note: the first revision [failed `integration-tests (2)`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/actions/runs/35952096935/job/107496126532) because `podman pull --policy` doesn't exist in podman 4 (`Error: unknown flag: --policy`); fixed by the `podman image exists` check above.

Accept and forward bootc's `--allow-missing-verity`, preserving `--allow-missing-fsverity` as a compatibility alias, and update the generated man-page options. Image-selected composefs requires bootc >= 1.17.0 inside the image; older bootc still rejects this option without `--composefs-backend`. Bootloader behavior, UKI-addon support and cache identity are unchanged.

Verified: the regression test failed before the fix and passes afterward; `just unit`, non-VM workspace tests, workspace test compilation, library rustdoc with warnings denied, and `git diff --check` passed. `just validate` could not complete because rustfmt and Clippy are missing. VM integration and real-image backend validation were not run.

Review: one adversarial pass, no blockers; follow-up is a real `to-disk` integration test covering image-selected composefs with bootc >= 1.17.0 and no explicit backend, plus non-composefs rejection validation.

issue.title: ephemeral: Give /var its own tmpfs, add --var-size

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
The ephemeral VM's `/var` was a directory on the initramfs `/run` tmpfs, which systemd caps at 20% of RAM. With the default 4G of memory that's ~780MiB, and there was no knob to raise it short of adding lots of memory, so e.g. a quadlet pulling a 2+GiB image at boot runs out of space. It also meant filling `/var` filled `/run`.

This mounts a dedicated tmpfs for `/var`, defaulting to 50% of guest RAM (the kernel's tmpfs default), and adds `--var-size` to `ephemeral run`/`run-ssh` (a size like `10G` or a percentage of guest RAM like `75%`). Together with `--add-swap` it allows a `/var` bigger than guest RAM. The size is passed to the initramfs unit as a drop-in in the CPIO that bcvk already appends, and the value is checked on the host so it can't inject other mount options or unit syntax. One behavior change to note: overfilling a `/var` that is larger than the memory available to back it now ends in the guest running out of memory rather than ENOSPC; the docs say so and suggest `--memory`/`--add-swap`.

A separate prep commit makes `parse_size` reject sizes that overflow `u64` (e.g. `17179869184G` used to wrap to 0), which also affects `--add-swap`.

The option is CLI-only for now; the varlink `Run` call keeps the default size.

## Is a tunable tmpfs the right first step?

In the issue, @cgwalters suggested making `/var` a bind mount of a directory inside the podman container, so its contents land in the host's container storage (the container's overlay upper). That removes the RAM limit completely, at the cost of a guest→host round trip for every write to `/var`.

I didn't do that here because of podman inside the guest. I checked on a devspace: with a host directory shared over bcvk's current virtiofsd setup (`--bind`, no `--xattr`), rootful podman in a centos-bootc:stream10 guest using that directory as its storage root fails with `'overlay' is not supported over <unknown> ... backing file system is unsupported for this graph driver`, and setting a `trusted.*` xattr there fails with `Operation not supported`. So with today's virtiofsd options, a virtiofs `/var` would break container storage in the guest. I didn't test whether enabling xattrs in virtiofsd would make overlay storage work, or whether podman would then be usable but slow.

A middle option would be a sparse file on the host attached as a virtio-blk scratch disk and formatted for `/var` in the initramfs, reusing the plumbing `--add-swap` already has. That gives a real block filesystem (overlay works, no RAM limit) at the cost of an mkfs at boot and needing mkfs tools in the initramfs.

Is a tunable tmpfs OK as the first step, with one of those as a follow-up if needed?

The second problem in the issue, `bcvk libvirt run --filesystem ext4` failing with `rm: cannot remove '/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay': Device or resource busy`, has the same cause as #351: the to-disk install VM booted the image's `default.target`, so the quadlet started and held files open under `/var/lib/containers`. e2be03d ("to-disk: Switch to a minimal boot target for to-disk installation") already fixed that on main.

Part of #200

## Testing

Run on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace with KVM, using `quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10` and `df -h /var /run` inside `bcvk ephemeral run --execute`:

| | `/var` size |
|---|---|
| main, default 4G memory | 782M (the same tmpfs as `/run`) |
| this PR, default | 2.0G (`/run` still 782M) |
| `--var-size 3G` | 3.0G |
| `--var-size 75%` | 2.9G |
| `--memory 8G --add-swap 10G --var-size 10G` | 10G |

With the last configuration, `podman pull quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:43` (1.96 GB) inside the guest succeeds, using 2.0G of `/var`. `--var-size 10G,exec` and `--var-size 99999999999T` are rejected when the arguments are parsed, and `--add-swap 17179869184G` now fails with "Size too large".

- `make validate` (fmt, clippy, rustdoc with `-D warnings`) and `cargo test -p bcvk` (85 tests, including the new `test_parse_size`, `test_parse_var_size` and `test_cpio_var_size_dropin`) pass.
- Integration tests with `cargo test --release -p integration-tests`: all 11 `to_disk` tests pass, including `test_to_disk_quadlet`. `test_run_ephemeral_mount_layout` now also checks that `/var` comes from the separate `bcvk-var` tmpfs, and it passes, as does the new `test_run_ephemeral_var_size`. Of the 33 `ephemeral` tests, 31 pass. The other two, `test_varlink_ephemeral_run_ps_and_ssh` and `test_run_ephemeral_journal_output`, time out waiting 120s for boot when the whole set runs in parallel. That reproduces identically on main, and both pass when run alone. `just test-integration` itself couldn't run because `go-md2man` isn't available on RHEL 10, so the same steps were run by hand.
- The man pages were regenerated with `cargo xtask sync-manpages`.

issue.title: ci: Scope App tokens so the scheduled gh-aw upgrade compiles
issue.body:
Part of tracker#1215. The bcvk inventory records three of five scheduled Upgrade gh-aw runs failing strict compilation on main; scheduled maintenance is separate from ordinary build/test pass rates. Evidence: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/1218#issuecomment-6619694573 . The completed attempt https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/actions/runs/41761911808 reported that adding repositories removes the first error but gh-aw v1.0.1 then rejects missing permission-* inputs; no fix was delivered because workflow paths were protected. Current drafter.md still shows unscoped App-token steps.

Retain this as one bounded repair of all six App-token steps in drafter.md, fix.md and review.md plus corresponding generated locks. After operator-approved workflow admission through tracker#1239, scope each token to the current repository and explicitly request only permissions its actual label operations need. Verify permission-issues versus permission-pull-requests against those operations and the action/compiler contract, rather than blindly granting both. Keep strict mode, triggers, safe-output policy and credential boundaries unchanged. Regenerate with the documented checked compiler; separately validate the exact compiler/upgrade sequence that failed, recording versions. Acceptance is all three workflows compiling strictly, reproducible lock regeneration without drift, and regression coverage showing absent scope/permissions fail. Record repeated authorized upgrade/compile outcomes on the final revision or explicitly disclose the live gate. Compiler success alone does not prove runtime label permissions. Deliver one draft in the allowed fork, never upstream. Do not broaden path/token policy inside this fix. The empty compiler-version file and missing check-drift job remain separate findings unless demonstrated necessary to this repair.

issue.title: ephemeral: Give /var its own tmpfs, add --var-size

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
The ephemeral VM's `/var` was a directory on the initramfs `/run` tmpfs, which systemd caps at 20% of RAM. With the default 4G of memory that's ~780MiB, and there was no knob to raise it short of adding lots of memory, so e.g. a quadlet pulling a 2+GiB image at boot runs out of space. It also meant filling `/var` filled `/run`.

This mounts a dedicated tmpfs for `/var`, defaulting to 50% of guest RAM (the kernel's tmpfs default), and adds `--var-size` to `ephemeral run`/`run-ssh` (a size like `10G` or a percentage of guest RAM like `75%`). Together with `--add-swap` it allows a `/var` bigger than guest RAM. The size is passed to the initramfs unit as a drop-in in the CPIO that bcvk already appends, and the value is checked on the host so it can't inject other mount options or unit syntax. One behavior change to note: overfilling a `/var` that is larger than the memory available to back it now ends in the guest running out of memory rather than ENOSPC; the docs say so and suggest `--memory`/`--add-swap`.

A separate prep commit makes `parse_size` reject sizes that overflow `u64` (e.g. `17179869184G` used to wrap to 0), which also affects `--add-swap`.

The option is CLI-only for now; the varlink `Run` call keeps the default size.

## Is a tunable tmpfs the right first step?

In the issue, @cgwalters suggested making `/var` a bind mount of a directory inside the podman container, so its contents land in the host's container storage (the container's overlay upper). That removes the RAM limit completely, at the cost of a guest→host round trip for every write to `/var`.

I didn't do that here because of podman inside the guest. I checked on a devspace: with a host directory shared over bcvk's current virtiofsd setup (`--bind`, no `--xattr`), rootful podman in a centos-bootc:stream10 guest using that directory as its storage root fails with `'overlay' is not supported over <unknown> ... backing file system is unsupported for this graph driver`, and setting a `trusted.*` xattr there fails with `Operation not supported`. So with today's virtiofsd options, a virtiofs `/var` would break container storage in the guest. I didn't test whether enabling xattrs in virtiofsd would make overlay storage work, or whether podman would then be usable but slow.

A middle option would be a sparse file on the host attached as a virtio-blk scratch disk and formatted for `/var` in the initramfs, reusing the plumbing `--add-swap` already has. That gives a real block filesystem (overlay works, no RAM limit) at the cost of an mkfs at boot and needing mkfs tools in the initramfs.

Is a tunable tmpfs OK as the first step, with one of those as a follow-up if needed?

The second problem in the issue, `bcvk libvirt run --filesystem ext4` failing with `rm: cannot remove '/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay': Device or resource busy`, has the same cause as #351: the to-disk install VM booted the image's `default.target`, so the quadlet started and held files open under `/var/lib/containers`. e2be03d ("to-disk: Switch to a minimal boot target for to-disk installation") already fixed that on main.

Part of #200

## Testing

Run on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace with KVM, using `quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10` and `df -h /var /run` inside `bcvk ephemeral run --execute`:

| | `/var` size |
|---|---|
| main, default 4G memory | 782M (the same tmpfs as `/run`) |
| this PR, default | 2.0G (`/run` still 782M) |
| `--var-size 3G` | 3.0G |
| `--var-size 75%` | 2.9G |
| `--memory 8G --add-swap 10G --var-size 10G` | 10G |

With the last configuration, `podman pull quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:43` (1.96 GB) inside the guest succeeds, using 2.0G of `/var`. `--var-size 10G,exec` and `--var-size 99999999999T` are rejected when the arguments are parsed, and `--add-swap 17179869184G` now fails with "Size too large".

- `make validate` (fmt, clippy, rustdoc with `-D warnings`) and `cargo test -p bcvk` (85 tests, including the new `test_parse_size`, `test_parse_var_size` and `test_cpio_var_size_dropin`) pass.
- Integration tests with `cargo test --release -p integration-tests`: all 11 `to_disk` tests pass, including `test_to_disk_quadlet`. `test_run_ephemeral_mount_layout` now also checks that `/var` comes from the separate `bcvk-var` tmpfs, and it passes, as does the new `test_run_ephemeral_var_size`. Of the 33 `ephemeral` tests, 31 pass. The other two, `test_varlink_ephemeral_run_ps_and_ssh` and `test_run_ephemeral_journal_output`, time out waiting 120s for boot when the whole set runs in parallel. That reproduces identically on main, and both pass when run alone. `just test-integration` itself couldn't run because `go-md2man` isn't available on RHEL 10, so the same steps were run by hand.
- The man pages were regenerated with `cargo xtask sync-manpages`.

issue.title: to-disk: Save guest dmesg and virtiofsd logs when the install fails

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
When `bootc install` fails in the to-disk VM, the guest kernel log and the virtiofsd logs are removed along with the container, and those are exactly what would explain flakes like the ESTALE errors from the host storage share in #157.

Now, before removing the container, bcvk saves the guest `dmesg` (fetched over SSH with a 30s timeout, since the guest may be wedged) and both virtiofsd logs to a file in the temporary directory, and prints one line with its path:

```
Logs from the failed install VM were saved to /tmp/bcvk-to-disk-failure-xGBUm7.log
```

If none of the three can be read (e.g. the VM never came up), no file is written and the reasons are logged at debug level. The tails of the logs (200 lines each) go to stderr only with `--debug`, debug logging, or `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS` set, since most failures (a broken image, a bad install option) are plain user errors that a wall of kernel log wouldn't help with. If the file can't be written, the tails are printed instead. This is documented in `docs/src/testing.md`. Base-disk creation for `libvirt run` goes through the same code, so it's covered too. For the varlink `to-disk` call, the path line goes to the server's stderr.

The integration test harness sets `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS`. For the logs to actually reach the test output, the to-disk integration tests now run bcvk through a small helper that includes its stdout and stderr in the error when it fails, since xshell's `.output()?` drops captured stderr on a non-zero exit.

To support the dmesg timeout, `ssh::connect_captured` gained a `timeout` argument; it had no callers before.

The companion nextest change that serializes the `test_to_base_disk_*` tests is a separate PR.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace with KVM:

- `make validate` and `cargo test` pass (84 + 22 unit tests, including table-driven tests for the log formatting).
- A deliberately failing integration test (a scratch test, not included here, running `to-disk --disk-size 2G` through the new helper under `cargo nextest run -P integration`) failed with bcvk's stderr in the test output: the `bootc install` out-of-space error, the path line, the dmesg tail (last 200 of 647 lines) and both virtiofsd logs. The junit report has them too.
- Forced failures by hand (the same 2G disk):
  - `bcvk to-disk`: prints the install error and the one-line path, and the 668-line file holds the full logs.
  - With `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS=1`, and with `--debug`: the three tails are printed as well.
  - `bcvk libvirt run --root-size 2G`: the base-disk failure also prints the path line.
  - The plain, env var and `libvirt run` cases were checked on the previous revision; that code is unchanged, and `--debug` was checked on this one.
- `test_to_disk` passes under the integration profile.

Not tested: the case where all three logs are unavailable.

CI note (2026-09-24): the [`integration-tests (2)` failure](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/actions/runs/35955666987/job/107510910165) is unrelated to this change: `test_run_tmpfs` failed with exit 255 from `ephemeral run-ssh` (ssh itself failing), a path this PR doesn't touch, matching the `ConnectTimeout` banner-exchange flake targeted by cgwalters-forge/bcvk#8. All to-disk tests in that partition passed. Reran the failed jobs once.

Related: #157

issue.title: static-checks: Add a repository hygiene action, starting with LICENSE

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Several public, non-fork repositories in the orgs have no license file. This adds a `static-checks` composite action that runs a table of named, offline checks over a checked-out tree. Later checks such as SECURITY.md or CODEOWNERS are new table entries. The first check, `license`, requires a top-level LICENSE, LICENSE-* or COPYING file whose text askalono recognizes as an SPDX license. A `license` field in Cargo.toml or package.json, when present, must name the same licenses: LICENSE-APACHE plus LICENSE-MIT matches `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`. askalono 0.5.0 is downloaded at a pinned version and checked against a sha256 hard-coded in the action. The check itself is a Node script that uses only the standard library: this repository ships no Rust crate, only the setup-rust action.

A check can be skipped only with a reason committed in the checked repository's `.github/static-checks.toml` (`[skip]` with `name = "reason"` lines). That way exceptions show up in review, and they also work for ruleset-required runs, which get no inputs. Listing a check in the `skip` input without a recorded reason fails. The action prints one pass/fail/skip line per check with a fix hint, and writes a job summary table. The README documents the inputs, the exception file, and how to scope an org ruleset with a custom repository property, since rulesets can't target non-forks directly.

## Files to add by hand

This change could not include files under `.github/`, so the reusable workflow and the CI job are below for a maintainer to add. The README already describes the workflow. It uses major tags such as `actions/checkout@v7`, which Renovate updates, following the existing workflows here rather than SHA pins. In another repository, and in ruleset-required runs, a relative `uses: ./static-checks` would resolve against the caller's checkout. So the workflow uses `bootc-dev/actions/static-checks@main` everywhere except in bootc-dev/actions itself. Its job is skipped in forks.

`.github/workflows/static-checks.yml`:

```yaml
# Repository hygiene checks, meant to be required org-wide via a ruleset
# (see README.md). Callers and ruleset-required runs use the action from
# bootc-dev/actions main; this repository tests its own copy.
name: Static checks
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      checks:
        description: 'Comma-separated checks to run, or "all"'
        type: string
        default: 'all'
      skip:
        description: 'Comma-separated checks to skip; each needs a reason in .github/static-checks.toml'
        type: string
        default: ''
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  # Ruleset-required workflows must report in merge queues too.
  merge_group:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  static-checks:
    name: Static checks
    # Forks inherit their source's hygiene; skipped jobs satisfy required checks.
    if: ${{ !github.event.repository.fork }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run static checks (this repository)
        if: github.repository == 'bootc-dev/actions'
        uses: ./static-checks
        with:
          checks: ${{ inputs.checks || 'all' }}
          skip: ${{ inputs.skip }}

      - name: Run static checks
        if: github.repository != 'bootc-dev/actions'
        uses: bootc-dev/actions/static-checks@main
        with:
          checks: ${{ inputs.checks || 'all' }}
          skip: ${{ inputs.skip }}
```

Add this job to `.github/workflows/test-actions-pr.yml`. It also checks this repository itself:

```yaml
  test-static-checks:
    name: Test static-checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./static-checks
      - run: node test/static-checks.js
        env:
          ASKALONO: ${{ runner.temp }}/askalono/askalono
```

## Verification and follow-ups

I ran `node test/static-checks.js` locally with the pinned askalono, and all 8 cases passed. The cases are this repository, no license, unrecognized text, Apache-2.0 with package.json, dual MIT/Apache with Cargo.toml, a Cargo.toml mismatch, a skip with a reason and a skip without one. The test builds its fixture trees in a temporary directory, because a committed tree can't contain its own `.github/`. I also ran the action's install step by hand, and it rejects a wrong checksum. Neither workflow above has run in CI.

One review pass ran and found no blockers. I fixed merge_group support, the skip-without-reason test, directories named like license files, per-check errors and annotation escaping. Left as follow-ups:
- Top-level files like LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY must also be recognized licenses; there is no ignore list.
- Unknown keys under `[skip]` are silently ignored.
- The `@main` path isn't covered by test-actions-published.yml.
- A repository that both calls the workflow and is covered by the ruleset runs it twice.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc-dev-actions/issues/6

Closes #6

issue.title: static-checks: An org-wide repository hygiene action, starting with LICENSE
issue.body:
The operator wants a standard way to check repository hygiene across the orgs, starting with "every repository has a LICENSE". A survey on 2026-11-13 found several of our public, non-fork repositories with no license file.

Build a **`static-checks`** composite action in this repository (bootc-dev/actions; this is its midstream fork, and the operator has asked for the PR to go upstream), plus a reusable workflow that calls it. The operator intends to make that workflow required org-wide, through an org ruleset, for repositories that aren't forks. The operator sets up the ruleset; this PR only provides the workflow it points at.

Design:
- **One action, a list of named checks**, each cheap, offline and deterministic, run over the checked-out tree. The first check is `license`: a top-level LICENSE, LICENSE-* or COPYING file exists, and its text is recognized as an SPDX license (use a small, established detector, e.g. askalono's or GitHub's licensee data, or an `spdx` crate; don't hand-roll matching). If a recognized license declaration (Cargo.toml `license`, package.json `license`) is present, it must agree with the file. Structure the action so later checks (e.g. a SECURITY.md, a CODEOWNERS that parses, no committed large binaries) are added as further entries, not new actions. Implement it in Rust if this repository already ships Rust tooling; otherwise keep it a short script, and say why in the commit message.
- **Inputs:** `checks` (default: all), and `skip` for opting out of a check, with the reason recorded in a committed `.github/static-checks.toml` in the caller, so an exception is visible in review rather than hidden in workflow YAML.
- **Output:** one line per check, pass or fail, with a fix hint (e.g. "add LICENSE; this org uses Apache-2.0 OR MIT"), and a job summary. It never needs a token beyond `contents: read`.
- **The reusable workflow:** `.github/workflows/static-checks.yml` with `on: workflow_call` (and `pull_request` for this repository itself), and `permissions: contents: read`. Pin actions by SHA, matching this repository's conventions.
- **Forks:** org rulesets can't target "non-fork" directly. Document in README how to scope it: a custom repository property (e.g. `static-checks: required`) set on source repositories, with the ruleset targeting that property. As a backstop, the workflow itself passes trivially when `github.event.repository.fork` is true.

Tests: fixture trees for no license, an unrecognized license, Apache-2.0, dual MIT/Apache, a Cargo.toml mismatch, and a skip with a reason. Run them in this repository's existing test-actions-pr workflow pattern.

Done when the tests pass and the action passes against this repository itself. Open the PR in this fork first. Promotion to bootc-dev/actions follows the usual promote path.

issue.title: composefs: install to-disk fails with 'Invalid splitstream content type'
issue.body:
Installing a composefs-native image with bootc 1.17.1 through bcvk's libvirt base-disk path (`bcvk libvirt run`, which runs `bootc install to-disk` over SSH in a VM) fails:

```
error: Installing to disk: Pulling image into composefs repository: Opening stream '': Creating new splitstream reader: Invalid splitstream content type
```

Seen in atomic-linux-sandbox#70's `vm-k3s` job (run 44148129342), on an image built `FROM scratch` from `bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs` output. Removing an empty top layer from the image didn't change it. The same image installs and boots in that PR's `vm-lifecycle` test, which installs a different way, so the failure depends on the pull or install path rather than the image contents. The empty stream name (`Opening stream ''`) suggests a layer or config lookup that came back with no name.

Find the source and make bootc either import the image or fail with a clear message, then add a test that installs a from-scratch composefs image through the same path.

Related: atomic-linux-sandbox#69.

issue.title: install: to-existing-root relabels the entire physical root
issue.body:
`bootc install to-existing-root` ends with a recursive SELinux relabel of the whole physical root (eb6bd011, "install: Add final SELinux relabel of the physical root filesystem"; `crates/lib/src/install.rs`, `ensure_dir_labeled_recurse` on `rootfs.physical_root`). For to-existing-root, the physical root is the existing host's entire filesystem. On a host with multi-terabyte disks and large container storage under the home directories, this last step walks every file single-threaded, with no progress output, for hours. Files that already have a label skip the write, but each one still costs a stat and an xattr read.

Fix, in order of payoff:
1. **Don't walk what the install didn't create.** For to-existing-root, limit the final relabel to what the install wrote (the new stateroot or composefs state, the bootloader and boot directories, and the top-level directories it created). Skip the host's existing `/var`, `/home` (and `/var/home`), and other ostree stateroots under `/ostree/deploy/*`, plus anything else that was already there. The new deployment's own `/var` is labeled when it's set up.
2. **Parallelize what's left,** using rayon over directory entries, as the fsck path does.
3. **Show progress:** files visited and relabeled, with a progress bar when attached to a terminal and periodic log lines otherwise.

Add a test that runs to-existing-root over a root with a large pre-existing `/var/home` tree and asserts the tree isn't visited, by count or an injected walk hook.

Related: atomic-linux-sandbox#68 (reprovisioning an existing host with to-existing-root).

issue.title: ci: Retry transient RPM and metalink download failures
issue.body:
Part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#1215. Groups 3 and 10 of the [bootc CI inventory](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/1216#issuecomment-6619694208).

**What fails:** RPM and repository metadata downloads in upstream bootc's package, test-container-export and integration jobs. Either every mirror returns HTTP 503 for an RPM (`all mirrors were tried`), or the Fedora metalink fetch times out with curl(28) and leaves empty metadata.

**How often:** HTTP 503: 14 runs (32 jobs), 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-02. Metalink timeout: 6 runs (7 attempts), 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-01. The run sets overlap. Classified as infra: same-SHA reruns passed.

**Evidence** (upstream bootc-dev/bootc, workflow CI):
- test-container-export, run 38911232876 attempt 2, job 119690576990, SHA b81d1b5febcb; error at 2026-10-22 07:14:31Z, compose-appstream RPM HTTP 503, all mirrors tried. Latest example: run 41463846825 attempt 2, job 125977526355, started 2026-11-03 14:25:12Z.
- Same-SHA recovery: test-baseconfigs (centos-10, root-transient), run 37491710626, job 112383201284 failed on attempt 1, job 114853170725 passed on attempt 3.
- Metalink: test-integration (fedora-44, composefs, xfs, grub, bls, unsealed), run 38368166194 attempt 1, job 115212971837, SHA 8d197a92a506, 2026-10-13. Same-SHA recovery: run 37877444133, job 113658284081 failed on attempt 1, job 114839411247 passed on attempt 3.

**Proposed fix:** audit the retry layers dnf already has in these jobs, then add a bounded network-only retry with backoff (dnf `retries`/`timeout` settings or a wrapper around the install step), or point the jobs at a more reliable compose mirror. Keep the final repository and HTTP diagnostics. A package that is really missing must still fail immediately.

**Triage: valid, still applies to current main (0ca885f). Ready to implement, no operator decision needed.**

The failures are real infra flakes, but adding retries to dnf won't fix them. `just build-fetch` already retries the network-heavy `fetch` stage 10 times (CI sets `BOOTC_CI_RETRIES: "10"`, [ci.yml#L34](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L34), [Justfile#L113](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/Justfile#L113)). The problem is that the jobs that failed never go through that retry. I checked the failed step in each example job:

- test-container-export, job 119690576990: failed in `Build and run container export test` → `just test-container-export` → `build`. The 503 came from rpm-ostree in the `target-base` stage ([Dockerfile#L52](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/Dockerfile#L52)). This job has no `build-fetch` step ([ci.yml#L647](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L647)).
- test-baseconfigs, job 112383201284: failed in `Build container with baseconfig`, during `dnf install createrepo_c` in `target-base` (`baseos` repomd, all mirrors tried). This job has no `build-fetch` step either ([ci.yml#L544](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L544)). test-coreos ([ci.yml#L608](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L608)) has the same gap.
- test-integration, job 115212971837: `build-fetch` and `Build container` both passed. Then the step before TMT runs `podman builder prune -af` ([ci.yml#L402](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L402)), and `test-composefs`/`test-tmt` depend on `build` ([Justfile#L192](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/Justfile#L192)). So `Run TMT integration tests` rebuilds the RPM and the whole image, `fetch` stage included, without retry. That is where the metalink curl(28) hit (`provision-fetch.sh`, `xargs dnf install`).

**Plan (one PR to upstream ci.yml/Justfile, small):**
1. Add a `just build-fetch` step, with `BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1` and the job's `BOOTC_*` env, before the build step in test-container-export, test-baseconfigs and test-coreos. `fetch` copies from `target-base`, so this also retries the compose-repo/rpm-ostree and baseconfig installs.
2. Stop the TMT step in test-integration from rebuilding. Either call `_build-upgrade-image` + `test-tmt-nobuild` (the composefs path needs an equivalent nobuild entry), or move the prune so it doesn't throw away the cache that `build-fetch` filled. Also pass `BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1` there, since the log shows it currently rebuilds `bootc-pkg`.
3. Optionally do the same for the unretried `tools` stage (`initialize-sealing-tools`, [Dockerfile#L206](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/blob/0ca885f/Dockerfile#L206)) and `Dockerfile.upgrade`, both used for UKI builds.

The retry is a coarse whole-stage retry, so a package that is really missing still fails, just after 10 attempts instead of 1. That is the existing behavior of `build-fetch` and already accepted. Per-request dnf `retries`/`timeout` tuning won't help here: the compose repos have a single baseurl, and the 503s and metalink stalls lasted longer than one dnf invocation.

**Unclear:** I didn't check whether the other 14 HTTP 503 runs all failed outside `build-fetch` (I only checked the three jobs above). I also didn't check whether `podman builder prune -af` is still needed for disk space once the rebuild is gone.

comment.body:
**Verdict: obsolete. The failure was a real race in the test, but the test that had it no longer exists. Close this issue; no fix needed.**

test-64 isn't on `main` here or upstream. It only exists in the open upstream PR bootc-dev/bootc#2603 (`fix/switch-target-imgref`). At the failing SHA b00d6b98176c, [`test-switch-target-imgref.nu`](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/b00d6b98176c4801210513edd66b8af110a1fedf/tmt/tests/booted/test-switch-target-imgref.nu#L158-L159) (also [L184-L185](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/b00d6b98176c4801210513edd66b8af110a1fedf/tmt/tests/booted/test-switch-target-imgref.nu#L184-L185)) ran `podman start $registry` after a `tmt-reboot` and then ran `skopeo copy` straight away, without waiting for the registry to come up. In the [job log](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/actions/runs/41206820574/job/124562165714) the registry works on the first boot, and the refusal comes right after that post-reboot restart. So the cause is readiness, not which address family the registry binds. The `[::1]` in the error doesn't point at the cause either: the port is published as `-p 127.0.0.1:5555:5000` and the refs say `localhost`. Go tries `::1` first and reports that error when both addresses fail.

The PR has since been rewritten. At its current head 686c19ee, [the test](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/686c19eeff2278e64eb5cf2861b4246ce3fb0529/tmt/tests/booted/test-switch-target-imgref.nu) uses only `containers-storage:` and starts no registry. All 22 `test-integration` jobs in [CI run 43166883361](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/actions/runs/43166883361) passed, including the `composefs, xfs, grub, bls, unsealed` job that failed before.

If the PR brings a registry back, the fix is to poll `http://127.0.0.1:5555/v2/` until it answers after each `podman run`/`podman start`, use `127.0.0.1:5555` in the refs, and dump `podman logs` when it fails. That belongs in review of #2603, not in this fork.

issue.title: ci: Retry transient RPM and metalink download failures
issue.body:
Part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#1215. Groups 3 and 10 of the [bootc CI inventory](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/1216#issuecomment-6619694208).

**What fails:** RPM and repository metadata downloads in upstream bootc's package, test-container-export and integration jobs. Either every mirror returns HTTP 503 for an RPM (`all mirrors were tried`), or the Fedora metalink fetch times out with curl(28) and leaves empty metadata.

**How often:** HTTP 503: 14 runs (32 jobs), 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-02. Metalink timeout: 6 runs (7 attempts), 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-01. The run sets overlap. Classified as infra: same-SHA reruns passed.

**Evidence** (upstream bootc-dev/bootc, workflow CI):
- test-container-export, run 38911232876 attempt 2, job 119690576990, SHA b81d1b5febcb; error at 2026-10-22 07:14:31Z, compose-appstream RPM HTTP 503, all mirrors tried. Latest example: run 41463846825 attempt 2, job 125977526355, started 2026-11-03 14:25:12Z.
- Same-SHA recovery: test-baseconfigs (centos-10, root-transient), run 37491710626, job 112383201284 failed on attempt 1, job 114853170725 passed on attempt 3.
- Metalink: test-integration (fedora-44, composefs, xfs, grub, bls, unsealed), run 38368166194 attempt 1, job 115212971837, SHA 8d197a92a506, 2026-10-13. Same-SHA recovery: run 37877444133, job 113658284081 failed on attempt 1, job 114839411247 passed on attempt 3.

**Proposed fix:** audit the retry layers dnf already has in these jobs, then add a bounded network-only retry with backoff (dnf `retries`/`timeout` settings or a wrapper around the install step), or point the jobs at a more reliable compose mirror. Keep the final repository and HTTP diagnostics. A package that is really missing must still fail immediately.

issue.title: bootc: read setup-root-conf.toml from the mounted composefs root (bootc#2300 prerequisite)
issue.body:
Prerequisite slice for https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/2300 under epic cgwalters-forge/tracker#15; it unblocks cgwalters-forge/tracker#90, which cgwalters deferred on bootc#2300 (A, tested drafts only, on cgwalters-forge/tracker#244). Design: bootc#2300 section 2.1.

Today `setup_root()` in crates/initramfs/src/lib.rs reads /usr/lib/composefs/setup-root-conf.toml from a host path (`args.config`, around line 557) before `mount_composefs_image` runs. That is only correct because crates/initramfs/dracut/module-setup.sh (line 27) bakes the image's copy into the initramfs. crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/soft_reboot.rs (line 128) passes `config: Default::default()`, so a soft reboot ignores the staged image's [etc]/[var]/[root] policy, and install-time root assembly (the next slice) has no baked copy at all.

Scope: read the config relative to the mounted composefs root fd after the image is mounted; remove the dracut bake-in and update docs/src/man/bootc-setup-root-conf.5.md; keep `Args.config` as a test-only override next to `--root-fs`; factor the `Args`/synthetic cmdline construction soft_reboot.rs does into a shared helper that the install-time assembly can reuse; unit test the new read path through the existing `--root-fs` override. Check first whether crates/lib/src/mount.rs (bootc#2483) already reads SETUP_ROOT_CONF_PATH from the mounted image and share that code instead of adding a second reader. Real cold boot must behave exactly as before.

Tested draft pull request only, in this repository: no upstream posting, no promotion; those remain cgwalters' call. Follow tracker's upstream-policy/bootc-dev/bootc.md for trailers and add no Signed-off-by.

issue.title: bootc: install to-filesystem/to-existing-root --assemble-root and --reassemble-root (bootc#2300)
issue.body:
Root-assembly flags from https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/2300 as a tested draft, stacked on the prerequisite slice, for epic cgwalters-forge/tracker#15. This is what cgwalters-forge/tracker#90 (Anaconda ISO composefs support) waits on per cgwalters' decision on cgwalters-forge/tracker#244; Anaconda itself stays deferred until bootc#2300 lands upstream.

Before coding, compare with `bootc install mount` (https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/pull/2483, crates/lib/src/mount.rs), merged after the design was written: it already assembles an offline deployment's root with /etc and /var at a caller-chosen directory for both backends. Scope the draft to what is missing from bootc#2300: `--assemble-root PATH` and `--reassemble-root` on `install to-filesystem` and `install to-existing-root` (not `to-disk`), the in-place relocation of ROOT_PATH to ROOT_PATH/sysroot, implied `--skip-finalize`, the pre-checks on the target path, the transient-etc warning, and the ostree backend's explicit var bind (design sections 2.2 to 2.5). Share the mount code rather than duplicating it, and record the comparison in the pull request.

Tests per design section 2.7: unit tests, plus a tmt test following the pattern of tmt/test-install-to-filesystem-var-mount.sh (confirm it exists) for both backends and both flags: usr, etc and var populated; `chroot TARGET /bin/true` works; TARGET/sysroot exposes the physical root; writes to etc and var land in persistent storage. Cover to-existing-root, a non-default --stateroot and --disable-selinux. Say which tests actually ran.

Tested draft pull request only; no upstream posting, no promotion. ckyrouac agreed the CLI spec upstream and left details to implementation: settle them in the pull request, not with the operator.

issue.body:
Every new tmt test edits the generated `tmt/plans/integration.fmf` and `tmt/tests/tests.fmf` at the same spot, so each open test PR conflicts whenever main gains one (most recently bootc-dev/bootc#2516, resolved by regenerating with `cargo xtask update-generated direct`).

Suggested durable fix: either a `.gitattributes` merge driver for those two files that re-runs the generator (needs per-clone git config, so a documented `just` setup step), or stop committing them and generate at build time (`just validate` then has nothing to check). The second removes the conflict class entirely; propose it upstream.

issue.title: bootc: stop recurring tmt generated-fmf rebase conflicts
issue.body:
Every new tmt test edits the generated `tmt/plans/integration.fmf` and `tmt/tests/tests.fmf` at the same spot, so each open test PR conflicts whenever main gains one (most recently bootc-dev/bootc#2516, resolved by regenerating with `cargo xtask update-generated direct`).

Suggested durable fix: either a `.gitattributes` merge driver for those two files that re-runs the generator (needs per-clone git config, so a documented `just` setup step), or stop committing them and generate at build time (`just validate` then has nothing to check). The second removes the conflict class entirely; propose it upstream.

issue.body:
`test-tmt` ran `just _build-upgrade-image` and `just test-tmt-nobuild` as
fresh `just` processes, which don't inherit command-line variable
overrides. So with the documented `just variant=composefs ... test-tmt ...`
pattern (which `test-composefs` also uses), the upgrade image was built with
the default boot_type/seal_state/filesystem, and `run-tmt` got
`--env=BOOTC_variant=ostree` even though the VM was a composefs install. CI
isn't affected because it sets `BOOTC_*` in the environment, so this only
bit local runs, silently.

This makes them dependencies of `test-tmt` instead, which run in the same
invocation with the overrides intact.

Testing, on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace: `just --dry-run variant=composefs
boot_type=uki seal_state=sealed test-tmt readonly` now shows the upgrade
image built with `boot_type=uki` / `seal_state=sealed` and
`cargo xtask run-tmt --env=BOOTC_variant=composefs ...`; on main, a real
`just variant=composefs ... test-tmt` run logged
`run-tmt --env=BOOTC_variant=ostree`. With this change on top of the
zstd:chunked test branch, `just variant=composefs bootloader=systemd ... test-tmt
--composefs-backend ... switch-zstd-chunked` passed and logged
`run-tmt --env=BOOTC_variant=composefs`, a plain `just test-tmt
switch-zstd-chunked` still passed with `BOOTC_variant=ostree`, and `just
validate` passed.

issue.title: install: Run fatal lints before installing

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

issue.body:
Images that fail our fatal lints install fine today and then break in confusing ways at runtime. The classic case is a `/var/run` directory created by a legacy package. Few people know to add `RUN bootc container lint` to their build. As the issue suggests, `bootc install` now runs the fatal subset of the lints against the image being installed, before anything is written to the target.

Details:

- It only runs when installing from the running container image. With `--source-imgref` we don't have the image root at hand.
- `etc-usretc` only prints a warning, for compatibility with existing images, as the issue asks.
- The ostree-specific fatal lints (`baseimage-root`, `utf8`) are skipped for `--composefs-backend`.
- The check runs after the SELinux re-exec, so it only runs once.
- The recursive lints walk the whole image root. At install time that root also contains host mounts: the target, container storage and so on. Those aren't necessarily on a different device (for example with the vfs storage driver), so this walk skips every mount point, not just the ones on other devices. The relabeling walk works the same way.
- `--skip-lints` (on to-disk, to-filesystem and to-existing-root) skips the check. The name matches the existing `--skip-fetch-check` and `--skip-finalize`.

Closes #960

## Testing

I tested on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace, rebased on current main (41049cca). The branch was built in its own checkout, with its own cargo target and buildah cache directories, and the built image reports `gd5c0cabe`.

- `just validate` passed.
- `just unit-tests` passed: 444 tests, including the new `lints::tests::test_lint_for_install`. It covers both backends, the etc-usretc warning, and the ostree-only lints.
- `bootc-integration-tests install-alongside localhost/bootc-install` passed all 7 tests. That includes the existing loopback and alongside installs of the default image, and a new test: a derived image with a `/var/run` directory fails `bootc install to-disk --via-loopback` with `Failed lint: var-run`, and the same install succeeds with `--skip-lints`. CI doesn't run this suite right now, because the install-tests job is disabled.
- Runtime: a loopback `bootc install to-disk` of the default centos-bootc:stream10-based image, with `RUST_LOG=bootc_lib::lints=debug`, logged `Install lints: passed=6 skipped=9 in 108.117108ms` and then completed. The walk adds about 0.1s to an install.

issue.title: tests: Check that GC keeps a V2 rollback in the 1.16 bridge test

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
**Stacked on forge #30** (`bot/cfs-bridge-1164`, itself on #18). Until those land this PR also shows their commits; only the last commit is new.

test-49 never ran a repository GC while a 1.16.0 install's V2 deployment was the rollback of a V1 one, which is what every such system looks like right after its first upgrade with current bootc. Its only GC ran after the rollback, with the V2 deployment booted, and without `--prune-repo`, so it only looked at boot binaries and could not report a removed object.

With the upgrade booted, the test now runs `composefs-gc --prune-repo` (the GC upgrades run) and checks that the rollback's boot entry, deployment state and EROFS image (still V2) survive, and that `cfsctl fsck` and `cfsctl oci fsck` of the rollback's bootc tag pass. Then it rolls back as before, which proves the V2 deployment still boots. The final `--assert-no-op` now includes `--prune-repo`.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

**Tested** on a 16-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-37011656929), Fedora 44 base, `just test-composefs-bridge`:

- at this head: `unsealed 1.16.0`, `sealed 1.16.0` and `bls 1.16.4` all passed; the boot2 GC removed the 1.16.0 or 1.16.4 install's leftovers (53-56 objects) and fsck and `oci fsck` passed, and the final `--prune-repo --assert-no-op` found nothing;
- that it catches a regression (run at c191f09b, this check before the tag prefix became a constant): with GC temporarily changed to drop a rollback whose EROFS format differs from the booted one's, `unsealed 1.16.0` fails at the new boot2 check (GC removed the rollback's manifest, so `bootc status` can no longer read the rollback), while the test from #30's head passes against the same broken GC;
- dropping `additional_roots` for non-booted deployments alone is not caught, correctly: the V2 boot image is also reachable from the rollback's tagged manifest config, so nothing is lost.

issue.title: cleanup: Mount the previous system's /var before removing its packages

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

issue.body:
Step 3 of the plan in https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/2559, stacked on #44 (which is stacked on #43): the fix for `bootc-destructive-cleanup.service` failing after an in-place reinstall.

### Root cause

`fedora-bootc-destructive-cleanup` runs `rpm -e --root=/sysroot` on every package of the previous OS. rpm runs the erase scriptlets chrooted in `/sysroot`, so they need the previous OS's `/var`. But `/sysroot` is only the previous root filesystem (btrfs `subvol=/root`); on Fedora 44 cloud images `/var` is a separate `var` subvolume that nothing mounts after the reinstall. netcat's `%preun` (`alternatives --remove`) then fails with `failed to create admindir`, `xargs` exits 123 and the unit fails.

The script is unchanged since f567f7eb (January 2026), so this is not a regression. It went unseen because nothing checked the unit until test 014 was added in 41049cca (2026-09-18), and the bcvk flows never boot a reinstalled system.

### The fix

In `contrib/scripts/fedora-bootc-destructive-cleanup` (plus its man page): if `/sysroot/etc/fstab` has a `/var` entry whose source resolves to a block device, mount it at `/sysroot/var` with `mount --fstab /sysroot/etc/fstab --target-prefix /sysroot /var` before removing the packages. The unit already has `PrivateMounts=true`, so the mount stays private to the service.

The mount is skipped, and the script behaves as before, when:

- `/sysroot/etc/fstab` does not exist or has no `/var` entry;
- `/sysroot/var` is already a mount point;
- the source is not a block device, e.g. a bind mount (warning);
- the mount fails (warning);
- the mounted `/var` turns out to be on the same filesystem as `/sysroot` or as the booted `/var`: it is unmounted again (warning).

The podman prune now runs only if `/sysroot/var/lib/containers` exists.

Not handled: nested mounts under `/var`, a `/var` defined by a `.mount` unit, and LVM or LUKS devices that are not active in the new system. Those give a warning and then the old behaviour. The script only uses `/sysroot` and `/var`, so it is the same for ostree and composefs; but on composefs `--cleanup` never writes the stamp file (only `ostree_install` does), so the service never runs there. That is a separate gap and is not fixed here.

### Alternatives the run listed

The run called this "not a clear-cut choice":

- (a) `rpm -e --noscripts`, `bootc-dev/bootc#2561`. Smaller, but it skips every scriptlet on every system (cgwalters called it a big hammer on that PR), and the old `/var` stays unreachable for the podman prune.
- (b) Record the needed mounts at install time in a state file (cgwalters' general idea). More general, but bigger and riskier.
- (c) Delete btrfs subvolumes instead of using rpm.

It chose the targeted mount because it matches cgwalters' stated preference ("special case mount preservation").

### Questions for the maintainer (from the run)

1. Fix design: I implemented a guarded mount of the previous /var from its fstab. The alternative is `rpm -e --noscripts` (`bootc-dev/bootc#2561`), which is smaller but skips all scriptlets. I recommend keeping the mount and closing that PR or rebasing it onto this; a maintainer should decide.
2. Not run here (no KVM): `just test-tmt-readonly`. Test 014 must now pass on the reinstall path, and the cleanup unit's journal should show `mount --fstab /sysroot/etc/fstab --target-prefix /sysroot /var` succeeding.
3. Should `install to-existing-root --cleanup` with the composefs backend write the cleanup stamp? Today it is silently ignored. I left it alone as a separate change.
4. `bootloader-update.service` failure after the reinstall on a BIOS-booted guest: file a separate issue (bootc removes `EFI/` while `bootupd --auto` installs only BIOS)? I recommend yes, after confirming the guest's boot mode. (The run inferred this cause; it did not verify it.)

### What the run did and did not run

Ran: `shellcheck` and `bash -n` on the script; `cargo xtask update-generated direct --check`; and the new function in an unprivileged user and mount namespace (`unshare -rm`) against a scratch fstab with `/sysroot` and `/var` relocated, 8 scenarios (a tmpfs `/var` entry mounts; no `/var` entry, no fstab, an already-mounted `/sysroot/var`, a non-block source and a bad mount option are each skipped; a `/var` on the same filesystem as the old root or as the live `/var` is unmounted again). The block-device check was stubbed for the cases that need a mount.

Not run: a real boot, a btrfs subvolume mount, `just test-tmt-readonly`, and the full `just validate` container build. There are no unit tests because the logic is bash. So as opened, this change has never executed on a reinstalled system; a devspace verification will follow as a comment.

labels.name: needs-human

issue.body:
**Stacked on forge #18** (`bot/cfs-ci-coverage`, which makes test-49 build its own fixtures and run in CI). Until that lands, this PR also shows #18's three commits. Only the last commit is new.

test-49 pinned only bootc 1.16.0, which (like 1.16.1 and 1.16.2) reads only the bare `composefs=` and stages the V2 fallback of a dual-format UKI. 1.16.3 already reads `composefs.digest=` first but still generates V2, so switching to a dual-format UKI fails there ("The UKI has the wrong composefs= parameter"). 1.16.4 is the first release to generate V1 (composefs-rs 080f925), and on a repository it created itself it stages V1 directly; nothing tested that path. BLS installs weren't covered either; on those the old client writes the boot entry for the new image itself.

Not covered: 1.16.3, and 1.16.4-1.16.14 staging on a system installed by 1.16.0-1.16.3. The EROFS format comes from the repository's `meta.json` (V2 when absent) and is never converted, so with a UKI that case fails (bootc-dev/bootc#2334); BLS is not affected. The commit also updates `docs/src/bootc-composefs.7.md` to say which paths are tested.

The test now takes the stager version, the format it is expected to stage, and the install mode (`sealed`/`unsealed` UKI or `bls`). `just test-composefs-bridge MODE [1.16.0|1.16.4]` pins bootc-1.16.4-1.fc44 next to 1.16.0. It now reads the booted image's EROFS format from its composefs header instead of only inferring it from the UKI arguments, and that also works on BLS. CI gets two more bridge legs, 1.16.4 sealed UKI and 1.16.4 BLS (grub, ext4), for four in total.

Rebased onto main 3c5d235a. The docs edit moved to `bootc-composefs.7.md` (upstream split the composefs chapter out of the experimental one). issue.title: ci: Cover composefs upgrade paths (Fedora 44 upgrade, 1.16 bridge, btrfs)

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
CI didn't cover several composefs upgrade paths. This closes three of those gaps.

- **Fedora 44 composefs upgrade**: re-enabled. It was excluded (bb674f11) because the Fedora 44 base image's bootc hit the pull-then-GC deadlock from #2364. That was fixed in 1.16.8, and `fedora-bootc:44` now ships 1.16.10.
- **test-49 (1.16.0 UKI bridge)**: it needed hand-built fixture images, so nothing ran it. `just test-composefs-bridge sealed|unsealed` now builds them from the tree. The stager is the current UKI image with bootc swapped for the pinned 1.16.0 Koji RPM (checksum verified; the version-locked `bootc-tests` and `system-reinstall-bootc` are removed first, so the downgrade still gets dependency checks), and its initramfs and UKI are regenerated by 1.16.0. The target fails early unless the base is Fedora on x86_64. A new `test-composefs-bridge` job runs both modes on Fedora 44. It runs with the heavy jobs instead of nightly: it takes less time than an existing sealed UKI leg, and there is no scheduled CI workflow whose failures anyone would see.
- **btrfs**: one Fedora 44 composefs leg (sealed UKI, systemd-boot) running the same plans as the other sealed legs. It is added through a computed `include`, so it doesn't multiply the matrix.

**Cost** (full-suite runs only; `ci/tier-1` adds nothing): 4 more jobs, next to about 19 test-integration legs. From a recent merge-queue run: an upgrade leg takes about 20 min, and a sealed UKI integration leg about 50 min, which the btrfs leg should match. Each bridge leg is one build plus one 4-boot VM run: 24 min on a devspace, including the package build.

**Tested** on RHEL 10 devspaces, following the CI job steps (`just build-fetch` and the same `just` targets):

- `just test-upgrade` with Fedora 44 and composefs: passed (booted 1.16.10, upgraded, readonly suite);
- `just test-composefs-bridge unsealed` and `sealed`: 1.16.0 install (the test checked the binary's checksum), then switch, upgrade, rollback and `composefs-gc --assert-no-op`, all passed;
- `just test-composefs systemd btrfs uki sealed`: passed (plan-01-readonly and plan-24-image-upgrade-reboot, installed on btrfs);
- after the review fixes (stager downgrade without `--nodeps`, Fedora/x86_64 check, empty label context), `just test-composefs-bridge unsealed` and `sealed` passed again at this head;
- actionlint: the new job only gets the same notes the existing jobs already have (unknown `ubuntu-26.04` label, SC2129 style).

This backs the upgrade and btrfs claims in the composefs stabilization work (following #2483): once it lands, its limitations text no longer needs to say that btrfs is untested or that the bridge test and the Fedora 44 upgrade are not in CI.

`cargo xtask run-tmt --provision` now takes a list (`--provision=bcvk,reinstall`, or the flag repeated). The selected plans run through each path in turn, with one summary labelled by path, and the command fails if either path fails. A setup failure on one path is recorded as a failure and the other path still runs. Prerequisites and the reinstall path's ostree/BLS constraint are checked up front. issue.title: tests: Check that GC keeps a V2 rollback in the 1.16 bridge test

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

issue.body:
**Stacked on forge #30** (`bot/cfs-bridge-1164`, itself on #18). Until those land this PR also shows their commits; only the last commit is new.

test-49 never ran a repository GC while a 1.16.0 install's V2 deployment was the rollback of a V1 one, which is what every such system looks like right after its first upgrade with current bootc. Its only GC ran after the rollback, with the V2 deployment booted, and without `--prune-repo`, so it only looked at boot binaries and could not report a removed object.

With the upgrade booted, the test now runs `composefs-gc --prune-repo` (the GC upgrades run) and checks that the rollback's boot entry, deployment state and EROFS image (still V2) survive, and that `cfsctl fsck` and `cfsctl oci fsck` of the rollback's bootc tag pass. Then it rolls back as before, which proves the V2 deployment still boots. The final `--assert-no-op` now includes `--prune-repo`.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

**Tested** on a 16-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-37011656929), Fedora 44 base, `just test-composefs-bridge`:

- at this head: `unsealed 1.16.0`, `sealed 1.16.0` and `bls 1.16.4` all passed; the boot2 GC removed the 1.16.0 or 1.16.4 install's leftovers (53-56 objects) and fsck and `oci fsck` passed, and the final `--prune-repo --assert-no-op` found nothing;
- that it catches a regression (run at c191f09b, this check before the tag prefix became a constant): with GC temporarily changed to drop a rollback whose EROFS format differs from the booted one's, `unsealed 1.16.0` fails at the new boot2 check (GC removed the rollback's manifest, so `bootc status` can no longer read the rollback), while the test from #30's head passes against the same broken GC;
- dropping `additional_roots` for non-booted deployments alone is not caught, correctly: the V2 boot image is also reachable from the rollback's tagged manifest config, so nothing is lost.

Related: cgwalters-forge/tracker#259

labels.name: needs-human
