issue.body:
**Stacked on forge #18** (`bot/cfs-ci-coverage`, which makes test-49 build its own fixtures and run in CI). Until that lands, this PR also shows #18's three commits. Only the last commit is new.

test-49 pinned only bootc 1.16.0, which (like 1.16.1 and 1.16.2) reads only the bare `composefs=` and stages the V2 fallback of a dual-format UKI. 1.16.3 already reads `composefs.digest=` first but still generates V2, so switching to a dual-format UKI fails there ("The UKI has the wrong composefs= parameter"). 1.16.4 is the first release to generate V1 (composefs-rs 080f925), and on a repository it created itself it stages V1 directly; nothing tested that path. BLS installs weren't covered either; on those the old client writes the boot entry for the new image itself.

Not covered: 1.16.3, and 1.16.4-1.16.14 staging on a system installed by 1.16.0-1.16.3. The EROFS format comes from the repository's `meta.json` (V2 when absent) and is never converted, so with a UKI that case fails (bootc-dev/bootc#2334); BLS is not affected. The commit also updates `docs/src/bootc-composefs.7.md` to say which paths are tested.

The test now takes the stager version, the format it is expected to stage, and the install mode (`sealed`/`unsealed` UKI or `bls`). `just test-composefs-bridge MODE [1.16.0|1.16.4]` pins bootc-1.16.4-1.fc44 next to 1.16.0. It now reads the booted image's EROFS format from its composefs header instead of only inferring it from the UKI arguments, and that also works on BLS. CI gets two more bridge legs, 1.16.4 sealed UKI and 1.16.4 BLS (grub, ext4), for four in total.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Rebased onto main 3c5d235a. The docs edit moved to `bootc-composefs.7.md` (upstream split the composefs chapter out of the experimental one). Since upstream 0c2f4879 the composefs test images no longer ship ostree's `prepare-root.conf`, which every 1.16 `bootc install` requires ("Failed to find ostree/prepare-root.conf"), so the stager fixture now writes one; that fix is squashed into the fixture commit from #18. issue.title: ci: Bound apt transport recovery in example-test setup
issue.body: Part of tracker#1215; G3 in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/blob/main/docs/composefs-rs-ci-2026-11-03.md . Four eligible runs failed fetching packages from azure.archive.ubuntu.com before example tests (22/26 October and 1 November); two later recovered, with mutable inputs, so this is evidenced infra rather than a proven test flake. The current ci.yml example setup still fetches from that mirror. Implement bounded package-acquisition transport recovery, retaining permanent solver/package failures and exhausted errors. No broad job retry, mirror/suite migration, workflow enablement or permissions change. Deliver a draft PR with fault-injection tests and explicit repeated-run evidence or a disclosed runner/Actions gate.

comment.body:
**Still valid against current `forge` (f5aa0a2), and an implement run can take it. It needs no operator decision.** The [example setup](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/composefs-rs/blob/forge/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L226-L259) is unchanged, and it still runs plain `apt-get install`/`apt install`/`build-dep` against `azure.archive.ubuntu.com`. #65 was closed by cgwalters on 6 November without merging. I read that as a rejection of the separate Python harness, so the next attempt should not revive it.

I re-read two of the four [G3](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/blob/main/docs/composefs-rs-ci-2026-11-03.md#g3--new-issue-candidate-no-exact-covering-issue-found) jobs. In [22 Oct](https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/actions/runs/39805639946/job/119917998225), the plucky podman download ran at 27 kB/s for 22 minutes before `Remote end closed connection`. In [1 Nov](https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/actions/runs/41257977229/job/124705107214), the mirror IP was unreachable for about 2 minutes. Both logs are full of `Ign:` lines, which are apt's own per-file retries (6 in the first job, 241 in the second). So apt already retries per file. Adding `Acquire::Retries`, as the earlier verdict proposed, would change little. A retry at the step level after a pause is the part that's missing. `apt-get update` succeeded in every log.

Plan (one draft PR, examples job only):
1. Add a helper under 10 lines, e.g. `ci/apt-get-retry`. It runs `apt-get --download-only "$@"` up to 3 times with a 60s pause, and retries only when the output contains `Failed to fetch`/`Unable to fetch some archives`. It then runs `apt-get "$@"` once. That last run reports solver errors, missing packages and an exhausted download with their original errors. Downloaded files stay in `/var/cache/apt/archives`, so a retry picks up where the last one stopped.
2. Use the helper for the install steps at lines 231, 243 and 257, and give each of those steps a `timeout-minutes` (about 20) so a slow mirror like 22 Oct's hits a limit. Leave packages, suites, mirrors, permissions and `apt-get update` as they are, and add no retry for the whole job.
3. Check it locally: an unreachable proxy (`-o Acquire::http::Proxy=http://127.0.0.1:9`) should exhaust the retries and exit 100 with the original `E:` lines, a nonexistent package should fail once without a retry, a normal install should succeed, and `actionlint` should pass.

Two things are unclear. I can't show that a 60s pause would have outlasted the 1 Nov outage, so expect only a modest gain. And the example job can't be run here, because the fork's `ci.yml` is `disabled_manually`. The PR should say so plainly and rely on upstream PR CI to exercise it, rather than enable workflows. If the implement handback refuses `.github/` paths, the PR should carry the ci.yml hunk in its description for a maintainer to apply.

issue.title: composefs-rs: Fix OCI whiteout handling to follow the image spec (#8)
issue.body:
Repo: composefs/composefs-rs

Task: https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/issues/8. The layer-merging code applies whiteouts without following https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/layer.md: a whiteout must only apply to lower layers, a file in the same layer as a whiteout can only be hidden by a later layer's whiteout, and an opaque marker (`.wh..wh..opq`) is applied before the same layer's new entries regardless of tar order. Find the merge code, write failing tests first for each of the three rules (including entries ordered after the whiteout in the tar), then fix.

issue.title: composefs-rs: varlink Oci.Pull: accept registry options (auth file, cert dir, TLS verify)
issue.body:
Repo: composefs/composefs-rs

Task: Decided in tracker#113 (accepted): v1 `Pull` carries registry options. Today `crates/composefs-ctl/src/varlink.rs` `pull(...)` takes only image, name, local_fetch, storage_root, bootable, xattrs and expected_digest, so a client can't pull from an authenticated or private-CA registry. Add one optional `registry_options` parameter (a struct with `auth_file: Option<String>`, `cert_dir: Option<String>`, `tls_verify: Option<bool>`, all optional so absent means today's behaviour) and pass it into the `ImageProxyConfig` that `PullOptions` hands to skopeo/containers-image-proxy (check how `cfsctl oci pull` already sets auth and cert dir, and reuse it). Repo: composefs/composefs-rs

Task: https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/issues/8. The layer-merging code applies whiteouts without following https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/layer.md: a whiteout must only apply to lower layers, a file in the same layer as a whiteout can only be hidden by a later layer's whiteout, and an opaque marker (`.wh..wh..opq`) is applied before the same layer's new entries regardless of tar order. issue.title: composefs-rs: varlink Oci.Pull: accept registry options (auth file, cert dir, TLS verify)
issue.body:
Repo: composefs/composefs-rs

Task: Decided in tracker#113 (accepted): v1 `Pull` carries registry options. Today `crates/composefs-ctl/src/varlink.rs` `pull(...)` takes only image, name, local_fetch, storage_root, bootable, xattrs and expected_digest, so a client can't pull from an authenticated or private-CA registry. Add one optional `registry_options` parameter (a struct with `auth_file: Option<String>`, `cert_dir: Option<String>`, `tls_verify: Option<bool>`, all optional so absent means today's behaviour) and pass it into the `ImageProxyConfig` that `PullOptions` hands to skopeo/containers-image-proxy (check how `cfsctl oci pull` already sets auth and cert dir, and reuse it). Paths are read by the service as the calling uid, which is the v1 model (same-uid subprocess), so no extra access check. Update the introspection/IDL test and any checked-in IDL that exists on main.

issue.title: composefs-rs: Fix OCI whiteout handling to follow the image spec (#8)
issue.body:
Repo: composefs/composefs-rs

Task: https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/issues/8. The layer-merging code applies whiteouts without following https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/layer.md: a whiteout must only apply to lower layers, a file in the same layer as a whiteout can only be hidden by a later layer's whiteout, and an opaque marker (`.wh..wh..opq`) is applied before the same layer's new entries regardless of tar order. Find the merge code, write failing tests first for each of the three rules (including entries ordered after the whiteout in the tar), then fix.

Acceptance: new data-driven tests for same-layer and cross-layer whiteout/opaque cases fail before and pass after; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo test --workspace` pass.

issue.title: varlink: Validate repository paths, names and received fd types (milestone B, slice 5)
issue.body:
Part of epic cgwalters-forge/tracker#160, milestone B (varlink API v1), slice 5 of the research in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/14#issuecomment-6233284561. This is a staged PR for the fork; nothing is posted upstream. It stacks on the repository-locking slice, which changes the same open path.

On upstream main 0f9e1f0, the varlink server in `crates/composefs-ctl/src/varlink.rs` checks only the count of received fds: `PutLayer` (L1705-L1720) treats `fds[0]` as a pipe and the rest as directories without checking either. Repository paths, ref names and image names from clients are passed on without a check against traversal.

Task: reject relative repository paths and names containing `..` components or NUL, with the interface's invalid-parameter replies; check each received fd's type with `fstat` (pipe or directory, as the method expects) and name the index of a wrong one; confirm received fds are close-on-exec and set it if zlink does not.

Acceptance: table-driven regression tests for traversal names, a relative path, a regular file where a directory fd is expected and a directory where the pipe is expected. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace --exclude composefs-integration-tests` pass.

issue.title: Make the Rust CLIs match composefs-c's command-line contract (milestone A, slice 1)
issue.body:
Moved from cgwalters-forge/tracker#704 (epic cgwalters-forge/tracker#160). This is a staged PR for the fork; nothing is posted upstream.

From the milestone A research in cgwalters-forge/tracker#698 (https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/tracker/issues/698#issuecomment-6233282976), read against upstream main f5aa0a2. Re-checked on 22 Oct against upstream 3280e06: the gaps are unchanged.

Task: fix the interface gaps that stop the Rust tools from being a drop-in for composefs-c:
- `composefs-info`: accept `--filter` and `--basedir` as global options, as C does (`composefs-info --filter=NAME dump IMAGE` is rejected today). Make `cmd_dump` honour the filter it currently ignores. Reject missing image/file operands instead of succeeding with no output.
- `mount.composefs`: reject malformed colon-separated basedir lists, as C does. `-h` exits 0.
- `mkcomposefs`: enforce `max_version` in image generation. Reject `--threads=0`, as C does.
- Command-line parse errors exit 1, as C's tools do (clap's default is 2).
- Update `man/composefs-info.md` and the other manuals so their options and exit status match the code.

Acceptance: differential tests (success, error and output) for each case above. C's `check-dump-filtered` and `check-should-fail` (which requires exit status exactly 1) pass against the Rust executables. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and the unprivileged tests pass.

labels.name: review:deep

issue.body:
Add an optional `registry_options` (`auth_file`, `cert_dir`, `tls_verify`) to varlink `Oci.Pull`, passed into the `ImageProxyConfig` used for the skopeo proxy. Omitting it keeps today's behaviour. It also touches composefs-oci and re-exports `ImageProxyConfig` from it so composefs-ctl can build the config. This is the first place these options are set; `cfsctl oci pull` sets none of them. Decided in tracker#113.

review.body:
VERDICT: CHANGES — the live workflow's authentication prerequisite is not deployed.

Reviewed head: `0c396c9a7a62f50504f9c53f1aa5920ad4981068` (against merge base `39c4ff5e06c1377749a3f792d80abfaabd8fbc04` on `origin/main`).

- [blocker] **Deploy the Octo-STS policy before enabling live runs** — `.github/workflows/renovate.yml:28–33`. The organization policy directory currently contains only `control-plane.sts.yaml`; `renovate.sts.yaml` is absent, and cgwalters-forge/.github#5 is still open and unmerged. Consequently every scheduled or manually dispatched main-branch run fails at the token exchange, before reaching Renovate. The later token fallback cannot recover from a failed step. Land the prerequisite policy first and confirm its subject and workflow claims restrict issuance to this repository's main-branch Renovate workflow. As admitted, the daily updater cannot perform its main purpose.

- [important] **Pin the executable Renovate image, not just its launcher** — `.github/workflows/renovate.yml:58–66`. The pinned action's `action.yml` and `src/docker.ts` default to `ghcr.io/renovatebot/renovate:44`; no image override is supplied here. That mutable tag determines the code receiving the live installation token, so replacing the image can change organization-wide write-capable code without any change to the reviewed action SHA. Supply an immutable image digest through `renovate-image` and arrange reviewed updates to it. The worst outcome is a compromised image stealing the installation token and writing repository contents/workflows wherever that token is authorized; the first-party repository filter does not constrain a stolen credential.

Boundary assessment: the non-PR/main condition prevents the normal PR path from invoking the exchange, non-live configuration selects a full dry run, checkout does not persist credentials, and repository discovery selects only unarchived first-party entries. Those bounds constrain ordinary execution, but do not prevent a compromised live container from using its token outside the selected list. No existing test suites, formatters, linters, or CI results were run or consulted.

VERDICT: CHANGES — repository discovery does not enforce the first-party boundary.

Reviewed admitted head: c80968f8960b6de92980a663a5b15c84ba646a72 (merge base: 39c4ff5e06c1377749a3f792d80abfaabd8fbc04).

- **blocker** — `.github/workflows/renovate.yml:41`: The REST search endpoint does not apply this custom-property qualifier. A focused read-only probe of the exact query returned 14 repositories, including `cgwalters-forge/base-images`; that repository's properties endpoint reports `origin=mirror`. Replacing the value with `props.origin:nonexistent-review-probe` still returned the same 14 repositories. Consequently, once STS is available, this workflow passes mirrors to the live org-wide writer and can create onboarding branches/PRs in repositories explicitly excluded by the checklist. `renovate/config.js:16` only excludes GitHub forks, not ordinary repositories used as mirrors. Enumerate repositories and explicitly check their actual custom-property values before passing them to Renovate; fail closed when properties cannot be read. Add coverage for first-party, mirror, fork and unset values rather than relying on search accepting the query.

- **important** — `.github/workflows/renovate.yml:30–33`: The live authentication prerequisite is not yet installed. At review time, the contents API returned 404 for `cgwalters-forge/.github`'s `.github/chainguard/renovate.sts.yaml` on `main`, and the referenced policy PR #5 was open/unmerged. A scheduled main run will attempt the exchange and fail at this step, rather than reach the advertised daily updates. Land the narrowly scoped trust policy before enabling this workflow, and make this merge dependency explicit.

- **important** — `.github/workflows/renovate.yml:41`: Discovery silently truncates at 100 results and never checks `total_count` or `incomplete_results`. As the organization grows, repositories beyond the first page will receive no updates while the job succeeds. Preserve pagination and completeness checks when replacing the unsupported property search, with coverage for more than one page.

Security bounds: the worst merged outcome here is organization-wide content/workflow writes outside the intended repository scope; the discovery bug means that scope is not currently enforced. The main-only token-step condition and the proposed STS policy's exact repository/main/workflow claims bound direct token issuance from PR runs, and checkout does not persist credentials. Neither restriction fixes which repositories the live main run can write. No existing test suite, formatter, linter or CI-result lookup was run; the probes above were read-only API requests directed at these specific concerns.

its pace. Until per-pool holds come from the snapshot (agent-board#233),
let fix rounds use claude only with a margin that matches its burst.

marginPercent back to 5).

body.title: plan: agenthome renders one templated role prompt per agent tool, with evals, for tiered-model runs (agentic-job#1367)

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Focus-area epic: its sub-issues are the work

body.body:
Goal: put the tiered-model work of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/agentic-job/issues/1367 in agenthome, as the operator asked there on 2026-10-19 at 22:43Z: one templated prompt per role (explore, plan, execute lead, worker, review), rendered for each agent tool, with evals before anything depends on it.

Evidence:
- agenthome holds only opencode's form today: opencode/opencode.json (GPT-6 tiers per sub-agent role on the OpenAI pool), opencode/AGENTS.md and skills/. Nothing renders the same roles for another tool.
- agentic-job#1367's follow-up proposes tier names (astra, sol, terra, luna) mapped per pool in configuration, never model names in prompts.
- No agenthome issue covers this (agenthome#2 and #16 are pins and misctool).

Steps, each its own pull request in agenthome:
1. Templates: a roles/ directory with one prompt template per role that names tiers only, and a small Node renderer (beside scripts/) that writes opencode's agent entries and AGENTS.md and the Claude Code form (CLAUDE.md plus agents/*.md). Rendered files are checked in; just check fails when they drift from the templates.
2. Tier map: a per-pool table (tier to model, with declared fallbacks) that the renderer reads, so templates never name a model. Agree the table's single home with agentic-job#1367's [models.tiers] proposal, so agenthome and agentic-job read one source.
3. Evals: a small fixed set of two or three real fix-round or small-implement tasks from our history, each run three ways (single strong model, single cheap model, explore then plan then execute by tier), recording tokens, cache hits, wall time and outcome. A research run sizes the set first; the report goes in agenthome's docs.
4. Adopt: point tracker's caller at the rendered configuration for one task class, only if step 3 shows a win.

Proof: just check passes with renders matching the templates in both tool forms; the eval report links its runs and compares the three arms on the same tasks.

Out of scope: the broker and agentic-job's run token, which stay with agentic-job#1367's questions 1 and 2.

items.title: release: Prepare digest signing and scoped verification
items.body:
## Executive summary

Prepare key-based image verification so downstream builds can authenticate an exact base digest before FROM. Add a checksum-pinned cosign v3.1.4 signing/verification helper, the candidate public key, inactive repository-scoped containers/image examples, and docs/signing.md. Enforcement stays off by default; derived images retain their own signing policy.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/issues/46

Depends on: cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox#38

The base/variant split merged in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/atomic-linux-sandbox/pull/54, but per-variant CI/promotion remains incomplete. This run cannot edit protected .github/ paths or AGENTS.md, so workflow integration and its stale credential guidance are deliberately omitted, not bypassed. No image publication or credential-bearing workflow was triggered.

The future caller must retain contents: read and packages: write, pass only the existing signing secrets to trusted main promotion, and sign/verify every tested variant digest before release tags advance, preserving VM/config gates, the stale-main guard and stable-last ordering. No permissions, action pins or release tags change here. The helper pins the cosign binary by verified release checksum and uses legacy .sig attachments with --new-bundle-format=false --use-signing-config=false; signing/key mismatch or verification failure exits nonzero. ## Executive summary

The image's bootc install config listed no block setups, so bootc 1.17 allowed only `direct` and refused `--block-setup tpm2-luks`. It now permits `tpm2-luks`, with `direct` still the default, so the layout is still chosen only by install options. docs/install.md shows how to install with a LUKS2 root unlocked by the TPM and how to add a separate encrypted data volume for `/var/home` and VM storage, so the root can be reinstalled without touching data. A new image test checks that the install config permits `tpm2-luks` and that the initramfs can unlock with the TPM. This guards against a later change of base image or an initramfs rebuild silently breaking unlock.

## More detail

The docs point out two limits of the key bootc enrolls with systemd 259: there is no recovery key, and the key is sealed to no PCRs. So it protects a removed disk, not a stolen machine. They then show how to enroll a recovery key, bind the key to PCR 7 and drop `headless=true` so the recovery prompt can appear. bcvk's `to-disk` has no `--block-setup` option and no TPM, so the bcvk rehearsal covers only the partition layout.

items.title: runner: Isolate job VMs on a bridge with an egress allowlist
items.body:
## Executive summary

CI jobs run untrusted code in per-job VMs, so they should not be able to reach the LAN, the tailnet, link-local metadata addresses or the host's own services. This adds `runner-network.service`: a dedicated `runnerbr0` bridge and an `inet runner_network` nftables table that let job VMs reach only DNS on the listed resolvers and an allowlist from `/etc/atomic-linux/runner-network.conf`; everything else, private ranges and the host included, is dropped. The unit is enabled but skipped until that file exists, and no addresses are baked in. A firewalld `runner` zone accepts the bridge so the table alone decides. docs/runner-network.md describes the config and the rules.

Part of #41. Part of #26.

## Verification

`just lint` (now also shellchecks the new script) and `just fmt-check` pass. `just build`, and so `just image-test` (which runs the new `nft -c -f` check of the example config) and `bootc container lint`, could not run: containers fail to start in this sandbox (crun sd-bus error), and nft needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, which isn't available here either. The ruleset syntax was only checked by reading it, and the config-refusal half of the test passed when run directly on the host. No VM test of actual traffic yet.

One review pass found no blockers. Its important findings were fixed: load the rules before creating the bridge, reload without detaching VMs, refuse prefixes with host bits set, drop spoofed sources, and correct the docs. Still open: a VM test that probes allowed and denied destinations through firewalld, and whether NetworkManager should be told to leave `runnerbr0` unmanaged.

Closes #41

items.title: runner: Ship a virtualization host stack for per-job VMs

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

items.body:
## Executive summary

The image's main job is to host CI jobs in fresh per-job VMs. This adds the virtualization stack through a new package drop-in: libvirt with only its QEMU and network drivers, QEMU with OVMF, swtpm, virtiofsd, bcvk, podman and nftables.

Fedora's VM guest agents are turned off with a systemd preset, because a plain `systemctl disable` would be undone by first-boot preset-all. `build/10-build.sh` now applies the image's own presets at build time. `ci-runner.service` is a disabled hook for an externally built runner daemon. `subids@<user>.service` gives a sysusers account subuid and subgid ranges for rootless podman, since sysusers assigns none. Both hooks are documented in the README.

## Verification

`just lint` and `just fmt-check` pass, and `systemd-analyze verify` reports nothing on the new units beyond the absent daemon binary and helper. `just build`, `just image-test`, `just hadolint` and `bootc container lint` were not run: no container can start in this sandbox (crun fails with an sd-bus error), so CI's build is the first real run. The new `tests/image/virt-host.sh` has never been run, and CI does not run `image-test` yet. No VM recipes were run.

## Follow-ups

One review pass found no blockers. It left these important findings open:

- The preset stops `qemu-guest-agent` from being enabled, but inside a VM with the guest-agent channel, its udev rule still starts it. Masking the agents or removing the packages would close this.
- Fedora's preset enables `virtqemud.service` at boot on every derived host, not only through socket activation.
- `ci-runner.service` runs with no systemd user manager, and its `RuntimeDirectory` is mode 0755. Rootless podman falls back to cgroupfs here, and `RuntimeDirectoryMode=0700` is probably wanted.
- The workflow's own shellcheck line does not cover `subids-add`.

Build and test cgwalters-forge/rpm-ostree#15 (RPM v6 importer) in the CI buildroot (Fedora 45, RPM 6.1.0), and hand back two patches to apply on top of its head with `git am`.

The PR builds and `make check` passes. Comparing imports by `main` and by the PR, over 26 Fedora packages and paired v4/v6 test packages, found that any package containing a socket failed to import. 0001 fixes that and extends the v4/v6 test to catch it. 0002 makes the test pass on non-x86_64 too. `main` fails on v6 packages and on v4 packages with a file over 4 GiB, and the PR imports both identically.

work/rpm-ostree-5657/RESULTS.md has the details, including what wasn't tested: sanitizers (that build is broken upstream), end-to-end compose/layering, and other architectures.

items.title: site: Port from Zola to Zensical
items.body:
## Executive summary

Port the organization site from Zola to Zensical 0.1.1, pinned with hashes in `site-requirements.txt`, so it builds the same way as our other docs sites (tracker#1724). Every page keeps its URL. The hand-written homepage is copied unchanged, apart from its feed link's type. Posts move to `content/blog/posts/` with YAML front matter, because the blog plugin needs both. The internal link check is now lychee.

**This needs the `site.yml` change below before it can merge.** This run cannot hand back files under `.github/` or `.gitignore`, so until someone applies that diff to this branch, CI still runs `zola build` and fails.

## More detail

Before and after, the build has 7 pages (the homepage, `/blog/`, and five posts) plus `404.html`, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. No page changed URL. `/blog/atom.xml` stays at the same URL but now serves RSS 2.0 with every post in full. The new build also writes `/feed_rss_updated.xml`, an empty `/search.json` and the theme's `/assets/`. The sitemap no longer lists `/`, because the homepage is a static file. Blog pages use the Zensical theme instead of the old templates. A one-block override keeps the "LLM generated" notice and the feed link on every page. Web fonts and search are off, and external links keep `rel="nofollow noreferrer"`.

Verified locally: `zensical build --strict`, the lychee command below (0 errors, and it fails on a broken page or anchor), and `tests/test_home.py` all pass. The URL list matches the Zola 0.23.6 build of the base commit.

The `.github/workflows/site.yml` change to apply to this branch:

```diff
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
-# Builds the site with Zola and checks its internal links on every pull
+# Builds the site with Zensical and checks its internal links on every pull
@@ -23,10 +23,11 @@ concurrency:
+# Zensical is pinned with hashes in site-requirements.txt.
 env:
-  ZOLA_VERSION: 0.23.6
+  LYCHEE_VERSION: 0.24.2
   # The release asset's digest as GitHub lists it.
-  ZOLA_SHA256: 8f5132b3522412d04e395e0b25f6d68613ad272a873e54a2b3ebf664873024a4
+  LYCHEE_SHA256: 1f4e0ef7f6554a6ed33dd7ac144fb2e1bbed98598e7af973042fc5cd43951c9a
@@ -41,17 +42,22 @@ jobs:
-      - name: Install Zola
+      - name: Install Zensical
         run: |
-          tarball="$RUNNER_TEMP/zola.tar.gz"
+          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/zensical"
+          "$RUNNER_TEMP/zensical/bin/pip" install --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: -r site-requirements.txt
+          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/zensical/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
+      - name: Install lychee
+        run: |
+          tarball="$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee.tar.gz"
           curl -fsSL --proto '=https' -o "$tarball" \
-            "https://github.com/getzola/zola/releases/download/v${ZOLA_VERSION}/zola-v${ZOLA_VERSION}-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
-          echo "${ZOLA_SHA256}  ${tarball}" | sha256sum -c -
-          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/zola"
-          tar -xzf "$tarball" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/zola"
-          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/zola" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
-      # Posts are written by agent runs, and Zola renders inline HTML as it
-      # is, on an origin that other pages trust (tracker#917). So a post may
+            "https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-v${LYCHEE_VERSION}/lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
+          echo "${LYCHEE_SHA256}  ${tarball}" | sha256sum -c -
+          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee"
+          tar -xzf "$tarball" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee" --strip-components=1
+          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
+      # Posts are written by agent runs, and Zensical renders inline HTML as
+      # it is, on an origin that other pages trust (tracker#917). So a post may
@@ -131,10 +137,10 @@ jobs:
-      - run: zola build
+      - run: zensical build --strict
       # Internal links and anchors only: the posts link to many GitHub
       # pages, which are slow and rate-limited to check on every change.
-      - run: zola check --skip-external-links
+      - run: lychee --offline --root-dir "$PWD/public" --index-files index.html --include-fragments --no-progress public
```

Also add `.cache/` to `.gitignore`, because `zensical build` writes it at the repository root.

Follow-ups:

- The `/blog/` page now renders each post in full, not a dated list of titles. The usual excerpt marker is raw HTML, which CI refuses.
- CI does not yet fail on a post outside `posts/` or with TOML front matter. Such a post builds green but renders wrong.
- `site-requirements.txt` hashes only the CPython 3.14 x86_64 wheels.

Review: one pass found no blocker, given the caller change below. I fixed its important findings: web fonts, a truncated feed, and the missing feed link. The `/blog/` listing and the CI post-path check are still open.

## Caller settings

The weekly post writer still targets the old path and format. Merge this change and update the caller together:

- Repository: `cgwalters-forge/tracker`
- File: `.github/weekly-digest.json`
- Key: `task`. Change the sentence that starts "Add one file, content/blog/{week}.md, with TOML front matter" so it names `content/blog/posts/{week}.md`, with YAML front matter giving `title: "Week ending {week}"` and `date: {week}`.
- Key: `brief`. Change `content/blog/{week}.md` to `content/blog/posts/{week}.md`.

Closes #17

items.title: static-checks: Add a repository hygiene action, starting with LICENSE

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

items.body:
## Executive summary

Several public, non-fork repositories in the orgs have no license file. This adds a `static-checks` composite action that runs a table of named, offline checks over a checked-out tree. Later checks such as SECURITY.md or CODEOWNERS are new table entries. The first check, `license`, requires a top-level LICENSE, LICENSE-* or COPYING file whose text askalono recognizes as an SPDX license. A `license` field in Cargo.toml or package.json, when present, must name the same licenses: LICENSE-APACHE plus LICENSE-MIT matches `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`. askalono 0.5.0 is downloaded at a pinned version and checked against a sha256 hard-coded in the action. The check itself is a Node script that uses only the standard library: this repository ships no Rust crate, only the setup-rust action.

A check can be skipped only with a reason committed in the checked repository's `.github/static-checks.toml` (`[skip]` with `name = "reason"` lines). That way exceptions show up in review, and they also work for ruleset-required runs, which get no inputs. Listing a check in the `skip` input without a recorded reason fails. The action prints one pass/fail/skip line per check with a fix hint, and writes a job summary table. The README documents the inputs, the exception file, and how to scope an org ruleset with a custom repository property, since rulesets can't target non-forks directly.

## Files to add by hand

This change could not include files under `.github/`, so the reusable workflow and the CI job are below for a maintainer to add. The README already describes the workflow. It uses major tags such as `actions/checkout@v7`, which Renovate updates, following the existing workflows here rather than SHA pins. In another repository, and in ruleset-required runs, a relative `uses: ./static-checks` would resolve against the caller's checkout. So the workflow uses `bootc-dev/actions/static-checks@main` everywhere except in bootc-dev/actions itself. Its job is skipped in forks.

`.github/workflows/static-checks.yml`:

```yaml
# Repository hygiene checks, meant to be required org-wide via a ruleset
# (see README.md). Callers and ruleset-required runs use the action from
# bootc-dev/actions main; this repository tests its own copy.
name: Static checks
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      checks:
        description: 'Comma-separated checks to run, or "all"'
        type: string
        default: 'all'
      skip:
        description: 'Comma-separated checks to skip; each needs a reason in .github/static-checks.toml'
        type: string
        default: ''
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  # Ruleset-required workflows must report in merge queues too.
  merge_group:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  static-checks:
    name: Static checks
    # Forks inherit their source's hygiene; skipped jobs satisfy required checks.
    if: ${{ !github.event.repository.fork }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run static checks (this repository)
        if: github.repository == 'bootc-dev/actions'
        uses: ./static-checks
        with:
          checks: ${{ inputs.checks || 'all' }}
          skip: ${{ inputs.skip }}

      - name: Run static checks
        if: github.repository != 'bootc-dev/actions'
        uses: bootc-dev/actions/static-checks@main
        with:
          checks: ${{ inputs.checks || 'all' }}
          skip: ${{ inputs.skip }}
```

Add this job to `.github/workflows/test-actions-pr.yml`. It also checks this repository itself:

```yaml
  test-static-checks:
    name: Test static-checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./static-checks
      - run: node test/static-checks.js
        env:
          ASKALONO: ${{ runner.temp }}/askalono/askalono
```

## Verification and follow-ups

I ran `node test/static-checks.js` locally with the pinned askalono, and all 8 cases passed. The cases are this repository, no license, unrecognized text, Apache-2.0 with package.json, dual MIT/Apache with Cargo.toml, a Cargo.toml mismatch, a skip with a reason and a skip without one. The test builds its fixture trees in a temporary directory, because a committed tree can't contain its own `.github/`. I also ran the action's install step by hand, and it rejects a wrong checksum. Neither workflow above has run in CI.

One review pass ran and found no blockers. I fixed merge_group support, the skip-without-reason test, directories named like license files, per-check errors and annotation escaping. Left as follow-ups:
- Top-level files like LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY must also be recognized licenses; there is no ignore list.
- Unknown keys under `[skip]` are silently ignored.
- The `@main` path isn't covered by test-actions-published.yml.
- A repository that both calls the workflow and is covered by the ruleset runs it twice.

Part of https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc-dev-actions/issues/6

Closes #6

items.title: prepare-root: Fix build with Amazon Linux 2023 headers
items.body:
## Executive summary

prepare-root fails to build on Amazon Linux 2023 (ostreedev/ostree#3696). With glibc 2.34 there, the `<linux/mount.h>` pulled in by `<linux/btrfs.h>` defines MS_* macros that break glibc's `<sys/mount.h>` enum. This change includes `<sys/mount.h>` first. It also teaches `ci/gh-install.sh` to set up AL2023 containers (the srpm builddeps plus test helpers) so the container test matrix can cover AL2023.

Verified in an AL2023 rootfs (podman containers don't start in this sandbox, so I used an exported image rootfs under `podman unshare` + chroot). I reproduced the reported error with the old include order. With this change, the CI job's own steps pass: `gh-install.sh`, then `gh-build.sh --without-selinux` as the unprivileged `builder` user (build, make check with 949 pass/38 skip, distcheck, install). Not verified: an actual GitHub Actions run.

The matrix entry is **not** in this diff, because this run can't change `.github/`. Add it to `.github/workflows/tests.yml` at the end of the `tests` matrix `include:` list:

```yaml
          # Amazon Linux 2023 has glibc 2.34 with new kernel headers,
          # which catches <sys/mount.h> vs <linux/mount.h> conflicts.
          #
          # https://gallery.ecr.aws/amazonlinux/amazonlinux
          - name: Amazon Linux 2023
            image: public.ecr.aws/amazonlinux/amazonlinux:2023
            pre-checkout-setup: |
              dnf -y install git
            # The build dependencies install an SELinux policy, so the
            # libarchive SELinux test would try to set security.selinux
            # as the unprivileged builder user and fail.
            configure-options: >-
              --without-selinux
```

Without `--without-selinux`, `/libarchive/selinux` fails: AL2023's build deps hard-require selinux-policy-targeted, so the test runs and gets EPERM setting security.selinux as a non-root user.

Review: one pass with no blockers. Its libsoup3/bubblewrap/gjs suggestions are applied. The gnupg2 and SELinux handling came after that pass, from test runs.

Part of #8

items.title: secure-host: Pin actions with the v0.6.14 image
items.body:
## Executive summary

**Do not merge this alone.** Once it lands, agent jobs that don't pass `secure-host-image-artifact-id` (agentic-job.yml, review.yml, example-compose.yml) get v0.6.14's standalone setup without `sandbox prepare`. That leaves no agents and no helper on the host, so every production agent run fails. #2656 is written to follow this pin, and #2070 says only #2656 may change that gating. Land #2656's agent.yml change together with this (on this branch or in the same merge window), or keep this as a draft until #2656 is ready.

The forwarder and site.yml move from actions 466a490 (v0.6.9) to actions main 6e720e9 (actions#271). 6e720e9 pins `secure-host:v0.6.14@sha256:02e5f14f...2a42`, attested from source 489c69d, the v0.6.14 tag. Its `secure-host/action.yml` is the same blob as at 466a490, so the forwarder's inputs are unchanged. The `secure-host-published` step no longer excuses the legacy deployment: the image must report `secure-host 0.6.14` under both names, with identical bytes, and pass the action's compatibility calls. The forwarder test's floor is now v0.6.14. The docs and the action comment now describe v0.6.14, which makes no second user. #3333 touches only action.yml's default-config path, so the two don't conflict.

Verification: `cargo test -p agentic-job --test workflows -- published_path the_public_secure_host`, `just fmt` and `just check` all exit 0. Not verified: Ubuntu `secure-host-published` setup/check and published-path agent E2E on this pin, which run only on push to main; RHEL is pending as well. Left for #2656: the `[sandbox]`/`[host]` accommodation and its comments in agent.yml, compose.rs and stable-interfaces.md, which still describe the old image.

Review: two passes. The first found the merge-order blocker above, which is left open for #2656.

items.title: initramfs: Read setup-root policy from the mounted image
items.body:
## Executive summary
Read setup-root configuration from the selected composefs image, sharing the reader with offline mounts, so soft reboot honors the staged image's policy instead of defaults. items.title: storage: Don't tag ostree symlinked mount points as discoverable
items.body:
## Executive summary

Fedora Silverblue systems with a separate /home partition boot into rescue mode since ostree 2026.3 (Fedora bug 2520626). Blivet gives a new GPT partition the Discoverable Partitions type of its mount point when `gpt_discoverable_partitions` is enabled, and anaconda.conf enables it. So /home gets the home type. Now that systemd-gpt-auto-generator can find the root disk, it generates home.mount for /home. On ostree /home is a symlink, so systemd refuses that mount.

For rpm-ostree and bootc payloads, new partitions that would get the home or srv discoverable type now get the generic Linux type instead. Existing partitions and explicitly requested types are left alone. The storage layout task learns the payload type from the Payloads service, the same way SystemdBoot already does, because the generic InstallWithTasks DBus method takes no arguments.

As the issue asked, fstab now also gets the canonical path (/home becomes /var/home). Each mount point is resolved inside the deployment, not the installer's root. The ostree bind mounts use the same resolver instead of os.path.realpath(). Absolute link targets are resolved against the deployment, as in the booted system, so they can't point outside it. A relative link that climbs out of the deployment is refused with an error.

## More detail

The fstab path alone doesn't stop the generator. It never reads fstab for /home or /srv. It only skips a path that is already a mount point or a non-empty directory, and fstab-generator names the unit var-home.mount either way, so the two units never collide. The partition type is the actual fix.

Existing installs keep their home-typed partition. They need `systemd.gpt_auto=0`, or the partition retyped to the generic Linux type (`sfdisk --part-type <disk> <n> 0FC63DAF-8483-4772-8E79-3D69D8477DE4`), or a fix on the ostree side. This PR documents that and doesn't build a migration.

Verified with the storage, payloads, core and modules/common unit tests in the anaconda-ci fedora-rawhide image: 1482 passed. The 4 failures in test_dnf_initialization.py also fail on the base commit. ruff is clean on the changed files.

One review pass ran with no blockers. Follow-ups it left open:
- The partition type test uses mock devices instead of a real blivet PartitionDevice on a GPT disk.
- The fstab test calls the helper directly instead of going through `_write_storage_configuration`.
- A mount point that resolves to `/`, or two that resolve to the same path, isn't rejected.
- `get_active_payload_type()` has no test of its own.
- `OSTREE_SYMLINKED_MOUNT_POINTS` lists paths that have no discoverable type today.

Closes #1

items.title: composefs-ctl: Test root-free varlink error replies
items.body:
## Executive summary

Add in-crate, root-free error-reply tests so regressions to generic errors are caught without privileged integration tests. Extract the useful dispatch tests and local-layout BootImageMismatch fixture from #22 (45dfa3557114776dd9cdc9ac0bc5b8acca0e556b), retaining current main interfaces and all existing layer-sync tests. This supersedes #22 without closing or editing it; no interface rename, OciTransfer split, registry options, workflows or approval boundaries change.

Use the existing Rust interface/error doc comments as the contract. Correct malformed digests to InvalidDigest (including mount), incorrect OCI mount FD counts to InvalidRequest, and typed missing images/refs to NoSuchImage/NoSuchRef; share the existing typed OCI absence mapping rather than classifying arbitrary I/O errors. No new option or control is added.

## Method / variant inventory

All handle-taking Repository and Oci methods are exercised through generated dispatch with both unknown and closed handles, asserting the interface-qualified InvalidHandle and exact handle payload, under SHA-256 and SHA-512. The following covers each method and its run_* helper, including nested layer helpers:

| Interface / methods | Additional coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Repository InitRepository, EnsureRepository | InvalidSpec for bad algorithms; InternalError for blocked parent paths; init mismatch; default algorithm; init and ensure idempotence (Created then Opened) |
| OpenRepository | InvalidSpec for absent/conflicting selectors; RepoNotFound for missing repository; valid explicit path and algorithm metadata |
| CloseRepository | Close, repeated close and monotonically newer reopened handle |
| Fsck, Gc, ListImageRefs | InternalError from damaged refs directory; both fsck modes and GC dry-run/real branches |
| ImageObjects, Mount | NoSuchRef for missing ref; InternalError for malformed ref; Mount InvalidSpec with wrong overlay/non-overlay FD counts |
| Oci GetInfo | Advertised capability tokens; no error-producing path |
| ListImages, Check | InternalError from damaged stream refs; missing-image Check is a successful reply reporting corruption, not a wire error |
| Inspect, ComputeId, OciMount | InvalidDigest; NoSuchImage for missing named ref; InternalError for damaged refs and missing digest-backed streams |
| Tag, Untag | Tag InvalidDigest; InternalError for absent tag/manifest |
| Pull | InvalidHandle, InvalidRequest for incompatible expected-digest options, InvalidDigest, InternalError for absent local layout, terminal BootImageMismatch after progress with exact expected/tried payload |
| HasLayer, GetLayer, PutLayer | InvalidDigest, InternalError; GetLayer/PutLayer InvalidRequest; existing layer-sync NoSuchLayer and DiffIdMismatch tests preserved |
| FinalizeImage | InvalidDigest for diff-id and layer verity; InternalError for invalid manifest/config; existing successful round-trip retained |

OCI mount InvalidRequest and missing boot EROFS InternalError are also tested at helper level using the existing finalized-image fixture, without a mount syscall. All five Repository variants and eight reachable Oci variants have root-free coverage.

## Limits and contract questions

Oci RepoNotFound has no producer: repositories are opened by Repository, and Oci only looks up handles. Oci FdLimitExceeded cannot be reached through this repository service: RepoLayerSource supplies one real directory, so the sparse layout totals at most seven FDs, below the 240-FD cap (layer_transport.rs and splitdirfdstream transport.rs). Neither is falsely claimed covered by constructing an error value. Successful mounts require privileges and are not attempted. Panic/task-join and resource-exhaustion branches are not injected; their InternalError variant is covered by ordinary I/O failures.

Ambiguous mappings are left for contract review: missing digest-backed streams produce untyped I/O before the library's typed image-absence check; Inspect/OciMount therefore return InternalError, and ComputeId's digest means a config rather than a manifest. OciMount previously labeled every open failure NoSuchImage; it now preserves typed absence and uses InternalError for other failures. Tag/Untag absence and invalid FinalizeImage content remain InternalError because method docs do not establish finer semantics. No new absence or validation semantics are invented.

## Verification

Formatting passes. composefs-ctl tests pass with defaults, --no-default-features, and --no-default-features --features oci (including the existing NoSuchLayer/DiffIdMismatch tests). Required workspace clippy/tests, with and without --features oci, all exit 101 before compilation: test-with/test-with-derive 0.17.2 require Rust 1.95, runner is 1.93.1; unchanged base f5aa0a2 fails identically. Supplemental clippy with --ignore-rust-version passes in both configurations. Supplemental workspace tests with --ignore-rust-version, both configurations and unchanged base, all reach the same 219 passed / 10 failed / 8 existing ignores in composefs, then stop at that failed test target. No tests were disabled or newly ignored.

Actual failing tests: erofs::reader::tests::test_pr188_empty_inline_directory (mkcomposefs missing); fsverity::ioctl::tests::test_measure_verity_opt and fsverity::tests::test_verity_missing (VerityMissing expectation assertions); fsverity::tests::{crosscheck_interesting_cases,test_enable_verity_maybe_copy_with_copy,test_enable_verity_maybe_copy_without_copy,test_verity_forking,test_verity_simple,test_verity_wrongdigest_sha256_sha512,test_verity_wrongdigest_sha512_sha256} (explicit FilesystemNotSupported errors). These are not all attributed to fs-verity.

Review: one adversarial pass, no blockers; follow-ups are the digest-absence contract question above and adding dispatch-level OCI mount-FD validation coverage (currently helper-level). Human review and signoff remain required.

Closes #78

items.title: tests/auto-prune: Cap the ext4 orphan file on the 1k-block /boot image

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

items.body:
Fixes the `ext.ostree.destructive.auto-prune.sh` failure in CoreOS CI on every PR, including ostreedev/ostree#3690: `mount: /var/mnt: fsconfig() failed: Structure needs cleaning`.

Since e2fsprogs 1.47.4, mke2fs gives this test's 1k-block image a 681984-byte orphan file. The kernel caps that at 512k and refuses the mount (`EXT4-fs (loop0): orphan file too big`). This passes `-E orphan_file_size=512K`, and falls back to the plain call on mke2fs versions without the orphan_file feature.

Checked with Fedora 45's e2fsprogs 1.47.4-2: the orphan inode is 681984 bytes by default and 524288 with the option. CentOS Stream 9's 1.46.5 rejects the option, and the fallback succeeds. Full analysis, including kernel 7.1/7.2 mount reproductions: https://github.com/bootc-dev/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox/blob/main/work/boot-2402/EUCLEAN.md

Tracked in cgwalters-forge/tracker#1574.

The complete patch was reconciled with upstream main at 00574d53bd49525cf1f6a58aa0ac259eaef443b3, including generated metadata and the lazy-unmount overlap: retain lazy detach inside failure-safe, error-reporting teardown. No VM install or booted reproducer result is claimed. bcvk, tmt and QEMU are absent; UID 1001 cannot access /dev/kvm (root:kvm 0660) or /dev/loop-control (root:disk 0660), sudo is denied, and Podman is rootless. Verified: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` (warnings), focused karg/immutable tests, workspace library tests, and the full workspace suite with the missing `ostree` executable supplied through a temporary PATH; generated metadata checks and Nushell 0.103.0 syntax/cleanup checks pass. The unchanged etc-merge permissions test passes here as UID 1001 with umask 0022; its earlier failure was not reproduced.

Upstream compatibility: inspected main at 00574d53bd49525cf1f6a58aa0ac259eaef443b3. The reused Rust fix merges cleanly; the test overlaps upstream's lazy-unmount cleanup change, replaced here by explicit error-reporting teardown. This patch remains against the supplied 0ca885f base, not a full rebase/import of upstream main; reconcile that base before promotion.

Outstanding: plan-40 attempts on both backends stop at missing `bcvk`; `tmt` and QEMU are also absent, KVM/loop devices are not accessible to this user, sudo is denied, and Podman is rootless. Neither VM installation nor the original booted-command-line reproducer was validated. On a properly provisioned development host run `BOOTC_variant=ostree just test-tmt install-karg-delete` and `BOOTC_variant=composefs BOOTC_boot_type=bls BOOTC_bootloader=systemd just test-tmt install-karg-delete`.

For the original reproducer, build the #2539 fixture with its FROM changed to a freshly built patched `localhost/bootc` BLS image, retaining `gapcfg=1`, `gapdel=1`, and `gapclidel=1`. With that image tagged `localhost/gaprepro:1`, run:
```sh
truncate -s 20G a.raw b.raw
podman run --rm --privileged --pid=host --security-opt label=type:unconfined_t -v /dev:/dev -v /var/lib/containers:/var/lib/containers -v "$PWD":/out localhost/gaprepro:1 bootc install to-disk --via-loopback --filesystem ext4 --generic-image --wipe --composefs-backend --karg-delete=gapclidel=1 /out/a.raw
```

Boot each disk in the development VM environment and run:
```nu
use std assert
let args = (open /proc/cmdline | str trim | split row " ")
assert ("gapcfg=1" in $args)
assert (not ("gapdel=1" in $args))
assert (not ("gapclidel=1" in $args))
```

Also check the expected composefs/ostree backend token. These commands are pending validation, not successful results.

## Executive summary

This continues #1303 (e12084d, carried over unchanged) toward a held-out evaluation of the architecture reviewer. Version 1's recorded deviations are resolved prospectively: protocol version 2 and its scoring rubric state every rule before discovery, including operator-authored PRs, non-UTF-8 omissions, identity byte accounting, read-only authenticated retrieval, deterministic metadata-only selection, the noise audit and stopping rules. The shipped prompt and library stay byte-identical to 2665dbb.

Version 2's discovery had a defect in how it computed the base: PRs merged with a merge commit compared as identical with their own base. That attempt is kept as abandoned evidence. Version 3 fixes only that and the handling of failed metadata requests. It was written after seeing version 2's metadata-only outcomes, and the freeze order is self-attested.

Version 3 found four eligible PRs, not five (bootc#2200, ostree#3624, #3626, #3640). By its stopping rule the evaluation is incomplete: no review or scoring ran, and no rule was relaxed. items.title: plan: Show job plans as a table with the brief as Markdown
items.body:
Closes #779.

Job-plan comments are now a short Markdown table (Kind | Item | Runner | Pool | Status) with the brief under it as plain Markdown. A hidden line carries the schema and the SHA-256 of the canonical plan, so parsing stays exact and edits are tamper-evident. Dispatch no longer posts a record comment. It keeps the record in the plan's own comment and rewrites the Status cell with the run link. A table plan is therefore one comment per job, holding the plan, the record and the run. The fenced `agent-board-plan` JSON is still parsed everywhere. The pass's own plans, epic-created job plans and the briefs that tell triage runs how to plan all move to the new format. docs/job-plans.md documents the format and gives a Python recipe for the hash.

## Details

- **Identity and ordering.** A table plan's identity is `COMMENT@sha256:HASH`, so dispatch's own edits don't make it look like a new plan. A recorded or released table plan is dated by when it was posted, so its status edits never shadow a newer plan.
- **Concurrent edits.** Every edit of a plan comment rereads it first and leaves it alone if anyone else changed it. The claim's Status also carries a nonce, so another dispatcher writing over the claim is caught on read-back. The race that remains is documented, and the pass runs in one concurrency group.
- **What stays fenced.** These keep the fenced format and record comments:
  - Epic planning requests: the pass edits them on every request, and epic health counts each record.
  - The native Forgejo pass, whose claim protocol needs unedited threads.
  - Briefs that would @-mention someone or link another owner's item. Plain Markdown links where JSON did not, so these would mark upstream timelines.
- **Request budget.** `START_REQUESTS` grows by 2 to cover the two single-comment reads.
- **Not done yet.** The run's outcome is still agentic-job's separate status comment. See the follow-ups at the end.

`just fmt` and `just check` pass (exit 0). New tests (plan/table.rs tables; `shown_plan_keeps_its_record_and_dispatches_once`; the pass tests now asserting one comment per job) fail without the change.

**Staging evidence** (local release build, cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test; no run was started, because the dispatch target `fork-evidence.yml` has no `workflow_dispatch` trigger):
- Test issue: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test/issues/86. A plan was posted in the new format, with its hash computed by the documented Python recipe.
- `agent-board dispatch --dry-run` parsed it and printed the request.
- `agent-board dispatch --apply` then claimed the plan and got GitHub's 422. It edited the plan's own Status row with the hidden record, posting no new comment ([comment](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test/issues/86#issuecomment-6707530344)). A second `--apply` refused: "has a dispatch record already".
- A preview `agent-board pass` on the staging board read that plan and held it as dispatched already. On a replacement plan it printed `start implement … plan=…@sha256:…`.
- Two applying passes (`--max-dispatch 1 --max-writes 2`, made-up usage snapshot on #87) reported `comments created 0, edited 2`. Each claimed the plan in place, got the 422 and rewrote the Status row ([after review fixes](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test/issues/86#issuecomment-6707727969)). #86 holds only the three plan comments.

**Follow-ups:**
- agentic-job: `agentic-job status` should update a table plan's Status cell instead of posting its own status comment. The cell must be rewritten in place, keeping the rest of the comment, so the hash is unaffected. This needs a dispatch input naming the plan comment, in tracker's dispatch.yml, sent by agent-board. agent-board's status-comment readers would then read the cell.
- agent-board: move epic planning requests and the Forgejo pass to the table format.
- agenthome: its skills don't describe the plan format, so nothing to change there.

items.title: install: Skip mirroring /run/udev when the host has none
items.body:
## Executive summary

`bootc install to-filesystem` fails on hosts without `/run/udev`, such as mdev-based hosts, because install always mirrors that path from the host. This makes only that mirror optional. If the host has no `/run/udev`, install logs at debug level and skips it without creating a local path. If the host has it, install creates a missing local mount point and compares filesystems and bind mounts as before. The other mirrors are still required. Errors other than not-found still propagate, and a path on a different filesystem still gets a bind mount. The blockdev code already falls back to `blkid` when there is no udev database.

This replaces #101 and so also supersedes #97 and #72. It is #101's patch refreshed onto current main. The required and optional mirrors now share one implementation (`plan_mirror`/`ensure_mirror` with an `optional` flag), which answers #101's review comment about duplicated helpers. The data-driven tests now cover both modes for every combination of the path existing locally and on the host. They also check that nothing is created when the host path is missing, that ELOOP propagates, and how host paths are mapped. None of them need privileged mounts.

While here, this replaces the remaining `str::len` calls that clippy.toml disallows with `as_bytes().len()`, which counts the same bytes. They are in `crates/ostree-ext/src/fixture.rs` (from #101), `crates/ostree-ext/tests/it/main.rs` and `crates/lib/src/deploy.rs`. These were meant to be a separate prep commit, but this handback produces a single patch, so they can be split out when promoting.

## Verification

I ran this on Ubuntu 26.04 with Rust, rustfmt and clippy 1.94.1 from rustup, plus the ostree 2025.7 CLI. items.title: xtask: Add vm-upgrade-test for version-matrix VM tests
items.body:
## Executive summary

Add `cargo xtask vm-upgrade-test`. Each version-matrix VM check (install bootc at one revision, switch to another, boot it) becomes one command instead of hand partitioning, `bcvk ephemeral` and a local registry. It builds both git revisions onto a base image (default `quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44`) and installs the first with `bcvk libvirt run` (`bcvk to-disk`) on the chosen filesystem and backend. Like the existing upgrade tests, it then switches to the second through the virtiofs-mounted host container storage, with `bootc switch --transport containers-storage`. Finally it reboots and checks the booted image. A btrfs row of bootc-dev/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox#36:

    git fetch https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc pull/2629/head
    cargo xtask vm-upgrade-test --from v1.16.0 --to FETCH_HEAD --filesystem btrfs --composefs-backend --bootloader grub

## More detail

Verification: the xtask unit tests and clippy pass. The image build ran to completion with the default base; dracut logged errors there, but stock `fedora-bootc:44` logs the same ones in that sandbox. bcvk wasn't available, so I haven't run the VM steps or the btrfs matrix from #36. Those still need a run on a host with bcvk.

Not done: UKI boot (it needs a sealed image build), and a mode for ext4 without verity beyond `--allow-missing-fsverity`. `--bootloader systemd` needs a base image that has systemd-boot.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers. The build-deps one is fixed. The other was to drive `run-tmt` and its readonly suite instead of a separate VM driver; I left that as a follow-up, since this command is meant to work without tmt. The second pass found no blockers.

Part of #108

## Caller settings

Repository `bootc-dev/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox`, file `AGENTS.md`: add a short section along the lines of "For version-matrix VM tests (install bootc at one version, then upgrade or switch to another), use `cargo xtask vm-upgrade-test --from <rev> --to <rev> --filesystem <fs> [--composefs-backend --bootloader grub]` from a bootc checkout, one command per matrix row; don't hand-roll partitioning, `bcvk ephemeral` or a local registry."

items.title: tmt: Add opt-in aarch64 composefs install smoke plan
items.body:
## Executive summary

CI only covers the composefs backend on x86_64. This adds a Testing Farm plan that turns a package-mode CentOS Stream 10 aarch64 guest into a composefs GRUB/BLS system with `bootc install to-existing-root --composefs-backend --allow-missing-verity`, reboots it, and checks the booted system. The plan and its test are both disabled unless the `bootc_smoke=composefs-aarch64` context is set, so Packit and `cargo xtask run-tmt` select neither and the ostree flow is unchanged.

## More detail

Before the reboot, `hack/migrate-packit-composefs.sh` mounts the new deployment with `bootc install mount` and carries over what tmt needs to reconnect and continue: SSH host keys (normalized to root 0600), NetworkManager connections, the hostname, cloud-init state (so cloud-init doesn't regenerate keys or network config), `/var/ARTIFACTS` and the tmt helpers. It then relabels with the deployment's own policy and unmounts. Private files are never printed. The preflight fails before anything destructive happens unless the guest is UEFI with an ESP, both kernels support EROFS and overlayfs, the initramfs (inspected with the host's `lsinitrd`) has the bootc module, and the image has sshd/NetworkManager enabled plus rsync, nu and bootc. The booted check requires a changed boot ID, aarch64, a composefs/BLS/GRUB status, `/` sourced from `composefs:<verity>`, an established SSH connection, active sshd/NetworkManager, a default route and unchanged host key fingerprints. It does not read `SSH_CONNECTION`. `system-reinstall-bootc` isn't used because it has no way to pass `--allow-missing-verity` or `--bootloader`, and it has no hook before the reboot.

Verified locally:
- `tmt lint` passes on the plan and test.
- The `enabled:true` plan and test lists match main in the default, CS10 aarch64 and image_mode contexts. With the opt-in, exactly this plan and test are added.
- Real `tmt` discovery selects the test only with the opt-in.
- `cargo xtask update-generated direct --check` passes.
- shellcheck and `bash -n` pass, and `nu --ide-check` is clean under nu 0.103 (the version the image uses).
- `testing-farm request --dry-run` accepts the documented request.
- The migration script ran in a container against a fake host and deployment, with `bootc install mount` and `setfiles` stubbed.

**This has not run on a guest.** No Testing Farm token or fork CI was available to this run, so aarch64 composefs coverage is not established until a linked passing run of the request in tmt/README.md exists. Keep this draft until then.

Review: two passes. The first found one blocker (copied host keys could keep a mismatched `ssh_keys` group), which is fixed. Still open: both scripts exceed REVIEW.md's ~50 lines, and `setfiles` validates the image's contexts against the host's loaded policy. The new scripts are mode 0644 and are invoked with `bash`.

items.title: composefs: Name Type 1 boot directories by boot digest
items.body:
## Executive summary

On composefs, the Type 1 kernel path on the ESP was `/EFI/Linux/bootc_composefs-<128 hex verity>/vmlinuz`, which is 163 characters. HP G10 firmware hangs loading a kernel from that path (bootc-dev/bootc#2585). New directories are now named after the sha256 boot digest of the vmlinuz and initrd they hold, which bootc already computes, so the path is 99 characters.

GC, status and the BLS parsers already treat the part of the name after the prefix as opaque, so existing verity-named directories stay valid. GC removes them once no entry references them. On upgrade, an existing directory with the same kernel and initrd is still reused, even if it has an old verity name. This means existing installs only get the short path once the kernel or initrd changes. Rollback to bootc older than 1.17.0 is unsafe, because its GC compared directory names against the verity. Type 1 entries on /boot (GRUB) get the shorter names too. UKIs are not changed.

## More detail

Verified with `cargo test -p bootc-lib --lib` (334 passed, including a new path-length test) and `cargo fmt --check`. I updated the tmt GC test to expect digest-named directories, but did not run it. Nobody has tested this on the affected hardware.

There was one review pass, with no blockers. Follow-ups it left open:
- The "Inconsistent state" guard in GC compares directory names with the booted verity, so it can no longer fire for digest-named directories. It should also compare against the booted `boot_digest`.
- `find_vmlinuz_initrd_duplicate` could look up `bootc_composefs-<digest>` by name before falling back to hashing every directory.
- The `testutils.rs` fixture still names directories by verity. Moving it to digest naming would let the GC unit tests cover the new layout and upgrades from the old one.

items.title: install: Skip mirroring /run/udev when the host has none
items.body:
Hosts without udev (e.g. mdev) have no /run/udev, and `bootc install to-filesystem` fails there because mirroring it from the host is mandatory. Make only that mirror optional: if the host path is missing, log at debug level and return without creating anything locally; if it exists, create the local mount point and compare/bind as before. Other mirrors stay mandatory, and lookup, comparison and mount errors other than not-found still propagate. This ports #97 (examined head 0d94dc9c) onto current main, superseding #97 and #72, and adds coverage of the wrapper skipping without creating anything that needs no privileged mounts.

While here, crates/ostree-ext/src/fixture.rs uses `as_bytes().len()` instead of `str::len` as clippy.toml requires. This was the known baseline clippy blocker. The task asked for it as a separate commit, but this handback is a single patch, so it is in this commit too. It can be split out on promotion.

Verified in Fedora 44 with install-buildroot prerequisites, ostree 2026.4, Rust/rustfmt/Clippy 1.94.1 (rustup) and tmpfs /tmp, /var/tmp and /run: `cargo fmt --check` exit 0, `cargo test` exit 0, `cargo clippy --all-targets` exit 101. **Acceptance is incomplete.** With fixture.rs fixed, clippy reaches more baseline `str::len` (disallowed_methods) errors: crates/ostree-ext/tests/it/main.rs:942, 1551, 1568, 1584, 1585 and crates/lib/src/deploy.rs:1820. Base 0ca885fe in the same environment also gives exit codes 0/101/0, but stops earlier at fixture.rs:274. None of these lines are touched here, and no lint configuration or assertion was changed. Fedora's own Rust 1.99.1 gives the same clippy errors, plus more warnings.

Full installation on an mdev host remains untested. Also note that `install to-disk` still runs `udevadm settle` unconditionally (crates/lib/src/install/baseline.rs), so this only fixes to-filesystem and to-existing-root.

Review: one pass. Its one blocker asked to collapse the plan/enum into an optional flag on the existing mirror helper. That would be a redesign of #97, which this task said not to do, so it is left as a follow-up. Also open: the plan and wrapper tests overlap, and a tmt test could run in a PID namespace with no /run/udev.

Part of #57
Part of cgwalters-forge/tracker#313; references bootc-dev/bootc#2239.

items.title: tmt: Add opt-in aarch64 composefs install smoke plan
items.body:
CI only covers the composefs backend on x86_64. This adds a Testing Farm plan that turns a package-mode CentOS Stream 10 aarch64 guest into a composefs GRUB/BLS system. It runs `bootc install to-existing-root --composefs-backend --allow-missing-verity` without `--cleanup`, reboots with the existing Ansible playbook, and then checks the booted system: boot ID, architecture, composefs status, root mount, network, and the evidence it collected. The plan is disabled unless the `bootc_smoke=composefs-aarch64` context is set, so Packit and `cargo xtask run-tmt` don't select it, and the existing ostree flow is unchanged unless the new `BOOTC_PACKIT_BUILD_ONLY` is set. The prepare script fails before the install if UEFI, an ESP, EROFS/overlayfs kernel support or the bootc initramfs module is missing. tmt/README.md gives the Testing Farm request.

Verified locally: `tmt lint`; the `enabled:true` plan list is identical before and after, with and without the Packit context; Packit config parses with unchanged jobs; `testing-farm request --dry-run`; `cargo xtask update-generated direct --check`; shellcheck; `nu --ide-check`. It has not run on a guest: no Testing Farm token or fork dispatch was available, so aarch64 coverage is not established until a linked passing run exists.

Review: one pass, no blockers. Follow-ups it raised: give the test itself the plan's opt-in `adjust`; run `lsinitrd` on the host instead of in the image; assert the root source is `composefs:<verity>` as test-49 does; drop the `SSH_CONNECTION` check; avoid `grep -q` in a pipe under pipefail; fix the `BOOTC_PACKIT_BUILD_ONLY` comment (the script installs localhost/bootc-composefs); reuse Containerfile.drop-lbis; call the derived image's `.Id` an ID, not a digest; the prepare script is longer than REVIEW.md's ~50 lines. items.title: examples: Add opt-in reboot failure diagnostics
items.body:
Part of #63 and tracker#1215.

The G8 example reboot failures end in SSH exit 255, and we have no guest evidence for them: verbose output keeps command lines and SSH stderr, but not reboot timing or the console from before IPC cleanup. This adds an opt-in `reboot_diagnostics` to `VirtualMachine`, enabled only in the test_basic fixture. Each reboot phase logs its start, completion or failure (name, elapsed time, exception type and return code, never the formatted exception). When a phase fails, the last 16 KiB of the local console is logged synchronously before the exception propagates. Redaction only covers what testthing knows is secret: configured credential values, the public identity and PEM private key blocks. Diagnostic errors never replace the primary exception or cancellation. Exit 255 is still a failure: no retries and no change to what counts as passing.

This revision drops the earlier worker thread and timeout budget, which a stalled log handler could hang at shutdown. It also drops the keyword and base64 heuristics that redacted hashes and everything after them.

Verified: the 24 deterministic tests in examples/test/test_reboot_diagnostics.py pass, and ruff format/check report nothing new on the changed files (the vendored testthing.py has six existing findings). No VM ran. Live reproduction, root cause and three exact-revision repetitions each of uki/fedora and unified-secureboot/fedora remain pending agentic-job#2891.

Review: two passes, no blockers left. Open follow-ups:
- whether this belongs in the vendored test.thing copy or upstream;
- the reboot reconnect wait has no timeout, so a guest that never returns is only diagnosed when something cancels the test;
- very short credential values over-redact;
- a key body with no marker inside the tail is not redacted;
- the phase logs use WARNING level.

items.title: xtask: Retry transient registry errors when pulling images

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Several CI jobs failed on the first attempt of `podman pull -q --retry 5 --retry-delay 5s` with `writing blob ... happened during read: unexpected EOF`. podman does not count that error as retryable, so its `--retry` never kicked in.

This adds `cargo xtask pull-images IMAGE...`. It runs `podman pull -q` and retries with capped exponential backoff, but only when stderr shows a transient transport error (EOF, connection reset/refused, i/o timeout, TLS handshake, HTTP 429/5xx). Signature-policy rejections, unknown manifests and other errors fail at once. `BOOTC_CI_RETRIES` and `BOOTC_CI_DELAY` set the attempt count (capped at 10) and the initial delay. The defaults are 3 attempts and 2s, so local runs stay fast.

The `package` pull and `_pull-lbi-images` now go through it. `build` also pre-pulls `{{base}}` when it is not already local, so jobs run with `BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1` no longer leave that pull to `podman build`. The Dockerfile never uses `buildroot_base`, so `build` has nothing to pre-pull for it. `build-fetch` keeps its unconditional retry loop, and the workflows and `podman push` are unchanged.
