items.title: ci: Retry the buildroot fetch and share the retry loop

labels.name: review:quick
labels.description: High-confidence bot draft: skim and approve

items.body:
Part of #87

The RPM and metalink flakes in the package, test-container-export, test-baseconfigs and test-integration jobs come from podman builds that fetch over the network without the retry loop `build-fetch` already has. This moves that loop out of `build-fetch` into `hack/ci-retry` so more than one recipe can use it. It also adds `just package-fetch`, which runs the `buildroot` stage (install-buildroot and `cargo fetch`, both before the `--network=none` cutoff) with retries and the same `base_buildargs` as `just package`, so the package build and its reproducibility check get a cache hit.

Without the workflow change below, nothing in CI calls `package-fetch` yet. This run cannot change files under `.github/`, so the diff below needs to be applied by hand. It adds a retried fetch before `check-buildsys` in the package job and a `build-fetch` step before the build in test-container-export and test-baseconfigs. In test-integration, it re-runs `build-fetch` after `podman builder prune -af`, because the prune removes the fetch layer that the TMT step's `just build` then needs again. It also sets `BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1` on the TMT step. Without that, the step rebuilt the RPMs from source and ran the buildroot fetch again with no retry. TMT now tests the RPM artifacts from the package job, the same ones the earlier steps in that job use.

A package that is really missing is still retried until `BOOTC_CI_RETRIES` runs out, as `build-fetch` already does. With CI's 10 x 60s, that also means a deterministic buildroot or `cargo fetch` failure in the package job takes about 9 minutes longer to report. dnf's and podman's output is still shown on every attempt.

Verified with `just --dry-run` on `package-fetch` and `build-fetch`, shellcheck on `hack/ci-retry`, a local run of the script against a failing and a passing command, and a YAML parse of the edited workflow. actionlint is not installed and no podman build was run, so the cache hits were worked out from the build args, not observed.

Review: one pass, no blockers. Follow-ups it noted: `just validate` and the `tools` stage of `tmt/tests/Dockerfile.upgrade` also fetch without retry; `package` could use `_local-deps-args` so its args cannot drift from `package-fetch`'s; the test-integration re-fetch also rebuilds the unused upgrade-source fetch stage.

## Caller settings

Repository cgwalters-forge/bootc, file `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/ci.yml b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
index 84006f0..685a47e 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -270,6 +270,9 @@ jobs:
           printf 'BOOTC_base=%s\n' "$BASE" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
           printf 'BOOTC_buildroot_base=%s\n' "$BUILDROOT_BASE" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
 
+      - name: Fetch package buildroot (with retry)
+        run: just package-fetch
+
       - name: Build packages (and verify build system)
         run: just check-buildsys
 
@@ -402,7 +405,13 @@ jobs:
       - name: Reclaim disk space before TMT
         run: podman builder prune -af
 
+      # The prune above dropped the fetch layer; the TMT step rebuilds the image.
+      - name: Re-fetch external dependencies (with retry)
+        run: BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1 just build-fetch
+
       - name: Run TMT integration tests
+        env:
+          BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE: "1"
         run: |
           if [[ "${{ matrix.variant }}" = composefs ]]; then
             just test-composefs "${{ matrix.bootloader }}"  "${{ matrix.filesystem }}" "${{ matrix.boot_type }}" "${{ matrix.seal_state }}"
@@ -541,6 +550,9 @@ jobs:
           name: packages-${{ matrix.test_os }}
           path: target/packages/
 
+      - name: Fetch external dependencies (with retry)
+        run: BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1 just build-fetch
+
       - name: Build container with baseconfig
         run: BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1 just build
 
@@ -644,6 +656,9 @@ jobs:
           name: packages-centos-10
           path: target/packages/
 
+      - name: Fetch external dependencies (with retry)
+        run: BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1 just build-fetch
+
       - name: Build and run container export test
         run: |
           BOOTC_SKIP_PACKAGE=1 just test-container-export
```

items.title: gke: Keep Flux off Forgejo while the nightly backup has it stopped
items.body:
Draft for colin-ci/llm-wiki#197: Flux sometimes scales Forgejo back up mid-archive and the nightly backup fails as inconsistent.

**Deviation from the agreed plan.** There is no separate forgejo Flux Kustomization; Forgejo is reconciled by `flux-system` (path `./clusters/gke`, all of layer 0, no `serviceAccountName`, so it applies as cluster-admin). Granting the backup orchestrator patch on it, even with `resourceNames`, would let that pod repoint it and get cluster-admin, and suspending it pauses all of layer 0. Instead the orchestrator sets Flux's per-object `kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/reconcile: disabled` annotation on `statefulset/forgejo` in-cluster before scaling down and clears it (null merge patch) in the existing EXIT/TERM/INT trap. kustomize-controller checks this annotation on the live object as well as the manifest (`fluxcd/pkg` `ssa.shouldSkipApply`). The orchestrator already has patch on that StatefulSet, so there are **no RBAC changes**. If you still want the Kustomization-suspend approach, it would mean first splitting Forgejo into its own Flux Kustomization, a bigger and riskier move because of `prune: true` and the PVC.

Hard-death safeguards: each run clears a leftover annotation at start, and the health checker's `forgejo_statefulset` check logs ERROR (existing alert policy) when the annotation is present and no `forgejo-backup` Job is active. The "restarted during the backup" check stays as a backstop.

Verified:
- `kubectl kustomize` of `clusters/gke` and `clusters/gke/forgejo`
- server-side `apply --dry-run=server` of the changed CronJobs and ConfigMap
- `patch --dry-run=server` of the annotation set and unset (generation unchanged)
- `auth can-i` for both service accounts
- shellcheck of the extracted script: clean at warning, no new info findings
- a fake-kubectl run of the success, failed-archive, stale-annotation and SIGTERM paths
- a stubbed run of the checker logic

items.body:
Extend `privileged_fuse_dumpfile_roundtrip` so that external processes check a real FUSE mount against the source dumpfile, covering every inode type. This updates retained draft #52 and supersedes the closed #48. It keeps the fixtures from #52 (all file types, empty and binary inline files, varied ownership and mode bits, xattrs on every type) and its fix for opening empty files, which the new fixture needed. It adds the external stat checks from #48. The dump scan reconstructs link counts from the tree it walks, so `stat` now checks each path's mode, link count, uid, gid and mtime, and checks that hardlinks share one inode. Every external process runs under `timeout`, so a missing FUSE reply fails the test instead of hanging it. The external files now span many pages with different contents, so a read of the wrong page fails.

Verified with Rust 1.95.0 (`docker.io/library/rust:1.95`) in a rootless `podman run --privileged --device /dev/fuse` container, as user-namespace root rather than real root or a bcvk VM. I built with `cargo build -p composefs-ctl -p composefs-integration-tests` (cfsctl's default features include `fuse`). Then `CFSCTL_PATH=.../cfsctl cfsctl-integration-tests --exact privileged_fuse_dumpfile_roundtrip` passed against a real FUSE mount. I temporarily changed `inode_fileattr` to return `nlink + 1`, a fault the dump comparison alone cannot see, and the same test failed with `stat mismatch ... expected mode:nlink:uid:gid:mtime 41ed:6:0:0:1700000000, got 41ed:7:...`. After I restored it, the test passed again. Without the empty-file open fix, the scan fails with EOPNOTSUPP. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` exit 0; Clippy only warns about files this change does not touch. I did not run the timeout path against a server that never replies, or the full VM suite.

items.title: varlink: Don't hold a repository lock while a handle is idle

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
An open varlink repository handle used to keep the shared flock that `Repository::open` takes for as long as the handle lived. An idle client therefore blocked gc indefinitely, and a `Gc` call contending with another lock blocked the whole server. Following the state model in the design, a handle now keeps only its directory fd. Each call takes a non-blocking shared lock for its duration, and `Gc` takes a non-blocking exclusive lock on a fresh file description; it never converts a held lock, because a failed `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` conversion drops the `LOCK_SH`. On contention both interfaces reply with a new `Busy` error. Method signatures are unchanged.

The library gets `Repository::open_path_deferred_lock` and `open_upgrade_deferred_lock`, which open without a lock, plus `try_lock_shared`, which returns a refcounted `RepositoryLockGuard`. gc in this mode unlocks explicitly, so a child forked during gc can't keep the lock held. The existing open functions and cfsctl's command line keep their blocking behaviour.

Verification:
- `cargo fmt --check`: exit 101. rustfmt is not installed here (`no such command: fmt`), so formatting was checked by hand only.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets`: not run. clippy is not installed. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` exits 0 with no warnings.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude composefs-integration-tests`: exit 101. 613 passed and 11 failed, all environmental: 10 fs-verity tests (ext4 here has no verity) and `test_pr188_empty_inline_directory` (no `mkcomposefs` binary). The local rustc is 1.93.1 and the `test-with` dev-dependency wants 1.95, so this ran with `--ignore-rust-version --no-fail-fast`.
- The new tests (`varlink::repository_lock_tests`, `repository::tests::test_deferred_lock_gc_busy`) pass. They cover an idle handle not blocking gc, gc replying `Busy` while a call on the same handle, another opener in this process, or a `flock(1)` child holds the shared lock, calls replying `Busy` while another process holds the exclusive lock, and success after release. With the varlink open switched back to the blocking open, all four varlink tests fail within 30s instead of hanging.

Review: two adversarial passes. The first found the fork/close lock-leak above, now fixed; the second found no blockers.

Left open:
- `InitRepository`/`EnsureRepository` still take the library's blocking lock through `init_path`/`ensure_path`, so they can stall the server while another process runs gc.
- `GetLayer` holds the shared lock until the client closes its keepalive fd.
- The `flock(1)`-based test needs util-linux 2.38 or later for `--no-fork`.
- The `(st_dev, st_ino)` keyed cache from the design belongs to the stateless-selector slice and is not here.

Closes #37

items.title: composefs: Report failed finalization on the next boot

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
A shutdown finalization error should not disappear into the previous boot's journal while the following boot looks successful. Persist its diagnostic and report it once through a composefs-only bootc-boot-complete.service, required and ordered before boot-complete.target so failure also prevents consumers such as systemd-bless-boot.service from blessing the boot. The check is inactive without a failure stamp and does not enable boot counting or automatic rollback.

Use /boot, as OSTree does, with the existing persistent /sysroot/boot layout when /boot is not mounted; the image's unmounted /boot is read-only. Successful finalization clears the stamp; reporting renames it to .previous. Reads and stored diagnostics are bounded to 16 KiB. The unit is installed by the existing systemd wildcard and enabled by the composefs generator. No production failure-injection option is added.

The registered three-boot TMT test stages a derived image, externally renames the staged deployment's etc directory to etc.saved after preflight, then checks the old deployment, failed service and diagnostic, and unreached boot-complete.target. A further reboot must be clean. The test explicitly pulls the passive target into the boot transaction, including on GRUB.

### Verification

Final checks and exit status:
- cargo test -p bootc-lib failure_stamp --lib: 0 (3 tests).
- cargo test -p bootc-lib boot_complete_required_dependency --lib: 0.
- cargo test -p bootc-lib --lib --quiet: 0 (337 passed, 1 ignored).
- cargo xtask update-generated direct: 0; cargo xtask update-generated direct --check: 0.
- PATH=/tmp/opencode/rustfmt/usr/lib/rust-1.93/bin:$PATH cargo fmt --all: 0; the same command with --check: 0.
- git diff --check: 0.
- just validate: 1; generated metadata check passed, but container setup could not reach the sandbox's loopback proxy to download CentOS repository metadata. Container clippy/man/schema validation did not run.
- just unit-tests: 1; blocked by the same container setup failure. The host library suite above passed, but this is not a passing container unit suite.
- cargo xtask run-tmt --env=BOOTC_variant=composefs --filesystem=ext4 --boot-type=bls --seal-state=unsealed localhost/bootc composefs-finalize-failure: 1; bcvk is missing, and tmt is also unavailable. The VM/reboot test did not run.
- systemd-analyze verify systemd/bootc-boot-complete.service: 1; this host lacks /usr/bin/bootc and its man page.

Early development checks caught and corrected a buffered-writer API error, an include path error, and directory fsync on an O_PATH descriptor. The initial host fmt attempt was unavailable; formatting subsequently used an extracted distribution rustfmt package.

Review: two passes; the first found an unmounted-/boot blocker and an enablement-test gap, both fixed; the final delta review left no blockers or follow-ups. Human review and an actual rebooting test remain required.

### Deferred documentation text

No man pages are changed because the boot failure detection page is being revised separately. Proposed replacement for the composefs Key Services discussion in docs/src/bootc-boot-failure-detection.7.md:

> bootc-finalize-staged.service finalizes staged composefs deployments during shutdown. If finalization returns an error, bootc saves its diagnostic in /boot/bootc-finalize-failure.stamp, or in /sysroot/boot/bootc-finalize-failure.stamp when /boot is not mounted. A successful finalization removes a stale stamp. On the next composefs boot, bootc-boot-complete.service runs when boot-complete.target is requested and a stamp exists. It reports the saved error and recommends journalctl -b -1 -u bootc-finalize-staged.service, then fails. Because boot-complete.target requires the service and is ordered after it, the target cannot be reached in that transaction and consumers requiring successful boot completion cannot bless that boot. The stamp is renamed with a .previous suffix, so the diagnostic is reported once rather than failing every subsequent boot. Failure to persist or consume the stamp can prevent this one-shot behavior. This detects returned shutdown finalization errors, not every interrupted shutdown or early-boot failure, and does not configure boot counting or automatic rollback.

items.title: ci: Build and unit-test without libselinux on Arch

labels.name: review:quick
labels.description: High-confidence bot draft: skim and approve

items.body:
Distributions without SELinux (here Arch Linux, which doesn't ship libselinux) need bootc to build and work without the `selinux` feature, and nothing currently checks that. This adds `just test-no-selinux`. In a clean Arch container it installs only the build dependencies and fails if libselinux is present as a package or as a shared library. It then builds with `make bin CARGO_OPTIONS='--no-default-features --features "install-to-disk pre-6.15"'` and runs `bootc --version`. The build fails if ldd or readelf show libselinux or an unresolved library, or if either tool fails. Finally it runs `cargo test -p bootc-lib --no-default-features --features install-to-disk`. The packaging doc points at the recipe for local reproduction.

Part of #74 (cgwalters-forge/tracker#103, plus the no-SELinux build part of tracker#232). Default-feature VM smoke tests are not included.

This patch can't touch `.github/`, so the CI wiring is left for a maintainer. It is a heavy-gated job aggregated into `required-checks-heavy`, and it changes nothing else:

```diff
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -289,6 +289,19 @@ jobs:
       - name: Unit tests
         run: just unit-tests
 
+  # Build and unit-test without the selinux feature on a distribution with no
+  # libselinux (Arch Linux), checking the binary doesn't link it.
+  test-no-selinux:
+    if: needs.compute-ci-level.outputs.run_heavy == 'true'
+    needs: compute-ci-level
+    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+      - name: Bootc Ubuntu Setup
+        uses: bootc-dev/actions/bootc-ubuntu-setup@main
+      - name: Build and unit-test without libselinux
+        run: just test-no-selinux
+
@@ -711,7 +724,7 @@ jobs:
   required-checks-heavy:
     if: ${{ always() && (github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.compute-ci-level.outputs.merge_queue_enabled != 'true')) }}
-    needs: [compute-ci-level, cargo-deny, validate, install-tests, docs, package, test-integration, test-upgrade, test-baseconfigs, test-container-export, test-ukiboot]
+    needs: [compute-ci-level, cargo-deny, validate, install-tests, docs, package, test-no-selinux, test-integration, test-upgrade, test-baseconfigs, test-container-export, test-ukiboot]
```

Verified: `just test-no-selinux` passed locally with rootless podman. The sandbox needed `generic_buildargs=--network=host` and a locally re-tagged Arch image trusting the egress proxy CA; neither is part of this change. `pacman -T libselinux` returned 127 (not installed) and `find` found no `libselinux.so*`. `bootc --version` printed `bootc 1.17.3`. ldd resolved every library with no libselinux, and readelf showed no libselinux entry. Unit tests: 329 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. actionlint 1.7.12 on the workflow hunk reported nothing new apart from the `ubuntu-26.04` runner label, which it doesn't know and which every existing job already uses. `cargo fmt --check` couldn't run (no rustfmt in the sandbox), and no Rust code changed.

Review: one pass with no blockers. I fixed its findings on swallowed `pacman`/`find` errors, the ldd comment, caching `~/.cargo/git`, and the doc wording. Still open: the Arch image is unpinned and x86_64 only, and the recipe doesn't pass `BOOTC_extra_src`.

items.title: composefs: Keep --enforce-container-sigpolicy in the origin

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
The composefs origin hardcoded `ostree-unverified-image:`, so a system installed with `--enforce-container-sigpolicy` silently stopped enforcing on later upgrades. This records the signature policy in the origin the way the ostree backend does (`ostree-image-signed:` when enforced), and has composefs upgrade and switch apply ostree's check: refuse when containers-policy.json defaults to `insecureAcceptAnything`, or when the image would come from a delta that skopeo never sees. The check runs before upgrade or switch touches any state, and again in the pull. Origins written without enforcement are byte-identical to before, so existing installs keep the behaviour they have.

Verified with new unit tests for the origin with and without enforcement and for the policy check, `cargo test -p bootc-lib --lib`, and the `validate-post-build` container target from `just validate` (fmt, clippy, generated files). I did not add a tmt test: proving that an enforced install still enforces on upgrade needs a VM that boots the enforced install and then upgrades, which a hosted runner can't run, and no existing tmt plumbing installs with this flag.

One review pass, no blockers. I fixed its two important findings (check ordering before `validate_update`, and `upgrade --check` skipping the check). Left open: an `ostree-remote-image:` origin is now carried through unverified rather than flattened, though nothing in composefs writes one; and `switch --enforce-container-sigpolicy` to the already-booted image still fails with "same fs-verity digest" where ostree would stage a new origin (this predates the change).

items.title: install: Skip mirroring /run/udev when the host has none

labels.name: review:quick
labels.description: High-confidence bot draft: skim and approve

items.body:
`bootc install to-filesystem` fails on hosts without `/run/udev`, such as mdev-based ones, because install mirrors it from the host unconditionally and the host-side statvfs fails with ENOENT. The workaround is creating an empty `/run/udev` on the host.

Now only the `/run/udev` mirror is optional: if the path is missing on the host, we debug-log and skip it without creating a local mount point. Otherwise it behaves as before: create the local directory, compare fsids, bind mount if they differ. All other errors still propagate. The other mirrored mounts are unchanged. Without udev state, blockdev already falls back to blkid.

One deviation from the issue: a missing local `/run/udev` with a present host one is still created and bind mounted, not skipped. In a plain `podman run` container it usually doesn't exist yet, so skipping there would turn the mirror off entirely.

Verified with a data-driven unit test covering present/missing paths on each side, plus a different-filesystem case that needs a bind mount. `cargo test` shows the same 20 failures as on the base commit, all environmental (missing `ostree`, the `/bin/sh` echo behavior, etc-merge permissions). `cargo check --all-targets` is clean. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` were not run because rustfmt and clippy aren't installed in the build environment. A full install on an mdev host was not run.

Review: one pass, no blockers. I added the bind-case test it asked for. Open nits: the optional helper partly duplicates `ensure_mirrored_host_mount`, and errors from it name only the local path.

items.title: lib: Deny (e)println! in bootc-lib, routing status output via ProgressWriter

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Library code printing directly to stdout/stderr bypasses --progress-fd and can corrupt machine-readable output, so this denies clippy::print_stdout and print_stderr (and anstream's print macros) in bootc-lib. User-facing status output now goes through ProgressWriter, which prints it as before and, when a progress fd is attached, also sends it as a new generic `Message` event (protocol 0.2.0). A command's actual results go to an explicit stdout writer. Output without --progress-fd is byte-for-byte unchanged.

This is the series from #1 rebased onto current main, which includes bootc-dev/bootc#2449, and supersedes #1. It also converts the prints that landed since #1's base: the UKI addon CLI, the global addon removal notice in the composefs update path, and `bootc usroverlay`. The two `eprintln!` calls #2449 added in delta_ostree.rs are in tests, which the clippy.toml `allow-print-in-tests` setting covers. The fsck commit from #1 dropped out because main already writes passing checks to the provided output. Two pre-existing `str::len` disallowed-method hits in test code (ostree-ext fixture.rs, a deploy.rs test) are fixed so `cargo clippy --all-targets` passes.

The issue asked to keep the series as small commits. This run hands back a single patch, so it lands as one commit. #1's branch keeps the per-commit split for reference.

Verified with cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -p bootc-lib --all-targets (default lints and the Makefile's CLIPPY_CONFIG), cargo test -p bootc-lib (333 passed), and cargo check --workspace --all-targets. The tmt test change was not run.

Review: one pass, no blockers. Follow-ups it left open:
- Writes to the progress fd now block, which stalls the current-thread runtime, pull included, if the reader stops draining it. Consider a writer thread.
- With a closed stdout, `message()` ignores the write error where `println!` panicked, so that edge case now exits 0 instead of 101.
- install_container still uses ProgressWriter::default() for PullProgress instead of state.prog.
- The progress-fd man page says status messages are "also sent" as Message events. Spinner text and pull step descriptions are not sent.
- No test checks the bytes `message()` writes to stdout/stderr.

Closes #61

items.title: gateway: Report prompt-cache hit rates in /usage
items.body:
#44 logs each Codex request's prompt-cache use in credential-proxy, but reading the cache share still means reading the logs. With `cache_stats: true` on `run_token`, `/usage` now has a `cache` section. It gives the hit rate (cached ÷ input) for each provider and model over the last hour and the last day. It also lists the ten busiest `prompt_cache_key` sessions, each with its request count, its first request's input, and its hit rate from the second request on. The gateway logs one warning per session whose hit rate is under 50% from its third request on.

The counting happens in the gateway rather than the proxy, because the gateway serves `/usage` and already sees every injected response's usage, Anthropic and Mistral included. It reads the session key from the Codex request body, which Praxis has already buffered. Sessions are named by the same 12-hex-digit SHA-256 prefix the proxy logs, and only for keys the proxy would hash too. No key, prompt, run or credential is kept. All of it is bounded: 64 provider and model pairs, 1024 sessions, and a day of five-minute slots. It is off by default because `/usage` is unauthenticated, and a session's hash, sizes and times tell whoever knows or can guess the key when it is in use. Each deployment keeps its own counts, so staging and production stay apart.

Verified with `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked` (no new warnings) on Rust 1.96.1. Review: one pass, no blockers. From that pass I fixed two things: only proxy-shaped keys are hashed now, and only Codex bodies are parsed. Left open:
- With a budget mounted, `cache` still covers the whole broker, while `spend` covers only the public consumer, so it can show private activity.
- Each Codex request's body is parsed a second time on the async worker, about 34 ms for a 32 MiB body. Reading the key from protocol-filter metadata, or capping the size parsed, would avoid that.
- `counts_cache()` locks a mutex on every injected request, and the warning is logged while that lock is held.
- Once 64 routes are active, each request for a new model rescans them all. A peer holding a run token can flush the session list with throwaway keys.

Part of #45

## Caller settings

The setting belongs in this repository's `praxis.yaml`, but this change leaves that file alone because it names hosts. To turn it on there, set `cache_stats: true` on the `run_token` filter, next to `spend: true`, in cgwalters-bot/praxis-credential-broker `praxis.yaml`.

items.title: capi: Check libcomposefs.so.1 ABI against composefs-c

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Part of #33

This adds `just check-capi-abi`, which checks that the Rust libcomposefs.so.1 can stand in for composefs-c's library at ec2573a. It compares the SONAME, the exported symbols and their versions, and the public struct layouts and constants: a small C program prints them from the C headers, and a Rust unit test checks the Rust definitions against the same `abi-layout.txt`. Then it runs C's unmodified `tests/test-lcfs` against the Rust library, and runs one C consumer binary, built against the C library, against both libraries and diffs the output. The recipe reuses `test-capi-container.sh`, which can now take a Containerfile and a pinned C commit.

The writer loop in `lcfs_write_to` now fails like C when a callback returns 0, where before it looped forever. A unit test covers this. The new checks also found three differences from C, now fixed. `digest_out` was only filled when `LCFS_BUILD_COMPUTE_DIGEST` was set, but C rejects that flag in write options, so callers never got a digest. An unknown `format` was accepted. And `lcfs_compute_fsverity_from_data(d, NULL, 0)` failed, so `test-lcfs` aborted. The stale "not yet started" note in cfsctl's docs is updated.

The image loader still differs from C in ways the consumer leaves out and the report lists: directories come back with nlink 1 and size 0, and overlay whiteout markers and user-set `trusted.overlay.*` xattrs are dropped. Fixing that means bypassing the lossy `FileSystem` conversion, so it's left as a follow-up.

ABI report from a local run (podman):

```
=== libcomposefs.so.1 ABI report: Rust vs C (ec2573a) ===
PASS  SONAME
      C: libcomposefs.so.1, Rust: libcomposefs.so.1
PASS  exported symbols and versions
      C exports 62, Rust 62; versioned: C 0, Rust 0
PASS  struct layouts and constants
      61 struct sizes, field offsets and constants vs abi-layout.txt
PASS  C tests/test-lcfs against Rust
PASS  C consumer binary against Rust
      22 lines of output compared
KNOWN DIFFERENCES (not compared): images loaded by Rust have directory nlink 1
      and size 0, and lack overlay whiteout markers and trusted.overlay.* xattrs
```

Verified: `just check-capi-abi` 0, `just test-capi` 0, `cargo fmt --check` 0, `cargo clippy --all-targets` 0 (also `--workspace`; no new warnings), composefs-capi unit tests 22/22. Run in a container with rustc 1.99 because the host's 1.93 is too old for the workspace. `cargo test --workspace --exclude composefs-integration-tests` exits 101: 11 fs-verity/mkcomposefs tests fail because the sandbox has no fs-verity and no mkcomposefs. The unprivileged integration tests also exit 101: 68 pass, and 44 fail for lack of ostree, varlinkctl and registry access. None of those failures touch the changed crates. The privileged tests (`capi_mount_*` and the other `privileged_*` VM tests) could not run here.

Not done: the CI job, because this change can't touch `.github/`; see below. Review: one pass, no blockers. It left open: the loader differences above; `lcfs_load_node_from_file`/`lcfs_build` ignoring buildflags and `lcfs_node_set_content` not enforcing `LCFS_INLINE_CONTENT_MAX`, none of which the consumer exercises; Rust unit tests for the digest_out, format and empty-fsverity fixes, which are only covered by the container check; and the layout check comparing offsets but not field types.

## Caller settings

Repository cgwalters-forge/composefs-rs, file `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add a job next to `capi`, and add `capi-abi` to the final job's `needs` list and `needs.*.result` checks:

```yaml
  capi-abi:
    name: C API ABI check
    needs: smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@v4
      - name: Check libcomposefs.so.1 ABI against composefs-c
        run: just check-capi-abi
```

items.title: workflows: Add a wrapper canary that runs a real dispatch and review
items.body:
#136 changed both agent wrappers, passed every check and review, and then broke every agent run for hours: nothing ran a real agent through a pull request's own wrappers, and the review ran the base branch's copy. This adds a wrapper canary. `wrapper-canary-gate.yml` sets a `wrapper-canary` status on every pull request to main. The status is success unless the pull request changes `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` or `cgwalters-review.yml`; otherwise it stays pending until `wrapper-canary.yml` passes. The gate uses `pull_request_target`, but runs base code and reads only the file list over the API.

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers, both fixed: the gate shared a file with the `@wrapper-canary` call, which GitHub resolves for every run, and the push procedure let a fork push run unread code. Still open:
- The ~10-minute bound is documented, not enforced. The dispatch wrapper has no timeout input, so its own 75-minute limit applies.
- A `pull_request` job named `wrapper-canary` in a fork could perhaps satisfy the required status, the same weakness `ci` has.
- Board-test's review runs are found by "newest since the reopen", not matched to the scratch pull request.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test, new file `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`:

  ```yaml
  name: wrapper-canary-review
  on:
    pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
      types: [reopened]
  permissions: {}
  jobs:
    review:
      if: github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)
      uses: cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary
      permissions: {contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: write, actions: read, id-token: write, statuses: write}
  ```

  board-test also needs the variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`, and its `AGENT` must be unset or a real agent.
- Tailnet federation and inference broker: admit `job_workflow_ref` `cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary` and `.../cgwalters-review.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary`.
- cgwalters-forge/actions:
  - The branch `wrapper-canary`, created at main, with a ruleset that lets only maintainers update it.
  - The variables `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`: a scratch issue, and a non-draft scratch pull request opened by a collaborator, both in board-test.
  - The environment `agent-apply`, and access to the organization secret `CGWALTERS_BOT_PAT`.
  - Last, the main ruleset's required status check `wrapper-canary`.

Closes #138

items.title: workflows: Add org-review.yml for an organization ruleset to require

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

items.body:
Today every repository carries its own review.yml, and a new one gets no review until someone copies the file in. org-review.yml is that caller made a required workflow: it runs on pull_request_target and calls cgwalters-review.yml at the commit tracker pins (d8e22f7), so the job_workflow_ref the tailnet and broker admit does not change. .github/rulesets/org-review.json is the ruleset for the operator to apply: evaluate mode, all repositories' default branches, no bypass actors, requiring the workflow at refs/heads/main of this repository.

Part of #129

The default task is not wired. At d8e22f7 the wrapper hardcodes workflow/review.toml and workflow/review.md, and agentic-job v0.6.2's policy reads them only from the target's checkout. So a repository without them fails policy. A fallback needs a review-task input on the wrapper, at a new pin, with the admission moved too.

Operator steps, none taken here: set the organization variables AGENT, AGENT_MODEL, AGENT_RUNNER, AGENT_CONFIG, AGENT_CONFIG_REPO, AGENT_CONFIG_PATH, INFERENCE_URL, INFERENCE_AUDIENCE and AGENT_REAL_REVIEWS. The wrapper at d8e22f7 defaults INFERENCE_URL to an older host, so set it. Then create the ruleset from the JSON (`gh api -X POST orgs/cgwalters-forge/rulesets --input .github/rulesets/org-review.json`), narrowed to one repository first. Merging this needs an owner bypass: workflows-check refuses a new pull_request_target trigger and its zizmor ignore.

Follow-ups from review: in a repository that keeps its review.yml, both workflows share the wrapper's `review-pull-N` concurrency group and cancel each other's agent job, so drop that repository's review.yml (step 4) when adding it. The required run passes when the wrapper skips (drafts; ruleset workflows never get ready_for_review) and whatever the verdict. workflows-check.md pins its ruleset to a commit SHA rather than a branch, which the operator may prefer here too. There is no merge_group trigger.

Verified with `node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs` (42 pass), actionlint, and zizmor offline. The runner-labels lint needs cargo, which wasn't available, so it did not run; the workflow has no runs-on of its own. One review pass; its one blocker is the missing default task above.

items.title: libvirt ssh: Start the domain if it is shut off
items.body:
A persistent VM that was stopped (by `bcvk libvirt stop`, a host reboot, or shutting down from inside the guest) made `bcvk libvirt ssh` fail with a hint to run `virsh start`. Since starting it and retrying is always the next step, `libvirt ssh` now does that itself for a domain that is shut off: it prints a notice on stderr (so a remote command's stdout stays clean), starts the domain, and waits for SSH with the same 180s timeout `libvirt run --ssh-wait` uses, since the guest has to boot first. Other states (paused, crashed, ...) still produce an error, since the right action there is less clear.

This is a behavior change for scripts: `bcvk libvirt ssh VM -- cmd` against a stopped VM used to fail fast, and now boots the VM (which keeps running afterwards) and runs the command.

This is the auto-start half of #158. Stopping idle VMs automatically would need something inside the guest (and, as noted in the issue, not every use case runs systemd), so it's left for later.

A second commit gives `libvirt start --ssh` the same longer wait: it used to connect with the 60s retry meant for an already running guest, right after `virsh start`.

A new integration test, `test_libvirt_ssh_autostart`, creates a VM, force-stops it, then checks that `libvirt ssh VM -- echo hello` succeeds with exactly `hello` on stdout, the notice on stderr, and the domain running afterwards. It boots a full VM, so it's added to the tests nextest runs one at a time. The man page documents the new behavior.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace with KVM and libvirt (`qemu:///session`):

- `make validate` and `cargo test` pass (82 + 22 unit tests).
- `test_libvirt_ssh_autostart` passes under the integration profile on centos-bootc:stream10.
- By hand: after `libvirt stop --force`, `bcvk libvirt start --ssh VM </dev/null` waited for the boot and exited 0 after 29s, with the domain running.

CI note (2026-09-24): the [`integration-tests (2)` failure](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/actions/runs/35952102962/job/107493840229) is unrelated to this change: `just pull-test-images` failed with "fetching blob: authentication required" from quay mid-pull, before any test ran, the flake targeted by cgwalters-forge/bcvk#2. Reran the failed jobs once.

Related: #158

The `Signed-off-by: Colin Walters <walters@verbum.org>` on these commits was added on cgwalters's approval of the review draft: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/pull/6#pullrequestreview-5629450771

items.title: composefs-ctl: match composefs-c's command-line contract

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Part of #31

composefs-info, mount.composefs and mkcomposefs now follow composefs-c's command-line contract, so scripts and C's own test suite can use them in its place. `--filter` and `--basedir` are global options in composefs-info (`composefs-info --filter=NAME dump IMAGE` works). The filter is applied when the image loads, so dump, ls, objects and missing-objects all honour it. Missing image or file operands are now an error. mount.composefs rejects `basedir` lists with an empty entry and exits 0 for `-h`. mkcomposefs rejects `--threads=0`. Every parse error now exits 1 instead of clap's 2.

mkcomposefs now applies C's version rules:
- It upgrades to format 1 when the image has a whiteout and max_version allows it. This changes the default digest for images with whiteouts, which now match C's.
- Setting one of `--min-version`/`--max-version` sets the other to 0.
- max_version below min_version is raised to it, not rejected.
- Versions above 1 are rejected.

The man pages now describe the real options and exit statuses.

Verification: new differential tests in `crates/composefs-ctl/tests/c_compat_cli.rs` check exit status and output against values recorded from C built at ec2573a. Results:
- `cargo fmt --check`: exit 0.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` (stable): exit 0, no warnings in composefs-ctl.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude composefs-integration-tests --no-fail-fast`: exit 101. All composefs-ctl tests pass. The 11 failures are in composefs and composefs-ioctls: they need fs-verity on the temp filesystem or a system `mkcomposefs`, and this sandbox has neither.

C's scripts run against the Rust tools:
- `test-should-fail.sh`: fails on `should-fail-empty-xattr-key.dump`, which Rust accepts. `should-fail-too-big.dump` is also accepted. Every other case exits exactly 1.
- `test-dump-filtered.sh`: fails. Rust's dumpfile parser rejects `special.dump` (512-byte inline limit). With C's mkcomposefs building the image, the filtered lines match, but the root line prints directory size 0 where C prints 4096.

Those parser, writer and dump-format gaps are left for follow-up.

Other follow-ups from one review pass, which found no blockers:
- A filtered dump recomputes nlink from the trimmed tree; C keeps the on-disk value.
- `--basedir` is never opened, so a nonexistent path makes every object "missing" instead of failing as in C.
- `missing-objects` without `--basedir` exits 1, which is deliberately stricter than C.
- mkcomposefs applies `--skip-devices` to `--from-file` input; C ignores it there.
- `--filter` only accepts UTF-8 names.
- The `FormatVersion::V0` docs still describe an auto-upgrade that the library writer does not do.

labels.name: area/documentation
labels.description: Updates to the documentation

items.body:
tmt: Generate one file per test and plan, drop test numbers

Every PR that adds a tmt test currently touches the same two generated files (`tmt/tests/tests.fmf` and the generated block of `tmt/plans/integration.fmf`) and picks the next free `# number: N` in its test header. Two PRs open at once therefore collide twice: textually in the generated files and logically on the number (there are already duplicates on main, and several open PRs claim 50).

This series removes both:

1. `xtask/tmt: Generate one fmf file per test and per plan`: `cargo xtask update-generated` writes `tmt/tests/tests/test-*.fmf` and `tmt/plans/integration/plan-*.fmf`, one each. fmf merges these directories into the nodes of `tests.fmf` and `integration.fmf`, which stay as the hand-written common settings, so names, and what `just test-tmt FILTER` selects, are unchanged. Removed tests have their files removed, and `--check` fails on stale ones.
2. `tmt: Identify tests and plans by name, not by number`: tests and plans are `test-<name>` / `plan-<name>` from the file name, the `# number:` header is gone, and test names must be unique (checked). The commit is mechanical: header lines dropped, three scripts and three legacy fmf files renamed, files regenerated, docs updated. Plans run in separate VMs, so nothing depends on their order and no replacement ordering field was needed.

A new test is now one `tests/booted/test-<name>.nu` file with its `# tmt:` header (documented in `tmt/tests/booted/README.md`) plus the two generated files for it.

Tested on a devspace at 43fae7a7, rebased onto bootc-dev/bootc main 1a04bf23 (AMD EPYC 9V45):
- `just validate` passes; `cargo test -p xtask` passes at both commits, and `cargo xtask update-generated direct --check` is clean at both.
- `tmt plan ls --filter enabled:true` lists 40 plans at the first commit, and the second generates the same 40 tests and plans under their new names.
- `just test-tmt readonly switch-zstd-chunked` with `BOOTC_variant=composefs BOOTC_bootloader=systemd`: `plan-readonly` and `plan-switch-zstd-chunked` (the Rust test upstream added since) PASSED.
- `just test-tmt readonly usroverlay` on the ostree variant: `plan-readonly` and `plan-usroverlay` PASSED.

For the VM runs, the image build needed a local, uncommitted workaround: the Dockerfile's `grub-cc-download` stage currently fails on main because `dnf download grub2-efi-x64-cc` finds no such package in Fedora ELN, so it was allowed to fail there. Neither bootloader tested uses grub-cc.

Open PRs that add or change tests will need to drop their `# number:` line, rename if their file has a numeric prefix, and rerun `just update-generated` after rebasing. The Rust booted tests in `crates/tests-integration/src/booted/` follow the same rule: their `// number:` header is gone too.

The `Signed-off-by: Colin Walters <walters@verbum.org>` on these commits was added on cgwalters's approval of the review draft: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/pull/41#pullrequestreview-5576285088

items.title: ci: Check that OpenSSL results are compared against 1
items.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/ostreedev/ostree/pull/3665 (now merged). Many OpenSSL functions (`EVP_DigestVerify`, `EVP_PKEY_verify`, `X509_verify`, ...) return 1 on success and 0 or a negative value on failure, so `if (f (...))`, `!f (...)` and `f (...) != 0` treat an error as success. This adds a coccinelle check, `tests/coccinelle/openssl-retval.cocci`, that flags those forms; `== 1`, `!= 1`, `> 0` and `<= 0` are accepted. The function list comes from the RETURN VALUES sections of the OpenSSL man pages.

`tests/coccinelle.sh` (`make check`, when spatch is installed) picks the file up automatically; its TAP plan always said `1..1`, which is fixed so that a second semantic patch doesn't break it. A new `just coccinelle-check` runs the semantic patches without a build.

This check fails on main as it is, because of the `EVP_DigestSign*` calls that the sign-side fix (the PR this one is stacked on) changes, so it must land after that one.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

> **Note: workflow change needed, not in this PR.** No GitHub job runs the semantic patches today. The agent run that wrote this could not change `.github/`, and suggests adding this under `jobs:` in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (not tested):
>
> ```yaml
>   coccinelle:
>     name: "coccinelle"
>     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
>     container: quay.io/coreos-assembler/fcos-buildroot:testing-devel
>     steps:
>       - name: Checkout repository
>         uses: actions/checkout@v4
>       # https://github.com/actions/checkout/issues/760
>       - name: Mark git checkout as safe
>         run: git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
>       - run: dnf -y install coccinelle just
>       - name: Check semantic patches
>         run: just coccinelle-check
> ```

What was run, by an agent with spatch 1.3.1 in a Fedora container (nothing was compiled):

- The semantic patch on a scratch C file with 11 bad and 9 good forms: exactly the 11 bad ones flagged.
- On d5fcd3e (before #3665): flags the `EVP_DigestVerify*` checks in `otcore-ed25519-verify.c` and `otcore-spki-verify.c`, and the sign calls in `ostree-sign-ed25519.c` and `ostree-sign-spki.c`.
- On main (3b9b60a): flags only the `EVP_DigestSign*` calls in those two sign files; `tests/coccinelle.sh` and `just coccinelle-check` exit 1 there, as intended.
- With those calls temporarily changed to `== 1`: no output, and both `tests/coccinelle.sh` (plan `1..2`) and `just coccinelle-check` pass.

Not verified: a full `make check`, the check against the actual commit this is stacked on (only an equivalent temporary edit), other spatch versions, and the suggested workflow job. A result stored in a variable and tested later is not tracked by the check.

items.title: cleanup: Mount the previous system's /var before removing its packages

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Step 3 of the plan in https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/2559, stacked on #44 (which is stacked on #43): the fix for `bootc-destructive-cleanup.service` failing after an in-place reinstall.

### Root cause

`fedora-bootc-destructive-cleanup` runs `rpm -e --root=/sysroot` on every package of the previous OS. rpm runs the erase scriptlets chrooted in `/sysroot`, so they need the previous OS's `/var`. But `/sysroot` is only the previous root filesystem (btrfs `subvol=/root`); on Fedora 44 cloud images `/var` is a separate `var` subvolume that nothing mounts after the reinstall. netcat's `%preun` (`alternatives --remove`) then fails with `failed to create admindir`, `xargs` exits 123 and the unit fails.

The script is unchanged since f567f7eb (January 2026), so this is not a regression. It went unseen because nothing checked the unit until test 014 was added in 41049cca (2026-09-18), and the bcvk flows never boot a reinstalled system.

### The fix

In `contrib/scripts/fedora-bootc-destructive-cleanup` (plus its man page): if `/sysroot/etc/fstab` has a `/var` entry whose source resolves to a block device, mount it at `/sysroot/var` with `mount --fstab /sysroot/etc/fstab --target-prefix /sysroot /var` before removing the packages. The unit already has `PrivateMounts=true`, so the mount stays private to the service.

The mount is skipped, and the script behaves as before, when:

- `/sysroot/etc/fstab` does not exist or has no `/var` entry;
- `/sysroot/var` is already a mount point;
- the source is not a block device, e.g. a bind mount (warning);
- the mount fails (warning);
- the mounted `/var` turns out to be on the same filesystem as `/sysroot` or as the booted `/var`: it is unmounted again (warning).

The podman prune now runs only if `/sysroot/var/lib/containers` exists.

Not handled: nested mounts under `/var`, a `/var` defined by a `.mount` unit, and LVM or LUKS devices that are not active in the new system. Those give a warning and then the old behaviour. The script only uses `/sysroot` and `/var`, so it is the same for ostree and composefs; but on composefs `--cleanup` never writes the stamp file (only `ostree_install` does), so the service never runs there. That is a separate gap and is not fixed here.

### Alternatives the run listed

The run called this "not a clear-cut choice":

- (a) `rpm -e --noscripts`, `bootc-dev/bootc#2561`. Smaller, but it skips every scriptlet on every system (cgwalters called it a big hammer on that PR), and the old `/var` stays unreachable for the podman prune.
- (b) Record the needed mounts at install time in a state file (cgwalters' general idea). More general, but bigger and riskier.
- (c) Delete btrfs subvolumes instead of using rpm.

It chose the targeted mount because it matches cgwalters' stated preference ("special case mount preservation").

### Questions for the maintainer (from the run)

1. Fix design: I implemented a guarded mount of the previous /var from its fstab. The alternative is `rpm -e --noscripts` (`bootc-dev/bootc#2561`), which is smaller but skips all scriptlets. I recommend keeping the mount and closing that PR or rebasing it onto this; a maintainer should decide.
2. Not run here (no KVM): `just test-tmt-readonly`. Test 014 must now pass on the reinstall path, and the cleanup unit's journal should show `mount --fstab /sysroot/etc/fstab --target-prefix /sysroot /var` succeeding.
3. Should `install to-existing-root --cleanup` with the composefs backend write the cleanup stamp? Today it is silently ignored. I left it alone as a separate change.
4. `bootloader-update.service` failure after the reinstall on a BIOS-booted guest: file a separate issue (bootc removes `EFI/` while `bootupd --auto` installs only BIOS)? I recommend yes, after confirming the guest's boot mode. (The run inferred this cause; it did not verify it.)

### What the run did and did not run

Ran: `shellcheck` and `bash -n` on the script; `cargo xtask update-generated direct --check`; and the new function in an unprivileged user and mount namespace (`unshare -rm`) against a scratch fstab with `/sysroot` and `/var` relocated, 8 scenarios (a tmpfs `/var` entry mounts; no `/var` entry, no fstab, an already-mounted `/sysroot/var`, a non-block source and a bad mount option are each skipped; a `/var` on the same filesystem as the old root or as the live `/var` is unmounted again). The block-device check was stubbed for the cases that need a mount.

Not run: a real boot, a btrfs subvolume mount, `just test-tmt-readonly`, and the full `just validate` container build. There are no unit tests because the logic is bash. So as opened, this change has never executed on a reinstalled system; a devspace verification will follow as a comment.

items.title: cli: Un-hide `bootupctl backend` and document its verbs
items.body:
`bootupctl backend` was hidden to keep the client side less confusing, but hidden commands cause more confusion than they avoid. Image build tooling uses it, and our own README, Dockerfile.bls and tests reference `backend install`, `generate-update-metadata` and `set-default-bootloader`, yet `--help` gives no hint that these exist or what they are for.

The first commit is a prep: `bootupctl backend` had its own hand-synced copy of the `bootupd` verbs, each individually hidden, so it now reuses `DVerb` and both entrypoints share one set of verbs and help text. The second shows `backend` in `bootupctl --help`, after the verbs for a booted system. It gets help text saying these commands act on an OS tree or target root at build/install time, and pointing users who want to update a running system at `update` and `adopt-and-update`. A unit test keeps `backend` and its verbs visible and documented.

```
Commands:
  status            Show components status
  update            Update all components
  adopt-and-update  Update all adoptable components
  validate          Validate system state
  backend           Low-level commands for building and installing OS images
```

For maintainers: this reverses the intent of the removed `FIXME(lucab)` comment, which planned to eventually drop `backend` from bootupctl after coreos/fedora-coreos-config#595. Since image build tooling still relies on it, documenting it seems better than keeping it half-hidden.

The issue also suggests detecting a booted system and giving clearer guidance there. That is not done here, because `backend install` is legitimately run on a booted host (e.g. `bootc install to-existing-root`), so a simple "systemd is running" check would misfire. The help text covers the guidance for now. So this is related to #1119 rather than closing it.

Testing, on a 16-core devspace in `rust:1.90.0` (the pinned lint toolchain in rust.yml): `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all-targets` (40 passed, 1 ignored). I also checked the `bootupctl --help` and `bootupctl backend --help` output by hand.

Related: #1119

items.title: generator: Mask gpt-auto's boot.automount over our /boot bind mount
items.body:
Since ostree 2026.3 systemd-gpt-auto-generator can find the root disk and claims the empty `/boot` for the ESP, so its `boot.automount` (2min idle timeout) ends up fronting our generated `/boot` bind mount. Once it idles out, `local-fs.target` is stopped along with `boot.mount`, and at shutdown the automount is torn down before `ostree-finalize-staged.service` runs, which then fails with `Remounting /boot read-write: Invalid argument` and the staged deployment is dropped. Mask `boot.automount` when we generate `boot.mount`.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Testing, on a 16-core devspace:
- Fedora 44 bootc (ostree 2026.4) VM, xfs: after an emulated idle expiry (`systemctl stop boot.mount; ls /boot`), a staged `ostree admin deploy --stage` is dropped at reboot with the error above; without the expiry it finalizes. With this change (F44 image built from this branch), `boot.automount` is masked and the staged deployment is booted after the same sequence.
- New `privileged_verify_boot_not_automounted` test fails on stock F44 (`/boot` is autofs) and passes with this change; `STREAM=stream10 just test-tmt` passes.

items.title: devspace: Log in over SSH as an unprivileged runner-sandbox user
items.body:
SSH sessions on a devspace ran as `runner`, the same uid (with passwordless sudo) as the workflow steps. The running keepalive step's `/proc/PID/environ` holds `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`/`_URL`, so any build script started over SSH could mint GitHub OIDC tokens that the Tailscale OAuth client trusts.

- **Separate uid (the boundary).** Sessions log in as a new user, `runner-sandbox`, with no sudo. Another uid can't read `Runner.Worker`'s or any step's environ or memory. `scripts/setup-runner-sandbox.mjs` (Node) creates it (kvm group and subuids; not libvirt, whose `qemu:///system` access is root-equivalent). It also fixes the real exposures of the umask-000 image:
  - `/home/runner` and `/opt/hca` become private, since the runner's `.credentials` and the compute agent's token were world-readable;
  - world write permission is removed, because `runner-sandbox` could otherwise add a polkit rule granting itself root;
  - `/etc/environment` loses runner's `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (actions/runner-images#14649), so logins get their own runtime directory;
  - the ssh crypto-policies include loses its group write bit, since ssh refuses a group-writable config.
- **No sudo or polkit for runner-sandbox.** It is in no sudoers rule or admin group anyway; a sudoers rule (`runner-sandbox ALL=(ALL:ALL) !ALL`) makes that explicit, and when polkit is installed a rule answers no to all its requests, `pkexec` included.
- **Use the token once.** The keepalive step, which lives as long as the devspace, re-executes itself without `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` and `ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN`. `tailscaled`, started by the action with `sudo -E`, still holds the token, readable only by root.
- **Hardening on top:** `ptrace_scope=1`, Cockpit's socket disabled, and no instance metadata service for `runner-sandbox` or its rootless containers.

The toolchain moves into the workflow (`packages.txt`), since sessions can't install packages. `scripts/runner-sandbox.mjs` is the single definition of the user and of how a step runs something as it (`run0`, so it gets its own login session like an SSH login's, with a fixed environment); `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` uses it for the dotfiles, and #3's agent.yml runs the same setup script. A first commit references the workflow's actions by major tag (checkout v7, tailscale v4) instead of SHAs, for Renovate.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

What's left: anything running as `runner` or root during setup (the runner, the actions it uses, package scriptlets), and root processes that are already running (tailscaled, sshd). `NoNewPrivileges` for the runner itself isn't possible from inside a job, because `Runner.Listener`/`Worker` run under the image's `hosted-compute-agent.service` and restarting that would end the job. Narrowing the Tailscale federated identity's claims and keeping `tag:bootc-dev-sandbox`'s ACL tight limit what a minted token is worth.

Testing, at this head (0edf5c1), on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace started from main (run 36275733071; main predates runner-sandbox, so this branch was pushed there):
- `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` (15 passed); `actionlint` and `node --check` locally.
- `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs` ran twice cleanly. Then runner-sandbox logged in over SSH, through a PAM sshd with this workflow's auth settings (on 127.0.0.1:2222, as its own unit, so the login got a systemd session). There `sudo -n true` and `sudo -l` fail, `pkexec` says "Not authorized", `systemctl restart sshd` gets "Access denied" (without the polkit rule, an earlier run showed it asking for interactive authentication instead), and `su` to root or runner fails authentication (both passwords are locked in the image, so nothing to lock). Rootless podman ran a container, `bcvk ephemeral run-ssh` booted centos-bootc:stream10, and runner keeps its sudo. Script and logs: https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/619656d679aad001f51cfa7b806942d1
- Outside the setup's `-xdev` sweep, `/run`, `/dev/shm` and `/mnt` have no world-writable non-sticky files other than sockets. `/mnt` is empty, and there is no swap on this runner size.
- `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` (runner-sandbox's dotfiles) and #3's isolation check (12 checks) passed at 558171a (run 36240484839). The token scrub and sshd admitting only runner-sandbox were covered by run 36206810916. None of these changed here.
- At 619398e (this head; the change since 0edf5c1 makes `/var/run/tailscale` root's only, since tailscaled's LocalAPI socket is 0666 and lets any user `tailscale nc` through the node and `tailscale status` the tailnet; the keepalive now runs `sudo tailscale status --self`): `cargo test` (15 passed) on a 16-core devspace (run 36415814928). There, with the directory at the image's 0755, `tailscale nc <tailnet host> 22` as runner-sandbox connected and `tailscale status` listed the tailnet; after the setup script both fail with permission denied, and `sudo tailscale status` still works for runner.
- At 391d342 (`runner-sandbox.mjs` uses `run0` instead of plain `systemd-run`, per review): on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (run 36487000792), `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` for a freshly created user, #3's isolation check (15 ok, applied on #3's head), rootless `podman run` through `asSandbox` (systemd cgroup manager, runroot in `/run/user/UID`), exit statuses passed through, and `cargo test` (15 passed). machinectl shell, run0 and systemd-run compared in a bcvk CentOS Stream 10 VM and on the runner: https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/f932edce0622dba38e1b9018c01c6c31
- At 7cb2947 (this head; the same plus `env -u` dropping the `SUDO_USER`/`SUDO_UID`/`SUDO_GID` run0 sets, and `CollectMode=inactive-or-failed`, since run0 otherwise leaves a failed unit for every nonzero exit): on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (run 36488428943), `setup-runner-sandbox.mjs --init Justfile` for a fresh user, `asSandbox` env has no `SUDO_*`, rootless `podman run` (systemd cgroups, runroot in `/run/user/1002`, exit 5 passed through), no failed units left, `cargo fmt --check`/`clippy -D warnings`/`cargo test` (15 passed). #3's and #5's checks at their restacked heads are in those PRs.
- devspace.yml itself (including the Tailscale action at v4 and checkout at v7) can only run from the default branch, so it is untested as a whole until merged.

homegit's bot-devspace now logs in as `runner-sandbox` and falls back to `runner` (cgwalters-bot/homegit#7).

items.title: devspace: Wait for SSH readiness after start
items.body:
`cargo devspace start` now returns only once ordinary SSH accepts the run's key, so callers no longer have to guess when the runner is usable. It still prints the run ID and URL first, so a failed wait stays recoverable with `ssh` or `stop`.

This is the rework of bootc-dev/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox#2 per review: instead of the deadline-bound process-group machinery there (and the rustix dependency), `start` reuses the polling loop `ssh` already had, factored out as `wait_for_ssh`. `start` waits up to 15 minutes (queueing plus provisioning before sshd starts, the same bound homegit's bot-devspace uses); `ssh` keeps its 3.

Tested: on GitHub runners (https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox/actions/runs/37056787507, this commit plus a scratch build workflow), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` (17 passed). With that build, `devspace start --duration 30 --cores 4` returned after 67s with SSH ready (run https://github.com/bootc-dev/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox/actions/runs/37056874540), `devspace ssh` then ran commands there, and `stop` cancelled it. Cancelling a second run during the wait (https://github.com/bootc-dev/cgwalters-devspace-sandbox/actions/runs/37057024954) made `start` exit 1 with `workflow completed (cancelled)` and the retry hint.

Rebased onto current main after the earlier fork PR (#13) was merged into the fork's main by mistake; the code is unchanged, so the results above are for the pre-rebase commit.

items.title: bootc: mount the deployment with bootc when it has `install mount`
items.body:
When the build root's bootc has `bootc install mount` (bootc-dev/bootc#2483), the customization stages after `bootc install` mount the deployment with osbuild's `org.osbuild.bootc.deployment` mount, for either storage backend; otherwise they keep `org.osbuild.ostree.deployment`. image-builder no longer needs to know the storage backend of non-UKI images: a bootc without `install mount` also predates choosing composefs from the container (bootc-dev/bootc#2500), so it installs those with ostree. The support is probed with `bootc install mount --help` (exit 2, clap's unknown-command error, means no), in the target container and in a separate build container, whose bootc is the one that runs.

- UKI images with `install mount`: users, groups, directories, files and the subscription are applied; kernel arguments, ignition, the bootloader configuration and extra mountpoints stay refused (warning). Without `install mount` the warning now says that /etc and /var customizations need it.
- `pxe-tar-xz` keeps `org.osbuild.ostree.deployment`, since its live root comes from the ostree deployment.
- Manifests for containers without `install mount` don't change (`tools/gen-manifest-checksums.sh`: no changes on any commit).

Supersedes #4 and #6; stacked on #2 (its two commits come first). Needs https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/osbuild/pull/1 for the mount. The first commit adds the README.md review marker that the repository's AGENTS.md requires.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Testing, on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (cgwalters-devspace-37053693285; [logs](https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/bbf8b3d25ae1377e269fc16b419250f9)), disks built as root by this branch's container with osbuild from cgwalters-forge/osbuild#1, with a blueprint adding kargs, a group, users with SSH keys and files, booted with qemu-kvm under UEFI:
- composefs image from bootc main (`BOOTC_variant=composefs` on fedora-bootc:44): all post-install stages use `org.osbuild.bootc.deployment`; boots composefs with all customizations and the karg.
- ostree image from bootc main: `org.osbuild.bootc.deployment`; boots ostree with all customizations.
- stock `quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:44` (bootc 1.16.13, no `install mount`): `org.osbuild.ostree.deployment`; boots with all customizations.
- `pxe-tar-xz` from the bootc main ostree image: builds with `org.osbuild.ostree.deployment`, manifest identical to upstream main's. It fails to boot in `ostree-prepare-root` (composefs mount I/O error) with upstream main's image-builder too.
- `go test -race ./...` in fedora:43 as the CI job: the same 29 `cmd/image-builder` failures as upstream main; `go vet`, `gofmt` clean; `tools/gen-manifest-checksums.sh`: no changes.

items.title: install: Add --output-{json,pairs}-{path,fd} for the install result

labels.name: area/install
labels.description: Issues related to `bootc install`

labels.name: area/documentation
labels.description: Updates to the documentation

items.body:
Adds options to `bootc install to-filesystem` (and `to-disk`, `to-existing-root`, which share the code) to write a machine-readable result once the install succeeded, as sketched in https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/542#issuecomment-5897670625:

```
--output-json-path PATH    --output-json-fd FD
--output-pairs-path PATH   --output-pairs-fd FD
```

At most one may be given. Pairs are `KEY="value"` lines as `lsblk --pairs --shell` (one per line; `"`, `\`, `$` and backtick are backslash-escaped as in os-release, so `eval` round-trips). Keys: backend, stateroot, deployment/etc/var paths relative to the target, bootloader, image, image transport and digest; JSON uses camelCase (`etcPath`), pairs upper snake case (`ETC_PATH`). A path is replaced atomically; an fd must be inherited (not close-on-exec) and writable, checked before anything is installed. The path's directory is opened up front and carried across bootc's re-execs, so `/tmp/...` doesn't silently land in the tmpfs bootc mounts there.

```sh
pairs=$(bootc install to-filesystem --output-pairs-fd 3 /mnt 3>&1 >&2)
eval "$pairs"
cp my.service "/mnt/$ETC_PATH/systemd/system/"
```

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Not covered: `install reset`, which has its own flow.

Testing, on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (AMD EPYC 7763; no fork CI):

- `just unit-tests` passed (bootc-lib: 290, including 7 new ones covering pairs quoting with a real `sh` eval round-trip, key names, rendering, and fd/path validation), and so did `just validate`.
- tmt `plan-23-install-outside-container`, extended to install with `--output-json-path` and check the reported deployment, `/etc` (a file written via `bootc install mount` is found under `etcPath`), `/var`, image and digest, plus that an fd the caller didn't pass is rejected before installing: passed for the ostree variant and for composefs (grub, ext4, BLS).
- By hand, in a `bcvk ephemeral` VM: `podman run --privileged --preserve-fds 1 localhost/bootc bootc install to-disk --output-pairs-fd 3 ... 3>&1 >&2` into `pairs=$(...)`, then `eval "$pairs"`; the reported `$ETC_PATH`, `$VAR_PATH` and `$DEPLOYMENT_PATH/usr` existed on the installed disk.

xref https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/542

items.title: tests: Check that GC keeps a V2 rollback in the 1.16 bridge test

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

items.body:
**Stacked on forge #30** (`bot/cfs-bridge-1164`, itself on #18). Until those land this PR also shows their commits; only the last commit is new.

test-49 never ran a repository GC while a 1.16.0 install's V2 deployment was the rollback of a V1 one, which is what every such system looks like right after its first upgrade with current bootc. Its only GC ran after the rollback, with the V2 deployment booted, and without `--prune-repo`, so it only looked at boot binaries and could not report a removed object.

With the upgrade booted, the test now runs `composefs-gc --prune-repo` (the GC upgrades run) and checks that the rollback's boot entry, deployment state and EROFS image (still V2) survive, and that `cfsctl fsck` and `cfsctl oci fsck` of the rollback's bootc tag pass. Then it rolls back as before, which proves the V2 deployment still boots. The final `--assert-no-op` now includes `--prune-repo`.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

**Tested** on a 16-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-37011656929), Fedora 44 base, `just test-composefs-bridge`:

- at this head: `unsealed 1.16.0`, `sealed 1.16.0` and `bls 1.16.4` all passed; the boot2 GC removed the 1.16.0 or 1.16.4 install's leftovers (53-56 objects) and fsck and `oci fsck` passed, and the final `--prune-repo --assert-no-op` found nothing;
- that it catches a regression (run at c191f09b, this check before the tag prefix became a constant): with GC temporarily changed to drop a rollback whose EROFS format differs from the booted one's, `unsealed 1.16.0` fails at the new boot2 check (GC removed the rollback's manifest, so `bootc status` can no longer read the rollback), while the test from #30's head passes against the same broken GC;
- dropping `additional_roots` for non-booted deployments alone is not caught, correctly: the V2 boot image is also reachable from the rollback's tagged manifest config, so nothing is lost.

items.title: Carry the operator's sign-off on attested reworks; /no-carry to revoke
items.body:
Carry the operator's DCO sign-off past a rework when a separate review agent attests that the new head isn't substantively different, as cgwalters asked (DCO churn like bootc#2500).

- `bot-git carry-signoff --was H0 --attestation FILE`: pairs H0 with H1 the way `rework` does, refuses any attestation that doesn't match the branch (SHAs, pairing, every eligible commit classed, no unpaired one), keeps the sign-off on classes a-d, drops it on (e), and never signs a commit that is new since H0. `bot-git drop-signoff` and `rework --drop-signoff COMMIT` replace the hand-run `commit-tree` plumbing.
- `bot-pr carry-note`: posts one audit comment per carried head, with classes, reasons, who attested, the range-diff command and a hidden record. It refuses chained carries. `bot-pr no-carry` acts on a `/no-carry` reply. `bot-signoff-due --apply` routes those replies through the sweeps, and bot-poll does the same on the hot path.
- `coordinator/carry-attest.md` is the brief for the attesting agent. AGENTS.md, upstream-pr, and the worker/reviewer preambles now spell out the exception. Merging still needs his approval where stale reviews are dismissed.

items.title: devspace: Give SSH sessions the soft deadline as DEVSPACE_DEADLINE
items.body:
SSH sessions on a devspace now get `DEVSPACE_DEADLINE` and `DEVSPACE_STARTED` (epoch seconds) through sshd `SetEnv`, and the keepalive loop counts down to that same deadline. Tools can then tell how long a devspace has left without hard-coding `timeout-minutes` or parsing run names (cgwalters-bot/homegit#58 reads it for `bot-devspace remaining`).

A runner can't see its own deadline: on a live devspace, SSH sessions have no `GITHUB_*`/`ACTIONS_*` variables, the `Runner.Worker` environment has no job metadata, and neither the job message nor the other `_diag` logs mention the job timeout, which GitHub enforces server-side. The `duration` input is only in the step's environment and `event.json`, which are workflow internals.
