items.title: tree: Replace ExternalNoVerity with ExternalPath, keep ostree's redirect
items.body:
ostree gives each file a libcomposefs payload of `xx/<checksum>.file` and sets the fsverity digest separately. composefs-capi turned the payload into an `ObjectID` (dropping `.file`), or ignored it when a digest was set, so the overlay redirect pointed at a file that doesn't exist and an ostree deployment on the Rust libcomposefs couldn't boot ("overlayfs: lazy lowerdata lookup failed", "No /sbin/init").

This replaces `RegularFile::ExternalNoVerity` with `ExternalPath { redirect: Option<_>, verity: Option<_>, size }`, which is how libcomposefs models a file: an optional redirect as given, plus an independent optional digest for the metacopy xattr. `RegularFile::external()` builds one from that pair and normalizes it, so the capi, the EROFS reader and the dumpfile parser all agree: a redirect that is the digest's object path gives `External` (the usual composefs layout), neither gives `Sparse`, and anything else is `ExternalPath`. The capi maps payload and digest exactly like C (empty files get no metacopy or redirect, an empty payload writes no redirect). `RegularFile::backing_path()` gives the redirect target of either external variant, which `composefs-info ls/objects/missing-objects` and `cfsctl`'s backing-path dump now list, like C's `composefs-info` does with the payload. `RegularFile::repo_object_id()` gives callers that open the backing object from a repository the object for either variant.

This is a public API change, and so is `dumpfile_parse::Item::Regular`'s `path` becoming an `Option` (see below). bootc needs a small change for both (`bot/composefs-externalpath` on cgwalters-bot/bootc, on top of `bootc-dev/bootc#2490`): four `ExternalNoVerity` matches and one `Item::Regular` in its GC. That only matters when bootc bumps to a composefs-rs release with this; the revdep workflow is disabled until then anyway.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (kernel 6.12):
- `OSTREE_IMAGE_C_DIGEST` comes from the C libcomposefs (composefs/composefs `ec2573a`): `tests/ostree-image.c` built against it in a Fedora container, then `fsverity digest` of its output. Besides ostree's forms (`.file` with and without a digest, an empty file, a symlink), the image has a digest-only file and one whose payload is the digest's object path. The capi test `test_ostree_image_matches_c` builds the same image through our capi, checks what the reader makes of each file, and gets the same digest.
- `just test-capi` passes, including the step that `cmp`s the image from `ostree-image.c` written by each library, and the C `test-checksums.sh`/`test-units.sh` suites.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude composefs-integration-tests -- --skip fsverity::` in a Fedora container like the `fedora` CI job: all pass (composefs 219, capi 22). After the last round of fixes, `cargo test -p composefs-capi -p composefs-ctl`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, fmt and `just test-capi` were rerun and pass. The fsverity tests were skipped since the container's /var/tmp has no fs-verity. `just clippy`, `check-feature-combos`, `fmt-check` and `check-fuzz` pass.
- `just test-integration` in the same container: 109 passed, 3 failed, and the same 3 fail on main there (no skopeo, no `security.selinux` on the container's /var/tmp, and a varlink connection reset).
- cgwalters-forge/composefs-rs#4 restacked on this: `just bootc/test-ostree` (bootc from the branch above) builds the composefs RPMs, confirms libostree and the initramfs load our libcomposefs, and bootc's `readonly` and `image-upgrade-reboot` plans on the ostree backend pass, so the deployment boots and upgrades through the Rust libcomposefs.

Design notes:
- **Digest without payload.** C writes a metacopy xattr with the digest and no redirect, so overlayfs looks the file up by its own path in the data layer. That is `ExternalPath { redirect: None, verity: Some(_) }` everywhere now: the capi no longer makes up a redirect from the digest, the reader no longer turns such a file into `External` (which would add a redirect when the image is rewritten), and the dumpfile parser accepts payload `-` with a digest, as C does and as our own writer emits. For that, `Item::Regular`'s `path` is now an `Option`. Such a file has no backing path, so `composefs-info objects` doesn't list it, like C.
- **Interior NUL.** A redirect with an interior NUL can't be a C payload; converting it for the capi now fails (EINVAL from `lcfs_load_node_from_image*`, with the error logged at debug) instead of silently dropping the redirect. The test for it has a subdirectory and a hardlinked pair converted before the bad file, so freeing the partial tree is exercised; it passes under ASan (nightly `-Zsanitizer=address`, with LeakSanitizer) on the devspace.
- **Absolute payloads.** `composefs-info missing-objects` trims leading slashes before joining a payload to `--basedir`, like C's `abs_to_rel_path()`, so a `/`-prefixed payload can't escape it.
- **V2 null chunk index.** V2 writes external files as chunk-based with a single chunk (format 31), so the inode needs one null chunk index, which `External` gets. `ExternalNoVerity` got none there. That was harmless in practice, since only the capi produced it and the capi writes V1. `ExternalPath` gets the same index as `External`. V1 output is unchanged, and no pinned V2 digest moved. `Sparse` in V2 still gets no chunk index; that looks like the same issue but is left alone here.
- **Stacking.** cgwalters-forge/composefs-rs#4 (the ostree revdep test) is stacked on this and should land after it.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Related: https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/issues/323

items.title: oci: Retry transient registry failures when pulling
items.body:
Pulls through skopeo have no retries at all, so a single 503 or dropped connection from e.g. quay.io fails the whole pull. That's a regular source of CI flakes for bootc (bootc-dev/bootc#2177). The proxy doesn't retry for us: in podman the retry loop lives in the caller (c/common `pkg/retry`), so this adds one here.

The proxy decides which errors are worth retrying. Since skopeo 1.19 it tags each failed reply with c/common's `IsErrorRetryable()` verdict, the same check podman's retry loop uses, and cgwalters-forge/containers-image-proxy-rs#2 exposes that as `Error::is_retryable()`. composefs-rs does no error-text matching of its own. With an older skopeo nothing gets retried, same as today. Only proxy errors count, so a local failure to import verified data is never retried.

Retries happen per proxy operation: opening the image, fetching the manifest, the config, and each layer or delta blob. That way a failed layer doesn't refetch the others. The schedule is podman's default, 3 retries after 1s, 2s and 4s, and a fixed delay can be set like `--retry-delay`. Only `docker://` pulls retry. `PullOptions` gains a public `retry: RetryPolicy` field to tune or disable it. Since `PullOptions` isn't `#[non_exhaustive]`, code that builds it with a struct literal and no `..Default::default()` needs updating. `cfsctl oci pull --retry N` exposes the count (`--retry 0` fails fast); the varlink API keeps the default. Note that `pull_image()` now retries by default too. Each attempt restarts the blob transfer, so a layer's `Started` progress event is sent again per attempt, and cfsctl replaces that layer's bar.

The first commit makes cfsctl print progress messages when stderr isn't a terminal. indicatif drops them otherwise, so retry warnings would never show up in CI logs. It could land on its own.

**Before merging:** the second commit points `containers-image-proxy` at the forge branch through `[patch.crates-io]`. The plan is to land cgwalters-forge/containers-image-proxy-rs#2 and release it as 0.11.1 first, then replace the `[patch]` with a version bump. The retry loop stays in composefs-rs for now; bootc already has its own, and switching bootc's classifier to `is_retryable()` is a separate follow-up (bootc-dev/bootc#2466).

The new integration test serves an OCI layout from a small in-process registry. The registry answers the first manifest request with a 503 and hangs up on the first request for each blob. The test checks that `cfsctl oci pull docker://...` recovers and yields the pinned image ID, and that `--retry 0` fails. It goes through the real skopeo, so it also checks that skopeo classifies both failures as retryable. That classification needs skopeo 1.19, so the test parses `skopeo --version` and skips with older versions (upstream's ubuntu-24.04 runners have 1.13.3). The skopeo check is now one shared helper in the integration tests' `main.rs`; before, `old_format.rs` had its own copy.

Testing ran on a 16-core devspace at head 39b7496, with proxy-rs pulled from the forge branch. Two containers were used:
- **`quay.io/fedora/fedora:latest`** (rustc 1.98, skopeo 1.22.3): `just fmt-check`, `just clippy` and `just check-feature-combos` were clean, and `cargo test -p composefs-oci -p composefs-ctl` passed (174 composefs-oci tests, including the retry and `fetch_layer` unit tests). `just test-integration` passed 112, including `test_pull_retries_transient_registry_errors` and the new `test_parse_skopeo_version`. It failed `test_ostree_pull_local_all_modes` and `test_varlink_open_repository_invalid_spec`, and main fails the same two in that container.
- **`ubuntu:24.04`** (skopeo 1.13.3, rust stable), as in upstream's smoke job: the retry test reports `skopeo (1, 13, 3) does not classify retryable errors (needs (1, 19, 0)), skipping registry retry test` and passes, and `test_parse_skopeo_version` passes. I stopped the full unprivileged suite there after it sat for 30 minutes with idle `cfsctl` processes. I didn't dig into that, and main wasn't run there for comparison.

The fs-verity-dependent unit tests, `just check-fuzz` and the privileged VM tests weren't run for this revision. The earlier revision passed `check-fuzz`.

Closes #348

items.title: install mount: Select the deployment from the default boot entry

labels.name: area/documentation
labels.description: Updates to the documentation

items.body:
`bootc install mount --latest` now mounts the deployment that the default boot entry boots, instead of requiring the sysroot to contain exactly one deployment. This is the follow-up to the review on #2483 (`mount.rs:90`). Design notes: https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/3d295a3185c75c5a24989dda21018573

A booted system knows its deployment from the kernel command line. Offline, the equivalent is the command line of the entry the bootloader would pick. The entries come from SYSROOT/boot and the ESP, and they are ordered with the same code `bootc status` uses: for GRUB, the `user.cfg` UKI entries or else the Type 1 entries sorted by file name; otherwise the Type 1 entries in BLS order. For a composefs entry, its digest (or UKI name) picks the deployment. For an `ostree=` entry, it is OSTree's own default (`deployments()[0]`, which OSTree orders from the same entries, as `bootc status` shows it), rather than re-sorting the entries: GRUB's file name order differs from OSTree's at ten or more deployments. The bootloader probe `get_bootloader` uses without EFI variables now takes the boot directories, so mount shares it. A new `--esp` option names the ESP, and defaults to SYSROOT/boot/efi.

Caveats:

- There is no `--boot`. OSTree loads its deployments from SYSROOT/boot, so /boot has to be mounted there anyway, and the man page says so.
- EFI variables (such as a one-time boot entry), boot counting, `loader.conf`'s `default` and grubenv's `saved_entry` are not considered. `bootc status` doesn't consider them either.
- With no boot entries at all, the old rule still applies: a sole deployment is mounted. That keeps a fresh install mountable without mounting the ESP.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace:

- Plan 23 (`install-outside-container`) is extended. On ostree it deploys the same commit ten more times (11 deployments, so file-name order would pick the wrong one) and checks that `--latest` follows OSTree's default, also after `ostree admin set-default`. On composefs it rewrites the installed boot entries to name a missing deployment and checks that the mount fails naming it, then restores them. An earlier two-deployment version of the test, run with main's bootc (683bb05f), failed with `target must contain exactly one deployment (found 2 OSTree, 0 composefs)`.
- With this change, plan 23 passes on ostree/grub, composefs grub/BLS/ext4 and composefs systemd-boot/UKI/ext4 (unsealed), and `just validate` and `just unit-tests` pass. The new unit tests cover entry ordering for each bootloader layout, the boot directory probe, and choosing the deployment.

The `Signed-off-by: Colin Walters <walters@verbum.org>` on these commits was added on cgwalters's approval of the review draft: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/pull/32#pullrequestreview-5354902430

items.title: fix(fips): check the UKI that systemd-stub booted
items.body:
The fips module's UKI check only globs `EFI/Linux/*-$(uname -r).efi`, so a UKI anywhere else can't boot with `fips=1`. bootc installs its UKIs as `EFI/Linux/bootc/bootc_composefs-<digest>.efi`, so a sealed bootc image with `fips=1` dies in the initramfs with "Failed for find UKI for checking".

systemd-stub (v257+) reports the partition and path it was loaded from in `StubDevicePartUUID` and `StubImageIdentifier`. When both are set, the module now mounts that partition and checks exactly the booted UKI against `.<name>.hmac` next to it. It fails rather than falling back if the identifier isn't a usable path (including any `..` component), the UKI is missing, or `boot=` names a different partition. Without the variables it keeps today's glob. The HMAC is now computed over the UKI itself and compared with the `.hmac` value, as `do_rhevh_check` does, rather than `sha512hmac -c`, which hashes whatever file the `.hmac` lists. Also adds FIPS cases to TEST-12-UEFI, a good and a corrupted HMAC (Fedora container only; needs mtools, added to its Dockerfile).

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Tested on 16-core RHEL 10 devspaces ([logs](https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/42fa0798504534efb02ebe39e3097d50); `01-round2.md` covers this head):
- `TESTS=12 test/test.sh fedora`, with mtools installed in the container at run time: passes. The corrupted-HMAC client dies with "HMAC sum mismatch"; the good one logs `BOOTX64.EFI: OK`. With `fips.sh` reverted to main, the FIPS clients fail with "Failed for find UKI for checking".
- Shell-level checks under dash, busybox sh and bash: identifier parsing, `..` rejection, the HMAC comparison, and `boot=` matching or not matching `StubDevicePartUUID`.
- Sealed composefs UKI on CentOS Stream 10 (dracut 107, systemd 257), built with rhel-bootc-examples' `sealing/` and bootc 683bb05f, with `fips=1` and this `fips.sh` added to the initramfs. The HMAC was written by hand to the layout bootc will produce (bootc-dev/bootc#2514): `.bootc_composefs-<digest>.efi.hmac` next to the UKI in `EFI/Linux/bootc/`. With this change the UKI passes the check and boots to multi-user; with a wrong HMAC value it dies. With main's `fips.sh` (tested at the previous head) it dies even with the HMAC in place.
- shfmt, shellcheck and `shellcheck -s busybox` are clean.

items.title: composefs: Rebuild SELinux policy when finalizing a staged deployment

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Proof of concept for #2511, the composefs counterpart of ostree#2569. After the /etc merge in `composefs-finalize-staged`, run `semodule -N --refresh` from the staged deployment's own EROFS root (via `ChrootCmd`, with the merged state /etc bound over it). Without this, a local policy module makes the merge keep the booted system's compiled policy, and every policy change in the new image is silently dropped.

Design notes, options and open questions (stage-time preflight, failure policy, sealed images): https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/7fa03dcf6c3866961aed7d5199366aaa

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Tested on a 16-core devspace with the new tmt test `plan-58-selinux-policy-finalize`, which installs a local CIL module at runtime, switches to a derived image that adds another module, and checks that both are in the loaded policy after reboot:
- composefs, grub, BLS, ext4, unsealed: passed.
- The same test on main (control build, verified to have a different `/usr/bin/bootc`): failed with "new image's policy was not loaded". Both modules were in the store but only the local one was loaded.
- ostree variant, same test: passed (ostree already does this refresh).
- The tmt runs above were on 09d79d8d. The current head only adds a warning-and-skip when semanage.conf's `store-root` isn't under /etc (only /etc is writable in the chroot) and a test comment. For that head, fmt, clippy and unit tests were rerun, but the VMs weren't.

items.title: bootc-base-imagectl: Add build-rootfs --bootloader=systemd
items.body:
Adds `bootc-base-imagectl build-rootfs --bootloader={bootupd:grub+shim,systemd-boot}` (optional; omitting it keeps each architecture's default bootupd set), backed by a `bootloader` manifest variable, so a sealed image can get systemd-boot straight from build-rootfs instead of removing bootupd/shim/grub2 afterwards and installing `systemd-boot-unsigned` offline. No `--sealed` mode and no key handling; signing and the UKI stay with the image build and bootc. This is step 3 of the plan in the [sealed-variant analysis](https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/3138132f4570f6d2d9aedbfbd913842d) for redhat-cop/rhel-bootc-examples#20.

This repo is a GitHub mirror of https://gitlab.com/fedora/bootc/base-images (main at 5014026); nothing has been posted to GitLab.

Notes:
- `--bootloader=systemd-boot` is accepted on x86_64 and aarch64 only. The variant also excludes `bootupd`, since bootc Recommends it and the standard tier (`recommends: true`) otherwise pulls it in.
- `microcode_ctl` moves from `bootupd.yaml` to `kernel.yaml` so both variants keep it; the `bootloader-update.service` preset is only written when that unit exists.
- `--sysusers` now merges into the manifest `variables` instead of replacing them.
- The default (`bootupd:grub+shim` on x86_64) package set is unchanged (bootupd.yaml's postprocess scripts now run at a different point, which looks benign).

Tests, on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (cgwalters-devspace-36272142812), with the tested tree identical to this head:
- `FEDORA_VERSION=44 just test` (standard tier): passes, including the new `tests/Containerfile.test-bootloader-systemd`: `systemd-boot-unsigned` and `microcode_ctl` present, no bootupd, shim, grub2 or efibootmgr, no bootloader-update preset, nobody at 65534 (so `--sysusers` still applies), `bootc container lint` passes. The default image still has bootupd, shim-x64, microcode_ctl and `bootloader-update.service` enabled, and the existing rootfs `bootupd` case passes.
- `ci/shellcheck` and `ci/validate` pass (run locally, since the devspace has no shellcheck).
- Sealed boot: rhel-bootc-examples `sealing/Containerfile` (forge branch `bot/sealing-split-kernel`) changed to build from this F44 image with `build-rootfs --bootloader=systemd-boot`, with the `boot-rpms` and `base-rootfs` stages and the `/var` scrub removed (penultimate is `FROM scratch` + `COPY`). The image builds, `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` passes without the scrub, and `bcvk libvirt run --secure-boot-keys` boots it: Secure Boot enabled (user), systemd-boot 259.9, root is composefs with `verity=require`, `/var/lib` labeled `var_lib_t`.
- On that boot `systemd-tpm2-setup.service` fails: an SELinux denial (`init_t` creating a file on `dosfs_t`) when writing `/boot/loader/credentials/nvpcr-anchor.*.cred`. That comes from systemd 259's NvPCR support and Fedora 44 policy, not from this change.
- Not tested: CentOS Stream 10 (it consumes this repo as a submodule of centos-stream/containers/bootc), rawhide, and aarch64.

items.title: tests: Cover bootc 1.16.4 and BLS in the 1.16 bridge test

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:problem

items.body:
**Stacked on forge #18** (`bot/cfs-ci-coverage`, which makes test-49 build its own fixtures and run in CI). Until that lands, this PR also shows #18's three commits. Only the last commit is new.

test-49 pinned only bootc 1.16.0, which (like 1.16.1 and 1.16.2) reads only the bare `composefs=` and stages the V2 fallback of a dual-format UKI. 1.16.3 already reads `composefs.digest=` first but still generates V2, so switching to a dual-format UKI fails there ("The UKI has the wrong composefs= parameter"). 1.16.4 is the first release to generate V1 (composefs-rs 080f925), and on a repository it created itself it stages V1 directly; nothing tested that path. Not covered: 1.16.3, and 1.16.4-1.16.14 staging on a system installed by 1.16.0-1.16.3. The EROFS format comes from the repository's `meta.json` (V2 when absent) and is never converted, so with a UKI that case fails (bootc-dev/bootc#2334); BLS is not affected. The commit also updates `docs/src/bootc-composefs.7.md` to say which paths are tested.

items.title: bootc: reject a UKI root that is not on a plain GPT partition
items.body:
A UKI command line has no `root=`, so the initrd finds `/` via systemd-gpt-auto-generator by the DPS root partition type. This makes the manifest fail with an error, saying what to change, for bootc containers with a UKI when `/` is on LVM, in a btrfs subvolume, on a DOS partition table, or on a partition without the root type. A LUKS volume directly on the root partition is allowed.

For btrfs this also covers the default table when the container's root filesystem type is btrfs, since image-builder puts `/` in a subvolume: gpt-auto mounts the default subvolume, which image-builder doesn't set, and the UKI has no `rootflags=`:

```
bootc containers with a unified kernel (UKI) need / directly on a GPT partition with the root partition type: the UKI command line has no root=, so the initrd finds / by its partition type, but the container's default root filesystem type "btrfs" puts / in a btrfs subvolume: use --bootc-default-fs (image-builder) or --rootfs (bootc-image-builder) with ext4 or xfs, or a plain partition for / in customizations.disk
```

Layouts that come from the container (its partition table, or a disk.yaml with filesystem or disk sections) are not checked.

Stacked on osbuild/image-builder#2719 (DPS root type) and #2; only the last commit is new.

items.title: composefs: Put systemd-boot entries and UKIs on XBOOTLDR

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
With systemd-boot, the composefs backend now puts the Type #1 entries, kernels and UKIs on an XBOOTLDR partition when the ESP's disk has one (GPT, or MBR type 0xea, formatted as FAT, which is all systemd-boot can read), keeping only systemd-boot and `loader.conf` on the ESP, per the Boot Loader Specification. GRUB is unchanged. A booted system only uses XBOOTLDR if the booted deployment's entry is there, so existing systems with an unused XBOOTLDR keep using the ESP.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

This is the first slice of the "single ESP, no XBOOTLDR" composefs limitation. Multiple ESPs (e.g. mirrored for RAID1) are left for a follow-up.

Rebased onto main b06e0b06 (after #2483 and the #2508 docs restructure); the rebase was clean, and the `bootloaders.md` edit now lives in `bootc-bootloaders.7.md`. Retested at 24519d0e on a 16-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-36601734885, CentOS Stream 10 base): `just validate`, `just unit-tests` (467 passed) and plan-55-composefs-xbootldr on composefs systemd-boot BLS (ext4, unsealed) all passed.

Before the rebase, tested on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace (cgwalters-devspace-36213499802):
- `just validate` and `just unit-tests` (with new unit tests for XBOOTLDR discovery, including MBR, and selection);
- composefs systemd-boot BLS (ext4, unsealed): the new plan-55-composefs-xbootldr and plan-24-image-upgrade-reboot both pass.

plan-55 installs with `bootc install to-filesystem` onto a loop device that has an XBOOTLDR partition, then splits the VM's own ESP into an ESP and an XBOOTLDR partition, moves the entries there, and reboots through a switch, a rollback and a second switch, after which GC must have removed the first derived image's kernel from XBOOTLDR. Before moving the entries, it checks that bootc keeps using the ESP while XBOOTLDR has no entry for the booted deployment. bcvk can't leave free space on the VM's disk (its base disk is sized to `--root-size`), which is why the booted part doesn't come from a real install. The tmt test skips UKI images; the UKI paths share the partition selection with BLS but weren't booted with XBOOTLDR.

Caveats:
- This conflicts trivially with cgwalters-forge/bootc#25 (boot counting) in `boot.rs` and the generated tmt plans.
- systemd-bless-boot renames entries on $BOOT, so with XBOOTLDR it needs XBOOTLDR mounted at `/boot` (systemd-gpt-auto-generator does that when there's no fstab entry); the SELinux `dosfs_t` caveat for renaming entries on the ESP applies there too.

Related: #1929, #1953

items.title: composefs: Build on CentOS Stream 10 with bootc from git, test through image-builder
items.body:
Lets the composefs examples build on CentOS Stream 10 with bootc from git, adds an unsealed composefs example, and adds an end-to-end test that goes from the Containerfile to a qcow2 made by image-builder, boots it, and upgrades it.

- `bootc-git/` builds bootc RPMs from a pinned commit of bootc-dev/bootc (`bootc-git/commit`, with the buildroot image pinned by digest next to it; `just bootc-git-bump` updates both. quay.io drops old digests of the often-rebuilt `centos:stream10` within days, so when the registry reports the pinned one as missing, `bootc-git/resolve-buildroot.py` falls back to the tag with a loud warning and a GitHub Actions annotation that quote podman's error; any other pull error fails, and a pin already in local storage isn't pulled again) the way bootc's `just package` does, into a small image that is also a dnf repository. The examples take it as `BOOTC_RPMS`.
- `sealing/` can use those RPMs, both in the sealed tree and in the stage that computes the composefs digest, and takes `EXTRA_PACKAGES` (redeclared in the sealer stage, so that a host that built with other packages doesn't reuse their UKI: buildah 1.43.2 still reused it, giving a UKI whose digest doesn't match the tree).
- `composefs/` is the unsealed variant: stock boot chain (GRUB), ext4 root, composefs backend. It defaults to `rhel10/rhel-bootc:10.2` like the other examples, and takes the same `base` variable as `sealing/` (from #1; `just base=centos-stream build composefs`), but was only tested on CentOS Stream 10.
- `just e2e sealed|unsealed` (`tests/composefs_e2e.py`, stdlib-only Python) builds three versions of an example, lints them, makes a qcow2 of the first with image-builder, and boots it under QEMU (for sealed, with Secure Boot and our keys enrolled). It checks for a composefs deployment, then switches to build 2 and upgrades to build 3, rebooting and checking after each (booted image digest vs. the pushed one, and the root partition's type: DPS for sealed). The sealed variant needs an image-builder with osbuild/image-builder#2719, merged but not released yet (`IB_IMAGE`), and says so up front. `E2E_SUFFIX` lets several runs share a host.
- A new workflow builds bootc from source at the pinned commit and builds and lints both composefs examples, on PRs and weekly (the example base images float on purpose, so that catches Stream drift). A failed bootc build fails that step rather than leaving the examples on the distribution's bootc. The workflow only calls `just` (`just base=centos-stream build sealing`, `just lint sealing`, and the same for composefs); the new `lint` recipes, which the e2e test uses too, show the image's bootc and run `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`. The VM steps need KVM and stay manual.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Stacked on #1, #2 and #3; only the last six commits are new.

Testing at 0068ab6, 123b26a (first review round) and, after the `base` rework, this head's tree (46e5b82, identical to 5d680ce), with bootc main 683bb05f, image-builder main fd7dc5cc (which has #2719), on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace ([logs](https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/6877dd16797e13e25c88cb85c0b2ebc0), see the addendum):
- `just e2e sealed` passed with upstream bootc and image-builder only: `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` on all three builds; the image-builder qcow2 booted with Secure Boot enabled, `/` on composefs with `verity=require` and a DPS root partition, and the switch and the upgrade each booted with the expected digest and packages.
- `just e2e unsealed` (`COMPOSEFS_BACKEND_CONFIG=1`) passed, but only with these unmerged changes: cgwalters-forge/bootc#23 (`composefs-backend` install config key), cgwalters-forge/bootc#29 (upgrades with a separate /boot, which every image-builder disk has) and cgwalters-forge/image-builder#4 (honor the key). Leaving out #29 fails `bootc switch`, leaving out image-builder#4 fails image-builder with "Could not find deployment", and without #23 the image is installed with ostree (re-verification on a 64-core devspace, same gist). Its root partition keeps the generic type, as image-builder only uses DPS for UKIs.
- At 123b26a (addendum 2 of the gist): `resolve-buildroot.py` falls back for the old, garbage-collected pin; uses the current pin, from local storage with the network broken; and fails with podman's error for the garbage-collected pin with the network broken (proxy to a closed port) and for an unresolvable registry. The new CI step fails with `BOOTC_RPMS` unset when `just bootc-rpms` fails, where the old one passed with it empty. `just e2e unsealed` passed again, with bootc RPMs built through the fallback.
- At 46e5b82 (addendum 3 of the gist), through `just` as the workflows call it: `just base=bogus build sealing` and `just base=centos-stream build aws` fail clearly; `rpms=$(just bootc-rpms)`, `just base=centos-stream build sealing|composefs` and `just lint sealing|composefs` pass without a subscription; `just e2e unsealed` (with the unmerged PRs above) and `just e2e sealed` passed. The sealed e2e passed on a second devspace: on the first (AMD EPYC 7763), QEMU aborted in the Secure Boot firmware (`cpu_asidx_from_attrs` assertion, qemu-kvm 10.1.0-16.el10_2.5), before the disk booted. The sealer cache fix was checked by building with `strace tmux` and then with no extra packages on one host: before it, the second image's UKI carried the first tree's digest; after it, both match.
- `composefs`: `just bcvk-test` passed earlier (GRUB, BLS, composefs backend); not rerun.
- The new workflow [passed on the fork](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/rhel-bootc-examples/actions/runs/36209526615) for an earlier head (d430120); not rerun since.

items.title: composefs: Support boot counting for new systemd-boot deployments

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
With systemd-boot, when `/etc/kernel/tries` is set (the kernel-install convention, opt-in like ostree's `boot-counting-tries`; read from the booted system at staging time, and a malformed file is warned about and ignored), a staged composefs deployment's boot entry (BLS Type #1, and the `.conf` entries used for UKIs) gets a `+N` boot counter per the Boot Loader Specification. systemd-bless-boot marks it good after boot-complete.target; if the deployment never gets there, systemd-boot falls back to the previous one. Entries with no attempts left now sort last like in systemd-boot, so `bootc status` shows the failed deployment as the rollback instead of reporting a queued rollback. GRUB and the initial install are unchanged. A prep commit also replaces `+` in the version part of entry names, since an os-release version like `1.2.3+42` already produced a name systemd-boot reads as a boot counter.

Caveat: the current CentOS Stream 10 (selinux-policy 42.1.27) and Fedora 44 (44.10) policies have no `allow init_t dosfs_t:file rename`, so systemd-bless-boot can't rename entries on the ESP: new deployments are never marked good, and after N boots systemd-boot falls back. That needs fixing in fedora-selinux/selinux-policy (and RHEL); until then counting stays opt-in via `/etc/kernel/tries`. The tmt test loads a one-line CIL module (`(allow init_t dosfs_t (file (rename)))`) to work around it.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Rebased onto main b06e0b06 (after #2483 and the #2508 docs restructure); the rebase was clean, and the `boot-failure-detection.md` edit now lives in `bootc-boot-failure-detection.7.md`. Retested at 81e37dac on a 16-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-36601734885, CentOS Stream 10 base): `just validate`, `just unit-tests` (468 passed) and, with composefs + systemd-boot BLS/ext4, plan-53-composefs-boot-counting all passed.

Before the rebase: tested on a 16-core devspace (CentOS Stream 10 base): the bootc-lib `bootc_composefs` unit tests, `just validate`, and with composefs + systemd-boot BLS/ext4 the new plan-53-composefs-boot-counting (staged entry has `+3`; after reboot systemd-bless-boot blesses it; renamed to `+0-3`, status shows the rollback queued and the next boot falls back to the previous deployment). An earlier revision of this branch, before the review fixes (test renumbering, `+` sanitizing, docs, and ignoring a malformed tries file), also passed plan-36-rollback and plan-24-image-upgrade-reboot on BLS, and readonly, image-upgrade-reboot and boot-counting on sealed UKI.

Follow-ups, not in this PR:
- File the SELinux policy issue (fedora-selinux/selinux-policy and RHEL), then consider enabling counting by default.
- Show a failed deployment explicitly in `bootc status`, and maybe warn on the next `bootc upgrade`.
- A composefs `bootc-boot-complete`-style check for bootc-finalize-staged failures, ordered before boot-complete.target.
- Count boots after `bootc rollback` too (it rewrites both entries without a counter), and decide what a soft reboot into a counted entry should do.

Related: https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/pull/1981

items.title: sealing: Rerun the Secure Boot signing steps when the key changes
items.body:
The sealing example passes the Secure Boot key and certificate to the signing steps only as build secrets, which aren't part of podman's layer cache key. After `just build` makes a new key, the signed systemd-boot and UKI layers come from the cache still signed with the old key, and the firmware refuses to boot ("Access Denied"). Same bug as bootc-dev/bootc#2498.

The public cert now comes in through `--build-context secureboot=keys` (keys/ has no private keys) and is copied into each signing stage and used from there, so a cert change reruns the signing. Signing systemd-boot moved into its own stage so the cert stays out of the sealed tree. The key stays a build secret.

The second commit fixes CI's "Write db private key" step, which never ran: its `if:` read an env var set on the same step. With the `SECUREBOOT_DB_KEY` secret set, non-PR builds now also need the matching `keys/db.crt` committed, which it isn't today; `just build` fails with an error saying so.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Stacked on https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/rhel-bootc-examples/pull/1 and https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/rhel-bootc-examples/pull/2 (both touch `sealing/Containerfile`, and the first also the workflow); only the last two commits are new here.

Testing, on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace against `quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10`, with key sets A and B from `util/keys.py` ([results](https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/ffcdb9a64cd60a3703a8fbaf892e3b82)):
- Before (those two PRs): build with A, then with B. The second build took both signing steps from the cache; `sbverify` shows systemd-boot and the UKI still signed with A, and booting with B's keys enrolled failed with `Access Denied -- rejected probably by Secure Boot`.
- After: A (signing ran), A again (fully cached), B (both signing steps reran; `sbverify` passes with B, fails with A). `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` passed, and `just bcvk-test` with B booted to a composefs root with `verity=require`.
- The CI change is checked with actionlint only (no secret to run it with).

Related: https://github.com/redhat-cop/rhel-bootc-examples/issues/20

items.title: composefs: Implement `bootc edit`
items.body:
`bootc edit` bailed on the composefs backend. It only supports two transitions, an image change and a boot order flip, and composefs already implements those as `switch` and `rollback`. This change shares the edited-spec parsing and validation between the two backends and dispatches to those. The first commit is a prep commit that splits up `switch_composefs`.

On composefs, editing the image back to one that is already deployed fails on the identical fs-verity digest, just as `bootc switch` does.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Testing: a new tmt test, `plan-50-edit`, covers a no-op edit, an image+rollback edit that must be rejected, an image change, and a boot order flip across reboots. It passed on composefs with GRUB and BLS (unsealed, ext4) and on ostree. Unit tests, including a new table-driven `test_validate_edited_spec`, and `just validate` also passed. Everything ran on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace. Sealed UKI with systemd-boot is still unverified: there the guest times out on reboot, and the existing `plan-36-rollback` fails the same way, so it looks like an environment problem. It still needs a run in upstream CI (the composefs sealed matrix leg).

items.title: tests: Don't require targets the host rustc can't compile for
items.body:
Several tests filter to x86_64/aarch64/windows targets, which fail on hosts whose LLVM lacks those backends, e.g. Alpine's rustc on ppc64le/armv7/armhf (`No available targets are compatible with triple`). #87 is the same root cause in the tool itself; this PR only fixes the tests.

The dep-kinds unit tests only count dependencies, so they now use the host target (`rustc --print host-tuple`) and run everywhere. The integration tests assert platform-specific results, so they skip themselves (with a message) when `rustc --print=cfg --target T` fails with that LLVM error. items.title: Ignore the [source] configuration when resolving dependencies
items.body:
The `.cargo/config.toml` that `cargo vendor` suggests replaces crates.io with `vendor/`, so with it in place vendor-filterer failed in its first `cargo metadata`, since `vendor/` doesn't exist yet. `cargo vendor` ignores `[source]` unless `--respect-source-config` is passed, and now the `cargo metadata` and `cargo tree` runs here do too.

Cargo can't drop part of its configuration, but it only discovers config files from the directory it runs in (plus `$CARGO_HOME`'s). So when one of them has a `[source]` table, these commands run in an empty temp directory with absolute manifest paths, and the project's config comes back via `--config` with `[source]` removed. Other settings are kept, and relative `[patch]` and `paths` entries in the rewritten file are made absolute. If `TMPDIR` is inside the project, it fails with a clear error, since cargo would find `[source]` again there. Known gaps: `[source]` in `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml` still applies, a relative `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` resolves against the temp directory, and the project's `rust-toolchain.toml` applies only when the rustup proxy already picked the toolchain (as for `cargo vendor-filterer`).

A prep commit fixes the per-platform `cargo metadata` runs silently dropping `--offline` (`other_options()` replaced it).

This conflicts trivially with #3 (#118) in the dep-kinds unit tests; if #3 lands first, this gets rebased on it.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Testing on a 4-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-36153045949), in the `rust:latest` container (Rust stable) with `zstd` installed for the `tar_zstd` test:
- CI steps: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features`: 29 unit + 30 integration tests passed. `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` also passes with Rust 1.86 (CI's lint toolchain).
- The integration test `source_config::vendored_sources_config` fails without the fix with the error from the issue; `vendored_sources_config_with_patch` (a `[patch]` with a relative path next to `[source]`) fails on the previous version of this PR. Unit tests cover the path rewriting, the `TMPDIR` check and skipping `$CARGO_HOME`'s config.
- Earlier, end to end with netavark v1.8.0 (from the test-crates CI job): vendor, install the suggested config, `rm -rf vendor`, vendor again with `--keep-dep-kinds no-dev`: this works now.

Closes #73

items.title: bootc: warn about customizations dropped for UKI images
items.body:
When a bootc container has a UKI, `raw_bootc` skips every customization stage after `bootc install` and drops the kernel arguments. Users, groups, files, directories, kargs, ignition, bootloader, subscription and extra mountpoints from the blueprint are all silently ignored, and the build succeeds without them.

This PR reports them as a manifest warning, the same way as other unsupported blueprint options: the image-builder CLI fails unless `--ignore-warnings` is given, and bootc-image-builder prints a warning. Only mountpoints the user names in `customizations.filesystem` or `customizations.disk` are reported, labelled by source. The default kargs from our definitions and the container's own disk.yaml aren't user input, so they aren't reported. `/boot` is left to the partition table code, which the companion DPS/XBOOTLDR PR (https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/image-builder/pull/1) turns into a clear error for UKI images.

A prep commit makes manifestgen print each warning as a `WARNING:` line; before, the text ran straight into the next progress message. This also changes the output of `image-builder --ignore-warnings`.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

Testing (16-core RHEL 10 devspaces cgwalters-devspace-36133088374 and, after review fixes, cgwalters-devspace-36140692613):
- `go test` on `./pkg/distro/... ./pkg/disk/... ./pkg/manifest/... ./pkg/manifestgen/... ./pkg/image/... ./cmd/image-builder/...` passes. No manifest checksums change.
- The container was built from this branch with `bootc-image-builder/Containerfile`. The input was an unsealed UKI composefs image from bootc main, with a blueprint adding a user, `kernel.append` and a `/var/data` filesystem:
  - `image-builder manifest --bootc-ref <uki>` exits 1 with `blueprint validation failed for image type "qcow2": the bootc container has a unified kernel (UKI), which does not support: customizations.user, customizations.kernel.append, customizations.filesystem mountpoints without an fstab (/var/data)`;
  - `bootc-image-builder manifest` prints the same text as a `WARNING:` line and continues;
  - the same config with `quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10` gives no UKI warning (only the existing `customizations.filesystem: not supported` one).

Related: #2560

labels.name: review:problem

items.body:
CI didn't cover several composefs upgrade paths. This closes three of those gaps.

- **Fedora 44 composefs upgrade**: re-enabled. It was excluded (bb674f11) because the Fedora 44 base image's bootc hit the pull-then-GC deadlock from #2364. That was fixed in 1.16.8, and `fedora-bootc:44` now ships 1.16.10.
- **test-49 (1.16.0 UKI bridge)**: it needed hand-built fixture images, so nothing ran it. `just test-composefs-bridge sealed|unsealed` now builds them from the tree. The stager is the current UKI image with bootc swapped for the pinned 1.16.0 Koji RPM (checksum verified; the version-locked `bootc-tests` and `system-reinstall-bootc` are removed first, so the downgrade still gets dependency checks), and its initramfs and UKI are regenerated by 1.16.0. The target fails early unless the base is Fedora on x86_64. A new `test-composefs-bridge` job runs both modes on Fedora 44. It runs with the heavy jobs instead of nightly: it takes less time than an existing sealed UKI leg, and there is no scheduled CI workflow whose failures anyone would see.
- **btrfs**: one Fedora 44 composefs leg (sealed UKI, systemd-boot) running the same plans as the other sealed legs. It is added through a computed `include`, so it doesn't multiply the matrix.

**Cost** (full-suite runs only; `ci/tier-1` adds nothing): 4 more jobs, next to about 19 test-integration legs. From a recent merge-queue run: an upgrade leg takes about 20 min, and a sealed UKI integration leg about 50 min, which the btrfs leg should match. Each bridge leg is one build plus one 4-boot VM run: 24 min on a devspace, including the package build.

**Tested** on RHEL 10 devspaces, following the CI job steps (`just build-fetch` and the same `just` targets):

- `just test-upgrade` with Fedora 44 and composefs: passed (booted 1.16.10, upgraded, readonly suite);
- `just test-composefs-bridge unsealed` and `sealed`: 1.16.0 install (the test checked the binary's checksum), then switch, upgrade, rollback and `composefs-gc --assert-no-op`, all passed;
- `just test-composefs systemd btrfs uki sealed`: passed (plan-01-readonly and plan-24-image-upgrade-reboot, installed on btrfs);

items.title: sealing: Keep the kernel only inside the signed UKI
items.body:
The sealed image shipped the kernel and initramfs twice: once inside the signed UKI, and again as plain files in `/usr/lib/modules/<kver>/`, which nothing boots from. Now `bootc container split-kernel-and-rootfs` moves them out of the target rootfs, and `bootc container ukify --kernel-dir` builds the UKI from there. That's the same flow bootc's own sealed images use. ukify also writes the UKI straight to `/boot/EFI/Linux/<kver>.efi`, so the separate step that looked up the kernel version and moved the file there is gone. The final image is about 108 MB smaller.

This needs bootc 1.16.4 or newer: `split-kernel-and-rootfs` first shipped in v1.16.4, and `--kernel-dir` in v1.16.1. According to the Red Hat catalog's rpm manifest for `rhel10/rhel-bootc:10.2` (10.2-1790218244), that image ships exactly bootc-1.16.4-1.el10_2. CentOS Stream 10 currently has 1.16.13.

Testing: I had no RHEL subscription, so all of this ran against `quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10`, with the `BASE_IMAGE` override from https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/rhel-bootc-examples/pull/1 applied on top. The Containerfile hunks are identical to the ones in this commit.
- `just keygen && BASE_IMAGE=quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10 just bcvk-test` passed on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace (bcvk 0.19.0). The VM booted with Secure Boot keys enrolled, `/` was composefs with `verity=require`, and the cmdline carried `composefs=<digest>`. In the built image, `/usr/lib/modules/<kver>/` no longer has `vmlinuz` or `initramfs.img`, and `/boot/EFI/Linux/<kver>.efi` is there as before. The unchanged Containerfile passed the same test.
- The CI build (`bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` included) [passed](https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/rhel-bootc-examples/actions/runs/36083789938) in a fork without secrets.

The leftover `/usr/lib/modules/<kver>/.vmlinuz.hmac` (the FIPS HMAC of the removed vmlinuz) is still there. `split-kernel-and-rootfs` doesn't touch it, which may be worth fixing in bootc.

Closes #19

items.title: ci: Don't fail PRs from forks for lack of RHEL secrets
items.body:
GitHub doesn't pass secrets to workflows run for PRs from forks, so "Build sealed composefs host" failed at "Register subscription" on every fork PR (e.g. runs 29842786424, 27534022172, 26833248795), and "Build examples" would do the same.

Without the secrets, the sealed host build now falls back to CentOS Stream 10 (`just base=centos-stream build`), which still runs the whole Containerfile, including `bootc container lint`. Only the RHEL build gets published to GHCR. For that to work, the first commit makes the GPG key handling in the Containerfile distro-neutral and adds a `base` variable (`rhel`, the default, or `centos-stream`) to the sealing and top-level Justfiles, so the workflow only calls `just` with an override and people can try the example the same way without a subscription (`just base=centos-stream build sealing`; `BASE_IMAGE` still overrides it with any image). At the top level, RHEL-only examples refuse another base, and `build-all` skips them. The other examples all need RHEL content, so without the secrets their builds are skipped with a notice.

Also:
- "Build examples" now runs weekly (upstream only, gated on the repository owner), so stale base image tags get noticed.
- Fixed a stale comment that said the sealing example uses CentOS Stream.

Testing:
- actionlint is clean apart from an existing SC2086 info on the GHCR push line.
- `just base=centos-stream build sealing` and `just lint sealing` passed on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace with no subscription, at the head of #4, which stacks on this; `just base=bogus build sealing` and `just base=centos-stream build aws` fail with a clear error.
- CI without secrets, on a PR inside a fork, before the `base` rework (the workflow then set `BASE_IMAGE` itself; not rerun since): [Build sealed composefs host](https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/rhel-bootc-examples/actions/runs/36083389652) passed on the CentOS Stream 10 base, with the subscription, login and GHCR steps skipped. [Build examples](https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/rhel-bootc-examples/actions/runs/36083389653) passed, with the build job skipped and the notice shown.

Caveat, not changed here: the "Write db private key" step's `if: env.SECUREBOOT_DB_KEY != ''` reads an env var set on that same step, which the `if` can't see, so the step is always skipped (it was skipped on main's last push run too). Enabling it would also need `sealing/keys/db.crt` committed, which it isn't.

items.title: common: Add the /signoff PR command to every repository
items.body:
Adds the `/signoff` PR command to every repository. A maintainer comments `/signoff`, and their `Signed-off-by` is added to all of the PR's commits, which otherwise stay byte for byte the same. `/rebase-signoff` also moves the commits onto the target branch. DCO is required by the org's `default` ruleset.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

This is plain Actions with no LLM, following the review of #261. The logic is the `pr-signoff` reusable workflow in bootc-dev/actions (https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/actions/pull/2 has the design, the security notes and the search for existing tools that #260 asked for). This PR adds:
- `common/.github/workflows/signoff.yml`, the stub, which sync-common installs in every bootc-dev and composefs repository;
- `.github/workflows/signoff.yml`, a copy for this repository, since the sync skips it;
- a DCO section in `docs/repository-structure.md`.

bootc gets the same file ahead of the sync in https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/pull/16.

About the stub:

items.title: pr-signoff: Add reusable workflow for /signoff PR commands
items.body:
Adds `pr-signoff`, a reusable workflow for two PR comment commands. With it, each repository only needs a small stub: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/pull/8 syncs that stub org-wide, and https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/pull/16 adds it to bootc first. This supersedes bootc-dev/infra#261. It is plain Actions with no LLM, runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, and handles all of a PR's commits.

<!-- cgwalters: context/rationale -->

**`/signoff [<sha>]`** adds the commenter's `Signed-off-by` to each PR commit that lacks it.
- Each commit is recreated with `git hash-object` in a bare repository.
- Tree, parent base, author line and message stay byte for byte (including non-UTF-8 encodings and trailing whitespace). Only the trailer and the committer change.
- dco-2 accepts a sign-off that matches the committer, and the commenter becomes the committer.
- Needs triage, or write on fork PRs.

**`/rebase-signoff [<sha>]`** does the same onto the target tip, using `git merge-tree` (no worktree). Commits that become empty are dropped, and a conflict is refused. Needs write.

**Which head gets signed off.** Only a head that GitHub's activity log shows was pushed before the comment. A SHA (12+ hex digits) must also match it. The push is `--force-with-lease` against that head.

**Refused, with a reply:**
- fork PRs without "Allow edits by maintainers";
- merge commits;
- heads that are the default branch, protected, or under a `non_fast_forward`/`update` rule.

**Ignored silently:** bots, and people without read access.

**Security.**
- Nothing from the PR is checked out or run. Git has hooks off, system/global config ignored, `* merge=text -filter` in `info/attributes`, https only, and no submodules.
- Untrusted text only reaches the script through `env:`.
- The App token is scoped to one repository.
- The script is checked out from the workflow's own commit (`job.workflow_sha`). Callers pin that commit, since they pass the App key.
- `create-github-app-token` and `checkout` are SHA-pinned.

**Runner cost.** GitHub can't filter `issue_comment` on the comment body, so every comment creates a run. The stub's job-level `if:` skips the job before a runner is requested, so other comments cost nothing.

**Existing tools.** Per bootc-dev/infra#260 I looked for existing ones before writing this:
- DCO checkers (cncf/dcochecker, tisonkun/actions-dco, KineticCafe/actions-dco) only report.
- dco-2's third-party remediation commits (`.github/dco.yml`) avoid a force-push, but someone still has to write and push a remediation commit per PR, and it leaves extra commits.
- `peter-evans/slash-command-dispatch` only adds a `repository_dispatch` hop (and needs a PAT) where a job-level `if:` suffices.
- I found no maintained comment-triggered sign-off action; the closest, GeorgLink/test_dco_signoff_action, is an abandoned 2019 experiment.

The command matching and role logic follow gh-aw's `slash_command` and `check_membership`.

## Testing

`pr-signoff/test.sh` has offline, data-driven tests and runs in this repo's PR CI:
- command parsing, role mapping and ranking, SHA length, and required roles;
- the rewrite in a scratch repo: byte-exact messages including Latin-1 and trailing whitespace, trees, authors, idempotence, rebase drop/keep-empty, and conflicts.

They pass on a 4-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-36074104378, git 2.52). Mutating the rank table, the SHA length, the fork rule, `addIfDifferent` or the encoding copy makes them fail. shellcheck is clean. actionlint 1.7.12 is clean apart from not knowing the `job.workflow_*` contexts (`-ignore` for those two).

Real runs on cgwalters-forge/infra, with the stub pinned to this commit and the `GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback:

- A plain comment produced a [skipped run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36074584067), with no runner.
- `/signoff` without a SHA on 2 unsigned commits worked ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36074584771)). One commit's message has trailing whitespace and the other is Latin-1 with an `encoding` header. Afterwards the trees and author lines were identical, each message began with the original bytes followed by the trailer, the encoding header was kept, and the commenter was the committer.
- `/signoff <12-hex head>` on the result replied "nothing to do" ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36075840107)).
- `/rebase-signoff <12-hex head>` after the base moved put both commits on the new tip, each with one trailer ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36075841289)).
- These were refused:
  - a 7-hex SHA, with the usage message ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36075842721));
  - a stale SHA ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36074585596));
  - a head branch with a `non_fast_forward` ruleset ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36074586515));
  - a head that is the default branch ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36074587334));
  - a fork PR without maintainer edits ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36075843859));
  - a fork PR with maintainer edits, which got as far as needing an App token ([run](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/infra/actions/runs/36074588059)).
- Reactions were :eyes: then :rocket: or :confused: on every command.

**Credentials:** in bootc-dev, the bootc-bot App's `GH_AW_APP_CLIENT_ID`/`GH_AW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are installed org-wide. For composefs this is unconfirmed: it needs that org variable and secret set, or its stubs fall back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

**Untested and required before relying on this:** the App-token path. That covers minting with `permission-workflows`, pushing commits that touch `.github/workflows`, and pushing to fork PRs. The forge has no App, so this must get one real run on an org with the bootc-bot App. Also untested:
- a commenter with triage only, or without access (the bot is admin wherever it can test);
- a bot commenter;
- dco-2 turning green (it isn't installed on the forge).

That an App push to a fork PR skips the "approve and run" gate for fork CI is an assumption I couldn't check. It is why fork PRs require write.

items.title: reboot: Propagate a refused reboot as an error

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
bootc reboots by running `systemctl reboot` through `systemd-run`, so that it runs outside bootc's mount namespace. Without `--wait`, bootc only learns that the transient unit started, not whether the reboot was accepted. It then parks and waits for the SIGTERM from shutdown. If logind refuses the reboot, that SIGTERM never comes, and `bootc upgrade --apply` (and so bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service) hangs instead of failing.

systemd 257 and later refuse reboots from root while a `block` mode shutdown inhibitor is held, so this can happen today. This PR adds `--wait --pipe --collect`, which brings the exit status and systemctl's error message back to bootc.

There is a small race. Once the reboot has been accepted, shutdown can stop the transient unit or kill systemd-run before it reports success. bootc would then print an error and exit while the system goes down, instead of being terminated by SIGTERM. The window is short, because `systemctl reboot` returns as soon as the job is queued, and the reboot happens either way.

`--wait` and `--pipe` also talk to systemd over the D-Bus system bus rather than /run/systemd/private. Where dbus isn't running (e.g. rescue.target), `--apply` now fails loudly and keeps the staged changes. A code comment notes this.

This is split out of the reboot inhibitor PR (bootc#1047), which builds on it.

## Testing

- Reproduction, in ephemeral bcvk VMs of the published images, run as root with `systemd-inhibit --what=shutdown --mode=block` held:
  - centos-bootc:stream10 (systemd 257): `systemd-run --quiet -- systemctl reboot`, which is bootc's current invocation, exited 0 and the VM stayed up. That's the case where bootc waits forever. `systemd-run --quiet --wait --pipe --collect -- systemctl reboot` exited 1 and printed `Operation inhibited by "probe" ... reason is "testing"`.
  - centos-bootc:stream9 (systemd 252): the current invocation just rebooted, because logind there doesn't enforce the lock for root. That's the gap the follow-up PR closes.
- `just validate` and `just unit-tests` (443 tests) passed on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace, rebased on current main (41049cca). The branch was built in its own checkout, with its own cargo target and buildah cache directories, and the built image reports `g2dde3623`.

items.title: install: Run fatal lints before installing

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Images that fail our fatal lints install fine today and then break in confusing ways at runtime. The classic case is a `/var/run` directory created by a legacy package. Few people know to add `RUN bootc container lint` to their build. As the issue suggests, `bootc install` now runs the fatal subset of the lints against the image being installed, before anything is written to the target.

Details:

- It only runs when installing from the running container image. With `--source-imgref` we don't have the image root at hand.
- `etc-usretc` only prints a warning, for compatibility with existing images, as the issue asks.
- The ostree-specific fatal lints (`baseimage-root`, `utf8`) are skipped for `--composefs-backend`.
- The check runs after the SELinux re-exec, so it only runs once.
- The recursive lints walk the whole image root. At install time that root also contains host mounts: the target, container storage and so on. Those aren't necessarily on a different device (for example with the vfs storage driver), so this walk skips every mount point, not just the ones on other devices. The relabeling walk works the same way.
- `--skip-lints` (on to-disk, to-filesystem and to-existing-root) skips the check. The name matches the existing `--skip-fetch-check` and `--skip-finalize`.

Closes #960

## Testing

I tested on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace, rebased on current main (41049cca). The branch was built in its own checkout, with its own cargo target and buildah cache directories, and the built image reports `gd5c0cabe`.

- `just validate` passed.
- `just unit-tests` passed: 444 tests, including the new `lints::tests::test_lint_for_install`. It covers both backends, the etc-usretc warning, and the ostree-only lints.
- `bootc-integration-tests install-alongside localhost/bootc-install` passed all 7 tests. That includes the existing loopback and alongside installs of the default image, and a new test: a derived image with a `/var/run` directory fails `bootc install to-disk --via-loopback` with `Failed lint: var-run`, and the same install succeeds with `--skip-lints`. CI doesn't run this suite right now, because the install-tests job is disabled.
- Runtime: a loopback `bootc install to-disk` of the default centos-bootc:stream10-based image, with `RUST_LOG=bootc_lib::lints=debug`, logged `Install lints: passed=6 skipped=9 in 108.117108ms` and then completed. The walk adds about 0.1s to an install.

items.title: reboot: Refuse to reboot while a shutdown inhibitor blocks it

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
When bootc reboots (`upgrade --apply`, `switch --apply`, `rollback --apply`, and so bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service), it runs `systemctl reboot` as root and not on a tty. In that case systemctl doesn't check inhibitors itself. logind in systemd 257 and later refuses such a reboot while a `block` shutdown inhibitor is held, but older systems such as CentOS Stream 9 (systemd 252) just reboot. Anything holding such a lock is explicitly asking not to be rebooted underneath it.

This PR does what rpm-ostree does (coreos/rpm-ostree#2862). Before rebooting, bootc asks logind for its inhibitors (`ListInhibitors` via `busctl --json=short`). It refuses when a lock has mode `block` and its `what` includes `shutdown`, and the error names who holds the lock. `delay`, `block-weak` and sleep/idle-only locks don't count. The error suggests `systemctl reboot --check-inhibitors=no`, and says pending changes take effect on the next boot. That wording also covers rollback and the composefs paths, not just a staged update. The man pages and `--apply` help text describe this.

If logind can't be queried (e.g. it isn't running), bootc prints a warning and reboots anyway. That deliberately differs from rpm-ostree, which fails closed. Failing closed would break every `--apply`, and the update timer, on such systems. Where logind does run, systemd 257 and newer already enforce block locks themselves.

An earlier version of this PR passed `systemctl reboot --check-inhibitors=yes` instead. That also refuses while any non-root user is logged in, including the administrator's own SSH session or a stray tmux. That would break `sudo bootc upgrade --apply` and automatic updates on many systems, so this version doesn't use it.

This builds on cgwalters-forge/bootc#13 (`reboot: Propagate a refused reboot as an error`). With that change, a reboot refused by logind shows up as an error instead of a hang. The composefs `systemctl soft-reboot` path is left alone, because logind 257+ already enforces shutdown inhibitors for it.

Behavior change: on any systemd version, bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service now fails instead of rebooting while such a lock is held. The update is applied at the next reboot, or retried on the next timer run.

Related: #1047. The issue asks for `--check-inhibitors=yes`, which this deliberately doesn't use (see above).

## Testing

Rebased onto main b06e0b06. The conflicts were context only: main now documents `--soft-reboot` in the `--apply` help and moved the soft reboot text out of bootc-upgrade(8), so the inhibitor sentences sit next to the new text.

I tested at 6fb9c7c0 on a 16-core devspace (cgwalters-devspace-36601734885, CentOS Stream 10 base). The branch was built in its own checkout, with its own cargo target, and the built image's bootc RPM is `g6fb9c7c017`.

- `just validate` passed.
- `just unit-tests` passed: 467 tests, including two new table-driven tests. `reboot::tests::test_blocking_inhibitors` checks which locks count: block/shutdown in a combined `what` counts, while delay, block-weak and sleep-only locks don't. Its input is in the JSON format that `busctl --json=short` prints on systemd 257. `test_blocking_inhibitors_malformed` covers empty input, non-JSON, a missing or wrong-shape `data`, too few fields, and wrongly typed fields.
- `just test-tmt plan-24-image-upgrade-reboot` (centos-bootc:stream10) passed. With `systemd-inhibit --what=shutdown --mode=block --who=bootc-test` held, `bootc switch --apply` failed with `Reboot blocked by shutdown inhibitor: "bootc-test" (PID 1659, UID 0): testing. Pending changes take effect on the next boot; use systemctl reboot --check-inhibitors=no to reboot anyway.` Once the lock was released, `--apply` rebooted into the new image. That run logged in over SSH as root, so this doesn't show the logged-in-user case directly. The bootc side doesn't look at sessions at all.
- Not tested end to end: the fail-open path when logind is unavailable. It's a small `match` on the query result. The query and parse failures it handles are covered by the malformed-input test.
- I didn't rerun on CentOS Stream 9. The bcvk probe in the prep PR shows that, on systemd 252, logind itself lets root reboot through a block lock, which is the case this check covers.

items.title: to-disk: Save guest dmesg and virtiofsd logs when the install fails

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

items.body:
When `bootc install` fails in the to-disk VM, the guest kernel log and the virtiofsd logs are removed along with the container, and those are exactly what would explain flakes like the ESTALE errors from the host storage share in #157.

Now, before removing the container, bcvk saves the guest `dmesg` (fetched over SSH with a 30s timeout, since the guest may be wedged) and both virtiofsd logs to a file in the temporary directory, and prints one line with its path:

```
Logs from the failed install VM were saved to /tmp/bcvk-to-disk-failure-xGBUm7.log
```

If none of the three can be read (e.g. the VM never came up), no file is written and the reasons are logged at debug level. The tails of the logs (200 lines each) go to stderr only with `--debug`, debug logging, or `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS` set, since most failures (a broken image, a bad install option) are plain user errors that a wall of kernel log wouldn't help with. If the file can't be written, the tails are printed instead. This is documented in `docs/src/testing.md`. Base-disk creation for `libvirt run` goes through the same code, so it's covered too. For the varlink `to-disk` call, the path line goes to the server's stderr.

The integration test harness sets `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS`. For the logs to actually reach the test output, the to-disk integration tests now run bcvk through a small helper that includes its stdout and stderr in the error when it fails, since xshell's `.output()?` drops captured stderr on a non-zero exit.

To support the dmesg timeout, `ssh::connect_captured` gained a `timeout` argument; it had no callers before.

The companion nextest change that serializes the `test_to_base_disk_*` tests is a separate PR.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace with KVM:

- `make validate` and `cargo test` pass (84 + 22 unit tests, including table-driven tests for the log formatting).
- A deliberately failing integration test (a scratch test, not included here, running `to-disk --disk-size 2G` through the new helper under `cargo nextest run -P integration`) failed with bcvk's stderr in the test output: the `bootc install` out-of-space error, the path line, the dmesg tail (last 200 of 647 lines) and both virtiofsd logs. The junit report has them too.
- Forced failures by hand (the same 2G disk):
  - `bcvk to-disk`: prints the install error and the one-line path, and the 668-line file holds the full logs.
  - With `BCVK_PRINT_FAILURE_LOGS=1`, and with `--debug`: the three tails are printed as well.
  - `bcvk libvirt run --root-size 2G`: the base-disk failure also prints the path line.
  - The plain, env var and `libvirt run` cases were checked on the previous revision; that code is unchanged, and `--debug` was checked on this one.
- `test_to_disk` passes under the integration profile.

Not tested: the case where all three logs are unavailable.

CI note (2026-09-24): the [`integration-tests (2)` failure](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/actions/runs/35955666987/job/107510910165) is unrelated to this change: `test_run_tmpfs` failed with exit 255 from `ephemeral run-ssh` (ssh itself failing), a path this PR doesn't touch, matching the `ConnectTimeout` banner-exchange flake targeted by cgwalters-forge/bcvk#8. All to-disk tests in that partition passed. Reran the failed jobs once.

Related: #157

items.title: ci: Retry test image pulls and prefetch Fedora CoreOS

labels.name: review:quick
labels.description: High-confidence bot draft: skim and approve

items.body:
CI keeps failing on transient quay.io errors that have nothing to do with the change under test. `just pull-test-images` is a single `podman pull` with only podman's built-in retries (3 quick retries a few seconds apart), which isn't enough to ride out an unexpected EOF from quay's CDN mid-blob ([example](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/35025230255)). The Ignition tests also pull `quay.io/fedora/fedora-coreos:stable` in the middle of the test run, so a 502/504 or dropped connection there fails a test directly ([1](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34819196417), [2](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34878492147), [3](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bcvk/actions/runs/34780568246)).

This wraps each pull in `pull-test-images` in a retry loop with exponential backoff (5 attempts, 15s doubling, about 4 minutes of total delay) and adds the FCOS image to the prefetched set. The image name now lives only in the Justfile and reaches the tests as `BCVK_FCOS_IMAGE`, like the other test images, instead of three copies kept in sync by a comment. The tests that pull an image already in that set (the Ignition tests, the varlink images tests, and the to-disk imgref test) now only pull it when `podman image exists` says it is missing, so in CI they reuse the prefetched copy, while still working when run standalone. (`podman pull --policy missing` would say this directly, but podman 4 on the Ubuntu 24.04 runners doesn't have it.)

Note that FCOS is now pulled by the build job and each of the 4 integration partitions (5 pulls per CI run), rather than only by the partitions that happen to run an Ignition test.

Tested on a 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace with KVM:

- `make validate` and `cargo test` pass (82 + 22 unit tests).
- `just pull-test-images` pulled all six images, FCOS included. With `ALL_BASE_IMAGES=localhost:1/nonexistent:x` it retried after 15/30/60/120s and failed after 5 attempts with a clear error (checked on the previous revision; the loop is unchanged).
- `cargo nextest run -P integration` for the touched tests: all 9 passed (the 4 registered Ignition tests, `test_to_disk_different_imgref_same_digest`, and the 3 `test_varlink_images_list*` tests). With `BCVK_FCOS_IMAGE=localhost/does-not-exist:x`, `test_run_ephemeral_ignition_invalid_path` fails pulling that image, so the variable is honored. `test_libvirt_ignition_works` is commented out upstream, so it only gets the same mechanical change.
- Rerun on the current revision (another 16-core RHEL 10.2 devspace, podman 5.8, libvirt/qemu-kvm/virtiofsd installed): `make validate` and the unit tests pass; the same 9 integration tests pass with the images prefetched; after `podman rmi` of FCOS, `test_run_ephemeral_ignition_invalid_path` pulls it and passes.

CI note: the first revision [failed `integration-tests (2)`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bcvk/actions/runs/35952096935/job/107496126532) because `podman pull --policy` doesn't exist in podman 4 (`Error: unknown flag: --policy`); fixed by the `podman image exists` check above.

items.title: lints: Warn when the kernel config lacks composefs support

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
Several people have built images with kernels lacking EROFS support, which
only shows up as a confusing mount failure at boot. When the kernel ships
its build configuration as `/usr/lib/modules/$kver/config` we can catch
that at build time.

This adds a `kernel-composefs` warning lint that checks each kernel's
config for what composefs needs: `CONFIG_EROFS_FS` with
`CONFIG_EROFS_FS_XATTR` (the overlayfs metadata lives in xattrs),
`CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS`, and a way to mount the EROFS image from a file, i.e.
`CONFIG_EROFS_FS_BACKED_BY_FILE` or `CONFIG_BLK_DEV_LOOP`. Built-in or
module both count. It's a warning, not fatal, because the config file is
optional and a kernel without composefs support can still be used with
ostree when composefs is not enabled. Note that with
`bootc container lint --fatal-warnings`, as in bootc's own Dockerfile, it
does become fatal. Kernels without a config file there are silently
skipped; that includes Debian/Ubuntu, which ship it as `/boot/config-$kver`.

Testing, on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace, rebased on current main: new
data-driven unit tests for the config parsing and for the lint itself;
`cargo test -p bootc-lib` (273 passed, 271 on main) and `just validate` passed. I
also checked the kernel configs of the public CI matrix base images
(centos-bootc stream9 and stream10, eln-bootc, fedora-bootc 42 through 46):
all enable EROFS (with xattrs), overlayfs and loop devices, and all but
stream9 also have `CONFIG_EROFS_FS_BACKED_BY_FILE`, so the lint stays quiet
on all of them.

Closes: #1030
