items.title: bootc-ubuntu-setup: Take the container stack from resolute on 24.04
items.body:
On ubuntu-24.04, bootc-ubuntu-setup installs podman 5.4.1 and buildah 1.39.3 from plucky, both built with go1.24.1. That Go has a runtime bug (golang/go#73141, fixed in go1.24.3) where a thread exiting after LockOSThread can segfault in mallocgc on kernels with vDSO getrandom, which the runners' 6.17 kernels have. podman/buildah exit locked threads while setting up RUN steps, so some image builds die with exit status 139 and no error output. Root cause analysis: https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/f19957abbef4121e4ee35210c48d0a86

This takes the container stack (crun, buildah, podman, skopeo, conmon, netavark, aardvark-dns, passt, catatonit, just) from resolute on 24.04, which is go1.25 throughout and exactly what 26.04 runners have natively. No other source works: questing's podman is go1.24.4 but its buildah and skopeo are still go1.24.1/1.24.2, and noble-backports and the plucky/questing -updates pockets carry no podman. Resolute is pinned at priority 50 and only selected with `-t resolute`, so plucky still supplies the libvirt stack as before.

There are three commits:

1. Detect the host OS once, before installing anything. Plucky's libc6 upgrades base-files, so the fixed-QEMU step re-read os-release, saw 25.04 and skipped: the Resolute QEMU (#53) has never actually been installed on 24.04 consumers. This redoes #54, which was merged into a stacked branch and never reached main, including its QEMU >= 10.2 assertion in test-virtualization. The detected value is exposed as a new `host-os` output.
2. Run the setup tests on 24.04 again. The Renovate bump in #61 moved both setup jobs to 26.04, so PR CI no longer covered the 24.04 path most consumers use. They are now one runner matrix.
3. The resolute switch itself. The basic-requirements check now fails if podman or buildah are built with go1.24.0-2, and runs a rootful container to exercise netavark.

Caveats: the `-t resolute` closure is wider than the container stack. It upgrades libc6 to 2.43 plus dpkg, passwd/uidmap, make and base-files. So needrestart is set to list-only (a test run saw rsyslog crash when it restarted services mid-job), and on every 24.04 job os-release reports 26.04 after this action, where before that only happened with libvirt enabled. Later steps that read os-release (lsb_release, add-apt-repository, actions/setup-python) will see 26.04; `host-os` has the real value. This also conflicts with #60 (RHEL 10 support): whichever lands second has to port this into #60's layout (packages/ubuntu-24.04-base, the `/plucky` suffix, the resolute pin), and #60's workarounds.sh has the same os-release re-read bug that commit 1 fixes.

Which consumers are affected: I scanned failed runs on default branches since 2026-06-24 across the repos that use this action on 24.04, grepping job logs for exit 139/SIGSEGV. Only ostreedev/ostree's bootc.yaml was hit, in 27 jobs over 26 runs. It is still happening: a later scan found 20 failed ci-bootc integration jobs with this signature, including main on 09-14 and 09-17 and the ostree#3611 PR run on 09-23 (https://gist.github.com/cgwalters-bot/e97ca68a8e017b97e8a9848e9d4e5693). Nothing turned up in bcvk (143 failed jobs scanned), bootc (835), infra (365), composefs-rs (349), bootupd (52) or rpm-ostree (109). bootupd pins this action by digest and will pick the fix up on its next bump. rpm-ostree vendors its own copy of the action with plucky podman, so this PR doesn't cover it. Given no hits there, it's left alone for now.

Testing:

- This fork PR at 60d2e9a (same code, only comments changed since): test-virtualization (https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/actions/actions/runs/35943108093) and test-ubuntu-2604-ovmf (https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/actions/actions/runs/35943108081) passed. test-actions-pr and test-container-integration were still queued on the fork's runners when this was written.
- The same commits on the bot's scratch fork (a74dd0e, plus a DO-NOT-MERGE commit enabling workflow_dispatch for test-actions-pr): test-actions-pr passed both setup jobs on 24.04 and 26.04 and every other job except openssf-scorecard, which fails on dispatch only because there is no PR base sha (https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/actions/actions/runs/35851847269), and test-virtualization passed (https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/actions/actions/runs/35851845242). An earlier revision (5735cd8) passed test-container-integration on amd64 and arm64 (https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/actions/actions/runs/35817130501) and test-ubuntu-2604-ovmf (https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/actions/actions/runs/35817133547).
- As a real consumer, ostree's ci-bootc workflow on current ostree main, pointed at this PR's head (`cgwalters-forge/actions/bootc-ubuntu-setup@bot/ubuntu2404-resolute-podman`, at 60d2e9a), passed all 4 jobs (unit-tests and integration on stream9 and stream10), with podman 5.7.0, buildah 1.42.1 and skopeo 1.21.0~pre1 from resolute: https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/ostree/actions/runs/35943443277. An earlier revision also passed there: https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/ostree/actions/runs/35817157996.
- actionlint only reports that it doesn't know the ubuntu-26.04 runner label, which main already uses.

items.title: staged-images: Only publish a manifest when every arch built
items.body:
The staged-images Manifest job ran with `if: !cancelled()`, so every weekly run in which the amd64 build failed replaced the multi-arch manifest with an arm64-only one. That is why ghcr.io/bootc-dev/fedora-bootc-staged:45 and centos-bootc-staged:stream9/stream10 currently list only arm64, which breaks amd64 consumers. The builds also ran after a failed Mirror job, silently building from whatever the mirror tag last pointed to.

A flat matrix can't gate on "this image's arch builds all succeeded", because `needs.build.result` aggregates over every image. So the per-image pipeline (mirror, build+test per arch, manifest) moves into a reusable workflow, `staged-image-pipeline.yml`, called once per image from `build-staged-images.yml`. Within it, a failed mirror skips the builds, a failed arch build skips the manifest, and either fails the run, while other images still publish. PRs still skip mirror/push/manifest and only build and test.

The first commit is a prep that masks bootloader-update.service in the amd64 boot test. Under `bcvk ephemeral` the root is virtiofs with no backing block device, so `bootupctl update` fails and the system is "degraded" on every run. Once the manifest is gated, that failure would block publishing amd64 entirely, so the mask goes first and this PR can land on its own. It can be dropped once coreos/bootupd#1072 (still open) ships in the base images.

Relation to #194 (the Renovate staged-images digest bump): its fix branch (cgwalters-bot/infra `bot/staged-images-fix`) carries the same mask plus a fedora-bootc:45 digest update, but the bot can't push to the Renovate PR, so that one is waiting on a human. The two are independent: whichever lands second should drop its copy of the mask commit (it touches the same boot-test step).

After merging, please trigger "Build chunkah-staged bootc base images" via workflow_dispatch instead of waiting for Monday's schedule, since the arm64-only manifests stay published until a run succeeds for both arches.

Testing: actionlint reports nothing new (only the pre-existing SC2016 info on the boot-test heredoc). A mock of the same job graph, with every step replaced by a stub that fails on demand, ran on the bot's fork for four scenarios: all success, a failed fedora amd64 build, a failed fedora mirror, and the PR event (https://github.com/cgwalters-bot/infra/actions/runs/35811290852; the run is red only because of the injected failures). Fedora's manifest was skipped when its amd64 build or its mirror failed, the builds were skipped after the failed mirror, the other images still published, and the PR event built without mirroring or publishing. The real PR path on this fork (build + boot test for each image, both arches) is still pending: the fork's runners were backed up and it had not started when this was written.

items.title: ephemeral: Give /var its own tmpfs, add --var-size

labels.name: review:problem
labels.description: Bot draft that is conflicting, duplicate or broken

items.body:
The ephemeral VM's `/var` was a directory on the initramfs `/run` tmpfs, which systemd caps at 20% of RAM. With the default 4G of memory that's ~780MiB, and there was no knob to raise it short of adding lots of memory, so e.g. a quadlet pulling a 2+GiB image at boot runs out of space. It also meant filling `/var` filled `/run`.

This mounts a dedicated tmpfs for `/var`, defaulting to 50% of guest RAM (the kernel's tmpfs default), and adds `--var-size` to `ephemeral run`/`run-ssh` (a size like `10G` or a percentage of guest RAM like `75%`). Together with `--add-swap` it allows a `/var` bigger than guest RAM. The size is passed to the initramfs unit as a drop-in in the CPIO that bcvk already appends, and the value is checked on the host so it can't inject other mount options or unit syntax. One behavior change to note: overfilling a `/var` that is larger than the memory available to back it now ends in the guest running out of memory rather than ENOSPC; the docs say so and suggest `--memory`/`--add-swap`.

A separate prep commit makes `parse_size` reject sizes that overflow `u64` (e.g. `17179869184G` used to wrap to 0), which also affects `--add-swap`.

The option is CLI-only for now; the varlink `Run` call keeps the default size.

## Is a tunable tmpfs the right first step?

In the issue, @cgwalters suggested making `/var` a bind mount of a directory inside the podman container, so its contents land in the host's container storage (the container's overlay upper). That removes the RAM limit completely, at the cost of a guest→host round trip for every write to `/var`.

I didn't do that here because of podman inside the guest. I checked on a devspace: with a host directory shared over bcvk's current virtiofsd setup (`--bind`, no `--xattr`), rootful podman in a centos-bootc:stream10 guest using that directory as its storage root fails with `'overlay' is not supported over <unknown> ... backing file system is unsupported for this graph driver`, and setting a `trusted.*` xattr there fails with `Operation not supported`. So with today's virtiofsd options, a virtiofs `/var` would break container storage in the guest. I didn't test whether enabling xattrs in virtiofsd would make overlay storage work, or whether podman would then be usable but slow.

A middle option would be a sparse file on the host attached as a virtio-blk scratch disk and formatted for `/var` in the initramfs, reusing the plumbing `--add-swap` already has. That gives a real block filesystem (overlay works, no RAM limit) at the cost of an mkfs at boot and needing mkfs tools in the initramfs.

Is a tunable tmpfs OK as the first step, with one of those as a follow-up if needed?

The second problem in the issue, `bcvk libvirt run --filesystem ext4` failing with `rm: cannot remove '/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay': Device or resource busy`, has the same cause as #351: the to-disk install VM booted the image's `default.target`, so the quadlet started and held files open under `/var/lib/containers`. e2be03d ("to-disk: Switch to a minimal boot target for to-disk installation") already fixed that on main.

Part of #200

## Testing

Run on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace with KVM, using `quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10` and `df -h /var /run` inside `bcvk ephemeral run --execute`:

| | `/var` size |
|---|---|
| main, default 4G memory | 782M (the same tmpfs as `/run`) |
| this PR, default | 2.0G (`/run` still 782M) |
| `--var-size 3G` | 3.0G |
| `--var-size 75%` | 2.9G |
| `--memory 8G --add-swap 10G --var-size 10G` | 10G |

With the last configuration, `podman pull quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:43` (1.96 GB) inside the guest succeeds, using 2.0G of `/var`. `--var-size 10G,exec` and `--var-size 99999999999T` are rejected when the arguments are parsed, and `--add-swap 17179869184G` now fails with "Size too large".

- `make validate` (fmt, clippy, rustdoc with `-D warnings`) and `cargo test -p bcvk` (85 tests, including the new `test_parse_size`, `test_parse_var_size` and `test_cpio_var_size_dropin`) pass.
- Integration tests with `cargo test --release -p integration-tests`: all 11 `to_disk` tests pass, including `test_to_disk_quadlet`. `test_run_ephemeral_mount_layout` now also checks that `/var` comes from the separate `bcvk-var` tmpfs, and it passes, as does the new `test_run_ephemeral_var_size`. Of the 33 `ephemeral` tests, 31 pass. The other two, `test_varlink_ephemeral_run_ps_and_ssh` and `test_run_ephemeral_journal_output`, time out waiting 120s for boot when the whole set runs in parallel. That reproduces identically on main, and both pass when run alone. `just test-integration` itself couldn't run because `go-md2man` isn't available on RHEL 10, so the same steps were run by hand.
- The man pages were regenerated with `cargo xtask sync-manpages`.

items.title: ci: Add opt-in bootc-operator reverse dependency test

labels.name: ci/operator
labels.description: Run bootc-operator e2e revdep test

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: The poll stopped here; a person decides what is next

labels.name: review:deep
labels.description: Bot draft that needs a real review

items.body:
bootc-operator drives `bootc switch`/`bootc upgrade` on Kubernetes nodes, so a bootc change can break it in ways our own tests don't cover. This adds an opt-in workflow that runs the operator's e2e suite against bootc built from the PR.

How it works: the operator's e2e tests boot [bink](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bink) node VMs from a prebuilt disk image. The workflow builds Fedora 44 RPMs from the tree (`just package`), layers them onto the same bink node image the operator tests with (read from the label of the operator's default disk image), round-trips it through the bink registry so its digest matches what the nodes see, and builds a disk image from it with bink's own `build-disk-image` (so the PR's bootc also does the `install to-disk`). It then runs the operator's own `deploy-bink` and `e2e` targets, skipping `seed-node-image` with `make -o` since we seeded the registry ourselves. The bink commit comes from the operator's CI workflow, so the two stay in step, and the host setup mirrors the operator's e2e job. No change to bootc-operator is needed.

It takes roughly 1.5 hours, so it's opt-in: for PRs labeled `ci/operator` (on the label being added, and on later pushes while it's present), via `workflow_dispatch` (with an optional operator ref), and weekly on `bootc-dev`. A maintainer needs to create the `ci/operator` label.

The catch is that this is coupled to internals of the operator (its `deploy-bink`/`e2e`/`seed-node-image` Makefile targets and `print-var-*` helper, the `localhost:5000/node:latest` registry convention, `BINK_COMMIT` in its CI workflow) and of bink (its `node-images/fedora` `build-disk-image` target). If either side reshuffles those, this breaks, as the header comment in the workflow says. A more robust follow-up would be for bootc-operator to expose its e2e job as a reusable `workflow_call` workflow taking an RPM artifact (or node image), so the knowledge of how to test it lives in one place and this file shrinks to a single `uses:`.

FYI: bink's `build-disk-image` currently builds bcvk from a personal fork branch, `Johan-Liebert1/bcvk@img-to-install-cli-opt` (a workaround for a digest mismatch, see bootc-dev/bcvk#314, still open), so the install path here also goes through that branch until bink switches back to upstream bcvk.

Design choices that came up in review, kept deliberately:

- The label is `ci/operator`, following the existing `ci/*` label naming.
- The weekly schedule stays: it's the only thing that notices drift on the operator/bink side when no one has labeled a PR. Note scheduled-run failures only get emailed to whoever last edited the cron line; if that's not enough, a follow-up could open an issue on failure.
- The `package` job isn't cached or shared. The better dedup would be to consume `ci.yml`'s packages artifact once that's practical, rather than adding a separate cache here.

Lessons from composefs-rs's `bootc-revdep.yml` (which records a failed run on every push because of an invalid `if:`): the gating here uses only valid expressions and actionlint is clean apart from the `ubuntu-26.04` runner label, which it doesn't know yet and which `ci.yml` already uses. Unlabeled PRs get a skipped run, not a failed one.

Testing:

- The workflow itself ran for real on a PR inside the cgwalters-forge fork, triggered by adding `ci/operator`: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/actions/runs/35929518061 passed. The node image picked up the PR's RPM (`bootc-202609232239.g43ff95f900`), and all 9 operator e2e tests passed (`ok .../test/e2e 1925s`). Wall time: 30 min for `package` (no build cache), 55 min for `e2e`, of which 10 min is the disk image build.
- After review fixes (concurrency grouping, the installed-RPM assertion, `package` timeout and `persist-credentials: false`), a second full run at the current head also passed: https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/actions/runs/35937468141. The new assertion held (`rpm -q bootc` = `bootc-202609240013.g5c07bd6a3f-1.fc44`, the PR build, replacing the stock `bootc-202609220256.g5ed9e3f700`), and all 9 e2e tests passed (`ok .../test/e2e 1915s`). Adding an unrelated label (`ci/merge`) while it was running produced its own skipped run (https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/actions/runs/35937496687) and did not cancel it.
- On the same fork PR, a push without the label gave a `skipped` run, and the `opened` event gave none.
- The same steps replayed by hand (as a script) on a 16-core RHEL 10 devspace: `just package` for fedora-44, node and disk image build, `make -o seed-node-image deploy-bink`, then `make e2e`, with all 9 tests passing in 1328s. That also confirmed that `make -o` skips the phony `seed-node-image` target and that `TestControllerMembership`'s booted-digest check passes with the round-tripped image.
- actionlint is clean apart from the `ubuntu-26.04` label, same as `ci.yml`.
- Not exercised: `workflow_dispatch` (including a non-default `operator-ref`) and the weekly schedule. After the test run, the only change was the duration wording in a comment.

CI note (2026-09-24): the [`test-integration (centos-10, composefs, xfs, systemd, bls, unsealed)` failure](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/actions/runs/35937496696/job/107446872219) is unrelated to this change: `plan-44-shadow-fixup` hit a guest reboot timeout because `bootc-finalize-staged.service` timed out stopping (the `/boot` automount expire deadlock), the known flake fixed by cgwalters-forge/bootc#6. Failed jobs will be rerun once the run completes.

Also note: the `labeled` event also re-runs `ci.yml` (it already lists `labeled`), which predates this change.

Closes: #2423

items.title: ci: Add experimental RHEL 10 runner coverage
items.body:
## Motivation

Move bootc CI workloads to the stock GitHub-hosted RHEL 10 partner runner without maintaining a parallel RHEL workflow, while retaining one Ubuntu 26.04 compatibility lane.

## Design

This draft depends on [bootc-dev/actions#60](https://github.com/bootc-dev/actions/pull/60) and temporarily uses `cgwalters-bot/actions/bootc-host-setup@bootc-host-setup-rhel10`. That action owns distro-specific dependency installation and the RHEL libvirt workaround. `ci.yml` remains the sole workflow: the existing workload matrices move to RHEL 10, while one Ubuntu 26.04 job builds the CentOS 10 package and runs the readonly TMT plan with it.

The xtask VM launch paths also remove Cargo's inherited `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before invoking `bcvk libvirt run`, so host QEMU does not accidentally load build-tool libraries.

## RHEL libvirt investigation

The remaining RHEL failure was caused by libvirt's per-domain sVirt labeling conflicting with the readonly virtiofs export of rootless Podman storage used by `bcvk --bind-storage-ro`. The host setup action now writes the unprivileged session config at `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/libvirt/qemu.conf` with `security_driver = "none"` on RHEL when libvirt is requested, and validates its exact contents. Host SELinux remains Enforcing; this only disables per-domain sVirt confinement for the ephemeral unprivileged libvirt session.

Controlled bootc run [35322108262](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/actions/runs/35322108262) passed the isolated RHEL readonly workload with this configuration. Actions PR #60's technical checks, including its RHEL 10 host setup and libvirt jobs, also pass.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check -p xtask`
- `cargo test -p xtask` (13 passed)
- `cargo xtask update-generated direct --check`
- `git diff --check`
- `actionlint` with the repository's pre-existing disabled-job diagnostic ignored
- Independent review found no correctness or workflow-gating defects
- Full validation run [35342593795](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/actions/runs/35342593795): package jobs, Ubuntu compatibility, upgrades, baseconfigs, container export, and all four sealed UKI integration jobs passed; four unsealed GRUB jobs failed in the pre-existing `plan-44-shadow-fixup` (two missing-group assertions and two guest reboot timeouts) after integration was moved to the reviewer-requested 4c runner.

## AI disclosure

Assisted-by: AI

The workflow and xtask changes were AI-assisted and validated with the commands above. Human review is required; commits intentionally have no `Signed-off-by` trailers.

items.title: ostree-ext: override root dir metadata on merge commit

labels.name: area/ostree
labels.description: Issues related to ostree

items.body:
When building the merge commit in `write_merge_commit_impl()`, `write_dfd_to_mtree()` inherits the root dir metadata from the temp checkout dir, which causes its mode to be 0o755 rather than 0o555.

Manually override it to uid=0, gid=0, and importantly mode=0o555. This matches the expectations of the filesystem RPM and systemd's /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/root.conf.

Without this change, systemd-tmpfiles fails with `fchmod() of / failed: Read-only file system` on systems with a read-only root since systemd v261.

See https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/2238

Assisted-by: llm

---

I've manually confirmed that this resolves the root permissions issues (`0o755 -> 0o555`) locally by comparing output from systems with `bootc 1.17.1` to systems with this patch included, using both:

- RPM overrides in `cosa` builds of Fedora CoreOS
- Bootc builds using packages built using `just build` and run using `just test-tmt-nobuild --preserve-vm readonly`

Example output without patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
755
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00755 0 0      0 /
```

Vs with the patch:

```sh
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# stat -c '%a' /
555
[root@ibm-p8-kvm-03-guest-02 ~]# ostree ls -d $(rpm-ostree status -b --json | jq -r '.deployments[0].checksum') /
d00555 0 0      0 /
```

Of course, let me know if I'm missing anything or if any changes are required.

Bumps [actions/github-script](https://github.com/actions/github-script) from 8.0.0 to 9.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/github-script's releases.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.
  • Orchestration ID in user-agent — The ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

Breaking changes:

  • require('@actions/github') no longer works in scripts. The upgrade to @actions/github v9 (ESM-only) means require('@actions/github') will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
  • getOctokit is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.
  • If your script accesses other @actions/github internals beyond the standard github/octokit client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

items.title: workflows: Add a wrapper canary that runs a real dispatch and review
items.body:
#136 changed both agent wrappers, passed every check and review, and then broke every agent run for hours: nothing ran a real agent through a pull request's own wrappers, and the review ran the base branch's copy. This adds a wrapper canary. `wrapper-canary-gate.yml` sets a `wrapper-canary` status on every pull request to main. The status is success unless the pull request changes `cgwalters-agentic-job.yml` or `cgwalters-review.yml`; otherwise it stays pending until `wrapper-canary.yml` passes. The gate uses `pull_request_target`, but runs base code and reads only the file list over the API.

The canary is dispatched on main by a maintainer. Before dispatching, they read the head and push that commit to the branch `wrapper-canary`. This keeps fork heads away from secrets until someone has read them, and stops a pull request from rewriting the check. The canary then runs, in board-test, one noop implement through the dispatch wrapper and one review through the review wrapper, both at that branch. It passes only if both runs called their wrappers at the head commit and their `agent` and `check / check` jobs succeeded. The README's "Wrapper canary" section says how to run it and gives the setup order.

`admit`, `deployment` and `tailscale` don't trigger the canary. The wrappers call them at main, so no run before a merge can test a pull request's copy.

Both new files add a `pull_request_target` trigger and a zizmor ignore. workflows-check refuses both, so an owner has to merge this past the ruleset.

Verified with the unit tests (`node --test .github/workflows/*.test.mjs`, `just test-review`), actionlint 1.7.12, zizmor 1.31.1 offline and markdownlint. I couldn't run the runner-labels and workflows-check binaries (no cargo here) or a live canary, since the settings below don't exist yet.

Review: two passes. The first found two blockers, both fixed: the gate shared a file with the `@wrapper-canary` call, which GitHub resolves for every run, and the push procedure let a fork push run unread code. Still open:
- The ~10-minute bound is documented, not enforced. The dispatch wrapper has no timeout input, so its own 75-minute limit applies.
- A `pull_request` job named `wrapper-canary` in a fork could perhaps satisfy the required status, the same weakness `ci` has.
- Board-test's review runs are found by "newest since the reopen", not matched to the scratch pull request.

## Caller settings

- cgwalters-forge-stage/board-test, new file `.github/workflows/wrapper-canary-review.yml`:

  ```yaml
  name: wrapper-canary-review
  on:
    pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
      types: [reopened]
  permissions: {}
  jobs:
    review:
      if: github.event.pull_request.number == fromJSON(vars.WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL)
      uses: cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-review.yml@wrapper-canary
      permissions: {contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: write, actions: read, id-token: write, statuses: write}
  ```

  board-test also needs the variable `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`, and its `AGENT` must be unset or a real agent.
- Tailnet federation and inference broker: admit `job_workflow_ref` `cgwalters-forge/actions/.github/workflows/cgwalters-agentic-job.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary` and `.../cgwalters-review.yml@refs/heads/wrapper-canary`.
- cgwalters-forge/actions:
  - The branch `wrapper-canary`, created at main, with a ruleset that lets only maintainers update it.
  - The variables `WRAPPER_CANARY_ISSUE` and `WRAPPER_CANARY_PULL`: a scratch issue, and a non-draft scratch pull request opened by a collaborator, both in board-test.
  - The environment `agent-apply`, and access to the organization secret `CGWALTERS_BOT_PAT`.
  - Last, the main ruleset's required status check `wrapper-canary`.

Closes #138

items.title: runner: Isolate job VMs on a bridge with an egress allowlist
items.body:
## Executive summary

CI jobs run untrusted code in per-job VMs, so they should not be able to reach the LAN, the tailnet, link-local metadata addresses or the host's own services. This adds `runner-network.service`: a dedicated `runnerbr0` bridge and an `inet runner_network` nftables table that let job VMs reach only DNS on the listed resolvers and an allowlist from `/etc/atomic-linux/runner-network.conf`; everything else, private ranges and the host included, is dropped. The unit is enabled but skipped until that file exists, and no addresses are baked in. A firewalld `runner` zone accepts the bridge so the table alone decides. docs/runner-network.md describes the config and the rules.

Part of #41. Part of #26.

## Verification

`just lint` (now also shellchecks the new script) and `just fmt-check` pass. `just build`, and so `just image-test` (which runs the new `nft -c -f` check of the example config) and `bootc container lint`, could not run: containers fail to start in this sandbox (crun sd-bus error), and nft needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, which isn't available here either. The ruleset syntax was only checked by reading it, and the config-refusal half of the test passed when run directly on the host. No VM test of actual traffic yet.

One review pass found no blockers. Its important findings were fixed: load the rules before creating the bridge, reload without detaching VMs, refuse prefixes with host bits set, drop spoofed sources, and correct the docs. Still open: a VM test that probes allowed and denied destinations through firewalld, and whether NetworkManager should be told to leave `runnerbr0` unmanaged.

Closes #41

items.title: build: Install bootc from the fork's pinned release by default
items.body:
## Executive summary

Adds `BOOTC_SOURCE=forge` and makes it the default: `build/15-bootc.sh` downloads bootc from the immutable prerelease [`forge-63c743548946`](https://github.com/cgwalters-forge/bootc/releases/tag/forge-63c743548946) of cgwalters-forge/bootc, checks it against a pinned sha256 and installs it. That build carries the `bootc install to-existing-root` fixes for #68 that are pending upstream (bootc-dev/bootc#1343, bootc-dev/bootc#404); switch the default back to `fedora` once Fedora ships them.

The fork publishes Fedora 44 RPMs. On this Fedora 45 base they install cleanly but also pull in `openssl3-libs`, since Fedora 45 moved to OpenSSL 4. Only x86_64 is built, and the script refuses other architectures.

## How verified

Ran `bash -n` and shellcheck on `build/*.sh`, plus `just fmt-check`. Built the server variant locally with `just build`: the sha256 check passed, bootc 1.17.4 from the fork was installed, the initramfs check and `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` passed. The desktop variant and the VM tests run in CI.
